definition: The expression means that while what the speaker says may be true, it will not change the situation.
example: Fewer people may come because of the bad weather, but be that as it may, it’s too late to cancel the event.

definition: This idiom means to be made available or be known about, appear for the first time.
example: Their new electric car will see the light of day in one week.

definition: When you reach the point of no return, you must continue what you have started, because you have gone so far that it is impossible to go back.
example: I’ve resigned from that boring job. Now, I’ve reached a point of no return.

definition: This expression means to be in the middle of fierce competition or debate.
example: Ann realized that she wouldn’t suit to the cut and thrust approach of journalism.

definition: If you work extremely hard or put a lot of effort into achieving something, you break your back to do it.
example: She’s not going to break her back for such a low wage.

definition: This idiom means to be exceptionally proficient at something.
example: The little girl has got a real knack for the guitar.

definition: If a person or organisation gets or gains the upper hand, they take control over a situation.
example: The local police claim to have gained the upper hand over drinking and driving.

phrase: Rome wasn’t built in one day
definition: This idiom means that major and important projects take time.
example: The highway won’t be finished for another ten years. Rome wasn’t built in on day, the authorities say.

definition: This idiom means completely.
example: When I asked her about it, she flat-out denied it.

phrase: know which way the wind is blowing
definition: This expression means that it is advisable to know how a situation is developing in order to be prepared for any changes.
example: Before we act, we need to know which way the wind is blowing.

definition: Something described as the last word is the most recent or most fashionable in its category.
example: Her smartphone is the last word in technology.

definition: If someone lives beyond their means, they spend more money than they earn.
example: The cost of living in Berlin was so high that I was soon living beyond my means.

definition: If you do someone a good turn, you act in a helpful way.
example: Do a good turn and help him load the truck, will you?

definition: When faced with a serious problem, if you take steps that you know in advance will be futile, to show that you made an effort, you wave a dead chicken.
example: The laptop was damaged, but the technician decided to wave a dead chicken to satisfy the customer before announcing the bad news.

phrase: to give somebody a big head
definition: This expression means to praise somebody so much that they start thinking very highly of themselves.
example: Don’t tell her she’s good-looking. You’ll give her a big head.

definition: This idiom refers to the malicious posting of sexual images online to harm the reputation of an ex partner.
example: She posted some nasty pictures of him from when they were together. It’s revenge porn, obviously.

definition: When faced with a difficult or unpleasant situation, if you say that someone will have to grin and bear it, you mean that they will have to accept it without complaining.
example: The only seat available is in the back of the bus. Grin and bear it!

definition: To describe a person, thing or situation as a different kettle of fish means that it is completely different from what was previously mentioned.
example: I may have good business ideas but implementing them in your county is a different kettle of fish.

definition: This expression means that either a person is in serious difficulty and something bad is going to happen or the time has come when they will die.
example: The police have located the murderer, so his number is up.

definition: This idiom means neat and with everything in its correct place.
example: Now that the party is over, it’ll take a while to get things shipshape again.

definition: If you turn up/on the heat on a person or organisation, you put pressure on them in order to obtain what you want.
example: If the project is not delivered this week, we’ll have to turn on the heat.

definition: This expression refers to the reason for someone to make money.
example: I’m counting on this job for my bread and butter.

definition: This expression refers to the extent to which the authority or power of law extends.
example: He fled to Serbia hoping to escape the arm of the law.

definition: A large number of untruthful statements is referred to as a pack of lies.
example: The story turned out to be a pack of lies.

definition: It means to count the number of people around you. This is generally used on a school trip, to check for missing students.
example: She was counting noses when I saw her in front of the bus.

definition: This idiom means to remain aloof and detached from another person or situation.
example: I advise you to keep your distance. They might be dangerous.

definition: In a situation where you lose face, you feel that you are humiliated or are not respected.
example: We will find a solution to this pressing problem and we’ll assure that nobody will lose face.

definition: This idiom means to die.
example: If you crash at 80 km/h, the odds are you’ll buy the farm.

definition: Some people consider television to lack educational value and refer to it as the idiot box.
example: The kid spends his time in front of the idiot box. I really don’t understand who his parents allow him to do so.

phrase: give or take (a quantity or number)
definition: This term is used when expressing an amount or estimate that is not exactly right.
example: The marketing cost for next year campaign is 10.000 dollars, give or take.

definition: This means in a confused, disordered state.
example: She panicked just before the interview. One could say she was all at sea.

definition: The person who holds / takes the reins is someone who is in complete control of a firm or organisation.
example: Mary has been holding the reins for 10 years.

definition: When someone says they can thank their lucky stars, they are expressing heartfelt gratitude or feeling particularly fortunate.
example: I can thank my lucky stars that I wasn’t in the car.

definition: If you are in the limelight, you are in the public eye. This means that there are people who actually care about your personal life aside from all the work that you do.
example: I tried to avoid the publicity as much as possible, but I was in the limelight that period.

definition: Someone who is as fresh as a daisy is lively and attractive, in a clean and fresh way.
example: I met a girl at the gym. She is as fresh as a daisy.

definition: A person who plays to the gallery tries to gain popularity by behaving in a way that will appeal to the majority.
example: It’s no secret that she was elected by playing to the gallery.

definition: This idiom means to be what someone likes or is interested in.
example: Car racing doesn’t really float my boat.

definition: If someone picks holes in something such as a plan, an idea or a proposal, they criticize it or try to find fault with it.
example: She is picking holes in all my ideas!

definition: The difficulties encountered during the initial stage of an activity or project are called teething problems.
example: We had some teething problems when we opened the local store.

definition: If you offer guidance and protection to someone younger or less experienced, you take them under your wing.
example: I am very grateful to you for taking me under your wing.

definition: This idiom refers to the confusion caused by the chaos of battle.
example: After the bombing raid we had no idea where the enemy were. That’s to be expected in the fog of war.

definition: This expression refers to a husband, a wife or a partner of someone.
example: My other half loves cats, even though I can’t stand them.

definition: If two people are at cross purposes, there is a misunderstanding regarding what each one is talking about.
example: It seems we are at cross purposes. You are talking about a house and I am talking about a home.

definition: Two or more people who are even stevens are equal to each other. None of them has more than the others; none is owed anything or has anything due.
example: The boys equally shared the money so they are even stevens.

definition: This idiom means to not be worried at all by something.
example: Do whatever you want, Olive. I don’t care a toss.

definition: This idiom means to join in and help with something.
example: Last weekend we pitched in and cleaned the garden.

definition: A person who keeps up appearances maintains an outward show of prosperity so as to hide their difficulties from other.
example: She continued to keep up appearances even when business was bad.

definition: This idiom means to produce excellent results or be extremely effective, especially unexpectedly.
example: This medicine does wonders!

phrase: start the ball rolling / keep the ball rolling
definition: If you start the ball rolling, you begin an activity in which other people will join. If you keep the ball rolling you maintain the momentum of an activity.
example: Let’s start the ball rolling by calling on our first guest.

definition: If an idea or project is pie in the sky, it is completely unrealistic or unlikely to be achieved.
example: His project about expanding to Africa is a pie in the sky.

definition: When people get down to the nitty-gritty, they begin to discuss the most important points or the practical details.
example: I was interested in the subject, but we didn’t get down to the nitty-gritty until all partners arrived.

definition: Before an election, when politicians are campaigning for support and votes, they are on the stump.
example: On the stump, they all say that great things will be done.

definition: This idiom means to squeeze one’s way out of something; to evade or avoid a job or responsibility.
example: They tried to weasel out of the deal later.

definition: This idiom means to drop in for a visit.
example: Hey, Steve! Why don’t you swing by around 8.30?

definition: The partner who wears the trousers/pants is the one who makes the important decisions.
example: Speak to her. She wears the pants.

definition: If you hammer home a point or an argument, you repeat it often to make sure that it is fully understood.
example: The teacher hammered home the importance of doing homework.

definition: If something, such as a plan or idea, has disaster written all over it, it is thought to be heading for complete failure or will cause a lot of trouble.
example: Your idea of travelling to the mountain has disaster written all over it.

phrase: do something out of force of habit
definition: When something is done out of force of habit, it has become automatic through repetition.
example: I always park in the back of the store out of force of habit.

phrase: burn the candle at both ends
definition: If you burn the candle at both ends, you exhaust yourself by doing too much, especially going to bed late and getting up early.
example: She looks bad. I think she has been burning the candle at both ends of late.

definition: To do somebody’s dirty work means to do the unpleasant or difficult work that another person does not want to do.
example: Life’s quite easy for her. She almost always finds a fool to do her dirty work.

definition: Someone who is on the wagon is no longer drinking alcohol.
example: No beer for me, please – I’m on the wagon.

definition: This idiom means to attempt to do something or to take a turn trying to do something.
example: I haven’t fixed a motor so far, but I’ll have a crack at it.

definition: If you do something quick as a flash, you do it very quickly.
example: Quick as a flash, she exited the room.

definition: A well-known and much-used trick, which is still effective today, is called the oldest trick in the book.
example: He slightly hit me to attract my attention while his accomplice stole my wallet – the oldest trick in the book!

definition: This idiom means to leave very quickly, often to avoid getting into trouble.
example: They are coming! We’d better scarper.

definition: This expression means everyone or everybody.
example: Every Tom, Dick and Harry has a smartphone nowadays.

phrase: from the cradle to the grave
definition: This expression means “during the whole of your life or throughout life”.
example: This insurance plan provides protection from the cradle to the grave.

definition: If you cross the Rubicon, you make an irreversible decision or commit to a course of action that cannot be changed.
example: I will cross the Rubicon and stop teaching arts.

definition: This expression is used as an apology for using crude or offensive language.
example: He’s a bloody bastard! Excuse my French.

definition: This idiom means to destroy an argument or theory.
example: They sent their proposal. It was all nonsense and it was shot down in flames.

definition: This expression refers to hidden or unsaid explanation behind an outlook or sight.
example: She is denying, but I am sure that she had done something; every picture tells a story.

phrase: make a mountain out of a molehill
definition: If someone makes a mountain out of a molehill, they make a small, unimportant problem seem much more serious than it is.
example: I don’t like to speak to her because she always makes a mountain out of a molehill.

definition: This phrase refers to a final drink taken just before leaving on a journey.
example: Oh, come on! One for the road!

definition: If you change horses in midstream, you change your plan, or choose a new leader, in the middle of an important activity.
example: I think it would be better if we go through with the original plan. It’s risky to change horses in midstream.

phrase: if you scratch my back, I’ll scratch yours
definition: This expression means to return a favour for a favour.
example: You know that I will help you as I’ve done before. If you scratch my back, I’ll scratch yours…

definition: This idiom refers to an old man, especially one who is eccentric, curmudgeonly or grotesque.
example: She married an old codger.

definition: This idiom refers to a large collection of something.
example: A whole raft of students protested against those measures.

definition: This idiom means “firmly or permanently established, not subject to change, unalterable“.
example: The law looks promising, but we’ll have to wait until it’s cast in concrete.

definition: This idiom means naked.
example: There were some photos of her in the buff.

definition: This idiom refers to a story invented in order to deceive.
example: The whole text is a tissue of lies.

definition: If someone is fighting a losing battle, they are trying to do something even when there is little chance of succeeding.
example: The director is fighting a losing battle trying to ban smartphone at desk.

phrase: to a T / down to a T / to a tee
definition: This idiom literally means “done precisely”.
example: She loves writing poetry. It fits her to a T.

definition: Someone who has horse sense is a practical thinker who has the ability to make sensible decisions.
example: I never worry when it comes to tough decisions. Kris has good horse sense and solves the situation.

definition: If you take action while the going is good, you do something before the situation changes and it is no longer possible.
example: There’s a 10% discount on the laptop I want. I will buy it while the going is good.

phrase: can’t for the life of me
definition: This expression can be used to say that it is impossible for you to do something, no matter how hard you try.
example: I can’t for the life of me find my feet in this job.

definition: Something that is wearing thin is decreasing or losing its interest.
example: This excuse is wearing thin!

definition: A person who is set in their ways is unable or unwilling to change their ideas, habits or methods, often because they are old.
example: My grandparents have the same routine daily. They are set in their ways.

definition: All told means the final number, when everything has been counted.
example: The number of visitors to the exhibition, all told, was 1459.

definition: If a person has his/her hands tied something such as an agreement or a rule is preventing them from doing what they would like to do.
example: Mary deserves to earn more, but my hands are tied by the salary agreement.

definition: This phrase refers to a sea trip from England to continental Europe to buy cheap drink.
example: Let’s go on a booze cruise.

definition: Someone who is as nutty as a fruitcake is insane or crazy.
example: You shouldn’t listen to what the old woman says; she’s as nutty as a fruitcake.

definition: This expression is said ironically when two people have matching thoughts.
example: Do you have the same solution? Well, I told you that great minds think alike.

definition: This expression refers to a comment or a prophecy that is expected to be proved incorrect.
example: I swore that I would not drink anymore. My famous last words.

definition: This idiom means “angry and likely to argue or punish”.
example: I don’t like when my girlfriend is on the warpath.

phrase: put your head on the block
definition: If you put yourself in a dangerous situation where you risk losing your job or your reputation if things go wrong, you put your head on the block.
example: She asked me to recommend her son for the job, but I won’t put my head on the block.

definition: If you badger someone into doing something, you persistently nag or pester them until you obtain what you want.
example: I badgered my parents into buying me a new smartphone.

phrase: make your hair stand on end
definition: If you are absolutely terrified of something, it makes your hair stand on end.
example: Even the idea of getting on a small plane makes her hair stand on end.

definition: If a discussion or debate generates more heat than light, it causes anger or intense reaction but doesn’t clarify anything.
example: The meeting on marketing budget generated more heat than light.

phrase: fly in the face of something
definition: If an action or statement flies in the face of something, it is completely opposite to what is usual or expected.
example: His style of repairing cars flies in the face of the firm’s methods.

phrase: in a class of one’s own
definition: If someone is in a class of their own, they are unequalled and considered better than anyone else of their kind.
example: As a boxer, he was in a class of his own.

definition: Someone who spends additional money on something that was already considered a bad investment is said to throw good money after bad.
example: Buying a second-hand laptop and then spending money to have it repaired is throwing good money after bad.

definition: This idiom is an euphemism for going to the lavatory.
example: John is visiting the ladies’ room.

definition: If you find it difficult to pay for your everyday needs because you have very little money, it is hard for you to make ends meet.
example: My salary was so low that I could hardly make ends meet.

definition: This idiom means to cause a particular situation to happen or a particular decision to be made, when other situations or decisions are possible.
example: Three quick goals from Rooney tipped the scales in favour of England.

definition: To say that someone is slinging mud at another person means that they are trying to damage that person’s reputation by saying bad things about them.
example: Candidates often sling mud at each other.

definition: When you stretch the truth, you exaggerate the facts or say things that are not exactly true.
example: Some politicians are tempted to stretch the truth about their skills or work experience.

definition: This expression is used when people are procrastinating or wasting their time on unimportant matters while there are more serious problems to be dealt with.
example: The management seems to be fiddling while Rome burns. They didn’t take any decision.

definition: This idiom means to have one’s relationship with someone completely diminished, typically due to an argument or unpleasant incident.
example: The man left home after falling out with his wife.

definition: If you make a clown of yourself, you are doing something that makes people laugh.
example: Even she wanted to entertain us, Ada couldn’t make a clown of herself.

definition: When someone, especially a woman, is dressed to kill, they are wearing very fashionable or glamorous clothes intended to attract attention.
example: My wife arrived at the reception dressed to kill.

definition: If you take something at its face value, you assume that it is genuinely what it appears to be.
example: The laptop seems to be in mint condition but don’t take it at its face value. Get an expert to check it out.

definition: If something is referred to as child’s play, it is considered to be simple or easy to do.
example: Using this new smartphone is child’s play as compared to the old one.

definition: The correct way to behave in a particular social situation is called the done thing.
example: Wearing jeans at an informal party is the done thing.

definition: This idiom means to try to discover things that are not really related to you.
example: I wish she’d stop sticking her nose into my business.

definition: If you are on the horns of a dilemma, you are faced with a choice between two equally unpleasant options.
example: I’m on the horns of a dilemma. Please let me a few days to consider your offer.

definition: If you speak about something in glowing terms, you talk about it in a very positive way.
example: I always talk about my home town in glowing terms.

definition: If one person can’t hold a candle to another, they are much less competent or do not perform as well as the other.
example: David is very intelligent but he can’t hold a candle to his sister when it comes to sports.

definition: This idiom refers to some backup that someone has in case of potential problems, often financial ones.
example: I always have money in my savings account as a safety net.

definition: If you carry the torch, you have strong feelings for someone with whom you do not or cannot have a relationship.
example: She has been carrying the torch for John since their college days.

definition: This expression means that the situation is improving and you feel more positive about the future.
example: I’ve got three job interviews next week so things are looking up.

definition: This phrase means to take care of issues that are not critical but have remained outstanding.
example: I’m almost ready to move, but I need to tie up some loose ends with my family.

definition: If someone or something opens the floodgates, they release something that had previously been held under control.
example: Easing price controls will open the floodgates to inflation.

definition: This expression is used to warm someone that if they do not improve, they will have to leave their job.
example: When she started neglecting the customers, she was told to shape up or ship out.

definition: This expression means to save money for later.
example: I’m not a stingy man. I’m just saving for a rainy day.

definition: This expression refers to a person who is extremely reluctant or unwilling to change a particular opinion, behaviour or course of action.
example: My brother is as obstinate as a mule, even if he’s wrong.

definition: If someone is able to keep body and soul together, they manage to survive.
example: That time I was unemployed and it was hard for me to keep body and soul together.

definition: If you are on the crest of a wave, you are very successful in what you are doing.
example: My small company in going from success to success. It’s on the crest of a wave.

definition: This idiom means that a thing which has neither rhyme nor reason makes no sense, from either a poetic or logical standpoint.
example: Your words have neither rhyme nor reason. What’s the point?

definition: This idiom refers to the authorities or a large organisation which tries to control every part of people’s lives and to know everything about them.
example: They have complained against the “Big Brother” regulations.

definition: If a person is at someone’s beck and call they are ready to obey orders instantly.
example: She’s incapable of doing anything herself. She is used to having people at her beck and call.

definition: If you have two left feet, you are clumsy or awkward in your movements.
example: I’m a bad dancer. I have two left feet!

definition: If you have more money than sense, you have a lot of money which you waste by spending it in a foolish manner.
example: She celebrated the birth of their baby by buying a yacht. She’s got more money than sense.

definition: If you are on automatic pilot, you do something without thinking about it or having to pay attention, because you do it regularly.
example: At first I was worried about looking after my brother but after a while I was on automatic pilot.

definition: During a conflict, when employees decide to do only the minimum amount of work required by company rules, and refuse any overtime, they work to rule.
example: All employees decided to work to rule, which was somehow normal.

definition: If you are in seventh heaven, you are extremely happy.
example: Every time I sell a book, I’m in seventh heaven.

definition: This idiom is used to say that something is typical of America.
example: Baseball is as American as apple pie.

definition: This expression means very happy and comfortable.
example: When my parents left for holiday, I was happy as a clam.

definition: If you show much more skill or ability than your opponent, you run rings/circles around them.
example: The teenage girl ran rings around the other contestants.

definition: If a project or contract receives a seal of approval, it receives formal support or approval from higher authorities.
example: We can’t make the deal without the manager’s seal of approval.

definition: This idiom means almost time or high time.
example: Hurry! It’s about time for the game to start. It’s about time I got a new pair of shoes.

definition: This idiom refers to a reversal or fortune or disappointment.
example: Her failure was a real knock-back for the couple.

definition: If you bite the bullet, you accept something unpleasant because you cannot avoid it.
example: If you don’t have health insurance, you have to bite the bullet and pay the hospital fees in case something happens.

phrase: to be on the home stretch
definition: To say that you are on the home stretch means that you are approaching the end of something such as a task, a race or a journey.
example: Don’t give up now – you are on the home stretch now!

definition: When things or people come out of the woodwork, they appear or emerge unexpectedly, as if from nowhere, and usually in large number.
example: As soon as we bought the tennis table, our children had “friends” coming out of the woodwork.

definition: If someone robs Peter to pay Paul, they pay one debt with money borrowed from someone else, thus creating another debt.
example: She borrowed from a friend to pay her overdraft. That’s a typical case of robbing Peter to pay Paul.

phrase: work your fingers to the bone
definition: A person who works their fingers to the bone is extremely hardworking.
example: I deserve my success because I have worked my fingers to the bone.

definition: This idiom means to be quiet.
example: We are in a meeting so please shut your cake hole!

definition: If someone causes offence or irritation by speaking or behaving in an inappropriate manner, you put them in their place by letting them know that they are not as important as they seem to believe.
example: He needs to be put in his place!

definition: This idiom means to be satisfactory and of an expected level.
example: I didn’t make the grade for the test, so I have to do it all over again.

definition: If you rule the roost, you are the most important and powerful person in a group or community.
example: Officially, she runs the company, but it’s her father who rules the roost.

definition: If you speak off the cuff, you say something without any previous thought or preparation.
example: I handle off-the-cuff interviews very well.

definition: This expression refers to intense competition and rivalry in pursuit of one’s own interests, with no concern for morality.
example: The local business context is tough nowadays. There’s a dog eat dog attitude.

definition: This expression means to win by getting one’s opponents to fight among themselves.
example: We have to use the divide and rule strategy to weaken our opponents.

definition: Someone who brings up the rear is the last person in a group of people who are walking or running.
example: The group walked calmly up the room, with the manager bringing up the rear.

definition: When someone hits the airwaves, they go on radio and/or TV to be interviewed or to promote something.
example: The man was embarrassed when his wife hit the airwaves with her side of the story.

definition: This expression means not to have the knowledge, experience or skills to deal with a particular subject or situation.
example: We realised that the subject was out of the depth of Marry.

phrase: you can’t teach an old dog new tricks
definition: This expression means that someone who is used to doing things in a certain way will find it difficult to change their habits.
example: My grandmother will never use a laptop. You can’t teach an old dog new tricks.

definition: If you raise/lower your sights, you raise or lower your expectations or you are more or less ambitious.
example: She had to lower her sights and accept a less well-paid job.

definition: If you are at your wits’ end, you are very worried about something and do not know what to do.
example: The whole situation made me be at my wits’ end.

definition: To say that someone has been put out to pasture means that they have been forced to retire or give up their responsibilities.
example: She feels that it’s too early to be put out to pasture.

definition: If you tell someone to put their house in order, you are saying that they should organize their own affairs before giving advice to other people.
example: I don’t accept your piece of advice. You should put your house in order first.

definition: A person who is full of beans is lively, active and healthy.
example: She may be getting old but she’s full of beans.

definition: This means to do something innovative.
example: This discovery definitely breaks new ground in the energy problem.

definition: A person who is as fit as a fiddle is in an excellent state of health or physical condition.
example: My father is nearly sixty, but he’s as fit as a fiddle.

definition: If something happens at the eleventh hour, it happens when it is almost too late or at the last possible moment.
example: I finished the project at the eleventh hour.

definition: If someone or something gets the better of you, it defeats you.
example: Steve tried not to drink anything for a week, but he couldn’t. His appetite for beer got the better of him.

definition: This is a humorous way of saying that someone is still alive.
example: Glad to see that you’re still in the land of the living!

definition: This idiom means to wait and not do anything until the time is right for action.
example: You’ll be promoted. Just sit tight and do your job well.

definition: Someone or something that turns out to be disappointing, for example after a promotional campaign or marketing strategy which led us to expect something better, is called all sizzle and no steak.
example: Owing to the electoral promises she made, which so far she has failed to keep, many people call the new president “all sizzle and no steak”.

definition: If you declare with force and authority that something must stop, and announce the consequences if it happens again, you read the riot act.
example: The manager read us the riot act after we lied to him.

definition: This idiom refers to someone who is formally dressed or well dressed.
example: Even the babies at that party were suited and booted.

definition: If someone looks down their nose at a person or thing, they consider that person or thing inferior.
example: I hate when she looks down her nose at me.

definition: This expression is used when it is the right moment to do something.
example: I managed to sell the house when the time was ripe.

definition: This phrase means to pass time idly having to wait for someone or something.
example: The player has been kicking his heels on the sidelines this season.

definition: This expression is used to say that opposing groups are ready to defend the reason behind the conflict.
example: The battle lines have been drawn between those who accept the changes and those who don’t.

definition: If someone’s jaw drops, they show total amazement.
example: When the winner was announced, Steve has jaw dropped.

definition: This phrase means that the wicked shall be tormented in hell.
example: You should act legally. There’s no rest for the wicked.

definition: This expression refers to something that is added to ensure that something else is made complete.
example: She never ceases to put her final touch to every food.

definition: If something costs the earth, it is very expensive indeed.
example: He wears watches that cost the earth!

definition: If you bite someone’s head off, you criticize them strongly (and perhaps unfairly).
example: I worked 14 hours a day all week and my boss bit my head off for not doing my part of the project.

definition: Someone who has a positive behaviour pattern on an occasional basis, but not generally. Random bursts of positivity.
example: She offered to cook dinner. I guess she has her moments!

definition: To go Dutch with somebody means to share the cost of something such as a meal or a concert.
example: I’ve gone Dutch with my girlfriend and eat at that cosy restaurant.

definition: An activity or task that requires too much effort is too much like hard work.
example: It’s so hot today and I have so many things to do in the garden. That’s too much like hard work.

phrase: want somebody’s head on a platter
definition: If someone makes you so angry that you want them to be punished, you want their head on a platter.
example: She was so angry when she read the article about her company that she wanted the journalist’s head on a platter.

definition: If someone or something is light years ahead, they are far more advanced in terms of development or progress.
example: We’ve got to invest more in roads – our neighbours are light years ahead.

definition: If you leave well alone, you decide not to interfere with or change something that is acceptable or adequate.
example: It would be hard to get a better offer. Let’s leave well alone.

definition: If you make short work of something, you do it or finish it quickly.
example: The team were hungry at the end of the day, so they made short work of the food.

definition: A person who has itchy feet is someone who finds it difficult to stay in one place and likes to move often so as to discover new places.
example: She never stays for a long period anywhere. She’s got itchy feet.

definition: This expression means that it is useless to try to win a battle against a politician, establishment or bureaucracy in general.
example: In the end, I decided that it was a waste of time and energy trying to obtain a tax refund – can’t fight the city hall!

definition: A high-flyer is a person who has achieved notable success, usually more quickly than normal. The term is also used to describe speculative stock that has reached a high price in a short time.
example: Can he be considered a high-flyer?

definition: If something cuts no ice, it has no effect or makes no impression on someone.
example: His explanations cut no ice with her. She won’t forgive him.

phrase: take the law into your own hands
definition: If you act personally against someone who has done something wrong, you take the law into your own hands.
example: I took the law into my own hands and hit the thief.

definition: Something which no longer exists or is rarely used today is a thing of the past.
example: Video cassettes are a thing of the past.

definition: This expression means that because horses race better on a course that suits them, it is important to match people with suitable jobs or tasks.
example: Her experience in the beauty industry doesn’t make her ideal for this job. Horses for courses, remember?

definition: This phrase refers to a false and exaggerated belief about one’s status or importance.
example: I advise you to get rid of this delusion of grandeur.

definition: When people rake over the ashes, they discuss an unpleasant event which took place in the past.
example: Her small business went bankrupt many years ago, but she still rakes over the ashes from time to time.

phrase: as poor as a church mouse
definition: If someone is as poor as a church mouse, they are utterly poor.
example: Let’s help the child. He’s as poor as a church mouse.

definition: This expression means to pursue a line of research that points the way to great discoveries.
example: The researchers have blazed a trail in developing new techniques for treating diabetes.

definition: We used this idiom for something that happens every year for many years in a row.
example: Year in, year out we go to the same holiday resort.

definition: This expression refers to the difficulty of coordinating a situation which involves people who want to act independently.
example: Trying to arrange a meeting for a group of people from different countries is like herding cats!

definition: Someone who has nerves of steel is not afraid in difficult or dangerous situations.
example: Most police officers need to have nerves of steel.

definition: Things that sell like hot cakes sell quickly or in large quantities.
example: Brian is a very successful author. His books always sell like hot cakes.

definition: The term “daylight robbery” is used when the price of something is thought to be much too high.
example: Do you want 15 euros for an orange juice? That’s daylight robbery!

definition: This expression refers to the unusual or unlikely association of two or more people, companies or states.
example: A priest and a politician – strange bedfellow don’t you think?

definition: If you use a shotgun approach, you cover a wide range in a non-selective, haphazard and inefficient manner.
example: We must get rid of this shotgun approach.

definition: If you look the part, your appearance makes you ideally suited for a particular job or role.
example: It was a mistake to choose a young boy to play the robber. He didn’t look the part at all.

definition: This idiom means to satisfy or fulfill everything that is necessary or desired.
example: This new game ticks all the boxes.

definition: If you meet someone halfway you accept to make a compromise and give them part of what they are trying to obtain.
example: The bank decided to meet us halfway by splitting the difference.

definition: A person who drinks alcohol often is on the bottle.
example: Maria went on the bottle after she lost her job.

definition: An activity or task that is no picnic is unpleasant or difficult.
example: I’ve told you that this mission is no picnic.

phrase: to be out of the red
definition: This expression means to be out of debt.
example: Our company if finally out of the red now!

definition: This idiom means that the show has come to an end. It’s all over.
example: Come on! Let’s go home. Elvis has left the building.

definition: A person who is as white as a ghost looks very pale and frightened.
example: Marry went as white as a ghost when she saw the gun.

definition: If someone is as happy as a lark, they are very happy (sometimes with the connotation of being carefree or unaware of grimmer realities).
example: I’m as happy as a lark with my wage raise.

definition: This idiom means “after death”.
example: Do you think there’s life beyond the grave?

definition: This idiom means to be taken by surprise.
example: The government was caught napping that day.

definition: This idiom refers to someone possessing poor judgment or knowledge.
example: Don’t consider his words. He doesn’t know shit from Shinola.

phrase: you can’t judge a book by its cover
definition: This expression means that you should not form an opinion about something from its appearance only.
example: She leads a simple life but in fact she’s quite wealthy. You can’t judge a book by its cover.

definition: People who are two of a kind are similar in character, attitude or tastes.
example: Mike and Anna are two of a kind. They enjoy skiing and skating.

definition: This expression literally means “have existed”.
example: There’s nothing new about smartphones – they’ve been around for years.

definition: If you are “all things to all people”, you please or satisfy everyone.
example: Monica is exhausted trying to be a good wife, a good mother and a good professor. She can’t be all things to all people.

definition: This idiom refers to a state of confusion, bad organization or untidiness or something that is in this state.
example: After the party, the house was a complete shambles.

definition: This term describes a situation where an accident or a disaster nearly happened.
example: I almost hit the child who ran in front of my motorcycle. It was a close shave.

definition: This idiom means “free”.
example: Ten prisoners are at large following a series of escapes.

definition: If you leave the door open, you behave in such a way as to allow the possibility of further action.
example: It’s good for you to leave the door open in any situation.

definition: If you are hell-bent on doing something, you are recklessly determined to do it, even if it is dangerous or stupid.
example: She was hell-bent on revenge.

definition: If you make a mistake as a result of misjudging something, you overshoot the mark.
example: Steven overshot the mark by about 30%.

phrase: make a point of doing something
definition: If you make a point of doing something, you make an effort to do what you think is the right thing to do.
example: The artist made a point of thanking the spectators.

definition: This idiom means that if you wait for something to happen it takes longer.
example: Stop waiting for her call. A watched pot never boils!

definition: If you teach something to someone through constant repetition, you drum it into their head.
example: I remember when I was at school and things like multiplication tables were drummed into my head.

definition: This idiom means being careful – taking double measures to avoid risk. It alludes to the use of both belt and braces to hold up a person’s trousers.
example: I wrote to the company and phoned as well – belt and braces.

definition: During a discussion or debate, if you play devil’s advocate, you pretend to be against an idea or plan in order to determine the validity of the arguments in favour of it.
example: I decided to play devil’s advocate just to see how determined they were about that mission.

definition: To describe something as a dog’s breakfast means that it is a complete mess.
example: The new employee made a dog’s breakfast out of the registers.

definition: This idiom means “with sincere intentions”.
example: The sides should be able to sit down and negotiate in earnest.

definition: Something or someone who tugs at the heartstrings causes others to feel a great deal of pity or sadness.
example: The hospital’s plea for funds tugged at the heartstrings of people.

phrase: handed to someone on a platter
definition: If someone gets something easily, without having to make an effort to obtain it, it is handed to them on a platter.
example: I was appointed marketing manager in my father’s company. The job was handed to me on a platter.

definition: The expression is used to express surprise at something that you find difficult to understand.
example: It beats me how they can live in that tiny house!

definition: If you weigh the pros and cons, you consider the advantages and disadvantages, the arguments for or against something.
example: We have to weigh the pros and cons for this merger.

definition: This phrase means to be up to the required standard.
example: We need a million dollars to get the facility up to snuff.

definition: If one person is tied to another’s apron strings, they remain dependent at an age when they should be independent.
example: All her decisions are influenced by her mother. She is still tied to her apron strings.

definition: The lion’s share of something is the largest portion or the best part.
example: He left little money to her; the lion’s share was passed down to their children.

definition: This expression means to have a possibility or a hope of success.
example: If funding is withdrawn, this school won’t stand a chance.

definition: If you have your head in the clouds, you are so absorbed by your thoughts that you are not paying attention to what is happening around you.
example: I don’t listen to her today – I have my head in the clouds.

definition: Such an idea or suggestion is considered to be silly, foolish or totally impractical.
example: You’ll never make any progress if you have nothing but harebrained ideas to offer for us.

definition: This idiom is used when you want something to stop.
example: Enough is enough – I won’t argue with you.

definition: This idiom means to make something known for everybody.
example: I had to break the news to them.

definition: If a person has a clean bill of health, they have a report or certificate declaring that their health is satisfactory.
example: All candidates for this important position must provide a clean bill of health.

definition: This idiom means to convince someone of something because you were persuasive.
example: You’ve sold me on going to the party with you.

definition: If you clap eyes on someone or something, you actually see them.
example: Well, I’ve heard of her but I’ve never clapped eyes on her.

definition: This expression means to follow the correct steps in order to get something done.
example: If you want to get a commercial licence, you will have to go through the proper channels.

definition: This idiom means parsimonious.
example: He’s a penny-pinching guy.

definition: People who are full of piss and vinegar are very lively and boisterous or full of youthful vitality.
example: The worst part is that we have to take care of kids full of piss and vinegar.

definition: If something has a very strong unpleasant smell, it stinks to high heaven.
example: Take off your socks – they stink to high heaven! Don’t you smell?!

definition: If you smell a rat, it means that you suspect that something is wrong or that someone is doing something dishonest or incorrect.
example: The organisation hasn’t performed well of late. I smell a rat.

definition: If you are determined to obtain or achieve something at all costs, you want it regardless of the expense, effort or sacrifice involved.
example: The officer was determined at all costs to get a report from the war zone.

definition: If you say “you could have knocked me down with a feather”, you mean that you were extremely surprised by something.
example: I won all the votes! You could have knocked me down with a feather!

definition: This phrase means disintegrated into small fragments by a sudden impact or explosion.
example: The city was blown to smithereens by the bombing.

definition: This idiom means to change to a lower level or earlier time.
example: These regulations have put the clock back five years.

definition: This idiom refers to an attempt to make someone say something nice to you or about you.
example: The little girl loves to fish for compliments when she manages to do her homework all by herself.

definition: If you polish something off, you finish it quickly or easily.
example: They thought there was too much food, but the guests polished it off in no time.

definition: A small group of people who resist change or disagree with a proposal, form a pocket of resistance.
example: The manager wants to introduce a new marketing plan, but there’s a pocket of resistance in the sales department.

definition: If you upset the apple cart, you do or say something to spoil a satisfactory plan or situation.
example: I hope Cristina doesn’t participate to this meeting; she could upset the apple cart.

definition: If something is accomplished at/in one fell swoop, it is done in a single action, usually rapidly and ruthlessly.
example: The houses were demolished in one fell swoop.

definition: This idiom means pretentiously self-important, haughty or pompous.
example: I don’t like Tim because is a hoity-toity man.

definition: If you spread yourself too thin, you do too many things at the same time and can’t do any of them well.
example: Don’t spread yourself too thin!

phrase: wind up in the wrong hands
definition: If something winds up in the wrong hands, it comes into the possession of someone undesirable, for example an opponent or a competitor.
example: Be careful with the plans. We don’t want them to wind up in the wrong hands.

definition: If you are caught in the crossfire, you suffer the effects of an argument or dispute between two people or groups.
example: When the two drivers started to quarrel, their passengers were caught in the crossfire.

phrase: a skeleton in the closet / cupboard
definition: This idiom refers to a secret and possibly ruinous source of shame.
example: We all have a skeleton in the closet.

definition: If you are out on the town, you are out enjoying yourself.
example: It’s good to have a night out on the town every now and again.

phrase: pluck something out of the air
definition: This expression means to say a name, date, number etc. spontaneously, without thinking about it.
example: I just plucked a name out of the air and called my cat Daisy.

definition: This idiom refers to a conventional and law-abiding course.
example: I want to open a new factory in China and I want the whole process to be strait and narrow.

definition: This phrase refers to confidence gained from being drunk.
example: After several beers, he’s got Dutch courage.

definition: This is an informal phrase used for keeping people away from your affairs.
example: I haven’t asked for your opinion. Mind your own beeswax!

definition: To say that the bubble has burst means that the success of an idea, a product or a situation has suddenly stopped.
example: Starcraft II was a phenomenal success but the bubble has burst.

definition: If you do something primarily to draw attention to yourself and feel important or superior to others, you are on an ego trip.
example: My opinion is that her speech about helping the underprivileged was a long ego trip.

phrase: standing on the shoulders of giants
definition: This phrase means to use the understanding gained by major thinkers who have gone before in order to make intellectual progress.
example: Standing on the shoulders of giants, she discovered a new formula.

definition: This expression means to describe something in a flattering (bright) or unflattering (dark) way.
example: I chose to paint everything about the hard times I was going through in bright.

definition: If you pull through, you recover from a serious illness.
example: She had to undergo brain surgery but she pulled through.

definition: To say this expression means that money is not easily obtained.
example: Be careful how you spend your pocket money, Mary. Money doesn’t grow on trees.

definition: This idiom refers to something that is too easy.
example: For him, changing a tyre is like shooting fish in a barrel.

definition: A person who holds the same position as oneself in another organisation is called one’s opposite number.
example: I’ve spoken to my opposite number in several local companies and we all agreed to join the campaign.

definition: This is a phrase used to express that a defeat was unjust, possibly due to an injustice committed by someone else.
example: After the goal was cancelled, the coach shouted: We were robbed!

phrase: by the sweat of your brow
definition: If you earn or achieve something by the sweat of your brow, you do it through hard work and no help.
example: I’ve got this job by the sweat of my brow.

definition: If someone has a finger in every pie, they are involved in many activities.
example: You should talk to Steve about the recreational activities in this little town. He has a finger in every pie.

definition: If you put your life at risk by doing something very dangerous, you dice with death.
example: Driving at such high speed is dicing with death.

definition: This expression means to confess completely.
example: He decided to make a clean breast of the robbery to the officer.

phrase: neck and neck / a two horse race
definition: In a contest, when two competitors reach the same level, they are neck and neck, so it is impossible to say who will win.
example: At the moment, the two players are neck and neck.

definition: When a person is tarred with the same brush, they are regarded as having the same faults or bad qualities as those they associate with.
example: You shouldn’t hang around with them. You might be tarred with the same brush.

definition: If something has seen better days, it has aged visibly in comparison with when it was new.
example: This car has seen better days.

definition: This idiom refers to a burden which some unfortunate person has to carry.
example: She has an albatross around her neck this period.

definition: This expression refers to people’s behaviour in a difficult or dangerous situation when action must be taken.
example: It’s when the chips are down that Jane is at her best.

definition: This idiom means to have to deal with a lot of people who are criticizing or attacking you.
example: Every day we had to run the gauntlet of hostile journalists.

definition: If you take care of yourself first, and look after your own interests rather than those of other people, you look out for number one.
example: I’ve told my daughter that looking out for number one should be her priority.

definition: This expression means that if something is easy to obtain then you are less worried about losing it.
example: I won a lot of money at the poker game last night, but I lost it on my way home. Oh well, easy come, easy go.

definition: If you fling yourself into an activity, you do it with a lot of energy and enthusiasm.
example: Since he flung himself into the political campaign, he seldom has a free moment.

definition: If an activity is a money spinner, it is a very successful way of making money.
example: Handing out brochures was quite a money spinner when I was a student.

definition: If you decide to fast track something, such as a task or project, you give it high priority so that the objective is reached as quickly as possible.
example: It was decided to fast track the construction of a new motorway.

definition: This idiom means to be satisfied with one’s past success and to consider further effort unnecessary.
example: If you want to become a manager you shouldn’t rest on your laurels.

definition: This is a term used to denote magic or trickery.
example: Hocus pocus - and the rabbit disappeared!

definition: This idiom is an euphemism, meaning pregnant.
example: After two years of relationship, Marry is now in the club.

definition: If a person keeps a stiff upper lip, they contain their emotion and do not let other people see their feelings.
example: When he heard the bad news, he somehow managed to keep a stiff upper lip.

definition: This expression means to cause an organization, system or activity to fail or end.
example: The shutdown of the local chemical industry sound the death knell for our store.

definition: Someone who is highly vivacious, energetic and full of enthusiasm is a live wire.
example: Things have been better since she arrived. She’s a real live wire.

phrase: a legend in one’s own lifetime
definition: This phrase refers to a living person of considerable fame.
example: This actor is a legend in his own lifetime.

definition: This idiom means to ride in the front passenger seat of a car.
example: I prefer to drive but I have drunk. I have to ride shotgun now.

definition: The main point or the most vital element of a discussion or argument is called the crux of the matter.
example: The crux of the matter is that she is too old to live alone.

definition: This expression means to have a secret advantage that is suddenly revealed to change the game.
example: The competitors should always be checked for cards up their sleeves.

definition: This expression refers to the most attractive woman at a party of similar event.
example: Johanna was the belle of the ball that night.

definition: This idiom means “very common or ordinary”.
example: His new book is a garden variety story.

definition: If you save someone’s bacon, you rescue them from a dangerous or difficult situation.
example: I knew she needed my help and I saved her bacon.

definition: This idiom refers to the only male in an all-female environment.
example: Steve is the cock in the henhouse in this department.

definition: Someone who beats a (hasty) retreat runs away or goes back hurriedly to avoid a dangerous or difficult situation.
example: The thief beat a hasty retreat as soon as he saw the police officer.

definition: This phrase means to prepare for a battle or to adopt a warlike stance.
example: That was the last straw! Let’s go to the mattresses!

definition: This phrase refers to a form of execution in which victims were forced to walk, often blindfold and with hands tied, off a plank of wood and into the sea.
example: Many crew members died. They were forced to walk the plank.

definition: This idiom means not to trust your enemies.
example: Did she give you a gift? Beware of Greeks bearing gifts!

definition: If someone or something is as silent as the grave, it is extremely silent.
example: The enormous room was as silent as the grave.

definition: This expression means to be easily successful, especially concerning sex or romance.
example: Lately, I’ve been in like Flynn with the girls.

definition: This expression refers to a quick approximate calculation done informally, as on the back of an envelope.
example: I don’t need the exact amount for this study. Just give me a back-of-the-envelope calculation.

definition: The expression donkey work is used to describe the unpleasant, repetitive or boring parts of a job.
example: I’ve had enough of this donkey work. I will resign next month.

phrase: it’s a game of two halves
definition: This expression refers to the fact that a football match can change unexpectedly throughout the 90 minutes.
example: I wouldn’t bet on them. Don’t forget that it’s a game of two halves.

definition: To say that there is not a cat in hell’s chance of someone doing or achieving something means that there is no chance at all.
example: Because of the storm, he didn’t have a cat in hell’s chance of landing safely.

definition: This idiom means to study hard, usually in preparation for a test.
example: I have to bone up on security paradigms before applying for a doctorate in that field.

definition: This expression is used to state what you consider to be more important than anything else.
example: First and foremost I want to thank you.

definition: If something bears fruit, it produces positive or successful results.
example: After years of hard work, her study finally begins to bear fruit.

phrase: paper / cream / grip / dough / bread / bank / bacon / cheddar / cheese / gravy (noun, always singular)
definition: This refers to money.
example: You need a lot of dough to buy a new Audi A3.

definition: If you lend yourself to something, you approve of it or become associated with it.
example: No sensible man would lend himself to domestic violence.

definition: To say that the coast is clear means that there is no danger in sight or that nobody can see you.
example: Hey! Enter now! The coast is clear!

definition: If you ride roughshod over something/somebody, you behave in a harsh or thoughtless manner, or you treat a situation with contempt.
example: The government rode roughshod over all opposition to the new civil code.

definition: A person who fights an uphill battle has to struggle against very unfavorable circumstances.
example: After that injury, I had to fight an uphill battle to recover.

definition: If someone turns on the waterworks, they start to cry, especially to obtain something.
example: She is so spoilt! If she doesn’t get what she want, she immediately turns on the waterworks.

definition: If you throw somebody a bone, you say something kind or reward them in some way to make them feel good.
example: Jane can’t help very much but I throw her a bone to keep her happy.

phrase: as honest as the day is long
definition: This idiom is used to describe somebody who is very trustworthy and honest.
example: I’ve known Paul for many years and he is as honest as the day is long!

definition: If you make no bones about something, you don’t hesitate to say something in a frank and open way.
example: I made no bones about it. I told her that the offer was unacceptable.

definition: If someone or something fits the bill, they are exactly right for a particular situation.
example: She wanted a quiet place to relax. My country inn fitted the bill, so I invited her.

phrase: take the rough with the smooth
definition: If you take the rough with the smooth, you accept what is unpleasant or difficult as well as what is pleasant or easy.
example: Life isn’t easy; you have to learn to take the rough with the smooth.

definition: This idiom refers to a utopian dreamland.
example: Ann thinks she will get a part in the movie. She needs to stop living in never-never land.

definition: When two people or things are very different, they are worlds apart.
example: We liked each other but we were worlds apart.

definition: If you pick someone’s brains, you ask questions about a particular subject in order to obtain advice or information.
example: I would like to pick your brains about buying a new car.

definition: If you follow instructions or directions to the letter, you do exactly as is told or written.
example: Much as I followed the instruction to the letter, I couldn’t get the device to work.

definition: If you say that someone is a glutton for punishment, you express your surprise that they continue to do something which they find unpleasant or difficult.
example: She gets seasick but she’s going to travel by boat – she’s a glutton for punishment.

definition: If something takes a load off your mind, it brings great relief because a problem has been solved.
example: When the firm closed down, finding a new job took a load off my mind.

definition: If you strike a false note, you do something wrong or inappropriate.
example: I struck a false note when I told that to her.

definition: If you are in someone’s black books, you are in disgrace or in disfavour with somebody.
example: After the argument, I am sure that I am in their black books.

definition: This expression means that someone or something is never late or is always at the same time.
example: In this county trains are as regular as a clock.

definition: If you play a waiting game, you deliberately delay taking action in order to be able to act more effectively later.
example: The fisherman keeps his eyes on the rods, playing a waiting game.

definition: A person who thinks on their feet is capable of making good decisions without previous thinking or planning.
example: You need to be able to think on your feet if you want this job. It’s not easy to be a lawyer.

phrase: bricks and mortar / bricks and clicks
definition: An established trading company (office or shop) is referred to as a “brick-and-mortar” business. On the other hand, “click companies” refer to internet-based operations. Companies which do both are called “bricks and clicks”.
example: Click businesses are more flexible than brick-and-mortar operations.

definition: This expression means that there will be no favouritism or preferential treatment. Therefore, people will be served strictly in the order they arrive.
example: Tickets for the race will be sold on “first come first served” basis.

definition: This expression means that success often lead to further successes.
example: The good sales of my first book made me continue writing. Nothing succeeds like success.

definition: This idiom means to meet someone by chance and not by choice.
example: The last time I crossed paths with Ann was last summer.

definition: This idiom means to express one’s repressed feelings about something.
example: Can we meet? I have something to get off my chest…

definition: When an argument, contract or treaty is signed, sealed and delivered, all the legal documents are in order.
example: I hope that the contract will be signed, sealed and delivered before the end of the day.

definition: If something sticks out a mile, it is very obvious or very easy to see.
example: This car has had a facelift – it sticks out a mile!

definition: If something scares you out of your wits, it makes you very frightened or worried.
example: The feeling that the house was haunted scared Maria out of her wits.

phrase: keep your nose to the grindstone
definition: A person who keeps their nose to the grindstone is someone who concentrates on working hard at his/her job or studies.
example: He was so determined to get the promotion that he kept his nose to the grindstone all year.

definition: This expression is used to describe an aspect of a person’s personality. It means that they tell people things they shouldn’t, for example secrets.
example: Don’t trust her. She’s a big mouth.

definition: If you press something home, you insist on a point in a discussion or argument.
example: My lawyer kept pressing home the fact that I was on holiday that day.

phrase: what’s sauce for the goose is sauce for the gander
definition: This saying means that what is appropriate for one person should also be appropriate for the other person concerned.
example: A woman should earn the same salary as a man for the same job. What’s sauce for the goose is sauce for the gander!

definition: This phrase is used to convey that there is or was nothing more to be said about a matter.
example: Every month, you have to pay 400 dollars and that’s all she wrote.

definition: This phrase means that one is careful with one’s spending of small sums of money but careless and wasteful with larger amounts.
example: My wife is penny wise and pound foolish.

definition: If something or someone is not a patch on an other, they are not nearly as good.
example: Her second presentation wasn’t a patch on the first one.

definition: If you spend your life hiding something important about yourself or inventing something which is not true, you live a lie.
example: To hide her childhood, she told her husband that she had no family.

definition: This idiom means to carefully look through an area or an item in an attempt to find someone or something.
example: I combed through the wreckage but I haven’t found my phone.

definition: This idiom means rich and of good social status.
example: Most well-to-do people drive luxury cars.

definition: A golden parachute is a clause in an executive’s employment contract stating that the executive will receive certain large benefits if their employment is terminated.
example: I will come to work for you only if you give me a golden parachute.

definition: To smooth the path for something means to make progress easier or enable it to happen.
example: Speaking the same language smoothed the path for negotiations.

phrase: at the bottom of the ladder
definition: Someone who is at the bottom of the ladder occupies the lowest or most basic position or is hired at entry level.
example: In my first job I started at the bottom of the ladder.

definition: This expression refers to something that is about to get over or fail.
example: Out marriage is done for. There is nothing more we can do.

definition: This expression means that I am overwhelmed and stressed and it is affecting my ability to think.
example: I couldn’t think straight with all that yelling and running around.

definition: This idiom refers to something bad that is called good out of politeness or timidity.
example: This problem is a curate’s egg.

definition: Food can make your mouth water when it looks and smells extremely good.
example: This pizza makes my mouth water.

definition: If you make the best of things, you react in a positive way to an unsatisfactory situation that you cannot change and do the best you can with it.
example: The house was badly located, but they decided to stay there and make the best of things.

phrase: two heads are better than one
definition: This idiom means that having more than one participant in an activity makes it better.
example: Let’s ask for his help. Two heads are better than one.

definition: If you accuse someone of greasing somebody’s palm, you are accusing them of giving money to someone so as to gain an unfair advantage or to obtain something they want.
example: In many countries, it is a practice to grease officials’ palms.

definition: If you’ve got eyes like a hawk, you have good eyesight and notice every detail.
example: Steve will notice the scratch on his bike – he’s got eyes like a hawk.

definition: This term refers to the higher levels of society, the upper class or the aristocracy.
example: She pretend to be from the upper crust.

definition: If you are left high and dry, you find yourself in a difficult situation without help or resources.
example: I couldn’t stand her anymore. So, I left her high and dry with one kid to raise.

definition: If you handle someone with kid gloves, you treat them very carefully or tactfully, either because they are very important or because they are easily upset.
example: He is so intent on obtaining the agreement that he is handling them with kid gloves.

definition: A person who burns the midnight oil stays up very late at night in order to finish a piece of work.
example: I have to burn the midnight oil so as to finish this project.

definition: This idiom refers to a commodity that is bought without first examining it.
example: She said the laptop was good and I listened to her. Eventually, it turned out that it was a pig in a poke.

definition: If something goes down a treat, people like it very much.
example: That new restaurant seems to be going down a treat.

definition: If you get your hands dirty in your job, you become involved in all aspects of it, including work that is physical, unpleasant or less interesting.
example: In time, I also won their respect by getting my hands dirty.

phrase: like a bull in a china shop
definition: This expression refers to an extremely awkward, clumsy person. It may also mean to be aggressive when in fact the need of the hour is to stay calm.
example: I behaved like a bull in a china shop last night. I’m so sorry.

definition: A person who drives a hard bargain always makes sure they gain advantage in a business deal.
example: This negotiations will be a tough one. They usually drive a hard bargain.

definition: If you scrimp and save, you spend as little as possible over a certain period of time in order to save money.
example: I scrimped and saved for two years so that I could buy a car.

phrase: pour your heart out to someone
definition: If you pour your heart out to someone, you express your feelings freely.
example: When Sheila needs to pour her heart out to someone, she goes to visit her parents.

definition: This expression refers to a situation where there are signs showing that a problem is going to occur.
example: We knew that something bad was about to happen. We saw the writing on the wall.

definition: A person who is just off the boat is naïve and lacks experience.
example: I have to work with a trainee who’s just off the boat.

definition: This term refers to an uncontrolled situation such as a discussion, arguments or fight where everyone present can do or say whatever they like.
example: This time, the battle is free-for-all.

definition: If you do something on the sly, you do it secretly or furtively.
example: They have done something on the sly but I can’t figure out what.

definition: This idiom refers to an intelligent and lively person (humorously).
example: A bright spark at the bank has accidentally closed my account.

definition: This idiom refers to a situation that allows or causes a particular group of people to be treated unfairly.
example: To pass this legislation would be to declare open season on minorities.

definition: If you follow your nose, you go straight ahead. It can also mean to follow your instinct in life.
example: The store should be at the end of this road. Just follow your nose.

definition: This is the term given to a young man idolised for great skill, usually in sport.
example: By most fans, he is seen as the golden boy of the team.

definition: This idiom refers to the most senior person in a group of equal rank.
example: His position within the company is considered to be the first among equals.

definition: If you say that you never looked back, you mean that after an event which changed your life for the better, you continue to be happy with the situation.
example: Since the day I decided to leave the company, I have never looked back.

definition: If a person has a spare tyre, they have a roll of flesh around the waist.
example: You’d better go to gym – you’re getting a spare tyre!

definition: A person who dies with their boots on dies while still leading an active life.
example: She says she won’t ever retire. She would rather dies with her boots on!

definition: This expression refers to a project or scheme which has been abandoned or is certain to fail.
example: The project for the new local store is going to be a dead duck because of funds shortage.

definition: If you leave someone to their own devices, you let them look after themselves, without help of supervision.
example: When left to their own devices, most children watch TV.

definition: This saying is used to express pleasure or surprise at something.
example: She finally called me! Wonders will never cease!

definition: A person or organisation at a low ebb is not as strong or successful as usual.
example: The local political crisis has left the company at a low ebb.

definition: If you rave about something, you protest noisily and forcefully.
example: The old man ranted and raved about the new security system.

definition: This expression means tending to attract attention, visually attractive or striking.
example: There were some eye-catching posters on the walls.

definition: This idiom refers to an imaginary idealistic state where everything is perfect. It is usually used with reference to someone who has an overly optimistic and unrealistic belief.
example: If you think that you can obtain a managerial position without at least three years experience you are living in cloud cuckoo-land.

definition: Someone who gets away with the murder can behave badly or do something that is forbidden, without being punished for it.
example: I think I might be too permissive. My children usually get away with the murder.

definition: If someone beats their brains out, they try very hard to understand something or solve a problem.
example: My grandfather beats his brains out every morning trying to do the crossword puzzle in the newspaper.

phrase: give a dog a bad name
definition: People who lose their reputation have difficulty regaining it because others continue to blame or suspect them.
example: It was another day when Steve was suspected, as usual. Give a dog a bad name!

definition: Someone who is not easily fooled or deceived is a sharp cookie.
example: You can’t fool my father. He’s a sharp cookie.

definition: This idiom refers to the pleasant route through life, of pleasure and dissipation.
example: Unable to enjoy her wealth, she felt she was being led down the primrose path to self-destruction.

definition: This idiom means to stay confident and positive.
example: Take heart my friend! Everything will be all right.

definition: If a plan or project falls by the wayside, it remains unfinished or people stop trying to do it.
example: They opposed so strongly that the plans for a new parking lot fell by the wayside.

definition: This expression means to spend a large amount of time considering different options before making a final decision.
example: You should mull over getting back to your ex.

phrase: put the cart before the horse
definition: A person who puts the cart before the horse is doing things in the wrong order.
example: Building a university before knowing the age of the population means putting the cart before the horse.

definition: This phrase refers to a publicity campaign, usually by politicians, that attempts to attract supporters by emphasizing their charisma or trustworthiness.
example: Don’t you think that her is charm offensive this period?

definition: Somebody who is weak at the knees is (temporarily) barely able to stand because of emotion, fear or illness.
example: The news made me go weak at the knees.

definition: This idiom refers to a position where one might receive severe criticism.
example: The suspect was in the cross hairs from the very beginning of the interrogation.

definition: Something that is short and sweet is brief but pleasant.
example: Our conversations was short and sweet.

definition: This idiom means jealousy.
example: When she saw my car, she turned into a green-eyed monster.

definition: If you tell someone to watch their step, you are advising them to be careful how they behave in order to avoid getting into trouble.
example: There is no tolerance for bad behaviour within this company, so watch your step.

definition: If you have another string to your bow, you have another skill or possible course of action if everything else fails.
example: Taking into considerations my qualifications, I certainly have another string to my bow to help me find a job, if needed.

definition: This expression means to be defeated by someone.
example: Brian lost to his brother in the tennis match.

definition: Someone with no apparent authority who has great influence over the person officially in charge is said to be the power behind the throne.
example: Women are generally though of as the power behind the throne in some societies.

definition: This idiom refers to a particular philosophy or a way of thinking about something.
example: There are various definitions, each corresponding to a school of thought.

definition: Someone who is out of circulation is unavailable or not joining in activities with others.
example: I’m going to do a three-week course in Spain, so I’ll be out of circulation for a while.

definition: This idiom means to put up your fists and prepare to fight.
example: Are you ready? Put up your dukes!

definition: A doubting Thomas is a person who will not believe something without proof or without seeing it for themselves.
example: I had to show him my credentials. What a doubting Thomas!

definition: This expression refers to a misfortune.
