example: She lost her job, exactly when she needed money to move house.

phrase: keep your ear to the ground
definition: If you keep your ear to the ground, you make sure that you are aware of all that is happening and is being said.
example: They don’t know anything about the changes, but Steve is keeping his ear to the ground.

definition: A person who does work that requires little action (office work), is called a pen pusher.
example: She enjoys being a pen pusher.

definition: If something moves at a snail’s pace, it moves very slowly.
example: The man was moving along the pavement at a snail’s pace.

definition: A person who keeps their nose / hands clean behaves well and avoids trouble.
example: Trust me! He’s a good guy who keeps his nose clean.

phrase: live to a ripe old age
definition: This expression means to live until you are very old.
example: If you lead a healthy life and exercise at the gym, you’ll live to a ripe old age.

phrase: out of the frying pan into the fire
definition: This expression means to go from one difficult situation to another one which is usually even worse.
example: The ride was delayed because of bad weather conditions. When the bus started, it had to turn back because of engine trouble – out of the frying pan into the fire!

definition: This expression means to adapt to one’s circumstances or to make sure one’s plans are appropriate to one’s resources.
example: I’d love a sports car, but I have to cut my coat according to my cloth.

definition: This idiom refers to something that someone says either to avoid answering a question clearly or to make someone believe something that is not true.
example: I don’t need weasel words. I need an answer!

phrase: pigs get fat, hogs get slaughtered
definition: You should be satisfied when you have enough; if you are too greedy, like a hog, you risk losing everything.
example: My son, please remember that pigs get fat, hogs get slaughtered.

definition: A slush fund is an account or fund in politics or business where money is set aside for various unofficial purposes, often unethical or even illegal.
example: We should make a slush fund for hard times.

definition: This idiom refers to expressing your love in public by constantly kissing and hugging.
example: I don’t want to go with them. They are so lovey-dovey…

phrase: eyes in the back of one’s head
definition: If someone has eyes in the back of their head, they are very observant and notice everything happening around them.
example: You need eyes in the back of your head to understand what happens in this organisation.

definition: If someone is on a fishing expedition, they are trying to obtain information in any way possible.
example: The dinner invitation was a fishing expedition to obtain information about my private life.

definition: To say that something is “the bane of your life” means that it is the cause of your problems or your unhappiness.
example: This computer is always breaking down! It’s the bane of my life!

phrase: wash one’s dirty linen in public
definition: To wash one’s dirty linen in public means to talk about unpleasant personal matters in the presence of others.
example: Hey! Shut up! You shouldn’t wash your dirty linen in public.

definition: This idiom means to make someone angry by inciting a thought.
example: The presentation touched off a very important point.

definition: This expression is used to show encouragement or agreement with something that has just been said, for example a good idea.
example: If we take the train, we’ll avoid all this traffic. Now you’re talking!

phrase: make a pig’s ear of something
definition: If you make a pig’s ear of something, you do a task or a chore very badly or make a complete mess of it.
example: They offered to paint the room but they made a pig’s ear of it.

definition: If you do something “against the clock”, you are rushed and have very little time to do it.
example: I’m working against the clock to have the presentation ready for Tuesday.

definition: This expression is used to refer to people or things that are considered to be very unattractive.
example: Have you seen her cat? It’s as ugly as sin.

definition: If you throw in the towel, you admit that you cannot succeed.
example: After some minutes, he threw in the towel.

definition: This idiom means to work together in order to achieve something that both groups want.
example: They’ve made common cause with local people to stop the pollution.

definition: If you are given red-carpet treatment, you receive special or royal treatment.
example: My aunt always gives me the red-carpet treatment when I go to visit her.

definition: A jack of all trades is a person who can do many different things but is not very good at any one of them.
example: I’m looking for an expert not a jack-of-all-trades.

definition: This term means basically, fundamentally or essentially, and refers to the most important or essential facts.
example: In essence, you have nothing to be afraid of.

definition: To describe somebody as a wolf in sheep’s clothing means that although they look harmless, they are really very dangerous.
example: Be careful what you speak. She’s a wolf in sheep’s clothing.

definition: If you are on somebody’s tail, you are following them closely.
example: I’ve heard that the police are on her tail.

definition: If a plan or project goes pear-shaped, it either goes wrong or it produces an undesirable result.
example: I’ve organized a hunting session but it went pear-shaped.

definition: If you feast your eyes on something, you are delighted and gratified by what you see.
example: As he drove along the road, we feasted our eyes on the scenery.

definition: This idiom refers to the freedom to do, say or feel what you want.
example: I gave my emotions free rein as I was kissing her.

definition: This idiom means to find derogatory information about something or somebody.
example: I will dig up dirt and find something about her.

definition: If you make somebody tick, it means that they really like you and respond well to you.
example: My wife really makes me tick.

definition: If you are a happy-go-lucky person, you are cheerful and carefree all the time.
example: I like her. She’s a happy-go-lucky girl.

definition: The nuts and bolts of something are the detailed facts and the practical aspects.
example: We need to discuss the nuts and bolts of the mission before going further.

definition: This idiom refers to basic or essential facts.
example: They gave us the bare bones of their difficult issues.

definition: To keep something under your hat means to keep a secret.
example: Trust me. I will keep it under my hat!

phrase: a red rag to a bull
definition: This expression means a deliberate provocation.
example: Telling him those words it was like a red rag to a bull.

definition: This is an expression of not believing something very strongly.
example: If you are able to run that fast then I’ll eat my hat.

phrase: a penny saved is a penny earned
definition: This expression means that money you save today can be spent later.
example: You should take the change. A penny saved is a penny earned.

definition: This expression is used to say that you do not believe what has just been said.
example: She said she’d found the document in the abandoned house – that’s a likely story.

definition: Something which is hard and fast is inflexible or cannot be altered.
example: Unfortunately, there are no hard and fast rules related to love.

definition: This idiom means “not a single word or sound from someone”.
example: There wasn’t a peep from the students for the rest of the day after the teacher sent John to detention.

phrase: on the spur of the moment
definition: If you do something on the spur of the moment, you do it as soon as you think of it, spontaneously, without any planning.
example: I decided to buy flowers for Ana on the spur of the moment.

definition: If someone or something is as sweet as honey, they are very sweet and/or charming.
example: Her words were as sweet as honey as she tried to convince him.

phrase: be glad to see the back of someone / something
definition: This idiom means that you are happy when you no longer have to deal with someone or something because they are annoying or unpleasant.
example: I was glad to see the back of that laptop – it was nothing but trouble.

definition: This idiom means childish and weakly sentimental.
example: She’s just a namby-pamby girl.

definition: This idiom means to snitch on someone or let their secret out.
example: I can’t believe you sold me out! I trusted you!

phrase: like the back of one’s hand
definition: If you know something like the back of your hand, you are very familiar with it and know it in detail.
example: Of course I won’t get lost. I know Paris like the back of my hand!

definition: This idiom means to separate or remove people from a larger group.
example: They use standardized test results as a means of culling the herd.

definition: If you make an effort to put someone or something into satisfactory condition or appearance, you lick them into shape.
example: I have to lick this place into shape before she arrives.

definition: Someone who does a double take looks again in surprise at something unexpected.
example: She did a double take when she saw her husband in a pub with an alluring woman.

definition: This expression is used to describe a final act before dying or ending something.
example: This project was my swan song. I’m going to resign.

definition: This idiom refers to a small cheap café selling fried food.
example: That morning, a fried breakfast in a greasy spoon was just what I fancied.

definition: If a new article is hot off the press, it has just been published and contains the most recent information on the subject.
example: This piece of news is hot off the press. Another local firm has gone bankrupt.

phrase: when all is said and done
definition: This phrase means when everything is finished and settled; when everything is considered.
example: When all is said and done, I believe she loved me.

definition: Someone who is the brains behind a project or action is the person thought to have planned and organized everything.
example: The police have arrested a woman believed to be the brains behind the murder.

definition: A person who holds all the aces is in a very strong position because they have more advantages than anyone else.
example: Given the high unemployment figures in those countries, employers hold all the aces.

definition: This idiom refers to an imaginary double, humorously referred to in order to explain the uncharacteristic bad behaviour of a normally moral person.
example: She is definitely sorry for what she has done. It was her evil twin.

definition: When you make a go of something, you succeed in your enterprise or produce good results.
example: Two years ago, he opened a local store and made a go of it.

definition: If you know your own mind, you know what you want or like, and are capable of making a decision.
example: I really don’t want to influence you. You are old enough to know your own mind.

definition: This phrase means to act as if you have a lot of power or authority.
example: The local manager came to our office and tried to throw his weight around. It was in vain.

definition: If you hope against hope, you continue to hope even when the situation looks bad.
example: The car crash was terrible. Her parents are hoping against hope that she escaped alive.

phrase: to be out on your ear
definition: This expression means to be thrown out – often of a workplace or home.
example: If you don’t start working, you’ll be out on your ear.

definition: This idiom refers to the activity of attacking someone and filming the attack, especially with a mobile phone.
example: They were provoked to happy slapping.

definition: If you are in a quandary, you find it difficult to decide what to do.
example: This job offer is interesting. I’m in a quandary about what to do.

definition: If you do a juggling act, you try to do different things in a way that is satisfactory for all concerned.
example: For most women, managing a career and looking after a family is a juggling act.

definition: Before doing something, if you try to discover what other people think about it by making discreet enquiries, you put out feelers.
example: Politicians put out feelers to test public reaction to their proposals.

definition: If you step into someone’s shoes, you take over a job or position held by someone else before you.
example: I have been trained to step into my father’s shoes when he retires.

phrase: butter wouldn’t melt in your mouth
definition: If you say that someone looks as if butter wouldn’t melt in their mouth, you mean that they look completely innocent, but that they are capable of doing unpleasant thing.
example: The girl who stole the car looked as if butter wouldn’t melt in her mouth.

phrase: take a leaf out of somebody’s life / book
definition: This idiom is used to follow an example set by another person.
example: You need to take a leaf out of your manager’s life and be more confident.

definition: If you follow in someone’s footsteps you lead a similar life or do the same job.
example: She didn’t want to follow in her mother’s footsteps and become an actress.

definition: To say that a skill, an ability or experience will stand you in good stead means that it will be beneficial to you in the future.
example: Being able to speak German will stand you in good stead.

definition: If you come to grips with a problem or situation, you start to understand or deal with it properly.
example: After the accident, she began to come to grips with her new disability.

definition: This idiom means to want somebody to be hurt or punished.
example: The crowd was baying for blood of the criminal.

definition: When something is difficult to accept or believe, it is hard to swallow.
example: She invented an excuse that was hard to swallow, but he knew she had cheated him.

definition: This term refers to hallucinations or strange imaginary things seen by people as a result of heavy drinking or the use of narcotics.
example: I don’t want any drinks, thank you! I’ll be seeing pink elephants otherwise.

definition: If you strike gold, you find exactly what you need: satisfaction, wealth, happiness etc.
example: I struck gold this time with my new job.

definition: If you go up a blind alley, you follow an ineffective course of action which leads nowhere or produces no results.
example: The suspects’ declarations lead the police up a blind alley.

definition: When someone is out of earshot, they are too far away to hear or to be heard.
example: They waited until Marry was out of earshot before discussing about her birthday party.

definition: If someone speaks out of turn, either they intervene at the wrong moment or they say something tactless or inappropriate.
example: At the first meetings I was afraid of speaking out of turn.

definition: When someone has a smile on their face because they are happy or satisfied about something, they grin like a Cheshire cat.
example: I knew things were all right because I saw him with a grin like a Cheshire cat.

definition: If you declare that you will do something come what may, you are saying that you will do it whatever the consequences may be.
example: Come what may, I won’t tell her that I’ve cheated on her.

definition: You can say “never say die” to encourage someone to persevere in their efforts and not give up or abandon their project.
example: It’s too soon to give up the race. Never say die!

definition: This idiom means to be impossible to believe or describe.
example: The murderer’s cruelty beggared belief.

definition: If something takes the biscuit, it is very irritating, annoying or exasperating.
example: After waiting for more hours, we were told that there were no tickets left. That really took the biscuit!

definition: If you are the only person to express a warning or an opinion on a matter which is ignored by most others, you are a voice in the wilderness.
example: I was a voice in the wilderness regarding economic crisis which was about to come.

definition: When someone feels the pinch, they begin to suffer from a lack of money.
example: At the end of the touristic season, the hotels and restaurants feel the pinch.

definition: If you use your connections with someone successful in order to achieve fame or success for yourself, without any personal effort, you ride their coattails.
example: She rode her uncle’s coattails in the hope of being hired.

definition: This expression means to perform well, often in a challenging situation.
example: As she couldn’t give a good account of herself in the interview, the company didn’t offer her a promotion.

definition: If you crave the limelight, you really like to be the center of attention.
example: I don’t want to spend my time with her. She craves the limelight and I don’t like that.

definition: If you overstep the mark, you go too far and upset someone by saying something or behaving in a way that is unacceptable.
example: She overstepped the mark when she called him an “old fool”.

phrase: like a moth to a flame
definition: This idiom means irresistibly and dangerously attracted to something or someone.
example: I’m sexually attracted to her like a moth to a flame.

definition: People who scream blue murder shout or complain very loudly as if something very serious has happened.
example: The crowd started screaming blue murder when the match was interrupted.

definition: A fly-by-night company or business person cannot be trusted because they are likely to get into debt and close down the business.
example: Be careful with that company, as I heard that it’s a fly-by-night firm.

definition: An offer with no strings attached is an offer made without conditions or restrictions, and requires nothing in return.
example: I managed to get a car loan with no strings attached.

definition: If someone gets the axe, they lose their job.
example: When our department was restructured, the old got the axe.

phrase: left hand doesn’t know what the right hand is doing
definition: This expression means that within a group or organisation, communication is so bad that one person doesn’t know what another person is doing.
example: I don’t like this company anymore. The left hand doesn’t know what the right hand is doing and this is driving me crazy.

definition: Something that is a notch above something else is a little better in every way.
example: Her poem was a notch above the others.

definition: This idiom refers to an ordeal or martyrdom. More recently, a soldier’s first experience of battle.
example: Their mission was truly a baptism of fire.

definition: If something happens willy-nilly, it happens even if the people who are involved do not want it to happen.
example: Both countries were drawn, willy-nilly, into war.

phrase: too many cooks spoil the broth
definition: This idiom means to fail because of too many opinions on how to do something.
example: The organization had too many decision makers. No wonder it was closed since too many cooks spoil the broth.

definition: Someone who raises their eyebrows at something shows surprise or disapproval by the expression on their face.
example: When the manager arrived in jeans, there were a lot of raised eyebrows.

definition: Money or other benefits that are made in a dishonest or illegal manner are called ill-gotten gains.
example: She has won some money by stealing and is now enjoying her ill-gotten gains.

definition: If someone is taken to the cleaners, they lose a lot of money in an unfair way, usually by being robbed or cheated.
example: When the company went bankrupt, she realized that she had been taken to the cleaners.

definition: If something comes in dribs and drabs, it arrives little by little, in small amounts or numbers.
example: People arrived in dribs and drabs at the conference.

definition: Every nook and cranny means every possible part of a place.
example: I searched every nook and cranny of the town looking for that store.

definition: If you sign on the dotted line, you formally give your consent to something by signing an official document.
example: I wasn’t sure so I took legal advice before signing on the dotted line.

definition: This idiom means not certain to get a place in a team, keep your job, win an election etc.
example: Those who hadn’t gained their certification were on the bubble with regard to keeping their jobs.

phrase: see the error of one’s ways
definition: When someone sees the error of their ways, they understand that what they are doing is wrong and accept to change their behaviour.
example: She talked to a psychologist who tried to make her see the error of her ways.

definition: If you find yourself on a sticky wicket, you are in a situation that is difficult to deal with.
example: I am on a sticky wicket because I don’t have enough money.

definition: If someone or something is as red as a lobster, they are very red.
example: He came out of the sauna as red as a lobster.

definition: This is said of two people, particularly lovers, who would prefer to be alone together rather than to have someone else with them.
example: Thank you for inviting me, but I have to decline it. You know, two’s a company, three’s a crowd.

definition: To say that someone is flogging a dead horse means that they are wasting time and effort trying to do or achieve something that is not possible.
example: My father is flogging a dead horse trying to get his money back from that firm which has gone bankrupt.

definition: If something opens doors, it provides opportunities or possibilities for the future.
example: A bachelor degree generally opens doors to major companies.

definition: If you say that something bad serves someone right, you mean that that person deserves it.
example: He injured me! It serves you right! You deserve it!

definition: If someone or something passes muster, they are considered to be satisfactory or acceptable.
example: The interview went well in my opinion. I hope I’ll pass muster.

definition: Something that is a good or lucky thing to happen.
example: It would be just as well to check the engine.

definition: This idiom means to apply unnecessary ornament – to over embellish.
example: No, I don’t like this. It seems to me like you have gilded the lily.

definition: If something gives you food for thought, it makes you think seriously about a particular subject.
example: The documentary on air pollution has given me food for thought.

definition: Someone who is as sly as a fox is cunning and clever at getting what they want, especially by deceiving or tricking people.
example: The saleswoman is as sly as a fox. Be careful.

definition: a conflict, argument or struggle where both sides are determined to win is described as a battle of wills.
example: When they broke up, neither party would make concessions – it was a battle of wills.

definition: Very early in the morning. The very first moments of sunrise.
example: I like to be on the river bank at the crack of dawn.

definition: People who are fixed in their ways do not want to change their normal way of doing things.
example: It has been proven that old people tend to be fixed in their ways.

definition: This simile means completely safe and secure.
example: This bank is as safe as houses.

phrase: hair of the dog that bit you
definition: This expression means using as a remedy a small amount of what made you ill, for example a drop of alcohol when recovering from drinking too much.
example: Here, have just a little drop of this. It’s a hair of the dog that bit you!

definition: This phrase means very fast.
example: I need the money PDQ.

definition: If an actions is big of someone, it’s good, kind or helpful. However, this idiom is usually used sarcastically when the person using it thinks that the other person could do a lot more.
example: It was big of Marry to spare a whole minute for you yesterday.

definition: If you put someone or something through their paces, you test their ability to do something by making them perform certain actions.
example: During the presentation, the smartphone was put through its paces.

definition: If you find it difficult to be patient with someone because of their irritating attitude or behaviour, you can say that they are trying your patience.
example: You constant interruptions are trying my patience.

definition: This expression means to destroy someone’s possibility of retreat or to act decisively.
example: She has already burned her bridges with the manager by publicly criticizing him.

definition: If you josh someone, you trick them.
example: I know you didn’t race with this car. Stop joshing me.

definition: This idiom means to surprise someone by doing something unexpected.
example: They threw in a curveball and said I had to take another aptitude test.

definition: This expression refers to an easy option or to an effortless, happy situation.
example: Sarah found out that taking care of children was not a bed of roses.

phrase: separate the sheep from the goats
definition: If you separate the sheep from the goats, you examine a group of people and decide which are suitable and which not.
example: Examining job applications for our organisation is the first stage in separating the sheep from the goats.

definition: This idiom refers to something as part of one’s genetic inheritance.
example: The whole family is good at cooking; it’s in their blood.

definition: If the effect of an action is more damaging than helpful, it does more harm than good.
example: Giving her money did more harm than good – she lost it playing poker.

definition: A blue-eyed boy is someone’s favourite.
example: He’s the principal’s blue-eyed boy!

definition: If something is different from a general belief or theory, it shows that the belief or theory is true.
example: Most students love fast food, but Marry is the exception that proves the rule. She tries to eat healthy.

definition: This expression means not to be able to cause harm to anyone, including even a tiny or insignificant insect.
example: Brian is such an innocent little child that he could not hurt a fly.

definition: If one thing is a far cry from something else, they are very different from each other, especially in quality or size.
example: My tiny flat is a far cry from my parents’ big house.

definition: This expression is used to underline the fact that one is telling something in a strange or symbolic manner.
example: I will tell you out secret because you are already family, so to speak.

definition: This expression means to be ambitious.
example: In order to achieve great things in life you have to think big.

phrase: dot the I’s and cross the t’s
definition: This idiom means to take care of every detail, even minor ones.
example: I had dotted the i’s and cross the t’s, so I was accepted into the organisation.

definition: If something is up to par, it meets the required standard.
example: She didn’t get the management position because her English wasn’t up to par.

definition: This idiom means to be successful in everything that you do.
example: She seems to be batting a thousand with her online business.

definition: If someone catches your eye, you find them attractive.
example: The pretty woman near the door caught my eye.

definition: The term is used to refer to an abnormally lucrative arrangement between two parties.
example: Critics say the contract was awarded to the builder as part of a sweetheart deal.

definition: This phrase is a euphemism for pregnant. It is used most commonly, although not exclusively, to describe unplanned pregnancy.
example: Have you heard? Marry is up the duff.

definition: If one person is in cahoots with another, they are working in close partnership, usually conspiring to do something dishonest.
example: There is a rumour that the businessman is in cahoots with the mayor.

definition: A smart alec is an annoying self-assertive person who tries to show off how clever they are.
example: Some smart alec interrupted the quiz.

definition: If you take someone down a peg, you make that person understand that they are not as important as they think they are.
example: She is far too proud. Somebody has to take her down a peg.

definition: When you learn to do something perfectly, you get it down to a fine art.
example: Protecting people is not a problem for me. I’ve got that down to a fine art.

definition: This idiom means to criticize somebody or somebody’s character.
example: They never missed a chance to cast aspersions on my decisions.

definition: This idiom means not to show any shock or surprise.
example: The accused stood there without batting an eye.

definition: If you do not know more about something after obtaining an explanation or if you fail to find information on the subject, you are none the wiser.
example: I tried to understand the system but I was none the wiser after her explanation.

definition: If you put it mildly, you express your opinion or reaction in a controlled way, without exaggeration.
example: Steven is 2 years old and already able to read. That’s promising, to put it mildly.

definition: To say that someone has a good quality to a fault, it means that they have a lot or even too much of that quality.
example: He is generous to a fault.

phrase: get a second bite / two bites at the cherry
definition: This expression means that you get a second opportunity to do or try something.
example: She was eliminated, but she will get a second bite at the cherry next competition.

definition: This idiom means to set the ending to a concerned issue.
example: The lawyer closed the books of that case.

definition: This expression means to feel sympathy for someone when they are distressed.
example: My heart goes out to all people who lost loved ones.

definition: If you teach somebody a lesson, you do something to punish them for behaving badly and make them understand that they should not do it again.
example: I’m sorry but I have to teach her a lesson.

definition: This phrase means to hurry up or to make every possible effort.
example: I will pull my finger out for the success of this mission!

definition: If a person sticks their neck out, they draw attention to themselves by saying or doing something that others are afraid to do.
example: I stuck my neck out and said that the sales target would be impossible to reach.

definition: If you clip someone’s wings, you do something to restrict their freedom.
example: Taking away his money is a sure way to clip his wings.

phrase: worm one’s way out of something
definition: If a person worms their way out of something, they use artful or devious means in order to avoid participating in it.
example: You’re not going to worm your way out of this project!

definition: This idiom mean to cause someone to feel intense discomfort or irritation.
example: The horrible sound set my teeth on edge.

definition: This phrase is used to ask someone what they are thinking about.
example: Brian, a penny for your thoughts.

definition: This expression is used to indicate that something is not very likely to happen.
example: The manager is thinking of me for that task? Fat chance!

definition: If you lock horns with somebody, you argue or fight with them about something.
example: If there is another incident like that one, the employees will lock horns with each other.

definition: This idiom means to gradually end, often in a disappointing or weak way.
example: They went to different universities. Therefore, their relationship just fizzled out.

definition: Two people who fight or argue like cat and dog frequently have violent arguments, even though they are fond of each other.
example: They fight like cat and dog but they are still together after 15 years.

definition: This idiom refers to a faulty or substandard car.
example: I can’t sell this car. It’s my Friday afternoon car.

definition: If you fall at the first hurdle, you fail to overcome the first difficulty encountered.
example: Marry has fallen at the first hurdle. She has missed the bus and lost the target.

definition: If someone loses their marbles, they become mentally confused or no longer behave sensibly or rationally.
example: Our grandfather has lost his marbles.

definition: This means you have to get something started right away, otherwise it won’t be finished on time.
example: Let’s hurry with that project. We have no time to lose.

definition: An area of a town or city where there is a concentration of sex, shops, prostitution, strip clubs etc. is known as the red light district.
example: A photograph of her taken in a red-light district caused the scandal.

definition: If you say “I would give my right arm for that”, you mean that you want it a lot and would do almost anything to obtain it.
example: I’d give my right arm to have a house in Paris.

definition: This idiom refers to unacceptable or dishonest behaviour, especially involving sexual activity or money.
example: There was a bit of hanky-panky at the party.

definition: If you play for time, you try to delay or prevent something from happening in order to gain an advantage.
example: I decided to play for time in the hope that the pc price would decrease.

definition: This expression is used to express an opinion based on what you actually see.
example: By the look of things, war is about to begin.

definition: If you can visualise something or see an image of it in your mind, you see it in your mind’s eye.
example: I can see the car in my mind’s eye, but I can’t remember the make.

definition: If you go too far, you do something that is considered extreme or unacceptable.
example: Lying is bad, but lying to them is going too far!

definition: This expression means to politely refuse something.
example: I beg to differ to your taste in clothes.

definition: If people run riot, they behave in a wild, uncontrolled manner, running around in all directions.
example: I don’t like when she comes to my place with her kids – she always allows them to run riot.

phrase: face only a mother could love
definition: This is a humorous way of saying that someone is ugly or unattractive.
example: The poor girl has a face only a mother could love.

definition: Someone who has a brain like a sieve has a very bad memory and forgets things easily.
example: Oh, I forgot to buy a sauce – I’ve got a brain like a sieve.

definition: This expression is said after a set of instructions are provided and one wants to convey that the work will be simple for the other person to do.
example: You add three cups of water to the mix and some vegetables, heat it for seven minutes and Bob’s your uncle, the soup is ready.

definition: This idiom refers to a relationship in which the two people are great together, because they complement each other so well.
example: Do you think they will marry? In my opinion they are a match made in heaven.

definition: People or organisations that are considered unimportant can be referred to as small fry.
example: The police seized a large quantity of drug and some small fry.

definition: A person who kicks up a fuss creates a disturbance, especially by complaining or protesting about something.
example: The food was so bad that several customers began to kick up a fuss.

definition: This idiom is said when the feasibility of some unlikely event is questioned.
example: I don’t believe her, but there’s not a problem. Stranger things have happened.

phrase: bite the dust / hit the dust
definition: The expression is a humorous way of referring to death.
example: It’s a story about an old man who hits the dust during a bank robbery.

definition: People who live on the breadline have a very low income or barely enough money to survive.
example: Due to the recent economic crisis, there are more people on the breadline.

definition: If someone is living in a fool’s paradise, they are in a state of contentment that will not last because their happiness is based on illusion or false hope.
example: He is living in a fool’s paradise if he thinks he will win the lottery.

definition: This term refers to a burden or problem that ties you down and prevents you from doing what you want to do.
example: My holiday mountain house has become a ball and chain – it’s just too much work to be done!

definition: Someone who is chasing rainbows is trying to get something they will never obtain.
example: Bluntly speaking, I think you are chasing rainbows.

definition: A desirable position which is well-paid and considered relatively easy is called a plum job.
example: I’d like to find myself a plum job in Berlin.

definition: Something that is as easy as ABC is very easy to do.
example: The test was as easy as ABC.

definition: A person who digs their own grave does something which causes their own downfall.
example: Be very careful what you say. You might dig your own grave!

definition: This expression refers to educated people who like to discuss and give their opinions about political and social matters.
example: That subject has become a trendy topic among the chattering classes.

definition: Something pleasant which also has disadvantages is called a mixed blessing.
example: I inherited a big house but the maintenance costs make it a mixed blessing.

definition: When there is a great lack of something which is urgently needed, there is a crying need for it.
example: There is a crying need for blood in our hospitals.

phrase: let the chips fall where they may
definition: This means to let something happen, no matter what happens next.
example: Don’t worry. It won’t help. Let the chips fall where they may.

definition: This idiom means to waste a great deal of time or effort in creating something that already exists.
example: You can use the existing blueprints. There’s no need to reinvent the wheel.

phrase: the early bird gets the worm
definition: This idiom means that the first people who arrive will get the best stuff.
example: You must be there as soon as possible. The early bird gets the worm.

definition: This idiom refers to someone having seen something that is extraordinary and causes their eyes to pop out.
example: I was bug-eyed looking at her wedding dress and jewelry.

definition: This idiom refers to a person with a lot of experience in something.
example: My manager is an old hand in the car business.

definition: If you are up in arms, you are very angry about something and protest very strongly.
example: The people were up in arms over the demolition of the old church.

definition: Someone who gets a free ride benefits from a collective activity without participating in it. It can also refer to the acceptance of your plans or ideas without having anyone question or criticize them.
example: No one has examined the manager’s marketing plan – he has gotten a free ride.

definition: If you ram something down someone’s throat, you force them to accept something against their will.
example: I encouraged her to learn German, but I couldn’t ram it down her throat.

definition: If you shake like a leaf, you tremble with fear or nervousness.
example: At the beginning of the interview I was shaking like a leaf.

definition: To say that somebody has the gift of the gab means that they are able to speak confidently and easily.
example: As a politician, you should have the gift of the gab.

definition: If you sponge off someone, you live at the expense of another person, accepting their hospitality without sharing the costs or doing something in return.
example: I didn’t like her because she tried to sponge off me.

definition: This idiom refers to a general agreement to keep silent about a subject for the purpose of secrecy.
example: On the security check, there is a conspiracy of silence; security agents bypass the known visitors.

definition: This idiom means to abandon taking responsibility for someone or something.
example: I can’t wash my hands of my best friend during his difficult times.

definition: This idiom refers to a feast day that falls on the same day of the week each year, but which has a date which varies.
example: Can you give an example of a movable feast?

phrase: imitation is the sincerest form of flattery
definition: This phrase has a literal meaning.
example: Have they copied our design? Well, imitation is the sincerest form of flattery.

phrase: as strong as a horse / an ox / a lion
definition: When using this expression to describe someone, it means that the concerned person is very strong.
example: Call on him to help you. He’s as strong as a horse.

definition: If somebody, usually a man, is thin on the top, they are losing their hair or going bald.
example: My grandfather is thin on the top.

definition: This idiom means heavily and formidably armed, usually with deadly weapons.
example: The robbers were armed to the teeth and looked merciless.

phrase: put your heart and soul into something
definition: If you put your heart and soul into something, you are very enthusiastic and invest a lot of energy and hard work in it.
example: I was determined to make a success of my project. I put my heart and soul into it.

definition: This idiom in an evangelical call to believe in and spread the Christian faith.
example: Fight the good fight, said the humble man.

definition: Something that is small potatoes is considered to be unimportant or insignificant.
example: My first publication was considered small potatoes.

definition: This idiom means to suddenly start to like or love someone very much.
example: I am completely smitten with love for her. Steve was smitten by her personality.

definition: This expression refers to something that is constantly changing, often making a person feel uncertain.
example: I’ve had trouble maintaining a job in the shifting sands of the economy.

definition: What everyone is asking and what we all want to know about, is called the burning question.
example: Who is the mole? That’s the burning question!

definition: This expression refers to a probable situation “if”, in all other ways, the conditions remain unchanged or equal.
example: All things being equal, a reduction in the cost of marketing should enable us to lower the prices.

definition: To refer to something as a needle in a haystack means that it is very difficult or even impossible to find.
example: Finding a restaurant in Berlin without knowing its name is like looking for a needle in a haystack.

definition: If you toot your own horn, you like to boast about your abilities and achievements.
example: I am discreet about my books. I don’t toot my own horn.

definition: A kangaroo court is an illegal tribunal set up by a group of people who have taken the law into their own hands and conduct trials which deny fundamental justice.
example: I don’t like your behaviour. Is this a meeting or a kangaroo court?

definition: When somebody understands, after something has happened, what could have been done to prevent it from happening, they are wise after the event.
example: There are people that find it very hard to be wise even after the event. They simply don’t understand.

definition: If you eat out of somebody’s hand, you are eager to please and will accept to do anything that person asks.
example: She is so persuasive that she has had him eating out of her hand in no time.

phrase: snatch victory from the jaws of defeat
definition: If you manage to win something such as a match or a contest, when you are on the verge of losing, you snatch victory from the jaws of defeat.
example: With this goal, they snatched victory from the jaws of defeat.

definition: If something makes your blood run cold, it shocks or scares you a lot.
example: The look in the suspect’s eyes made my blood run cold.

definition: Someone who has a heart of stone is a cold person who shows others no understanding, sympathy or pity.
example: They don’t like him because he has a heart of stone.

definition: To play by ear means to improvise or act without preparation, according to the demands of the situation.
example: It’s impossible to know how the situation will develop. Let’s just play it by ear.

definition: To refer to someone as a wet blanket means that they spoil other people’s fun, or make an event less enjoyable than it could have been.
example: Come on man! Don’t be such a wet blanket!

definition: This slang expression means to pay attention or take notice of something.
example: Hey! Get a load of that tuxedo!

definition: If someone is quick off the mark, they are quick to react to an event or take advantage of an opportunity.
example: You’ve got to be quick off the mark when the store announce special offers so as to get that laptop.

definition: When someone has a short fuse, they are likely to become angry easily or quickly.
example: The manager has a short fuse today.

definition: If you are angry and threaten to skin someone alive, you mean that you are going to punish them severely.
example: If those kids damage my car again, I’ll skin them alive!

definition: This expression refers to a child or young person who thinks and expresses themselves like an older more-experienced person.
example: When I heard the little girl advising her brother not to go out in such weather, I thought: “An old head on young shoulders”.

definition: This idiom means to be determined to work very hard.
example: The organisation needs me to pull my socks up now that the context is so intricate.

definition: If a situation or feeling reaches fever pitch, it becomes very intense and exciting.
example: Reactions to the conflict have reached fever pitch and the war is about to begin.

definition: When you are happy or excited because of a pleasant event that makes you feel as if you were floating, you are walking on air.
example: Since my project was implemented I have been walking on air.

definition: This expression is the promise or prediction that people responsible for some failure or disaster will be dismissed or otherwise held to account.
example: This is unacceptable! Heads will roll!

definition: This phrase refers to a decision made before the evidence for it is known. It’s like an inevitable conclusion.
example: Taking into consideration all the aspects, isn’t it a foregone conclusion?

definition: Someone who adopts an ostrich strategy/policy chooses to ignore or evade an obvious problem in the hope that it will resolve itself or disappear.
example: Adopting an ostrich strategy will only make matters worse.

definition: This expression means to be attracted to someone exclusively.
example: They have eyes only for one another and are always seen together.

definition: Any situation that is potentially risky or dangerous is called a dicey situation.
example: The police officer was in a dicey situation.

phrase: a drowning man will clutch at a straw
definition: This saying refers to the desperate measures that someone in need may take in order to come out of the situation.
example: Steven tried his hand at that interview to get a job because a drowning man will clutch at a straw.

definition: This idiom refers to something you do no want to experience because it is so unpleasant.
example: When you’re young an boisterous, an evening at home with your family seems like a fate worse than death.

definition: After an attempt at something, if you are sent away with a flea in your ear, you are angrily reprimanded or humiliated.
example: The cheater was sent away with a flea in his ear.

definition: If you give something a lick and a promise, you make a quick attempt to clean it, with the intention of doing it more thoroughly later.
example: I gave the bathroom a lick and a promise before I ran to work.

definition: If you say that it is only/just a matter of time before/until something happens, it is certain to happen or will inevitably take place, although you do not know when.
example: More regulations will have to be introduced. It’s only a matter of time.

phrase: a miss is as good as a mile
definition: This means that some endeavours either succeed or they don’t – this means that missing narrowly is still a failure.
example: She has almost broken the record. Sadly, a miss is as good as a mile.

definition: This expression is an amusing way of referring to a very long period of time.
example: I haven’t been to the cinema in a month of Sundays.

definition: This idiom refers to a group of iniquitous people, congregating together.
example: No, I won’t go there. There’s a nest of vipers and I don’t want to meet them.

phrase: a nod is as good as a wink
definition: This phrase refers to passing signals to convey a message. This signal can be subtle for those who want to understand it.
example: Between lovers, a nod is generally as good as a wink.

phrase: a stitch in time saves nine
definition: This idiom means that it’s better to fix the problem now because it will get worse later.
example: You should speak with her today. A stitch in time saves nine.

definition: This idiom refers to a persistent difficulty or annoyance.
example: This week I will solve this problem out. It has been like a thorn in the flesh for me.

phrase: a trouble shared is a trouble halved
definition: This idiom means that the intensity of a issue can be lowered down by discussion.
example: Don’t hesitate to share your problem with me. A trouble shared is a trouble halved!

definition: This term refers to a complete change of opinion or policy.
example: The manager’s recent declarations indicate an about turn in company policy.

definition: If something has existed or been somewhere “all along”, it has been there all the time, from the beginning.
example: She had been looking for the car keys for some time before she realized they had been in her pocket all along.

definition: If all hell breaks loose, a situation suddenly becomes noisy and violent, usually with a lot of people arguing of fighting.
example: When they saw each other all hell broke loose.

definition: This is said about someone who talks a lot about doing something but never actually does it.
example: Mary keeps saying that she’s going to resign but she’s all mouth and no trousers.

phrase: an iron fist / hand in a velvet glove
definition: This expression is used to describe someone who, behind an appearance of gentleness, is inflexible and determined.
example: To impose the necessary company reforms, the manager used persuasion followed by wage reductions – an iron fist in a velvet glove.

definition: If something is in apple-pie order, it is well organized or in perfect order.
example: They made sure the room was in apple-pie order before their parents arrived back home.

definition: If you argue the toss, you dispute a decision or choice which has already been made.
example: The final choice was made two days ago, so you shouldn’t argue the toss now!

definition: This idiom refers to a loud argument or disagreement that is not usually serious.
example: It has been just a bit of argy-bargy between them.

definition: If you say that someone is bright as a button, you say that they are very intelligent and also a pleasant person.
example: Your daughter is as bright as a button.

definition: This expression means that there is no real difference which alternative is chosen.
example: What do you think I should do? Take the train or fly? It’s as broad as it’s long.

definition: This simile means to be very stupid or foolish.
example: The meeting will be boring. She’s as daft as a brush.

definition: If somebody is as drunk as a lord, they are extremely drunk.
example: When I met him he was as drunk as a lord.

definition: This simile means very happy and content.
example: Every time we go to that old chalet he is as happy as a sandboy.

definition: To say that something could be done at a pinch means that it would be possible to do it if absolutely necessary.
example: The big hall can seat 100 people, and a few more at a pinch.

definition: If someone thinks they are the bee’s knees, they have a high opinion of themselves.
example: Darius thinks he’s the bee’s knees since he got his new job.

phrase: beard the lion in his den
definition: If you visit someone important in the place where they work, in order to challenge him/her or obtain something, you beard the lion in his den.
example: If he continues to refuse my calls, I will have to beard the lion in his den.

definition: If you beat someone to the draw, you react more quickly and manage to do something before they do.
example: Carrie was determined to be the first to arrive. She managed to beat the others to the draw.

definition: This is a shorthand for a life of indulgence spent in the pub.
example: One day she will find out that life isn’t all beer and skittles.

definition: This expression means to do a dangerous job.
example: You might bell the cat and join the army!

definition: The action most likely to succeed is called one’s best bet.
example: Your best bet would be to try calling them at home. They might answer.

phrase: best-laid schemes of mice and men
definition: This phrase means that even the most carefully prepared plans may go wrong.
example: We have taken all the necessary measures, but don’t forget: best-laid schemes of mice and men.

definition: The expression refers to a person who has a lot of power and influence in an organization.
example: My father is a big cheese in the oil industry. So, tell me how can I help you.

phrase: birds of a feather flock together
definition: This expression means that people who are alike are often friends (it is usually used negatively).
example: No wonder they are friends. Birds of a feather flock together.

definition: This expression refers to a place in which things are lost, never to be seen again.
example: Her purse is a black hole.

definition: Someone who blots their copy-book does something to spoil their good record or reputation.
example: She blotted her copy-book when she was arrested for drug dealing.

definition: This idiom means utterly lazy.
example: Nicole is a bone idle woman.

definition: To say that someone is bowing and scraping means that they are being excessively polite or servile.
example: The prime-minister was greeted with much bowing and scraping.

definition: This expression means extremely cold weather. The complete expression is “Cold enough to freeze the balls off a brass monkey.”
example: The weatherwoman says minus 15 degrees and strong winds for tomorrow. That’s a brass monkey weather.

definition: If you break fresh ground, you innovate by introducing or developing a new method or system.
example: The cook has broken fresh ground in his exploration of new recipes.

definition: If someone is breathing down your neck, they are watching you too closely and making you feel uncomfortable.
example: The atmosphere at work is not great at all. The manager keeps breathing down my neck all time.

definition: This idiom means to make somebody accountable for their conduct.
example: The police failed to bring anyone to book for the crime.

definition: If something happens in broad daylight, it takes place in the clear light of day when everyone can see what’s going on.
example: Her car was stolen in broad daylight.

definition: If you are browned off, you are bored, fed up or disheartened.
example: John is browned off with his job and he wants to make a change.

definition: After an unpleasant or unexpected event, this expression means that everything is continuing in a normal way, in spite of the difficulties.
example: It was business as usual at the bank after the hold-up.

definition: This is a name playfully applied to someone who fails to catch a ball or lets something slip from their fingers.
example: Bob is a butterfingers. Don’t take him in our team.

definition: This expression may mean: not at all; not in any way; not by any means. It depends on the context.
example: The situation hasn’t been solved yet, not by a long shot.

definition: This literally means as a result of something.
example: She got what she had wanted by dint of threatening.

definition: The term by virtue of might mean “due to”, “because of” or “on account of” something.
example: The old man got the best place by virtue of his age.

phrase: cake / game is not worth the candle
definition: To say that the cake (or the game) is not worth the candle means that the advantages to be gained from doing something are not worth the effort involved.
example: They recorded an outstanding album but sold very few copies; the cake wasn’t worth the candle.

definition: A calculated risk is a risk taken with full knowledge of the dangers involved.
example: The firms took a calculated risk when they hired Marry directly out of college.

definition: This idiom refers to an exact duplicate.
example: This smartphone is a carbon-copy.

definition: This phrase means to do something pointless and superfluous.
example: I don’t understand you. It’s like carrying coals to Newcastle.

definition: This idiom means to have complete authority.
example: I have carte blanche over who goes into this mission.

definition: This term refers to an example which serves to illustrate, support or prove a point which is currently under discussion.
example: Not even the best athlete is guaranteed a long career. The latest accident is a case in point.

definition: This idiom refers to a payment made immediately.
example: They requested cash on the nail for the goods.

definition: This idiom refers to items of quality offered to those who aren’t cultured enough to appreciate them.
example: You are casting pearls before swine with your good advice.

definition: A catch 22 situation refers to a frustrating situation where you cannot do one thing without doing a second, and you cannot do the second before doing the first.
example: I can’t get a day off without finishing the project and I can’t finished the project with all this stress. It’s a catch 22 situation!

definition: This expression means that you try to get something in any way possible.
example: It’s difficult to get much free time with this new project – it’s catch-as-catch-can these days!

definition: This expression refers to someone who considers themselves to be better than others in a particular area: beauty, competence, intelligence, sport etc.
example: Since he got a promotion, he thinks he’s the cat whiskers!

definition: If someone is caught unawares, they are surprised and unprepared for what happens.
example: The police officer moved so silently that the thieves were caught unawares.

definition: If something causes a stir, it creates an atmosphere of excitement or great interest.
example: The arrival of the actor caused quite a stir in the town.

definition: If you chance your arm, you decide to do something even though there is little hope of success.
example: He knew there was little hope of getting into the Police Academy but he decided to chance his arm.

phrase: chance would be a fine thing
definition: This phrase means that there is not much chance of that thing, welcome though it would be.
example: I’d like to win the contest. Chance would be a fine thing.

definition: A cruel, unfair or unwarranted comment or verbal attack is called a cheap shot.
example: Referring to Jane as a “poor speaker” was really a cheap shot.

definition: When people are cheek by jowl, they are crammed uncomfortably close together.
example: The refugees are living cheek by jowl in a camp.

definition: If you chop and change, you constantly change your opinion, plans or methods and often cause confusion.
example: I strongly advise you not to chop and change all the time.

phrase: cock a snook at somebody / something
definition: This phrase means to do something intentionally to show you have no respect for someone or something.
example: I can seldom resist to cock a snook at traditional life.

definition: This idiom means an unbelievable tale.
example: Oh, don’t listen to her. It’s just another cock and bull story.

definition: This idiom means in a state of exuberant elation.
example: I was cock-a-hoop when the team won.

definition: To say that someone has come up trumps means that they have achieved unexpectedly good results.
example: Against all my expectations, the team came up trumps in the cup final.

definition: This idiom means not to succeed at something.
example: He seemed to come a cropper shortly after his promotion as a team manager.

definition: This idiom means to develop into a bad, unfortunate or difficult situation.
example: Things have come to such a pretty pass that parents are afraid of criticizing their children.

definition: This expression refers to an area of shared beliefs, interests or mutual understanding between people or groups who often have disagreements.
example: Any common ground among the European countries will contribute to future unity.

definition: To describe something such as a plan, a contract or a financial arrangement as copper-bottomed means that it is completely safe or reliable.
example: We signed a copper-bottomed contract with a distributor.

definition: If you do a crash course, you do an intensive training course in order to obtain quick results.
example: Before going to Germany, she did a crash course in German language.

definition: This expression refers to modern conveniences (such as hot water or central heating) that make life comfortable and pleasant.
example: She needs her creature comforts. I don’t know how she would survive without hot water.

phrase: cross a bridge before one comes to it
definition: This phrase means to worry about the future in advance.
example: Thanks to my anxiety, I often cross a bridge before I come to it.

definition: The period of time just before a project has to be completed and everyone has to work hard.
example: It’s crunch time at work, so we’re not getting enough sleep these days.

definition: This expression refers to affection given in order to gain a reward.
example: Her affair with that man was just cupboard love.

definition: If a person cuts a dash, they make a striking impression by their appearance and attractive clothes.
example: Wearing his uniform, my uncle cut a dash on his wedding day.

definition: If you are a dab hand at something, you are very good at doing it.
example: I think you should call him. He’s a dab hand at planning parties.

phrase: discretion is the greater part of valour
definition: This idiom means to be quiet about it after helping someone out.
example: He taught me that discretion is the greater part of valour.

definition: If something does you a world of good, it is beneficial and makes you feel a lot better.
example: A few days off would do you a world of good. Trust me.

definition: This expression means that you should not form an opinion based on outward appearances only.
example: He looks extremely confident but don’t judge by appearances. As far as I know, he’s a shy man.

phrase: don’t teach your grandmother to suck eggs
definition: This expression means that you shouldn’t teach someone who is really experienced to do something new, because the changes are they know it better than you. This idiom can be used if somebody is patronizing you or not treating you like an adult.
example: I know how to use the present tense! Don’t teach your grandmother to suck eggs.

definition: This expression refers to rules about what you must do and what you must not do in a specific condition.
example: There’s a list of the dos and don’ts of diplomatic receptions.

definition: A person who is down-at-heel is someone whose appearance is untidy or neglected because of lack of money.
example: Do you know Sarah, my down-at-heel neighbour? She died.

definition: This idiom refers to the fulfillment of a wish after a long time.
example: This car is my dream come true.

definition: Someone dressed up to the nines is wearing very smart or glamorous clothes.
example: He must be going to a party or something – he’s dressed up to the nines.

phrase: dull at ditchwater / as dull as dishwater
definition: Something or someone as dull as ditchwater is very boring.
example: Let’s go. He’s as dull as dishwater.

definition: This idiom refers to a guess that is made using judgment and a particular level of knowledge and is therefore more likely to be correct.
example: I can’t tell you exactly how much this building will cost but I can make an educated guess.

definition: Even someone who never complains will react to an intolerable situation.
example: If she continues to treat her husband badly, he’ll leave her – even a worm will turn.

definition: If someone has a face like a wet week-end, they look sad and miserable.
example: Is everything all right? You have a face like a wet week-end.

definition: When the facts of a situation are so clear that no further explanation or extra details are necessary, the facts speak for themselves.
example: There’s no need to tell you that the results are amazing. The facts speak for themselves.

definition: This idiom means not very good but not bad.
example: What’s his English like? Oh, fair to middling.

definition: If something falls between two stools, it is neither totally one thing nor another and is therefore unsatisfactory.
example: The study wasn’t read because it fell between two stools. It appealed neither to general public nor to lawyers.

definition: If a joke, a story or a form of entertainment falls flat, it does not amuse people or fails to have the effect that was intended.
example: She tried to make some jokes but they fell flat.

definition: If something proves inadequate or insufficient or does not reach the required standard, it falls short of what is expected.
example: Sales of this smartphone fell short of our expectations.

definition: In a dangerous or risky situation, if you make a false move, you do something which may have unpleasant consequences.
example: The terrorism suspect is under close surveillance. If she makes one false move, she will be immediately arrested.

definition: This expression means that the better you know someone the less you like him.
example: After several months, she didn’t like him anymore. Familiarity breeds contempt.

definition: This idiom literally means “unlikely to be true”.
example: His story was a far-fetched one.

definition: If you fight shy of something, such as a task, a problem or a duty, you want to avoid doing it or you are unwilling to confront it.
example: I’ve fought shy of learning a new language but now I don’t have a choice.

definition: This idiom means to be exactly suitable for a particular situation.
example: He fills the bill for this mission.

definition: If you are fit to be tied, you are extremely irritated, upset or angry.
example: I was fit to be tied when her cat dug up one of my little trees.

definition: A person who is footloose and fancy free has few responsibilities or commitments of any kind and feels free to do as they please.
example: I won’t get married in near future. I like being footloose and fancy free.

phrase: forbidden fruit is always the sweetest
definition: This expression means to desire something that is not within a feasible reach.
example: Everybody knows that the forbidden fruit is always the sweetest.

definition: This expression means that if you know something is going to happen, you can be prepared for it.
example: They said that the war would begin soon. Forewarned is forearmed!

definition: This idiom means that people who face problems with determination and courage are the ones who attain massive levels of success.
example: Why does she have such success? Fortune favours the bold!

definition: If you act in a way that harms your own interests, your position or your reputation, you foul your own nest.
example: He fouled his own nest by stealing from their house.

definition: An activity or situation that is fraught with danger is full of risks or serious difficulties.
example: Their abroad mission is fraught with danger because that is a war zone.

definition: This idiom refers to a person who freely lives a life of their own way.
example: I find her attractive because she is a free-spirited woman.

definition: In a contest, race or election, the front runner is the person who is most likely to succeed or win.
example: I think Steve is the front runner of today’s competition.

definition: This idiom refers to an old-fashioned and foolish type of person.
example: He’s a real fuddy-duddy.

phrase: full of the joys of spring
definition: If you are full of the joys of spring, you are happy, enthusiastic and full of energy.
example: Amanda is full of the joys of spring. Has she got a new boyfriend?

definition: This idiom means to annoy somebody.
example: With all her remarks, she has got on my wick.

definition: This idiom means to become agitated or angry.
example: Don’t let her get your dander up.

definition: If you get your money’s worth, you receive good value for the amount of money you spend.
example: We bought a touristic pass and we really got our money’s worth.

definition: This idiom means to show no mercy or concession.
example: Give no quarter! They have mistaken and deserve to be scolded.

definition: If someone or something is going great guns, they are doing very well.
example: The newly-opened store is going great guns.

definition: If you go hell for leather, you go somewhere or do something very fast.
example: I saw a man going hell for leather towards the car.

definition: This idiom means to speak or act prematurely.
example: Why do you always go off at half-cock?

phrase: go somewhere under your own steam
definition: If you go somewhere under your own steam, you do so without any help from others.
example: Don’t worry. We’ll get there under our own steam.

definition: If you go spare you lose your temper completely.
example: My wife would go spare if she knew how much our son spent in Berlin.

definition: If something goes to rack and ruin, it falls into very bad condition because of lack of care.
example: After the automobile repair shop closed down, the building went to rack and ruin.

definition: The most important rule or principle to be remembered when doing something is called the golden rule.
example: You should not be seen. That’s the golden rule for us.

definition: This idiom means no longer functional – a reference to a person who has died or an item that has been broken.
example: This laptop has gone for a burton.

definition: This idiom refers to someone who compassionately helps another who is in need.
example: My neighbour played the Good Samaritan and gave me some money.

definition: This expression means that respecting one another’s privacy helps create a good relationship between neighbours.
example: I always try not to disturb the people next door. Good walls make good neighbours!

definition: If you give or get the green light, you give or get a signal or permission to do something.
example: I am ready to launch the marketing campaign as soon as I get the green light.

definition: To refer to something as a grey area means that it is not clear or easy to define and is therefore difficult to deal with.
example: The law concerning e-commerce is still a grey area in some countries.

definition: Grey matter refers to the brain, or they grey colour of brain tissue.
example: Try using your grey matter and solve this problem.

definition: Enjoying something which is not generally held in high regard, while at the same time feeling a bit guilty about it, is called a guilty pleasure.
example: Playing PC games is my guilty pleasure.

definition: This idiom means extremely enthusiastic about doing something, especially going to war.
example: He’s such a gung-ho man… I like him!

definition: If you have a gut feeling about something, you have a strong intuition that you cannot explain, but you’re sure that you are right.
example: As I listened to her, I had the gut feeling that she was lying… and I was right!

definition: This idiom means “making you feel very upset or worried”.
example: I’ve seen some gut-wrenching scenes of violence.

definition: To say that someone has had their chips means that they have completely failed in what they set out to achieve.
example: After the third round, it looked as if John had had his chips.

definition: Someone, especially an old person, who is hale and hearty is in excellent health.
example: My grandfather is still hale and hearty at the age of eighty.

definition: This idiom refers to a difficult, unpleasant or adverse situation.
example: It’s hard cheese for the employees of that company.

definition: This idiom means to have had a wonderful past but no present or future in the field.
example: Our relationship is now just a has-been.

phrase: have an eye to / for the main chance
definition: Someone who has an eye to / for the main chance is always ready to use a situation to their own advantage.
example: I always have an eye for the main chance.

definition: This idiom means to reject or to have nothing to do with.
example: I have no truck with this man.

definition: This idiom means to punish someone severely.
example: if you breathe a word to anyone, I’ll have your guts for garters.

definition: This idiom means to be too busy.
example: If you have too much on your plate, my secretary can help you.

phrase: hide one’s light under a bushel
definition: If you hide your light under a bushel, you are modest or do not reveal a talent, quality or skill you possess.
example: I didn’t know she plays the piano. She has hidden her light under a bushel.

definition: This phrase means mixed up and in no particular order.
example: Her clothes were all higgledy-piggledy in the drawer.

phrase: hitch one’s wagon to a star
definition: Someone who hitches their wagon to a star has great ambitions and is very determined to reach their goal.
example: He decided to hitch his wagon to a star and become an astronaut.

definition: This idiom refers to a favourite topic that one frequently refers to or dwells on; a fixation. It may also refer to a child’s toy.
example: I admit that fishing is a hobby-horse of mine.

definition: This expression means that being honest is always good and fruitful.
example: I learnt as a kid that honesty is the best policy.

definition: This means that even criminals have a sense of loyalty and they respect a certain code of behaviour.
example: The thief refused to reveal the names of his accomplices, which shows that there is honour among thieves.

phrase: hope for the best, but prepare for the worst
definition: This idiom means to be optimistic but ready for hard times as well.
example: My father was hoping for the best, but was prepared for the worst anytime.

phrase: I can’t be doing with it / something
definition: This idiom refers to a person who is not willing to tolerate something.
example: The noise is outrageous! I’ll go to my neighbour to tell him that I can’t be doing with it.

phrase: idle hands are the devil’s tools
definition: This expression means that you are more likely to get in trouble if you have nothing to do.
example: No wonder she has got into trouble. Idle hands are the devil’s tools!

phrase: if the cap / shoe fits, then wear it
definition: You can say “if the cap fits, wear it” to let someone know that the critical remark they have just heard applies to them.
example: “Are you referring to me when you say that terrible things?” “If the cap fits, then wear it!”

definition: This idiom means in a position where advance and retreat are both impossible; in a fix.
example: I’m in a cleft stick with regard to our relationship.

definition: This idiom means prosperous, living well.
example: After I earn a million, I’ll be in a clover.

definition: This idiom means to be on the rise to becoming more influential or more successful.
example: The price of gold has been in the ascendant since I started to save money.

definition: If you are in the pink of health, you are in excellent physical condition.
example: He look in the pink of health after the holiday.

phrase: in the twinkling of an eye
definition: Something that happens in the twinkling of an eye happens very fast.
example: You should keep in mind that public opinion can change in the twinkling of an eye.

phrase: in the wrong place at the wrong time
definition: This expression is used when something unlucky happens, something that would not have normally happened.
example: Poor you! You’ve been in the wrong place at the wrong time.

phrase: in two shakes of a lamb’s tail
definition: To do something in two shakes of a lamb’s tail means to do it very quickly.
example: I can solve it! I’ll be ready in two shakes of a lamb’s tail.

phrase: it is a poor workman who blames his tools
definition: This expression means that if you can’t do the job, don’t blame it on others.
example: I told you not to call on him. It’s a poor workman who blames his tools.

definition: If you find something that you want for a very low price, much lower than what it is worth, you can say “it’s a steal!”.
example: She selling the smartphone for $100? At that price it’s a steal!

definition: This idiom refers to a conspicuously self-assured, carefree and brash young man.
example: He is like the Jack the lad.

definition: This idiom refers to some pleasant event in the future, which is never likely to materialize.
example: It’s your option, but this sounds like Jam tomorrow for me.

definition: If you describe something as being just the job, you mean that thing is well-suited for a specific purpose.
example: I don’t need a big bag. That small plastic bag is just the job.

definition: If something is just the ticket, it is exactly right or just what you need.
example: I’ve had dinner at home, so a beer would be just the ticket.

definition: This idiom means to say little or nothing about one’s opinions or intentions.
example: Our manager is notorious for keeping his own counsel.

definition: This idiom means to be prepared and save your resources until they are needed.
example: Don’t buy a new car now. Keep your powder dry!

definition: People who have a lot in common and share the same beliefs, attitudes and feelings are kindred spirits.
example: I immediately felt that we were kindred spirits.

definition: This idiom means to be experienced in or knowledgeable about a subject.
example: Her advice is invaluable. She knows her onions!

definition: A lame excuse is an explanation which is weak and unconvincing.
example: If you don’t want to do it, just say so. Don’t invent a lame excuse!

definition: This idiom means to laugh coarsely or loudly, especially at the discomfort of others.
example: When I entered into the restaurant she was laughing like a drain.

definition: If you laugh up your sleeve, you are secretly amused at another person’s problems or difficulties.
example: She felt that the show wasn’t so good as she had expected and that her colleagues were laughing up their sleeve.

definition: A person who does something stupid or ridiculous which causes others to laugh becomes a laughing stock.
example: If you wear that suit, you’ll be the laughing stock of the company.

phrase: lay something on thick / with a trowel
definition: This idiom means to grossly exaggerate or overemphasize something.
example: Just to make sure the significance of his remarks was not missed, the general manager laid it on with a trowel.

definition: If a plan or project leads to a dead end, it develops no further because it has no future.
example: In spite of our efforts, the marketing research led to a dead end.
