definition: If you learn the hard way, you learn through your own experience, rather than from the advice or guidance of others.
example: Her refusal to accept my help meant that she had to learn the hard way.

definition: The length of time needed to learn something new is called the learning curve.
example: This system has a long learning curve so we will need more time.

definition: If you lend an ear to someone, you listen carefully and sympathetically.
example: I know you and it seems that something is troubling you. I will lend an ear to you if you want to talk about it.

phrase: life is just a bowl of cherries
definition: This expression means that life is pleasant and uncomplicated. Keep in mind that this phrase is often used ironically to mean the opposite.
example: Life is just a bowl of cherries. You should love more!

definition: A person who lives the life of Riley has a comfortable and enjoyable life, without having to make much effort.
example: Steve married a well-off woman, and since then he has been living the life of Riley.

definition: If someone or something moves like a scalded cat, they move very fast, usually because they are frightened or shocked.
example: As soon as they saw the policemen, they ran off like a scalded cat.

phrase: live high off / on the hog
definition: Someone who lives high off/on the hog has a lot of money and a very comfortable lifestyle.
example: As far as I know, they are living high off the hog now.

phrase: live up to your / its reputation
definition: This expression means to have all the positive or negative attributes that other people have described.
example: I enjoyed the movie, but I don’t think it lived up to its reputation as the greatest action film of all time.

definition: This term is used to express surprise, especially at a sudden or unexpected appearance.
example: I was in Barcelona sitting in a café when, lo and behold, my wife walked in.

definition: This idiom means that if you love someone, you cannot see the faults in that person.
example: Love is blind and it is so true in their case.

definition: If someone is made of sterner stuff, they have a strong character and are better able to deal with difficulties than others.
example: You can’t upset her. She is made of sterner stuff.

definition: If someone does something commendable, not deliberately but because they have no choice, and pretends to be doing it willingly and happily, they make a virtue of necessity.
example: When, because of the high price of petrol, I decided to take the bus to work instead of taking my car, I made a virtue of necessity.

definition: This expression means to make a problem worse.
example: To make matters worse, he can’t come today to repair the machine.

definition: If something makes your ears burn, you are embarrassed by what you hear, especially if the conversation is about you.
example: Her low opinion of me has made my ears burn.

phrase: many a true word is spoken in jest
definition: This idiom has a literal meaning, that the truth is often found in comic utterances.
example: Has he said something special when joking? Many a true word is spoken in jest.

definition: This is an axiom that encourages careful first steps in order to avoid extra work later on.
example: “Measure twice, cut once” should be your new motto!

definition: A very easy way of earning money is called money for jam.
example: As a promoter for this company, all you have to do is hand out brochures. It’s money for jam.

definition: Money earned from a task that required very little effort is called money for old rope.
example: Getting paid for opening the doors is money for old rope!

definition: Someone who does a moonlight flit leave a place quickly and in secret, usually to avoid paying debts.
example: Exactly before the rent for three months was due he did a moonlight flit.

definition: If you rush, you make mistakes and end up taking longer.
example: I didn’t know what version you needed. More haste, less speed.

definition: This expression means “very similar” or “almost alike”.
example: It’s quite hard to choose between the two wrist watches – they’re much of a muchness.

definition: An unprofitable or ill-advised activity that only a fool (mug) would do is called a mug’s game.
example: I told her that spending hours making cakes for few customers is a mug’s game.

definition: This idiom refers to a nonsense or meaningless speech.
example: His speech was just a mumbo-jumbo.

definition: This expression is used to show that you do no believe something that has just been said.
example: She said she had a sports car? My foot!

phrase: needs must when the devil drives
definition: The expression means that you are sometimes forced by circumstances to do something that you do not want to do.
example: I’d rather stay at home with you than attend the meeting, but needs must when the devil drives.

definition: This phrase refers to two things which are so different as to have no opportunity to unite.
example: She can’t meet a wealthy man. Never the twain shall meet.

definition: If you can’t have exactly what you want, the next best thing is the best alternative possible.
example: The smartphone I wanted was far too expensive so I chose the next best thing.

definition: This idiom refers to a novelty that loses its appeal after a few days.
example: This product has been a nine days’ wonder.

definition: To say that there are no flies on someone means that they are quick to understand and cannot be tricked or deceived easily.
example: It’s better to tell Samantha the truth. There are no flies on her.

definition: This idiom means to require help from other every now and then because of one’s limitations.
example: Having a baby has taught him that no man is an island.

definition: If you say you wouldn’t do something for (all) the world, you mean that you never do it, no matter what you were offered.
example: Not for (all) the world would I do that!

definition: If you are not getting anywhere, you are making no progress at all.
example: I’ve spent the whole week looking for a solution but I’m not getting anywhere.

definition: If you do not give a hang about something, you are totally indifferent to it and do not care at all about it.
example: I’m not interested in tennis, so I don’t give a hang about it.

definition: If an explanation or statement doesn’t hold water, it can be shown to be unfounded.
example: I’m sorry, but your statement doesn’t hold water.

definition: Something that is not to be sneezed at should not be rejected or refused.
example: An offer like that is not to be sneezed at.

definition: If someone does not turn a hair, they show no emotion in circumstances where a reaction is expected.
example: When the police officer arrested the thief, he didn’t turn a hair.

definition: This means that something has to be done now or can’t be done at all.
example: You’ve got one chance. It’s now or never!

definition: Something which is null and void has no legal force or is invalid.
example: Our contract was declared null and void.

definition: If you do something of your own accord, you do it spontaneously or willingly, without being influenced or forced by anyone.
example: The girl went of her own accord to see the owner and admitted breaking the window.

definition: This expression means that something/someone is unlikely to succeed, or is unlikely to gain much advantage if they do.
example: Politically speaking, we are on a hiding to nothing in the long run.

definition: If something happens on cue, it happens at exactly the appropriate or expected moment.
example: My girlfriend was blowing out the candles on her birthday cake when, right on cue, the gift arrived.

definition: To say that an idea, plan or scheme seems good on paper means that it looks good in theory or in writing but may not work when put into practice.
example: Your marketing plan looks good on paper.

definition: This expression means that after giving the matter more thought, you have changed your mind.
example: My idea was to buy a car, but on second thoughts, I’d rather have a bicycle.

definition: If something is on tap, it is easily obtained or available for immediate use, like water from a tap.
example: You can find a lot of useful resources on tap on the internet.

definition: This expression refers to a point in time that marks a transition or the beginning of a change.
example: After the failed coup, the country is on the cusp.

definition: This expression is used to refer to an event that is most likely going to happen soon.
example: I’m sure a promotion is on the horizon.

definition: Something that is done on the QT is done quietly and discreetly.
example: We plan to get married to each other on the QT.

definition: If you do something to be on the safe side, you do it as a precaution, to avoid any risks.
example: I think I locked the car, but I’ll check again to be on the safe side.

definition: This is a slang term for alone.
example: The party is over. I’m on my tod.

definition: This term refers to the art of gaining and keeping an advantage over other people.
example: He’s a brilliant man, but his one-upmanship has left him with no friends.

definition: If you do something that is the cause of your own failure, loss or downfall, it is your own undoing.
example: If he continues to play poker like that, it will be his own undoing.

definition: If you pay for something out of your own pocket, you cover the cost with your own money.
example: Breakfast is included but you have to pay for dinner out of your own pocket.

definition: This idiom refers to a thrilling book.
example: This book is a page-turner.

definition: This idiom refers to a state of high alert, often a simulated panic for comic effect.
example: One week before an exam it’s always panic stations.

definition: This term refers to a person, organisation or country that is less powerful or threatening than they appear to be.
example: Don’t worry. He’s just a paper tiger and he doesn’t have the power to do that.

definition: If something is par for the course, it is typical of what to expect in that particular situation.
example: I’ve done my job very well, but nobody congratulated me. That’s par for the course in this firm.

definition: Something that is part and parcel of an activity or role is a key component or an essential element that cannot be avoided.
example: I’m a tourist agent. Travelling is part and parcel of my job.

definition: A person who helps you to plan something dishonest or unlawful is called your partner in crime. This expression can also be used jokingly.
example: My wife was my partner in crime.

definition: This phrase refers to a feeling of calm or not being worried.
example: For my peace of mind, please check the door.

definition: This idiom refers to a motivational speech.
example: I met Adrian for a pep talk because I had an important interview the very next day.

definition: This expression is used when the speaker really hopes that something will not happen.
example: If I lost my job, perish the thought, I know what I would have to do.

definition: This idiom means intensely dark, usually in reference to a moonless, starless night.
example: The sky was pitch dark.

definition: Plan B is an alternative solution to be adopted if one’s original plan does not succeed.
example: Plan B is to move the production unit to another county.

definition: This idiom means to be inconstant and unreliable.
example: Playing fast and loose is not a solution!

definition: If you play gooseberry, you join or accompany two people who have a romantic relationship and want to be alone.
example: I was invited to join them but I didn’t want to play gooseberry.

definition: A young person who plays truant stays away from school without permission or excuse.
example: Marry hasn’t any reason to be absent again from school – she’s playing truant!

phrase: plenty of other fish in the sea
definition: If you say this, you mean that there are many other people just as good as the person mentioned.
example: Did she refuse the job?! Never mind – there are plenty of other fish in the sea.

definition: Poetic justice is an ideal form of justice in which virtue is rewarded and evil punished.
example: It is poetic justice that the country responsible for starting the war should suffer most from its effects.

definition: This idiom means to fire something at such close range that it cannot be missed. It can also mean “frankly” or “straightforwardly”.
example: He asked her point blank whether she had cheated on him.

definition: This idiom means that diligent practice leads to expertise.
example: You are making good progress. Keep going – practice makes perfect.

definition: This idiom means to look dismal and unhappy.
example: She pulled a long face after being scolded.

definition: If you pull your horns in, you become less ambitious and curb your enthusiasm.
example: The team came bottom of the league this season. They’ll have to pull their horns in when making bids for new players, don’t you think so?

definition: This idiom means short-term adolescent love.
example: Don’t worry about them. It’s only puppy love.

definition: This idiom refers to an overly elaborate or effusive piece of writing. Also, a period of notable success or good luck.
example: She’s on the purple patch now! It’s the best period of her life.

phrase: put a sock / cork in it
definition: This idiom means to impolitely tell someone to stop talking or making a noise.
example: Hey! I’m trying to concentrate! Put a sock in it!

definition: If you tell someone to put on their thinking cap, you ask them to find an idea or solve a problem by thinking about it.
example: This is today’s questions. It’s time to put on your thinking cap!

phrase: put that in your pipe and smoke it
definition: This expression means that you have to accept what the speaker says, whether you like it or not.
example: I’m not going to buy you a new smartphone, so put that in your pipe and smoke it.

phrase: put your shoulder to the wheel
definition: If you put your shoulder to the wheel, you start putting a lot of effort into a difficult task.
example: We have to put out shoulders to the wheel so as to deliver the project on time.

definition: A victory that is obtained at a tremendous cost or causes such a great loss that it is not worth winning, is called a Pyrrhic victory.
example: I won the court case, but it was a Pyrrhic victory because of the legal fees.

definition: This idiom means to ruin a plan or undertaking.
example: This new building has really queered the pitch for my store.

definition: This idiom refers to something that is given to a person in return for something they have done.
example: The government has promised bigger wages as a quid pro quo for the stopping of violence.

definition: This expression is used to express sympathy with someone who has to do something unpleasant or difficult, and you would not like to be in their situation.
example: I have to announce the bad news. Oh, Steve, rather you than me.

definition: If your behaviour or attitude makes someone cry, you reduce them to tears.
example: The criticism of his project was so harsh that he was reduced to tears.

definition: If something is still unknown or a decision has not yet been taken, it remains to be seen.
example: The construction of a new shopping mall has been voted, but the location remains to be seen.

definition: This idiom means to do something in a different way in order to make it more interesting.
example: Let’s ring the changes on packed lunches.

definition: When an action has an effect on something, which in turn effects something else, it is said to have a ripple effect.
example: An increase in the price of electricity will have a ripple effect on the economy as a whole.

definition: This idiom refers to an event or activity often performed or experienced as part of passing from one stage of life to another.
example: Getting lost while trying to find their classrooms is a rite of passage for freshmen at this university.

definition: This idiom refers to the procedure of becoming healthy again.
example: The road to recovery from cancer is a long and draining one.

definition: If you say that something it’s not rocket science, you express the fact that something presents no major difficulty.
example: Maria will explain how it works. It’s not rocket science.

definition: If an action is performed thoroughly or completely, it is done root and branch.
example: The causes of the security incident must be eliminated root and branch.

definition: If you rue the day, you did something during the day and you bitterly regret.
example: She will rue the day that she bought that car.

definition: When a group or organisation is run in a well-ordered and disciplined manner, the person in charge runs a taut/tight ship.
example: The general manager runs a taut ship.

phrase: run with the hare and hunt with the hounds
definition: If you run with the hare and hunt with the hounds, you want to stay on friendly terms with both sides in a quarrel.
example: I want to keep everyone happy within the organisation but this time I can’t run with the hare and hunt with the hounds.

definition: If you are rushed off your feet, you are extremely busy.
example: I would like to date you but these days I am being rushed off my feet.

definition: If you are saddled with debt, the amount of money that you owe is a financial burden.
example: If we buy an apartment that is too expensive, we could be saddled with debt for many years.

definition: To say that something is a safe bet means that it is very likely to happen.
example: It’s a safe bet that you’ll get a good job if you graduate from this university.

definition: This expression means that being part of a group makes people feel more secure and more confident when taking action.
example: We went sightseeing in group, knowing there was safety in numbers.

definition: This idiom refers to the days of one’s youthful inexperience and enthusiasm.
example: I’m too old to believe these stories. I am well past my salad days.

definition: When the scales fall from your eyes, you finally understand the truth about something.
example: It was only when my neighbour was arrested for theft that the scales fell from my eyes and I understood where his money came from.

definition: If you tell someone, in an irritated or unfriendly way, to go away, you send them about their business.
example: A bank representative keeps calling on my father, but I told him to send him about his business.

definition: This idiom means to be ignored or ostracised. This behaviour often takes the form of pretending that the shunned person, although conspicuously present, can’t be seen or heard.
example: They sent the little boy to Coventry.

definition: When you consider something to be very important or valuable, you set great store by it.
example: She is setting great store by this job interview – I only hope she gets it.

definition: This idiom refers to a long, rambling story or joke, typically one that is amusing only because it is absurdly inconsequential or pointless.
example: That was a shaggy-dog story.

definition: If something, such as a trend or fashion, is the shape of things to come, it is a sign of what is likely to be used or enjoyed by many people in the future.
example: Do you think that electric cars are the shape of things to come?

definition: Trying to achieve something by using underhand, deceitful or dishonourable means, that are barely within the law, is called sharp practice.
example: The company is under investigation for sharp practice.

definition: If you shilly-shally, you hesitate a lot about something and have difficulty reaching a decision.
example: Stop shilly-shallying and make a decision now!

definition: If people or organisations sink their differences, they decide to forget their disagreements.
example: We must sink our differences and build a strong team.

definition: This idiom refers to an imaginary intuitive facility.
example: My sixth sense is telling me that today it’s going to be a good day.

definition: If a business or organisation works with a skeleton staff/crew, it is run with the smallest number of people necessary.
example: The office is closed during legal holidays but there will be a skeleton staff to assist you.

definition: If you smooth someone’s ruffled feathers, you make that person feel less angry or offended.
example: Come here, darling. Let me smooth your ruffled feathers…

definition: This expression is used when one is certain that something will happen, but is unsure exactly when.
example: She will call me sooner or later.

phrase: spare the rod and spoil the child
definition: This phrase means that children will only flourish if chastised, physically or otherwise, for any wrongdoing.
example: You should do something! Spare the rod and spoil the child!

definition: If you speak ill of someone, you say bad or unkind things about them.
example: I like him because he refuses to speak ill of his colleagues.

definition: This phrase means to use a public lavatory.
example: Well, I need to spend a penny. Can you wait for me?

definition: If something is described as state-of-the-art, it is the most advanced model currently available, incorporating the latest and best technology.
example: This state-of-the-art laptop doesn’t cost so much.

definition: If you steal a march on someone, you do something in an unexpected or secret way that enables you to gain an advantage over them.
example: We are able to steal a march on other competitors by offering a discount.

definition: This idiom refers to an event or experience that helps you achieve something else.
example: I see this job just as a stepping stone to better things.

definition: This idiom refers to a narrow-minded or unprogressive person; one who lacks initiative.
example: I don’t want her in my team because she’s just a stick in the mud.

definition: A sticking point is a controversial issue that causes an interruption or blocks progress in discussions or negotiations.
example: The choice of gas distributor was a sticking point in the negotiations.

definition: Someone who is a stickler for the rules is a disciplinarian who demands strict observance of the rules and procedures.
example: Make sure that you use the proper document. She is a stickler for the rules.

definition: If you keep a straight face, you look serious although you really want to laugh.
example: She said such a foolish thing that I could barely keep a straight face.

definition: If a person or organisation is streets ahead of another, they are much better or more advanced.
example: In measures regarding pollution reduction, the Scandinavians are streets ahead of us.

definition: If you sugar the pill, you try to make some unpleasant news more acceptable by saying something pleasant at the same time.
example: She tried to sugar the pill by telling me that she would be home at weekends.

definition: This idiom means to shirk one’s labour; to malinger.
example: I will swing the lead this time. It’s too difficult for me this task.

definition: Someone who has a swollen or swelled head has become proud or conceited, usually because of a recent success.
example: Nicole’s promotion has given her a swelled head.

definition: A person who takes something in good part reacts to it in a good-humoured way, without taking offence.
example: She got a lot of teasing about her project but she took it in good part.

phrase: take the bit between your teeth
definition: This idiom means to take control of a situation.
example: It’s enough for them. You should take the bit between your teeth.

phrase: take the bitter with the sweet
definition: This phrase means to accept both the good and the bad that happens.
example: You should be prepared to take the bitter with the sweet if you intend to get married.

definition: This phrase means to be displeased or offended by the actions of others.
example: She takes umbrage against anyone who criticises her.

definition: If something takes you unawares, it surprises you because you weren’t expecting it.
example: Her reaction took me unawares.

phrase: take up or throw down the gauntlet
definition: This idiom means to accept or issue a challenge.
example: A price war looks likely now that a leading competitor has thrown down the gauntlet to its adversaries.

definition: Someone who talks nineteen to the dozen speaks very quickly.
example: She was talking nineteen to the dozen so I lost the thread.

phrase: talk the hind leg off a donkey
definition: This expression is used to describe a very talkative person.
example: I avoid talking to her because she can talk the hind off a donkey.

definition: A tall story is a story or statement which is difficult to believe because it sounds unlikely.
example: This really sounds like a tall story.

definition: This expression is used to refer to the teacher’s favourite student.
example: Nobody likes her because she’s teacher’s pet.

definition: This means to gossip or spread rumours.
example: I wish Steve wouldn’t tell tales out of school.

phrase: that’s the way the ball bounces!
definition: This expression means that things don’t always work out as planned, and there’s nothing we can do about it – that’s life.
example: She didn’t get the job she expected. That’s the way the ball bounces!

definition: This expression means to take indirect or unofficial route to get something done.
example: I managed to slide the contract through the back door.

phrase: the bigger they are, the harder they fall
definition: This idiom means that while the bigger and stronger opponent might be a lot more difficult to beat, when you do they suffer a much bigger loss.
example: It’s hard, but not impossible to defeat them. Don’t forget: the bigger they are, the harder they fall!

definition: This idiom refers to an uncomfortable feeling in the stomach caused by feelings of nervousness or slight fear.
example: I’ve got the collywobbles about the exam.

phrase: the course of true love never did run smooth
definition: This idiom means that people in love often have to overcome difficulties in order to be with each other.
example: I hate being in a long distance relationship. The course of true love never did run smooth.

definition: This expression means that you should think of yourself and not worry about other people.
example: Every one for himself and the devil take the hindmost.

definition: When trouble breaks out or a situation deteriorates as a result of something said or done, it is said that the fat hits the fire.
example: The context was tense indeed, but the fat hit the fire when she admitted cheating.

phrase: the pen is mightier than the sword
definition: This expression means that words and communication have greater effect than war and fighting.
example: The final treaty put an end to the conflict – the pen is mightier than the sword.

phrase: the proof of the pudding is in the eating
definition: This expression means that something new can only be judged after it has been tested.
example: I’m going to try out my new laptop. The proof of the pudding is in the eating.

phrase: there will be the devil to pay
definition: This is a way of announcing that there will be trouble if something happens.
example: Please take care! There’ll be the devil to pay if you fall off the motorcycle.

definition: If something such as a feeling or reaction is thinly veiled, it is barely hidden.
example: Her disappointment was thinly veiled when she saw the gift.

definition: If you are faced with a thorny issue, you have to deal with a difficult or unpleasant problem.
example: Content duplication is a thorny issue nowadays.

phrase: those who live in glass houses shouldn’t throw stones
definition: This idiom means that people who are morally questionable shouldn’t criticize others.
example: She has no right to say that. Those who live in glass houses shouldn’t throw stones.

definition: When someone, usually a capricious person, throws a wobbly or wobbler, they have a fit of nerves or bad temper and lose all self-control.
example: She is the sort of woman to throw a wobbly if she doesn’t have a clean skirt.

definition: When something ticks all the right boxes, it is perfect for you because it meets your entire list of criteria.
example: The house I’ve visited today ticks all the right boxes.

definition: This expression refers to someone who is unwilling to speak about an event.
example: She is quite tight-lipped when it comes to speaking about her job.

definition: This idiom means to fight enemies who do not really exist.
example: No, he doesn’t have anything against you! You are tilting at windmills!

definition: This means to be pleased and happy.
example: Thank you for the present! I’m chuffed to bits.

definition: This idiom means totally, fully, completely, utterly.
example: The news of his sudden death shocked her to the core.

definition: People who are toffee-nosed consider themselves to be better than other people, especially than people of a lower social class.
example: She’s a toffee-nosed single woman.

definition: Attempting to achieve a satisfactory result by testing and eliminating various methods until the best one is found, is called trial and error.
example: Some of the best marketers learn by trial and error.

definition: This idiom refers to troubles and events that cause suffering.
example: She speaks about the trials and tribulations of marriage.

definition: If a method is tried and tested, it can be trusted because it has been used successfully in the past and is known to work.
example: Trust me. This method is tried and tested.

definition: This expression means that despite efforts to conceal the facts, the truth cannot be hidden forever.
example: It’s just a matter of time. Truth will out eventually.

definition: This idiom refers to the point after which things become better.
example: The turning point of her life was when she found that she was pregnant.

definition: If you obtain something under false pretences, you deceive others by lying about your identity, qualifications, financial or social position, in order to get what you want.
example: Steve obtained the job under false pretences.

definition: This idiom refers to a person who makes a substantive, yet unrecognized contribution.
example: They are the unsung heroes of the Revolution.

definition: If you have a vested interest in a situation or event, you expect to benefit or gain an advantage from it.
example: I have a vested interest in this company. I hope to get a job in it.

definition: This expression means that if you don’t waste things, you will always have enough.
example: My motto? Waste not, want not.

definition: This idiom means to have more than one set of responsibilities or to hold more than one office.
example: The financial manager is currently responsible for marketing too. He is wearing more than one hat.

definition: This means to drink something alcoholic.
example: Would you like to join us tonight and wet your whistle?

definition: This idiom refers to a collection of money made by a group of people that is then given to a particular person or used to but a present for them.
example: We have a whip-round at work for people who are leaving. It’s the best way to say goodbye.

definition: A whiz kid is someone, usually young, who is very talented and successful at doing something.
example: The intern is whiz-kid from I’ve heard.

definition: It means believing that something that you want to happen is really happening or will happen, even though it is neither true nor likely.
example: I think the weather will be fine, but perhaps that’s just wishful thinking.

definition: This idiom refers to an attempt to blame and punish people who hold unpopular views and opinions, often under the guise of some other investigation.
example: Their witch hunt against the terrorists has sparked a civil war.

phrase: without so much as a by-your-leave
definition: This phrase means without asking for permission.
example: She walked in without so much as a by-your-leave and picked some books.

definition: This phrase is said when there will be trouble for someone or someone will be punished if they do a particular thing.
example: This is the second time she has been sent home, so woe betide her if it happens again!

definition: This phrase is said to express how unhappy you are.
example: I am cold and I have to walk all the way home. Woe is me!

definition: This idiom means that the work continues.
example: The highway is closed for repair. The work is in progress.

definition: Someone who deserves respect because they do their job well is a person who is worth their salt.
example: Any police officer worth their salt would have checked the papers carefully.

phrase: a place for everything and everything in its place
definition: This phrase is advisory in nature which talks about things being stacked neatly and should be put back in its place when one is not using that particular item.
example: He is a strict father and teaches his child to make a place for everything and have everything in its place.

phrase: a rose by any other name would smell as sweet
definition: This idiom means that what matters is what something is, not what it is called.
example: Here is your new BMW car. A rose by any other name would smell as sweet.

definition: This expression means that it is considered preferable to finish one’s work before going to relax and enjoy oneself.
example: I’d love to have dinner with you, but I’ve got a financial report to finish – business before pleasure!

phrase: children should be seen and not heard
definition: This is an old proverb suggesting that children should not impinge on the adult world.
example: I still believe that children should be seen and not heard.

phrase: do unto others as you would have them do unto you
definition: This expression means to treat people fairly. It is also known as “The Golden Rule”.
example: Then he said to his son: “Do unto others as you would have them do unto you”.

definition: This idiom means that an exchange of two things of equal value is a reasonable and honest trade.
example: What’s you problem? Fair exchange is no robbery!

definition: This idiom means that faith is immensely powerful.
example: Trust your skills! Faith will move mountains!

definition: This idiom means that life begins to be better in one’s middle age.
example: I’ve told you that life begins at forty!

definition: This was a wartime expression meaning “unguarded talk may give useful information to the enemy”.
example: Be careful what you speak in this city. Loose lips sink ships!

phrase: man doesn’t live by bread alone
definition: This phrase means that physical nourishment is not sufficient for a healthy life; man also has spiritual needs.
example: I like her very much. Man doesn’t live by bread alone…

definition: This idiom means to give equal shares to all.
example: The inheritance will be shared and shared alike.

definition: The survival of the fittest means that the most able or those best capable of adapting to particular conditions will survive.
example: Don’t forget the nature laws. It’s the survival of the fittest.

phrase: the best is yet to come
definition: This expression means that whatever is happening now will be surpassed by something better in the future.
example: I’m glad that you are enjoying this period. The best is yet to come!

phrase: the best things in life are free
definition: This idiom means that things that cost money should not be prioritized over free things like family and friends.
example: My daughter, don’t ever forget that the best things in life are free.

definition: This idiom refers to the unconventional or uninvestigated option.
example: To solve this problem, I think we should take the road less travelled.

phrase: the triumph of hope over experience
definition: This is a literal view of the subject of remarriage.
example: He still believes in the triumph of hope over experience.

definition: This idiom means that getting a good start is important.
example: I like the project introduction. Well begun is half done.

definition: This expression means that dirt and muddle are evidence of products being manufactured and money (brass) being made.
example: That time, the business was brisk – where there’s muck there’s brass.

definition: This idiom refers to work that still needs to be done.
example: After my holiday I returned to a backlog of work.

definition: This idiom refers to a situation in which someone cannot make a fair decision because they will be affected by the result.
example: I need to declare a conflict of interest here.

definition: Someone who has a lot at stake is in a risky situation, with a lot to be won or lost.
example: I was nervous about signing the contract because there was a lot at stake.

definition: This idiom refers to a situation in which danger or problems are barely avoided.
example: The man barely made it over the tracks before the train came. What a narrow escape!

definition: An argument or debate where people shout loudly at each other is called a shouting match.
example: The debate between the two politicians turned into a shouting match.

definition: A quick decision based on an impulse, without taking time to weigh the consequences, is called a snap decision.
example: I made a snap decision to go cycling.

definition: A person who acts as an informer, especially one who gives information to the police or the authorities, is called a stool pigeon.
example: I don’t trust her. I think she is a stool pigeon for the police.

definition: This idiom refers to a privileged or distinguished person.
example: All tall poppies were invited to raise charity.

definition: This phrase refers to something that is insignificant or worthless.
example: I wouldn’t give a tinker’s damn on it.

definition: If something is done “after the fact”, it’s done too late, after something has actually happened, especially a crime or an accident.
example: They realized that they had put people in danger, but that was of no help after the fact.

definition: If something happens ahead of time, it happens early, before the set time or with time to spare.
example: If you finish the project ahead of time, we’ll be able to go out.

definition: If you are allowed to do something after a check-up to make sure that everything is all right, you get the all clear.
example: Dad says he’s going to play football again as soon as he gets the all clear from his medical doctor.

definition: This phrase refers to everything or everyone is accounted for.
example: All present and correct, so we can start the meeting.

definition: This expression refers to something or someone that is full of verve, vivacity and liveliness.
example: They went home from the party all singing, all dancing.

definition: This expression means getting quite close to the end.
example: We’re almost there! Come on, we are approaching the finish line.

definition: This phrase refers to a stance, with the hands on the hips and elbows directed outwards.
example: She was waiting there, with her arms akimbo.

definition: This idiom refers to a person who is totally bald.
example: The Chemo Therapy has left her as bald as a coot.

definition: If something is as dark as pitch, it is extremely dark/black.
example: Her eyes were as dark as pitch.

definition: This simile means very fast.
example: The car moved as fast as greased lighting.

phrase: as fit as a butcher’s dog
definition: This simile means very fit.
example: I like that boy because he is as fit as a butcher’s dog.

phrase: as if to the manner born
definition: This phrase means “naturally at ease in a specified job or situation”.
example: Since he became famous he has begun to rub shoulders with the upper crust as if to the manner born.

phrase: as neat as a new pin
definition: If a place is as neat as a new pin, it is very neat, tidy and clean.
example: Their apartment was as neat as a new pin.

definition: This idiom refers to something that is extremely easy to understand.
example: Every new employee has to undergo an orientation course; it’s as simple as that.

definition: This idiom means not to be alert on opportunity.
example: The security guard fell asleep at the switch and thieves entered into the building.

definition: If you experience something yourself directly, without any intermediary, you experience it at first hand.
example: Seeing the football match at first hand is much better than watching it on television.

definition: When talking about the length of time or amount of money necessary to do something, at the outside indicates the highest estimate or the largest amount.
example: How long will it take to get there? Three hours at the outside.

phrase: at this late stage in the game
definition: This idiom means at this point.
example: There’s nothing I can do at this late stage in the game.

definition: When it is possible to do something at will, you can do it as and when you please, wherever and whenever you wish, without limit or restriction.
example: One day, I will be so rich that I might be able to travel the world at will.

definition: Saying that you have to go back to the salt mines is a humorous way of talking about returning to work, usually with some reluctance.
example: We got three days off at Easter and then it was back to the salt mines.

definition: This term refers to people who do important work but have no contact with the public.
example: Back-room boys don’t receive the credit they deserve for their work in our IT company.

definition: This expression literally means “with all one’s belongings”.
example: The landlord asked them to vacate the house, bag and baggage, in a week’s time.

definition: This idiom means to argue persistently.
example: I haven’t come here to bandy words with you Olive.

definition: This idiom refers to a general mayhem or a free-for-all fight.
example: This is a battle royal! May you win!

definition: This expression is a warning that something dangerous is imminent. In reality, this is usually said with comic intent. The thing being warned of is more likely to be mildly unwelcome than actually dangerous.
example: The librarian asked about your overdue books – be afraid, be very afraid.

phrase: be in a stew about / over something
definition: When someone is in a stew about something, they are worried and agitated.
example: Adrian is in a stew about his return on investment.

phrase: be of no use to man or beast
definition: This phrase means to be completely useless, to serve no purpose, to be unsuitable to anyone or anything.
example: This tool is of no use to man or beast.

definition: This idiom is an expression of excitement when seeing the object of one’s romantic affections.
example: She kissed me and I told myself, be still, my beating heart.

phrase: before one can say Jack Robinson
definition: This idiom means very suddenly.
example: She was gone before I could say Jack Robinson.

definition: This expression means to laugh uncontrollably.
example: I get belly laugh when I am talking with my cousin.

definition: This idiom refers to one’s best clothes.
example: She was wearing her best bib and tucker.

phrase: between you, me and the bed-post
definition: This phrase is used when divulging a secret; it refers to something that only the speaker and the listener should hear.
example: Between you, me and the bed-post I tell you that I don’t want to marry him.

definition: This idiom means to be undecided about something.
example: The little boy was betwixt and between which of his parents to choose during the divorce trial.

definition: This idiom means beyond our understanding.
example: We’re sorry but this issue is beyond our ken.

definition: This idiom refers to one who is here today and gone tomorrow.
example: She’s a true bird of passage. Don’t fall in love with her!

definition: This idiom refers to something which is difficult to accept.
example: The workers had to take the bitter medicine of a pay cut.

definition: If you say this regarding someone, it means that they are of superior quality or distinction, the best of a group.
example: A blue ribbon group of officers were demanded to investigate the murder.

definition: This phrase refers to a prize given to make fun of the loser in a contest or game.
example: She was given a booby prize.

definition: This phrase means having wide hips or buttocks.
example: That lady is quite broad in the beam.

definition: To say that someone is as brown as a berry means that they are very tanned.
example: Olivia came back from their holiday as brown as a berry.

definition: An unmitigated disaster is a complete failure or a total catastrophe.
example: The storm caused an unmitigated disaster.

definition: If you present someone with plain facts, without trying to embellish or soften the reality, you give them the unvarnished truth.
example: Tell me how it happened. I want the unvarnished truth.

phrase: wait for the cat to jump
definition: If you wait for the cat to jump, or wait to see which way the cat jumps, you delay taking action until you see how events will turn out.
example: Waiting for the cat to jump was the best thing we could do.

definition: If you are given your walking papers, your contract or a relationship has ended.
example: After causing the accident, I was given the walking papers.

definition: This idiom refers to the early hours of the morning, between twelve o’clock at night and the time when the sun rises.
example: I was up until the wee hours trying to finish the project.

definition: When people talk about where the shoe pinches, they are referring to an area that is often a source of problems or difficulties.
example: He thinks public transport system works fine, but he’ll find out where the shoe pinches soon.

definition: This idiom refers to a child or impertinent youth.
example: We can’t lose again! Let’s show those whipper snapper who we are!

definition: This expression refers to someone or something without order or control.
example: We have a wild and woolly love affair.

definition: This phrase means with all of one’s strength.
example: I will complete this mission with might and main.

definition: This idiom means to be able to hear something or someone.
example: She was within earshot when you started discussing her cooking abilities.

definition: A person who is wool-gathering is daydreaming and is not concentrating on what is happening.
example: She spent the whole day wool-gathering. She must be in love.

definition: This phrase is a disparaging response, indicating that something previously said was predictable, repetitive or tedious.
example: I had to listen to the usual yada yada about road safety.

definition: This idiom literally means “a long time back”.
example: I’ve been living in this house since the year dot.

definition: This idiom refers to someone especially a politician whose career is finished.
example: The officer is retiring next month. Soon enough, he will be a yesterday’s man.

definition: An obligation, commitment or restraint that becomes an oppressive burden is called a yoke around one’s neck.
example: When I lost my job, the loan became a yoke around my neck.

definition: If your memory serves you well, you remember correctly.
example: We’ve met this year, if my memory serves me well.

definition: This expression can either mean very high up in the sky or high on drugs or excitement.
example: She was ecstatic that she won the game. She was as high as a kite.

definition: Means you are utterly impressed by it.
example: The car exhibition blew me away.

definition:
This expression is used to show irritation, exasperation or anger.
said when you are annoyed, and to emphasize what you are saying:
example: For crying out loud, turn the volume down!

definition: To say that the heat is on means that you are under a lot of pressure to get something done, usually within a time limit.
example: The mission must be fulfilled until next Monday, so the heat is on.

definition: To say that something is in black and white means that there is written proof of it.
example: It’s an obligation you have to fulfill. It’s in black and white in your contract.

definition: This idiom means to exclude out something.
example: The new drug claimed to rule out the pain.

definition: If you say that a person, a process or an organised event is running out of steam, you mean that there is a loss of impetus, energy or enthusiasm.
example: The movement seems to be running out of steam.

definition: This expression is used to say that something seems logical or is as expected.
example: I’ll have to get a bicycle support after it arrives. That figures!

definition: This expression means that this is the latest unpleasant event and that you cannot tolerate the situation any longer.
example: Last night quarrel was the last straw for me.

definition: This idiom means to increase the demands or risks to obtain better results.
example: The protesters upped the ante by refusing to work until their demands were satisfied.

definition: If you jump the gun, you do something too soon or take premature action based on incomplete information.
example: She ordered a new house before the job was confirmed – now that’s jumping the gun!

definition: This idiom refers to making a lot of progress.
example: The stock market is on a roll at the moment. I need to invest soon.

definition: This idiom means to calm down and behave normally.
example: I’ve understood that you had a bad day, but please pull yourself together.

definition: If you blackmail somebody, you extort or take money from them by using their secret against them and threatening to reveal it to others.
example: I need help to stop that man because he has been blackmailing me for some time.

definition: To come out of one’s shell means to be less shy or more talkative and outgoing.
example: Gradually, the new students started to come out of their shells.

definition: If someone pulls no punches, they speak openly and honestly, holding nothing back.
example: The medical doctor pulled no punches. He explained in detail the risks of the operation.

definition: This expression refers to an act that unintentionally harms one’s own interests.
example: She scored an own goal by quitting her job.

definition: If you sell someone down the river, you betray a person who trusts you.
example: I have been sold down the river by her.

phrase: to go red in the face
definition: This expression means to become embarrassed.
example: I went red in the face when the manager scolded me.

definition: People who work the system learn how a state or public organisation works in order to benefit as much as possible from the system.
example: It took me some time to work the system in this country, but now we can start doing business.

definition: To say that money, time or energy has gone down the drain, means that it has been wasted or lost.
example: My years of marketing research went down the drain when the organisation was closed.

phrase: get the show on the road
definition: If you manage to put a plan or idea into action, you get the show on the road.
example: Ok, we have all the detailed we need. Let’s get the show on the road.

definition: This term refers to a discriminatory barrier perceived by women and minorities that prevents them from rising to positions of power or responsibility.
example: Olivia knew she would never break the glass ceiling and rise to a management position.

definition: not important to or not involved in a situation:
example: He used to be an important member of the team, but he's gradually drifted out of the picture.

phrase: a bigger bang for your buck
definition: This idiom means that you receive a better value for your money.
example: Those clothes are so cheap. You clearly get a bigger bang for your buck.

definition: If you bring the house down, you give a very successful performance.
example: If they sing like that on Monday, they will bring the house down.

phrase: jump / thrown in at the deep end
definition: If you jump or are thrown in at the deep end, you start doing something new and difficult without help or preparation.
example: She got a job as a saleswoman for which she had no training. She just had to jump in at the deep end.

definition: This idiom means to leave or abandon something that is not doing well.
example: I decided not to jump ship and try again.

definition: To say that something is nothing to write home about means that it is not of great interest or importance.
example: She has done a couple of projects, but nothing to write home about.

definition: This expression means “in a planned way and without pity or other emotion”.
example: One young woman was shot dead in cold blood.

phrase: jump at something (a chance or opportunity)
definition: This expression means to seize the opportunity to do something.
example: I jumped at the chance to do an internship with Apple.

phrase: keep / hold your cards close to your chest
definition: This expression means to be secretive or cautious or to give nothing away.
example: I like to keep my card close to my chest.

definition: This idiom means to spend time talking useless things.
example: Instead of shooting the breeze, they should get to work.

definition: This idiom means to be the most remarkable or foolish of its kind.
example: He won every match. He will take the cake.

definition: If you need to tighten your belt, you must spend less money or be careful how you spend it because there is less available.
example: Another car problem? I’ll have to tighten my belt this month!

definition: This idiom means to criticize someone behind their back.
example: No one wants to hire someone who bad mouths people.

definition: If something takes place so suddenly that you don’t have time to become aware of it, it happens “before you know it” or “before you know where you are”.
example: The doorbell rang and, before we knew it, a surprise party was under way.

definition: This idiom refers to a man pursuing women.
example: Steve is a sex addict. He is always chasing tail.

definition: This expression refers to a homeless or penniless person.
example: After losing her job, she was left down and out.

definition: To refer to something as out of this world means that you think it is extremely good or impressive.
example: I liked that restaurant. The food was out of this world.

definition: This idiom means to provide active aid to someone.
example: The local politician is a sitting shotgun for his sister’s company.

definition: If you have your back to the wall, you are in serious difficulty with very few options available.
example: With her back to the wall, the businesswoman had to accept the deal

definition: If something is in the pipeline, it is currently in progress or being organised.
example: A new TV show is in the pipeline at the moment.

definition: People say this when they are surprised to meet someone familiar in an unexpected place.
example: I never expected to meet her in Berlin. It’s a small world indeed.

definition: If you miss the boat, you fail to take advantage of an opportunity because you don’t act quickly enough.
example: I managed to get my order through before the end of the promotion but I nearly miss the boat.

definition: This phrase means to pass the critical point and start to improve.
example: After five months of poor sales we’ve finally turned the corner.

definition: This idiom refers to an exact duplicate.
example: Steve can’t tell the twins apart. They are dead ringers of each other.

definition: This idiom refers to a further, later or unspecified point.
example: The leaders thought that military action was a long way down the line.

definition: This idiom means to go to extreme lengths to get something done or to please someone.
example: It was a period when I jumped through hoops for her.

definition: If you nip a problem or an unacceptable situation in the bud, you stop it at an early stage, before it develops or becomes worse.
example: She wanted to be a police officer, but her parents soon nipped that idea in the bud.

definition: Something which is on the house is offered free of charge.
example: The owner of the bar offered them a drink on the house.

definition: When people raise the roof, they make a lot of noise by cheering, shouting, whistling or clapping their hands.
example: The party was such a success – the participants raised the roof.

definition: This expression is often used by parents or people in authority to indicate that the situation is not amusing at all.
example: This is an intricate mission so wipe that smile off your face!

definition: To say that something was a breeze means that it was very easy or that everything went smoothly.
example: The interview was a breeze – scarcely 13 minutes and I got the job!

definition: If you say that “all hell broke loose”, you mean that there was a sudden angry or noisy reaction to something.
example: All hell broke loose when the manager announced that the business was going to close down.

phrase: by the skin of your teeth
definition: To do something by the skin of our teeth means that you just manage to do it, but that you almost fail.
example: I passed the driving test by the skin of my teeth.

definition: to tell the truth about something that you have been keeping secret:
example:
come clean with:
I thought it was time to come clean with everybody.
come clean about:
I thought it was timeto come clean about what I'd been doing.

definition: If someone tells you to give it a rest, they are asking you to stop doing something such as complaining or talking continuously.
example: It’s the ninth time I’ve heard this story. Give it a rest!

definition: If something hits the spot, it is exactly what is needed or wanted.
example: On such a hot day, a couple of beers would really hit the spot!

definition: To keep your head above water means to try to survive by staying out of debt, for example a small business.
example: This year business has been slow. I barely managed to keep my head above water.

definition: This expression is used to describe the person that you envision spending your future with.
example: She wishes that she could meet Mr. Right.

definition: This idiom means to be updated, to not be behind, to have all the current information.
example: I’m going to bring you up to speed with the latest developments.

definition: This idiom means to clash with another person on a particular issue.
example: We are always bumping heads with each other.

definition: This idiom means to dance in a stylish way.
example: These new cheerleaders are amazing – they are busting some moves.

phrase: give a piece of your mind
definition: If you tell someone exactly what you think in a very angry manner, you give them a piece of your mind.
example: I was so irritated by her remarks that I decided to give her a piece of my mind.

definition: If something leaves you in the lurch, it leaves you in a difficult or embarrassing situation.
example: When she missed the last train, she was left in the lurch.

phrase: not have a leg to stand on
definition: To say that someone doesn’t have a leg to stand on means that they can’t prove what they say.
example: Two women testified against him. He didn’t have a leg to stand on.

phrase: scrape the bottom of the barrel
definition: If you scrape the bottom of the barrel, you use the worst or the least satisfactory ideas, things or people because you have no choice.
example: When they started to recruit, they had to scrape the bottom of the barrel because the salary was low.

definition: A very successful performance in music, films, theatre etc., is called a smash hit.
example: Their last movie was a smash hit.

definition: If you spill the beans, you reveal a secret or talk about something private.
example: Come on! Spill the beans! What did she say?

definition: This idiom means to take action in response to an opportunity or crisis.
example: We have to step up to the plate and make the most of this mission.

definition: This idiom means to lose a considerable amount of money or to get punished for something not done right.
example: The younger sibling never takes a beating.

definition: A person who is as cool as a cucumber is not anxious, but relaxed and non-emotional.
example: His mother stayed as cool as a cucumber all through the ceremony.

phrase: be on its knees / bring to its knees
definition: When a country or organisation is on its knees or is brought to its knees, it is in a very weak situation.
example: The civil war brought Syria to its knees.

definition: This phrase means to greatly or specifically irritate or annoy someone.
example: It really grinds my gears when they go zipping through red lights!

definition: The term means a very small amount or almost nothing.
example: My red shirt didn’t cost much. I bought it for next to nothing.

definition: This expression means to go public about something private or hidden.
example: She was in her late teens when she came out of the closet.

definition: This idiom means to realize or understand something.
example: After his terrible grade in economics, the student saw the light and started working harder.

definition: If you talk about the big picture, you refer to the overall situation, or the project as a whole rather than the details.
example: While each aspect is extremely important, please try not to miss the big picture.

definition: This idiom may refer to something deposited on a beach by the tide or to something finished and failed, with no further chance of success.
example: 1. There’s a whale washed up on the beach. 2. She was a great actress before she started to drink. Now she’s all washed up.

phrase: bang your head against a brick wall
definition: If you bang or knock your head against a brick wall, you continue vainly to try to achieve something in spite of several unsuccessful attempts.
example: I’ve been banging my head against a brick wall trying to explain the study to her.

definition: If you decide to draw the line, you determine when an activity or situation becomes unacceptable.
example: When one’s private life is concerned, the news agencies should know where to draw the line!

definition: This idiom means to watch for danger or threats to oneself.
example: Ben is always looking over his shoulder.

definition: If you claim that someone has said something or suggest what they should say, you are putting words in their mouth.
example: Stop putting words in my mouth! I didn’t say that!

definition: A red herring is a fact or argument introduced into a discussion which draws attention away from the main point.
example: Procedures are a red herring. The crisis is important at this moment.

definition: If you set the stage for an event or a development, you create conditions that allow it to happen.
example: The agreement set the stage for our business relations.

definition: This idiom means to be very sick, with the flu or a cold.
example: I don’t feel good at all. I’m as sick as a dog.

definition: If you call something a white elephant, you consider it useless although it may have cost a lot of money.
example: The new council building is a white elephant.

definition: If you say that you could eat a horse you mean that you are very hungry.
example: I’m starving! Let’s get something to eat! I could eat a horse right now!

definition: This expression refers to a minor car accident. There is little damage and no injuries.
example: That fender bender caused a major traffic jam in the city.

definition: If you get worked up about something, you become upset, annoyed or excited, often unnecessarily.
example: Tomorrow it’s my first day at the office and I’m all worked up about it.

definition: If someone goes off on a tangent, they change the subject completely in the middle of a speech or conversation.
example: It’s difficult to speak a subject in detail to her. She usually goes off on a tangent.

phrase: kick the can down the road
definition: This expression means to postpone dealing with something in the hope that it becomes someone else’s problem.
example: You can’t continue to kick the can down the road. She needs to know the truth.

definition: If something speaks volumes, it expresses a reaction or opinion very clearly, with no need for words.
example: Her smile when she opened the gift spoke volumes about my choice.

definition: If a business or a project is up and running, it has started and is fully operational.
example: Finally, the local store is up and running.

definition: A sitting dusk is an easy target, a person who is easy to deceive.
example: The man was a sitting duck for the enemy. He had to move briskly.

definition: This idiom means to be in a tough situation with limited options.
example: The company has its back against the wall.

definition: If something is beyond your wildest dreams, it is better than you imagined or hoped for.
example: The student received a grant from the university, which was beyond his wildest dreams.

definition: If someone jumps down another person’s throat, they suddenly start shouting at them in a very angry manner.
example: When I said the things weren’t clear, the manager jumped down my throat.

definition: If you have no hard feelings, you feel no resentment or bitterness about something.
example: After she had been promoted, she said to Mary: no hard feelings, I hope.

definition: If you refer to somebody as a pain in the neck, you think they are very irritating.
example: Steve is a pain in the neck the way he is forever complaining!

definition: To refer to something as a piece of cake means that you consider it to be very easy.
example: The Spanish test was a piece of cake!

definition: To say that two people are as thick as thieves means that they are very close friends who are very loyal to each other.
example: She always takes Maria’s side. They are as thick as thieves.

phrase: at the drop of a hat
definition: If you do something at the drop of a hat, you do it immediately and without hesitation.
example: I’m ready to help you at the drop of a hat.

phrase: have your cake and eat it
definition: To say that someone wants to have their cake and eat it means that they want the advantages of two alternative situations when only one is possible.
example: She enjoys her comfort but is also complaining about the cost of things. She can’t have her cake and eat it.

definition: This phrase means to allow a situation to become calm or normal again after something exciting or unusual has happened.
example: I suggest that we let the dust settle before we decide what to do.

definition: Somebody who has had one too many has drunk too much alcohol.
example: I think she has had one too many.

definition: The term refers to a potentially disastrous situation, often caused by negligence or insufficient precaution.
example: She said that in many respects, the tragedy was an accident waiting to happen.

definition: This idiom refers to the condition where extreme fear or nervousness causes a person to feel a chill along with moist skin or sweat.
example: I woke up from a nightmare in cold sweat.

definition: This expression refers to a situation where two bad things happen at the same time.
example: She left me and I lost my wallet too. Quite a double whammy, isn’t it?

phrase: Stand/stick out like a sore thumb
definition: If something sticks out like a sore thumb, it is very obvious or visible in an unpleasant way.
example: The old house sticks out like a sore thumb among the modern buildings.

definition: to do something which is useless, unnecessary and has no chance of success.
example: It was a fool’s errand to look for a dentist’s in that isolated area.

definition: This idiom literally means to be exact; to be correct; to be proper.
example: The documentary was bang on the subject.

definition: When something causes a plan, project or venture to collapse or fail, the bottom falls out of it.
example: When rain was forecasted, the bottom fell out of our plans for a beach party.

definition: If you dodge a bullet, you narrowly avoid a very serious problem or a disaster.
example: I certainly dodged a bullet when I missed the bus. It crashed completely soon after.

definition: If you keep your fingers crossed, you hope that something will be successful.
example: I’m sitting in for the final exam tomorrow. Keep your fingers crossed for me.

definition: This idiom means to do what is the best course of action in the given situation
example: - we need to book a flight before it's too late- Don't worry, I'm on the case

phrase: Give someone a taste of their own medicine
definition: If you give someone a taste of their own medicine, you treat them in the same unpleasant way that they have treated you.
example: I have given her a taste of her own medicine and she didn’t like it.

definition: This idioms refers mainly to the workplace. It means that as a group you all get on well together and things seem to run very smoothly.
example: Last month our company was like a well-oiled machine. Thank you all for that!

definition: This expression refers to distance measured in a straight line.
example: It’s three miles from here to the petrol station as the crow flies.

definition: If someone goes through the roof, they become very angry.
example: I went through the roof when I saw her with another man.

definition: This idiom literally means “feeling or exhibiting great resentment”.
example: After waiting an hour, he drove off in high dudgeon.

phrase: time flies when you’re having fun
definition: This idiom means that you don’t notice how long something lasts when it’s fun.
example: Look how late it is. Time flies when you’re having fun!

definition: If you are stumped, you are unable to proceed, often regarding being confounded by some intellectual puzzle.
example: I will speak to you later. Now I’m stumped.

definition: Someone who is wet behind the ears is inexperienced or immature.
example: I wouldn’t give that job to her. She’s still wet behind the ears.

definition: When a situation gets out of control and everything starts to go wrong, the wheels fall off.
example: The wheels fell off his career when he started taking drugs.

definition: If you are beside yourself (with an emotion), you lose your self-control because of the intensity of the emotion you are feeling.
example: Samuel was beside himself with grief when he lost his dog.

definition: If you egg someone on, you urge or strongly encourage them to do something.
example: She doesn’t want to learn German but I keep egging her on!

definition: A period of unnatural calm before a difficult time or violent activity is called the lull before the storm.
example: Honestly, I think this is the lull before the storm.

definition: If you say that someone has made a killing, you mean that they have had great financial success.
example: Mike made a killing on the stock market last year.

definition: If you are paid peanuts, you have a very low salary.
example: There was a time in my life when I was paid peanuts.

definition: This is a rhetorical question, suggesting that what is being spoken of is without fault.
example: This car is perfect for your needs. What’s not to like?

definition: A sarcastic retort about something that most likely will not happen.
example: - I might win the big prize. - Oh, you wish!

definition: An action or remark described as below the belt is considered to be unfair or cruel.
example: Politicians often use personal information to hit their rivals below the belt.

definition: If you do something “day in, day out”, you do it every day without fail over a long period of time.
example: I go for a 30-minute running after work day in, day out.

definition: This expression is used to indicate that you completely understand the situation and you do not need any further details.
example: Did your wife arrive unexpectedly last night? Enough said!

definition: This idiom refers to a happy simplistic ending to a story, similar to those found in fairy tales.
example: Fairytale endings don’t match real life.

definition: A person who gets the picture understands what is being explained or described.
example: He fired the gun and people started running everywhere – you get the picture.

phrase: in a world of your own
definition: If you are in a world of your own, you are so preoccupied by your own concerns that you are unaware of what is happening around you.
example: Marry is in the garden in a world of her own.

definition: If you lash out at somebody, you attack them, usually verbally.
example: He suddenly lashed out at her and blamed her for cheating.

definition: To say that someone or something goes, runs or behaves like clockwork means that everything happens exactly as expected.
example: I am impressed. In their company everything works like clockwork.

definition: This idiom means to make a lot of money.
example: This is the best period. I’m making paper!

definition: This expression means to receive or express praise for a job well done.
example: She received a pat on the back from her boss.

definition: This phrase refers to a straightforward task that can easily be accomplished.
example: Beating this game is a piece of piss.

definition: If you refer to a plan or idea as a recipe for disaster, you think it is likely to produce bad results.
example: Our children together for Christmas? Sounds like a recipe for disaster.

definition: If someone toes the line, they obey the rules and accept the principles laid down by a person, group or organisation.
example: If you want to stay in this company, you’ll have to toe the line.

definition: This expression means to ask someone to do something for you or for a favour that is difficult, time consuming or inconvenient for the person you’re asking.
example: I know it’s a big ask, but is there any chance you could borrow me $10.000?

definition: This idiom means to begin to eat.
example: I know you are all hungry, so chow down.

definition: If you accept as certain that you will not get something that you want, you kiss goodbye to it.
example: There will be no substantial bonus this year, so I can kiss goodbye to the laptop I wanted.

definition: This idiom refers to a notional place characterized by fantasy, self-absorption and blissful lack of touch with reality.
example: I do worry about Peter sometimes. I try and have a conversation with him but he’s away in la-la land

definition: When faced with a choice, a person who is on the fence has not yet reached a decision.
example: I like her, but getting married to her… That’s still on the fence!

definition: If you pull someone’s leg, you tease them by telling them something that is not true.
example: Of course I’m not going to buy her a house. I was just pulling your leg.

definition: To say “let’s call it a day” is a way of suggesting that it is time to stop doing something for the rest of that day, whether or not the work or activity has been completed, usually because of tiredness.
example: After another solved case, I decide to call it a day.

definition: The term eager beaver refers to a person who is hardworking and enthusiastic, sometimes considered overzealous.
example: The new employee works way too much. She’s an eager beaver.

definition: This idiom refers to a scapegoat.
example: I don’t want to be your fall guy.

definition: This idiom means to do things strictly according to the written rules.
example: The most successful officers are not those who always go by the book.

phrase: make somebody an offer he / she can’t refuse
definition: This idiom means that the person has two choices: to accept the offer or to be killed.
example: Don’t worry about it. I have the power to make her an offer she can’t refuse.

definition: This phrase is used to indicate that a mistake or instance of misconduct should be excused because it has not caused damage.
example: It was trespassing, but no harm, no foul.

definition: This is a humorous way of referring to someone who is an accountant or who is very good at working with numbers and calculations.
example: Mary’s a number cruncher who understands our financial situation.

definition: If you steal someone’s thunder you take their idea or plan and draw attention and praise away from them by presenting it first.
example: She has developed a plan to reduce marketing costs but the manager stole her thunder.

definition: If you say “cut it out” to someone, you tell them to stop doing something.
example: I’ve had enough of your allegations. Cut it out!

definition: Someone who is two-faced is deceitful or insincere; they will say one thing to your face and something else when you are not there.
example: I don’t trust Mona. I find her two-faced.

definition: This idiom refers to an act of believing something that is not easily believed.
example: It took a big leap of faith to quit my job.

definition: Someone who is a happy camper is generally content or satisfied with what is happening in their lives and has no complaints.
example: With my new job and my new motorbike, I am a happy camper.

definition: If something is in limbo, it is in an uncertain situation, over which you have no control.
example: We are in limbo until the new manager arrives.

definition: This is a term used to describe a moment when something that was once great has reached a point where it will decline in quality and popularity.
example: That TV series has clearly jumped off the shark.

phrase: let the cat out of the bag
definition: If you let the cat out of the bag, you reveal a secret, generally not intentionally.
example: When she told her cousin about the weekend plans, she let the cat out of the bag.

definition: If you have other/bigger fish to fry, you have more important things to do.
example: I won’t attend the office party. I have other fish to fry.

definition: This idiom refers to a margin that is too close to determine a winner.
example: This match is too close to call, but I trust that my team will win.

definition: describes a person who uses clever, complex, or shady methods to get an advantage or make a profit. The term often appears in Cambridge Dictionary to describe people who bend the rules in business or politics
example: There has been a lot of wheeling and dealing this year due to election campaign.

definition: This expression refers to giving someone recognition for trying hard to do something even though they may not be successful.
example: He definitely deserves an A for effort.

definition: The black sheep is one who behaves very differently or badly, and is considered disreputable by the other members of the family.
example: He was the black sheep of the family.

definition: This idiom means to understand something by piecing together hints or other bits of information.
example: Once I started to connect the dots I realized how wrong I was.

definition: To say that the dust has settled means that the situation has become calmer after a series of unpleasant or chaotic events.
example: The dust has finally settled. We can act now.

definition: If you eat your words, you have to admit that what you said before was wrong.
example: After saying that dreadful things to her, I had to eat my words.

definition: If something is in the works, it is currently being prepared or planned.
example: Updates for the website are in the works.

phrase: on the edge of one’s seat
