definition: Someone who is on the edge of their seat is very interested in something and finds it both extremely exciting and nerve-wracking.
example: Look at him! He’s on the edge of his seat watching that football match.

definition: This idiom means not as good as another.
example: The boy really wanted to date her, even though he knew she was out of his league.

definition: Someone who picks a fight deliberately looks for an opportunity to start a quarrel or begin an argument.
example: Some people were teasing her, trying to pick a fight.

definition: This idiom refer to the online dating app Tinder. It indicates that one finds someone attractive or unattractive by moving one’s finger to the right or left across an image of them on a touchscreen.
example: I like her, so I swipe right.

definition: If something, such as a plan or decision, is up in the air, it has not been decided or settled yet.
example: I don’t know what to say. The project is still up in the air.

definition: Someone who is a “barrel of laughs” is very funny or entertaining.
example: Let’s invite her to our party. She’s such a barrel of laughs!

phrase: cross that bridge when we come to it
definition: This is another way of saying “we will deal with that problem when it occurs and not worry about it before”.
example: My dear, what will happen if we can’t pay the loan? Oh, John. We will cross that bridge when we come to it.

definition: This idiom has two meanings. It may mean to adjust a device so as to reduce sound or temperature or it may mean to reduce one’s emotional reaction to something.
example: 1. Can you dial down the thermostat? 2. I know your favourite didn’t win the contest, but it’s time to dial down.

phrase: don’t give up the day job
definition: This idiom is used as a humorous way of recommending somebody not to pursue something at which they are unlikely to be successful.
example: Don’t give up the day job, Mike. This is not for you.

definition: If you say that someone got a raw deal, you think they were treated unfairly or badly.
example: I don’t like that company at all. You got a raw deal when you worked for them.

definition: If you blow a fuse, you suddenly lose your temper and become very angry.
example: She blew a fuse yesterday when she discovered that her phone had been stolen.

definition: When a furious person blows a gasket, they explode with anger.
example: When the shop was burgled for the fourth time, the administrator blew a gasket.

definition: This idiom means to deal with every part of a situation or activity.
example: I think I have covered all the bases of this problem.

definition: If you go ape, you go crazy.
example: She will go ape if she should hear that he has cheated on her.

phrase: hit it out of the park
definition: This idiom means to have enormous success.
example: I’ve really hit it out of the park with this idea!

definition: This expression is used to describe a sudden moment of inspiration, comprehension or realization.
example: I had a light-bulb moment when I realized what was wrong with the watch.

definition: If you say that your lips are sealed, you promise not to reveal a secret.
example: You can easily trust me. My lips are sealed!

definition: This idiom means to stop being able to control your emotions and suddenly start to shout, cry or laugh.
example: Ignore him. He has lost it.

definition: This idiom means crazy, out of one’s mind.
example: Don’t mind him. He’s off his rocker.

definition: This expression means that to dress up something unappealing, in a vain attempt to make it look better, is like putting lipstick on a pig.
example: Flowers on that house premises would be like putting lipstick on a pig.

definition: If something rings a bell, it is vaguely familiar to you, but you can’t remember the exact details.
example: Daniel Smith? The name rings a bell but I don’t remember him.

definition: This idiom refers to a situation when everyone is facing the same challenges.
example: This company will merge with another and some of us will be fired. We are all in the same boat.

definition: This expression is used to describe something that is badly bruised.
example: His face was black and blue after the boxing match.

phrase: go down like a lead balloon
definition: This idiom means to be received badly by an audience.
example: My joke went down like a lead balloon.

definition: If someone asks you to keep them posted, they want you to keep them informed about a situation.
example: She promised to keep us posted on the stage of the construction.

definition: If a person is out like a light, they are so tired that they fall asleep very quickly.
example: It was a tiresome day. As soon as my head touched the pillow, I was out like a light.

definition: This idiom is said by someone who has experience of a situation.
example: You don’t need to show me how to do it. This ain’t my first rodeo.

phrase: at the end of somebody’s rope
definition: This idiom means to have no more patience or strength.
example: I’m at the end of my rope with these children.

definition: If you do something wrong and manage to get off the hook, you avoid punishment or blame.
example: I ran a red light but I got off the hook. The policeman was a friend of mine.

definition: Someone who doesn’t lift a finger makes no effort to help or provide assistance when it is needed.
example: Many people saw the accident but none of them lifted a finger.

definition: This idiom refers to a performer or act, usually a singer or band, who has just one popular success.
example: It was just an one-hit wonder.

definition: When you recharge your batteries, you take a break from a tiring or stressful activity in order to relax and recover your energy.
example: She needs a holiday to recharge her batteries.

definition: To say that two people are an item means that they are involved in a romantic relationship.
example: So Dave and Nicole are an item, are they?

definition: This expression refers to something that can easily be broken or crumble by itself.
example: The police brought the illegal business down like a house of cards.

definition: This idiom refers to a good invention, innovation, idea or plan.
example: This laptop is the best thing since sliced bread.

definition: This means to exaggerate or say things that aren’t true to make you seem better or more knowledgeable than in reality.
example: She’s blowing smoke. I don’t think that she has read the project.

definition: If you cry your eyes out, you cry a lot and for a long time.
example: My girlfriend cried her eyes out when I told her the truth.

definition: If something, such as a television programme or a film production is dumbed down, it is deliberately made less intelligent or less demanding in order to attract a larger audience.
example: I strongly think that they are dumbing down their programmes so as to increase ratings.

definition: When something goes downhill, it deteriorates or gets worse little by little.
example: My grandfather’s health is going downhill, unfortunately.

definition: This is another way of saying “not a problem”.
example: Thank you for helping me! No sweat!

definition: This idiom refers to the tense, final stages of a competition.
example: It’s squeaky-bum time and he’s so depressed. His favourite team is losing the game.

phrase: take the bull by the horns
definition: This expression means that a person decides to act decisively in order to deal with a difficult situation or problem.
example: The bar owner took the bull by the horns and called the police.

definition: If you take the easy way out, you choose the easiest way to deal with a difficult situation, even if it is not the best solution.
example: She took the easy way out and cancelled her appointment.

definition: This idiom refers to something similar to other things of the same type, especially in a way that shows little imagination.
example: This is a neighbour of cookie-cutter houses.

definition: If something has gone down the pan, it is wasted and unrecoverable.
example: Unfortunately, their house has gone down the pan.

definition: This idiom means to explain something in a very clear way with details.
example: They have refused to spell out their plans so far.

definition: A poker term which means an advantage or resource kept hidden until needed.
example: She clearly has an ace in the hole that will ensure victory … you’ll see!

definition: This expression means a lot or to a great extent. It’s used to emphasise an action.
example: You owe me big time for this favour.

definition: To say that somebody pulls their weight means that they do their fair share of the work.
example: It’s a pleasure to work with them. They always pull their weight.

definition: This expression refers to an exhausting and repetitive routine, a hectic struggle for success.
example: I am tired of the rat race. Next year I will retire and move to the country.

definition: When a person shows their true colours, their behaviour reveals their real nature, with their qualities and/or weaknesses.
example: In times of crisis he shows his true colours.

definition:
This expression indicates agreement with what has just been said.
something that you say to tell someone that you are in the same unpleasantsituation, or have the same negativefeelings as them:
example: - I find the speech rather mundane- That makes two of us!

definition: This idiom means to do something in order to be allowed more time.
example: We need to do something so as to buy us some time.

definition: If someone pulls strings, they use influential friends in order to obtain an advantage.
example: I can help you by pulling some strings. Don’t worry too much.

definition: If someone is sent on a wild goose chase, they waste their time looking for something that there is little chance of finding.
example: I tried to find out who sent the anonymous letters, but it was a wild goose chase.

definition: This expression is used to give someone permission to do something.
example: If you’d like to use my smartphone, be my guest.

definition: This idiom refers to a list of things you plan to do before you die.
example: I’ve always wanted to go to Hawaii. I will add that to my bucket list.

phrase: can’t see the forest for the trees
definition: This phrase means that one cannot see, understand or focus on a situation in its entirety due to being preoccupied with minor details.
example: Let’s move on. You can’t see the forest for the trees!

definition: Someone who is down to earth is not a dreamer but a realistic and practical person who has sensible reactions and expectations.
example: You can always count on his advice. He’s a down to earth man.

definition: If something amazes you, it knocks your socks off.
example: This project will knock the socks off everyone in the office.

definition: Someone who is referred to as a loose cannon cannot be completely trusted because of unpredictable and irresponsible behaviour which can cause trouble.
example: Keep an eye on her. She turns into a loose cannon when she has a few drinks.

definition: To say that someone’s attitude is sour grapes means that they are trying to make others believe that something they cannot have is of no importance.
example: When she failed in obtaining the job, she said she wasn’t that interested in it, but that’s just sour grapes!

definition: To say that the jury is still out means that something is under consideration but no decision has been reached yet.
example: The jury is still out as concerns the location of the new mall.

phrase: between a rock and a hard place
definition: This idiom means between two unwelcome options.
example: These are not good choices – I’m between a rock and a hard place.

definition: This expression refers to an open-handed slap in the face intended to be humiliating.
example: Bitch-slapping is what he needs after doing that horrible thing to you.

definition: This idiom means that family loyalties are stronger than those to other people.
example: It was just me and his niece in the interview. I had no chance, blood is thicker than water.

definition: A general atmosphere of pessimism and a feeling that the situation is not going to improve, is referred to as doom and gloom.
example: Unfortunately, it’s doom and gloom for all businesses nowadays.

definition: A situation in which a lot of people attack, pursue or compete with each other in an excited or frantic way, because they all want to obtain something, is called a feeding frenzy.
example: As soon as the investment plan was approved, there was a feeding frenzy among companies to obtain contracts.

definition: This expression refers to a crime committed by or with the help of someone living or working in the place that it took place.
example: The police officers concluded that it had been an inside job.

definition: If you put a project or issue on the back burner, you decide to deal with it at a later date because you do not consider it to be that urgent or important.
example: When Jasmine was offered a promotion she put her college plans on the back burner.

definition: If you are over the moon about something, you are very happy about it.
example: After I heard the results I was over the moon.

definition: If you sail through something, for example a test or an exam, you succeed in doing it without difficulty.
example: The English test was no problem for me. I sailed through it.

phrase: stuck / caught in a time warp
definition: Something that has not changed at all from some time in the past, when everything else has, is caught or stuck in a time warp.
example: This building seems to be stuck in a time warp.

definition: This expression means that the third try is often successful.
example: This time you will be successful! Don’t forget – third time’s the charm!

definition: Originating as a humorous comment about one’s hair being unmanageable, this term had broadened to mean “a day when everything seems to go wrong”.
example: Hey! What’s wrong with you? Are you having a bad hair day?

definition: This idiom refers to a very tasty food or meal.
example: The pizza that you’ve cooked is finger licking good.

definition: This means that you decide not to marry someone just before the wedding.
example: Are you going to leave John at the altar?

definition: If someone has a screw loose, their behaviour is strange and they appear slightly mad.
example: The man wears a fur coat in the summer – I think he has a screw loose!

definition: If you tell someone to hold their horses, you think they are doing something too fast and should slow down and not rush into further action.
example: Hold your horses! We need to get her approval first.

phrase: keep one’s eye on / take one’s eye off the ball
definition: This expression means to keep (or fail to keep) your attention focused on the matter at hand.
example: I must keep my eye on the ball all the time because I want my business to succeed.

definition: If you speak frankly and make something very clear, you lay it on the line.
example: The manager laid it on the line and told Mary that she had made a mistake.

definition: If you lie through your teeth, you lie openly and brazenly, knowing that what you are saying is completely false.
example: If she denies it, she’ll be lying through her teeth. I saw her when she did it!

definition: Telling someone to mind their own business is a rude way of saying that they are too interested in what others are doing.
example: Don’t tell me what to do! Mind your own business!

definition: This idiom means to be in a hurry or to be leaving a place in a rush.
example: They zoomed off and lived happily for ever.

definition: This idiom refers to an obsessive and dangerous female, in pursuit of a lover who has spurned her.
example: Now she’s a bunny boiler.

definition: If you crack someone up, you make them laugh.
example: She’s hilarious. She cracks me up.

definition: To cry wolf is to call for help when you are not really in danger. As a result, nobody believes you when you really need help.
example: There’s John screaming again! Does he really have a problem or is he just crying wolf again?

definition: If you eat, sleep and breathe something, you are so enthusiastic and passionate about it that you think about it constantly.
example: I’m an enthusiastic fisherman; I eat, sleep and breathe it!

definition: This expression means to deliberately ignore someone.
example: After expressing my opinion, she gave me the cold shoulder.

phrase: have your work cut out for you
definition: If you have to face a difficult task or a challenging situation, you have your work cut out for you.
example: I’ve got two months to reorganize the company. I have my work cut out for me.

definition: If someone tells you to make it snappy, they are asking you very sharply to hurry up or be quick about something.
example: Fill out the document and make it snappy.

definition: If you suggest that a subject be taken offline (during a meeting for example), you consider that it is a separate issue and should be discussed at another time.
example: Maria, you are confusing things. Let’s take that issue offline for now.

definition: If you drop the ball, you make a mistake and disappoint everyone.
example: Unfortunately, today I’ve dropped the ball in the negotiations.

definition: This expression means to keep something away.
example: Why do you keep the new car at bay?

definition: This expression means to take it easy.
example: Just lighten up! Everything will be fine.

phrase: like a bat out of hell
definition: This expression means very fast and crazily.
example: I saw him driving like a bat out of hell.

definition: This idiom is used when an attempt fails and it’s time to start all over.
example: I missed this objective. Let’s go back to the drawing board.

definition: The expression is used to indicate that the speaker is familiar with the situation mentioned. It can also refer to an attitude which reflects a certain boredom at the idea of repeating an experience that has lost its novelty.
example: Her suggestions produced a “been there, done that” attitude which undermined my enthusiasm.

definition: If someone has a chip on their shoulder, they feel resentful because they feel they are being treated unfairly, especially because of their background, their sex or their colour.
example: She’s got a chip on her shoulder because she’s from a low-class family.

definition: Cutting corners means not following the correct procedure in order to save time, effort or money (often with unsatisfactory results).
example: I want the mission well done – no cutting corners this time!

phrase: don’t beat around the bush / stop beating around the bush
definition: The expression is used to tell someone to say what they have to say, clearly and directly, even if it is unpleasant.
example: Stop beating around the bush! Just tell me what has been decided in that meeting.

definition: If you tell someone to fire away, you encourage them to begin to talk or ask question.
example: I know you have questions. Fire away!

definition: This expression means to end or fail suddenly and spectacularly.
example: Our project went down in flames when we ran out of funds.

definition: If someone is kept or left in the dark about something, they are not informed about it.
example: The officer was kept in the dark about the transfer until the last minute.

definition: If you put someone on the spot, you put them in an uncomfortable position, for example by asking difficult questions which they cannot avoid.
example: The police officer was put on the spot when the criminal pointed a knife at him.

definition: This is a rude way to tell someone to be quiet.
example: Shut your pie hole and mind your business!

definition: If you water down something such as a report, declaration or proposal, you try to make it weaker or less likely to cause anger.
example: I tried to water down her negative feedback.

definition: If you use this term in an explanation or discussion, you refer to the most essential point or the conclusion reached.
example: The bottom line is that the marketing plan needs to be changed.

phrase: cut class / play hooky / skip class
definition: Each of these expressions means to play truant.
example: She has cut class again today.

definition: This idiom means to be fired.
example: I’m not going to get the boot if the manager finds out about the mistake.

phrase: hit the nail on the head
definition: When you hit the nail on the head, you are absolutely right about something or have guessed the exact nature of a problem or situation.
example: You hit the nail on the head when you said that she had lost her job.

definition: To keep one’s eyes peeled means to watch out very carefully for something.
example: I mislaid my watch at home, so I asked my wife to keep her eyes peeled.

definition: This idiom means “that’s true, I agree”.
example: - She is a beautiful woman- You can say that again!

definition: This idiom refers to finding a way to stay cool when it is very hot outside.
example: I am going to Norway in order to beat the heat.

definition: To shed crocodile tears means to shed false tears or show insincere grief.
example: Olivia pretended to be sad but I knew that her tears were crocodile tears actually.

phrase: in the eye of the storm
definition: A person or organisation who is in the eye of the storm is deeply involved in a difficult situation which affects a lot of people.
example: During the way in Syria, they were in the eye of the storm.

definition: If someone asks you for something and you reply “no dice!”, you mean that it is impossible or it can’t be done.
example: The boy asked if he could go to the party, but his mother said no dice.

phrase: wouldn’t be caught dead / seen dead
definition: If someone says that they wouldn’t be caught or seen dead in a particular place or doing something, they mean that they would be too ashamed or embarrassed.
example: Our child thinks he’s a grown up boy. He wouldn’t be caught dead holding our hands in front of his friends.

definition: This idiom means to take immediate and drastic action.
example: I’ve decided to jump off the deep end and leave her. I want to completely change my life.

definition: If you land on your feet, you make a quick recovery after a difficulty such as a business failure, an illness, a loss etc.
example: I know that you’re strong! You always land on your feet.

definition: This idiom refers to a bad situation or habit that, after it has started, is likely to get very much worse.
example: You’re on a slippery slope when you start lying.

definition: If a business or project goes belly up, it is unsuccessful or goes bankrupt.
example: The store went belly up before the end of the second year.

definition: If you hand it to someone, you admit, perhaps unwillingly, that they deserve credit or praise for their achievements.
example: You’ve got to hand it to Steve. His presentations are always excellent.

definition: A person who keeps a low profile tries not to attract public attention.
example: The thief is trying to keep a low profile these days.

definition: This idiom means to do something fast or energetically as if it were your last opportunity to ever do it.
example: In this race you should run like there’s no tomorrow.

definition: If you live on the edge, your lifestyle involves dangerous or risky activities.
example: Extreme sportsmen are just an example of people who live on the edge.

definition: If you are out of your depth, you are in a situation which is too difficult for you or which you know little about.
example: I started building a website without HTML knowledge, so I was soon out of my depth and asked for help.

definition: If you are pressed for time, you have hardly enough time to do something, so you must hurry.
example: Sorry, I can’t talk to her right now. I’m pressed for time.

definition: If someone is raring to go, they are very eager and enthusiastic about the idea of doing something.
example: They can’t wait to go on holiday. They are raring to go!

definition: Someone who has sticky fingers has a tendency to steal.
example: It is rumored that she has sticky fingers, so be careful.

definition: This expression indicates the reality that it is not possible to always succeed.
example: Oh well, don’t be sad. You can’t win them all!

definition: Someone who goes through the school of hard knocks learns through the positive and negative experiences of life rather than through a formal classroom education.
example: She didn’t go to college but the school of hard knocks made her a shrewd businesswoman.

definition: If you take the rap for something, you accept blame or punishment for it, even if you have not done it.
example: The whole team had to take the rap.

definition: This expression is an impolite way of saying “it will never happen”.
example: She will forgive you when hell freezes over.

definition: If you say that someone is asleep at the wheel, you mean that they are not sufficiently attentive, especially at a critical moment when vigilance is required.
example: When the firemen arrived too late at the scene, the night watchwoman was accused of being asleep at the wheel.

definition: This idiom describes a person who earns a living or provides financial support to the home.
example: You need to find a job and bring home the bacon.

definition: A figment of one’s imagination is an appearance, event or incident that is not considered to be real.
example: Others saw the motorcycle, so it’s not a figment of our imagination.

definition: To say that a person, group or country is top dog means that they are better or more powerful than others.
example: She’s a top dog in fashion industry.

phrase: when the shit hits the fan
definition: This phrase refers to the moment when the disastrous consequences of something become public.
example: Our organisation hates it when the shit hits the fan.

definition: This expression means a strategy worked out in advance.
example: I need to come up with a better game plan for this mission.

definition: This expression means no chance at all.
example: She won’t succeed. This is like a snowball’s chance in hell.

definition: To say that something comes with the territory means that it has to be accepted as a part of a job or responsibility, even if it is unpleasant.
example: A successful singer has to expect intensive media coverage – that comes with the territory!

definition: This idiom means to stop wasting a lot of time in useless or boring or trivial works.
example: You are working way too much! Get a life, dude!

definition: If you give someone a hard time, you annoy them or make things difficult for them.
example: By assigning this project to Marry, I’ve given her a hard time.

definition: This expression refers to an event that is so important or unusual that it will be recorded in history.
example: The latest discovery will go down in history.

phrase: not get a word in edgewise / get a word in edgewise
definition: During a discussion, if you can’t get a word in edgeways, you can’t say something because the others are talking so much. Vice-versa is available.
example: I tried to express my opinion about the marketing plan, but I couldn’t get a word in edgeways.

definition: The practice of looking over somebody’s shoulder when they are using a computer, cash dispenser or other electronic device, in order to obtain personal information is called shoulder surfing.
example: I dared him to shoulder surfing.

definition: This phrase refers to someone who behaves oddly, as a sick puppy might; for example, a lovesick person who pines after their beloved.
example: She on a business trip and he’s a sick puppy these days.

definition: This idiom means to put someone in difficulty, often by making it appear that they are to blame for a misdemeanour.
example: She hid the money in my jacket, so she stitched me up for the crime.

definition: This idiom means to move past someone or something very fast.
example: The woman just zipped past me in the queue today.

definition: When a person falls passionately in love with another, they are said to be head over heels in love.
example: No way of speaking to him these days. He’s head over heels in love with that new girl.

definition: If you pull out all the stops, you do everything you can to make something successful.
example: I’ll have to pull out all the stops to get the store ready for the opening day.

definition: When you try to satisfy two or more people or groups who have different needs, and keep everyone happy, you perform a balancing act.
example: Many women, especially my wife, have to perform a balancing act between work and family.

definition: This idiom means to have an especially good time.
example: I enjoyed the holiday. I had a blast!

definition: If you jazz something up, you add something to try to improve it or make it more stylish.
example: This car needs some accessories to jazz it up.

definition: If something is kept under wraps, it is held secret and not revealed to anyone.
example: The mission details were kept under wraps until it was over.

definition: If an explanation or statement doesn’t hold water, it can be shown to be unfounded.
example: I’m sorry, but your statement doesn’t hold water.

definition: If a person or organisation leaves a paper trail, they leave evidence in writing or in document form that will serve as proof of their actions.
example: The police haven’t found any paper trail.

definition: This expression is used to express total lack of interest in something.
example: That woman stole a bottle of wine. Well, I couldn’t care less.

definition: This phrase means “I don’t want to discuss that”.
example: We’ve spoken enough. Don’t go there.

definition: A drop in the ocean/bucket is a very small quantity compared to the amount needed or expected.
example: The revenue from the newly-introduced tax is just a drop in the ocean.

phrase: fly by the seat of your pants
definition: If you fly by the seat of your pants, you do something without any knowledge or experience, using only your instinct and hoping that you will succeed.
example: Ten years ago, without any formal training, Steve decided to fly by the seat of his pants and move to Berlin.

definition: If you join a group of people you find interesting, without wanting to take an active part in their action, you go along for the ride.
example: Not all members were active in the campaign – some just went along for the ride.

definition: If an idea or proposal goes down well, it is well accepted.
example: Our marketing plan went down well. The manager congratulated us.

definition: This idiom refers to two people who are inseparable.
example: We are very much in love, but we aren’t joined at the hip, you know.

definition: If something happens out of the blue, it happens very unexpectedly.
example: I had almost given up hope when out of the blue I was offered a part-time job.

definition: If you phone in a performance, you perform something in an uncommitted and disinterested manner.
example: The actor phoned in his performance without a hint of personality.

definition: After hearing an unlikely story, this is a way of telling the speaker that you neither believe what they say nor whatever they may say next.
example: You’ve obtained a date with Sarah? Yeah, now pull the other one!

definition: This idiom refers to something that suddenly and strongly makes you remember a previous time in your life.
example: Seeing that photo again was a real blast from the past.

definition: If you jump out of your skin, you are extremely surprised or shocked.
example: Steve almost jumped out of his skin when the car entered the house.

definition: If you are in a difficult or unpleasant situation and somebody rubs salt into the wound, they do or say something to make things worse.
example: Mentioning her ex just rubbed salt into the wound.

phrase: run around like a headless chicken
definition: If a person rushes about like a headless chicken, they act in a disorderly way, without thinking or analyzing the situation carefully.
example: As soon as the store opened, my brother started running around like a headless chicken, searching for a laptop.

definition: If something difficult or unpleasant took place in the past but is no longer important, it is referred to as water under the bridge.
example: As a couple, we had a serious disagreement but that’s water under the bridge today.

definition: This expression is used when somebody is in a state of great fear or anxiety.
example: You are as white as a sheet. What’s the matter?

phrase: from the bottom of my heart
definition: This expression means with sincere and deep feeling.
example: The woman loved him from the bottom of her heart.

definition: If you get bent out of shape, you become annoyed or upset about something that is usually not that important or cannot be avoided.
example: Please don’t get bent out of shape if you’re delayed. We’ll wait for you.

definition: By saying this to somebody, you express sympathy for an unpleasant experience that you have had too.
example: My phone has been stolen. Mine was stolen last month – join the club!

phrase: laugh all the way to the bank
definition: A person who makes a lot of money easily, is said to laugh all the way to the bank.
example: If we fail to renew that contract, our competitor will be laughing all the way to the bank.

definition: An open-and-shut case is one where the facts are so clear that the matter can be dealt with or solved easily.
example: Her lawyers think that she has an open-and-shut case.

definition: If someone or something puts a damper on a situation or event, they make it less successful or enjoyable.
example: The plan was going well until her complaints put a damper on it.

definition: If you are saved by the bell, something happens at the last minute to rescue you from a difficult situation.
example: A friend arrived just when I needed help. Saved by the bell!

definition: To describe a situation as a can of worms means that it is complicated, unpleasant and difficult to deal with.
example: The discovery of the stolen car turned out to be a real can of worms.

definition: A person who cooks the books is one who changes the facts or figures in the financial accounts, often so as to steal money.
example: The man discovered after some time that his partners was cooking the books.

definition: If you keep someone at arm’s length, you do not allow yourself to become friendly with them.
example: It’s not easy to become friends with Cristina; she tends to keep everyone at arm’s length.

definition: If you stand your ground you maintain your position and refuse to yield or give way.
example: We have to stand our ground at all costs.

definition: Something very unpleasant or difficult to accept is a bitter pill to swallow.
example: Losing her job after arranging the merger between the companies was a really bitter pill to swallow.

definition: If you go overboard, you are over-enthusiastic about something and do too much or behave in an excessive way.
example: We need to prepare the room for the meeting but don’t go overboard with it.

definition: When you hold the fort, you look after a place or a business in the absence of the person who is normally in charge.
example: John, could you hold the fort for two hours? I need to go to her place.

definition: To refer to something that happens as the luck of the draw means that it is the result of pure chance, with no possibility of choice.
example: You can’t choose who you play against – it’s the luck of the draw.

phrase: one sandwich short of a picnic
definition: This idiom can be used in a humorous way to refer to someone who is crazy or stupid.
example: Steve is one sandwich short of a picnic.

definition: When you push the envelope, you do something in an extreme way or exceed the limits of what is considered acceptable.
example: Some TV producers push the envelope when they expose people’s private lives.

definition: To refer to something as a whole new ball game means that it is a completely different situation due to a new set of circumstances.
example: Facebook and Instagram have made business communication a whole new ball game.

definition: This expression refers to doing or saying things which are certain to cause a serious disagreement or a fight between them.
example: The United States and Iran are on a collision course.

definition: If you black out, you lose consciousness.
example: When she saw the police, she blacked out.

definition: If you dial it back, you reduce the intensity of something or tone it down.
example: When the kid started getting excited, his mother said: dial it back a little!

phrase: get your ducks in a row
definition: If you get your ducks in a row, you get things well organized.
example: As I have some free time at the office and the files are unorganized, I will get my ducks in a row.

definition: To say that a person has gone nuts means that they have become completely foolish, eccentric or mad.
example: I think he has gone nuts. He talks about dating his wife, but he is a widower since five years ago.

definition: If something is not in the same league, it is of much lower standard than something else.
example: She has a good voice but she isn’t in the same league as Mariah Carey.

definition: Someone who is riding high is enjoying a period of success or popularity.
example: The actress has been riding high since the last movie.

definition: This expression means to start performing better.
example: If you want to get the job, you’ll have to step up your game.

definition: This phrase means outside the range of what is normally considered believable.
example: The fact that she kissed him is beyond belief.

definition: If you punch above your weight, you try to perform at a level that is beyond your ability.
example: I submitted my business plan for the contest, but I knew I was punching above my weight.

definition: If you swallow your pride, you accept something humiliating or embarrassing, for example having to admit that you are wrong, or that you have less knowledge than you thought.
example: When I failed the exam, I had to swallow my pride and repeat the course.

phrase: throw / push / shove under the bus
definition: This idiom means to betray a partner, colleague or close friend for self-benefits.
example: She always looks for someone to throw under the bus for her failings.

definition: This idiom means to fall asleep very promptly.
example: After a hard working day, I zonked out.

definition: Someone who is asking for trouble is behaving so stupidly that he or she is likely to have problems.
example: Driving so fast on this highway is really asking for trouble.

definition: A dead man walking is someone who will inevitably be in great trouble very soon, especially a person who is about to lose their job or position.
example: Taking into consideration the way the officer handled the last missions, I think he is a dead man walking.

definition: This idiom means to think that one is very important in a way that annoys other people.
example: I don’t like her because she’s so full of herself.

definition: When someone goes ballistic, they become very angry.
example: My mother went ballistic when she saw how the house looked after the party.

definition: This term is used to refer to a journey that leaves late at night and arrives early in the morning.
example: I had to catch the red-eye bus last night and I’m completely exhausted now.

definition: If a person has the best of both worlds, they have the benefits and advantages of two different things.
example: I live in the centre of town, but only 7 minutes from the tram station. I have the best of both worlds.

definition: This idiom means to behave very badly and without respect.
example: The manager treats all his employees like dirt. He won’t last any longer.

phrase: up shit creek without a paddle
definition: This idiom means to be in deep trouble with no solution.
example: When he saw the police he knew that he was up shit creek without a paddle.

definition: To add insult to injury means to make a bad situation worse by harming or upsetting someone you have already harmed in some other way.
example: He stole money from me and he added insult to injury by hitting my wife!

definition: This idiom refers to a film with characterization and story-lines that appeal especially to women.
example: That’s just another chick flick.

definition: To say that someone, for example an athlete or entertainer, is a class act means that they are very good at what they do.
example: His career is just beginning, but he is already a class act.

definition: you delay a decision or participate without any real enthusiasm.
example: Stop dragging your feet and finish that task!

definition: If a person or organisation is in the red, they owe money or have a negative account.
example: I’m afraid I can’t buy it now. I’m in the red.

phrase: not sleep a wink / not get a wink of sleep
definition: If someone doesn’t get a wink of sleep, they don’t sleep at all.
example: I didn’t get a wink of sleep. It was too noisy.

definition: This idiom refers to something that is very easy and is therefore certain to be a success.
example: The exam was a cinch.

definition: If you exaggerate the importance of something, you blow it out of proportion.
example: The importance of the latest event was blown out of proportion by the media.

definition: This idiom refers to a very serious situation.
example: After my wife lost her job, we were in deep water.

definition: This idiom means at risk of failing or being harmed.
example: Policemen regularly put their lives on the line.

definition: This idiom refers to an honest and straightforward man of good character.
example: Claudio is a real stand-up guy!

definition: To say that you take a rain check means that you cannot accept an invitation or offer now, but you will be happy to accept it later.
example: I’m afraid I’ll take a rain check on your invitation. I don’t have much time to finish the project.

definition: If you touch base with someone, you make contact or renew communication with them.
example: I’ll try to touch base with her next week.

definition: If a person is at a loss, they don’t know what to say or do in a particular situation.
example: When I saw her kissing another man I was at a loss.

definition: If you blow up, you go crazy.
example: When I saw her look, I knew she’d blow up.

definition: This expression is used by someone who absolutely refuses to allow someone to do something.
example: Can I get my ear pierced? Over my dead body!

definition: This idiom means to indulge in a series of sexual relationships.
example: I have three girlfriends on the go at once. I like playing the field.

definition: This idiom means to betray someone’s confidence.
example: They have been sold out by their government in the negotiation.

definition: A person who steals the show gets more attention or praise than the other participants.
example: The German competitor stole the show at the Olympic games.

definition: This rhetorical question is asked of someone who has done something stupid or outrageous. The point being that it is quite obvious what the person in question is like.
example: You got fired. What are you like?

phrase: What part of no do you not understand?
definition: This phrase means “I am plainly saying no and I mean just that”.
example: You are not allowed here. What part of no do you not understand?

definition: If you chicken our of something, you decide not to do something because you are afraid.
example: He decided to join a fight club, but chickened out very soon.

definition: This idiom means to give someone a harsh scolding.
example: She gave me hell about not leading a healthy lifestyle.

definition: This idiom refers to something common.
example: Stamps like this are a dime a dozen.

definition: This expression refers to an opportunity or turn of events that leads to success. A big break is often used for people involved in the arts, to talk about one specific opportunity that led to their work being recognised and to them being successful.
example: Marry had her big break in 2011 and the phone hasn’t stopped ringing since.

phrase: dip your toes in the water / get your feet wet
definition: If you dip your toes in the water or you get your feet wet, you start to do something new or unfamiliar, or explore new territory for the first time.
example: This job is challenging, but I can’t wait to dip my toes in the water.

definition: failing to remember something or being unable to find an answer or result
example: He asked me for my phone number and I drew a blank - I just couldn't rememberit.

definition: Someone who is green with envy is a person who is very envious.
example: She will be green with envy when she sees Mary’s new motorcycle.

definition: If you shed light on something, you help to explain it or make it easier to understand.
example: I hoped that her testimony would shed light on the circumstances of the car crash.

definition: This idiom means a boost or encouragement.
example: Seeing them cheering me was a real shot in the arm.

definition: This idiom means to go crazy.
example: I can’t be late tonight. My girlfriend will hit the roof.

definition: If you say that you could murder something, such as food or drink, you mean that you want it very much.
example: I’m so hungry. I could murder a burger.

definition: When somebody’s feelings or thoughts are very clear, you can say that they are written all over their face.
example: His love for her was written all over his face.

definition: This phrase means to wait until you know all the facts before forming an opinion or making a judgment. It can also mean to be willing to change your opinion.
example: I don’t usually like blondes but I keep an open mind.

definition: This idiom means to throw a tantrum.
example: You shouldn’t throw a hissy fit for such a trivial thing.

definition: This idiom means that a person is responsible for someone’s death.
example: People with blood on their hands don’t stand a chance in our justice system.

definition: If you put your foot in your mouth, you do or say something that offends, upsets or embarrasses someone else.
example: He really put his foot in his mouth by saying such things about her.

definition: If you have your hands full, you are very busy or have a lot to do.
example: I can’t help you this week. I have my hands full.

definition: A person who twiddles their thumbs has nothing to do, or is doing nothing useful.
example: Come and help me! You can’t twiddle your thumbs all day.

definition: If you cover your tracks, you conceal or destroy evidence of what you have been doing or where you have been.
example: Don’t forget to cover your tracks or they might put you into jail.

definition: This idiom means to pass on the responsibility.
example: Steve passed the torch to me after having completed so much of the project himself.

definition: This phrase is an ironic name for the imagined crime of being a black driver.
example: Driving while black? Is that your best joke?

definition: If something is referred to as icing on the cake, it is an extra benefit that makes a good situation even better.
example: I’ve got the job and icing on the cake, they have offered me a company car too.

definition: If something happens in the nick of time, it happens at the last minute, when it is nearly too late.
example: The little girl was standing in front of the open window. Her father caught her in the nick of time.

definition: This idiom means to overeat in a slovenly manner.
example: I told the babysitter not to pig out, but when I got back there were five pizza boxes.

definition: This expression is used when there are signs that a fight is about to start.
example: They have insulted each other and now the gloves are off.

definition: Something that is as easy as pie is very easy to do.
example: How difficult was the exam? Well, as easy as pie!

definition: This term refers to a deceptive commercial practice of advertising a low-priced item to attract customers, then telling them that the product is out of stock and persuading them to buy a more expensive article.
example: This general store is famous for its bait and switch tactics.

definition: If you talk about how someone is or feels, deep down, you are describing what they are like or what they really feel deep inside, behind the outward appearance.
example: He appears to be indifferent to his wife’s success but deep down he is happy.

definition: This idiom means to use violence or extreme measures.
example: Don’t get medieval here! Calm down!

definition: This means to study very hard.
example: You have that exam next month. It’s high time you were studying.

definition: Someone who doesn’t mince their words expresses their opinions or thoughts very clearly, even if they offend others by doing so.
example: I like her because she doesn’t mince her words.

definition: This expression means to speak directly.
example: I prefer you to shoot from the hip next time we speak.

definition: This idiom is used to say that you feel the same way or have had the same experience.
example: - She’s driving me crazy with her ways. - Tell me about it!

definition: This expression means to reveal the true identity.
example: The officer recognised the woman from a wanted poster and blew her cover.

definition: To say that someone is coming apart at the seams means that they are extremely upset or under severe mental stress.
example: She has had so many problems recently that she’s coming apart at the seams.

definition: If somebody or something drives you up the wall, they do something that greatly annoys or irritates you.
example: Please, turn the volume down! It’s driving me up the wall.

definition: You say this when you think that a difficult situation or argument cannot be the fault of one person alone.
example: Okay, I was wrong, but it takes two to tango.

definition: This expression means to sell really well, a popular product.
example: These homemade cakes are jumping off the shelves.

definition: If a situation becomes so confusing that you are unable to understand what is happening or what you are supposed to do, you lose the plot.
example: The TV instructions were so long and confusing that I just lost the plot.

definition: If a group of people are packed like sardines, they are pressed together tightly and uncomfortably because there is not enough space.
example: The tube was very crowded – we were packed like sardines!

definition: This idiom means to impolitely tell someone to stop talking or making a noise.
example: Hey! I’m trying to concentrate! Put a sock in it!

definition: This expression means to gamble or take a chance on something or someone.
example: I decided to roll the dice and use the money for playing a poker game.

phrase: wise up to something / get wise to something
definition: If you wise up or get wise to something, you become fully aware of the facts and are no longer fooled.
example: When I wised up to the methods being used, I resigned from the organization.

definition: A person who is larger than life attracts special attention because they are very impressive in their appearance, behaviour or personality.
example: Steve is a larger than life man. I’m glad that you have met him.

definition: This idiom refers to the publication of the identity of a person or group that is culpable in some anti-social act in order to shame them into remorse.
example: The entire group has been named and shamed for their deeds.

phrase: not play with a full deck of cards
definition: Someone who is not playing with a full deck of cards lacks intelligence or does not have full mental abilities.
example: She wasn’t playing with a full deck when she bought that fancy sports car.

phrase: on the tip of your tongue
definition: To say that a word or answer is on the tip of your tongue, means that you’re sure you know it but have difficulty finding it.
example: Ah. Please wait. I have her name on the tip of my tongue.

definition: If you take a back seat you choose to have a less important function and become less involved in something.
example: I decided that it was time to take a back seat for the rest of the day.

definition: If a person turns over a new leaf, they decide to change their behaviour and lead a better life.
example: When Tim left prison, he was decided to turn over a new leaf.

definition: This idiom means to do the things you have said you would do, especially when you reach a position of power.
example: Business groups are waiting to see if the new president will walk the talk.

phrase: where the rubber meets the road
definition: This idiom refers to the point in a process where there are challenges, issues or problems.
example: We have identified the main area of dissent. This is where the rubber meets the road.

definition: This means ready to go.
example: We are all set to go on holiday.

definition: This idiom means everything possible. The whole thing.
example: She provided the full monty for us.

definition: If you hold your breath, you wait anxiously or excitedly for something to happen or be announced.
example: My girlfriend went for a second interview today and now she’s holding her breath.

phrase: march to the beat of your own drum
definition: When somebody does things the way they want to, without taking anybody else or anything else into consideration, they march to the beat of their own drum.
example: I’ve tried talking to her, but it was in vain. She marches to the beat of her own drum.

definition: If you don’t know what hit you, you are so surprised, shocked or confused by something that you do not know how to react.
example: When I was told that I wasn’t the winner of the competition, I didn’t know what hit me.

definition: If you are on the lookout for something, you are constantly watchful and attentive so as not to miss it.
example: As a collector, I am always on the lookout for interesting items.

definition: This term refers to money paid illegally for favourable treatment.
example: They were accused of giving kickbacks to local authorities.

definition: When you are or mean the world to someone, you are very important or precious to them.
example: She says that her husband is the world to her.

definition: This expression is used when comparing two things that cannot be compared.
example: I can’t choose. It’s like comparing apples to oranges.

definition: This expression refers to the best people or things in a particular group.
example: As usual, the cream of the crop of this year’s university graduates were offered good jobs.

phrase: Wear your heart on your sleeve
definition: If you wear your heart on your sleeve, you allow others to see your emotions or feelings.
example: I could easily see she was hurt – she wears her heart on her sleeve.

definition: If you suggest that someone should let their hair down, you are telling them to relax and enjoy themselves.
example: We’re not at work now, so you can let your hair down.

definition: When someone has to roll with the punches, they have to deal with a difficult situation by being flexible.
example: The atmosphere has become aggressive. We have to roll with the punches.

phrase: when the rubber hits the road
definition: The moment when you put a theory into practice, or actually apply what you have learned, is when the rubber hits the road.
example: The plan sounds really good. I’ll be there when the rubber hits the road.

definition: This idiom refers to a store that fulfills various requirements which is preferable by customers.
example: That corner store is a one stop shop for anyone.

definition: This idiom means to make an effort to present oneself well-dressed and smartly turned out.
example: She was amazed by me. It’s true that I scrubbed up that night.

definition: To say that the honeymoon is over means that the initial period of friendship and cooperation between people, groups or organisations has ended.
example: I don’t understand. She was elected only two months ago and now the honeymoon is over.

definition: This means that something will never happen.
example: I will buy you a new car when pigs fly.

definition: This idiom means “for sure”.
example: Am I going to the party? You bet!

definition: This idiom refers to confusion or forgetfulness caused by lack of sleep when caring for a new-born.
example: She put the milk in the oven today – must be baby brain.

definition: This term means to immediately and completely stop an addictive substance, a regular activity or a behavioural pattern, instead of ending it gradually.
example: When I decided to stop smoking, I did it cold turkey.

definition: This is said to warn someone to be careful what they say so as not to upset or offend anyone.
example: They don’t tolerate rudeness so mind your language.

definition: This idiom means perfect in appearance.
example: Almost every hill was crowned with a picture-perfect village.

definition: This idiom means to criticize and offer advice, with the benefit of hindsight. It can also means to foresee the actions of others before they have come to a decision themselves.
example: It doesn’t help to second-guess their decision.

definition: If something has slipped your mind, you have forgotten about it.
example: It slipped my mind that the local store is closed today.

definition: This idiom means to adopt an aggressive stance.
example: The whole gang copped an attitude when they saw the police.

definition: If you give the game away, you reveal a secret or a plan, often unintentionally.
example: The woman hoped nobody would recognize her, but the security guard gave the game away.

definition: If your heart misses/skips a beat, you have sudden feeling of fear or excitement.
example: When the car lights suddenly went out, my heart missed a beat.

phrase: like a fish out of water
definition: If you feel like a fish out of water, you feel uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings.
example: As I don’t like going to a reception, I felt like a fish out of water.

phrase: turn up your nose at something
definition: If you turn up your nose at something, you reject it because you think it is not good enough for you.
example: She’s out of work and still turns up her nose at job offers.

definition: If you are on the ball, you are aware of what is happening and are able to deal with things quickly and intelligently.
example: We need someone who is really on the ball to head the marketing campaign.

definition: This idiom means to have strong feelings of love for someone.
example: Last year, I had a crush on my colleague.

definition: This idiom means in charge of things or situation.
example: Money and skills will put you in the driver’s seat.

definition: If you cross the line, you go beyond the authorized limits and do something which is not acceptable.
example: Don’t be mad with me. I have an unpleasant habit of telling jokes that really cross the line.

definition: This idiom means to leave out all the unnecessary details and get straight to the point.
example: That’s enough talk. Let’s cut to the chase and make a decision.

phrase: give someone a run for their money
definition: If you give someone a run for their money, you present strong competition in circumstances where the other person expects to win easily.
example: We didn’t win the contest but we gave the other team a run for their money.

definition: to cause someone to remain alert and ready for anything that might happen.
example: The officer likes to keep the soldiers on their toes.

definition: This means to work with a person or organisation or to be involved with them, in a way which causes other people distrust you.
example: They were accused of being in bed with terrorists.

definition: A product or service which is a regular source of income for a company is called a cash cow.
example: Her latest inventions proved to be a real cash cow.

phrase: give as good as you get
definition: This expression means that you are prepared to treat people as badly as they treat you, and fight for your beliefs.
example: You want me to help her?! Do you remember teaching me to give as good as I get? I hope so, because not for the world would I help her.

definition: If you are very respectful and submissive, giving way to the wishes of a person or organisation in authority in order to please them, you kowtow to them.
example: She refused to kowtow to us anymore.

definition: This expression is used to encourage someone to persevere and not give up in spite of the difficult circumstances.
example: Just hang in there! I will help you immediately.

definition: When you keep your options open, you postpone making a decision so that you can choose among several possible courses of action.
example: The price is good, but I keep my options open until I’m sure this is the best choice.

definition: This idiom refers to a person, group or thing that is known for or limited to only one unique or noteworthy skill, talent, ability, quality, area of success etc.
example: The company has been seen as an one-trick pony ever since that breakthrough success.

definition: If something spells trouble, it signifies possible problems in the future.
example: This weather spells trouble for this year’s harvest.

definition: If something such as a project or a match goes down to the wire, the situation can change up until the last possible moment.
example: Contract negotiations for more than 50,000 employees are expected to go down to the wire.

definition: If you make the cut, you reach a required standard or succeed in passing from one round of a competition to another.
example: After intensive training, he made the cut and joined the army.

definition: When you ask someone to marry you, you pop the question.
example: It was during a trip to Rome that Steve popped the question.

definition: If someone stabs you in the back, they betray you by doing something harmful to you when you thought you could trust them.
example: She stabbed me in the back and I won’t ever forget that!

definition: If one person two-times another, they cheat on their partner by having a romantic relationship with another person at the same time.
example: She left me when she discovered that I was two-timing her.

definition: If you beef something up, you improve it by making it stronger or more substantial.
example: You’d better beef up your arguments if you want to get the job.

definition: When someone has come a long way, they have made a lot of progress or have become successful.
example: Nicole has come a long way since she opened her first confectionery.

definition: A hasty method or solution, usually cheap and temporary, that is not without flaws is quick and dirty.
example: I’ve repaired your car but keep in mind that this is a quick and dirty solution.

definition: When you try to understand what motivates someone or makes them behave the way they do, you want to know what makes them tick.
example: She’s a strange woman. It’s hard for me to figure out what makes her tick.

definition: If you come to your senses you start to think clearly and behave sensibly.
example: She finally came to her senses and realized that using the bicycle was better than driving the car in that town.

definition: If you tell someone not to rock the boat, you are asking them to do nothing that might cause trouble or upset a stable situation.
example: It’s fine to have a party at our house, but don’t rock the boat!

definition: If someone goes through the motions, they do something because they have to, but without enthusiasm.
example: After that dreadful car accident when her son died, she went through the motions trying to continue her life.

definition: If you play into someone’s hands, you do exactly what your opponent or enemy wants you to do, so that they gain an advantage over you.
example: When the protesters became violent, they played right into the hands of the police.

definition: This idiom refers to the time spent with a child, spouse or friend in an uninterrupted and attentive way.
example: I need some quality time with Ann.

definition: If someone sees red, they suddenly become very angry or annoyed.
example: Lies make me see red.

definition: If a person is caught red-handed, they are caught while they are doing something wrong or illegal.
example: She was caught red-handed.

phrase: give someone the benefit of doubt
definition: If you give someone the benefit of doubt, you choose to believe that they are innocent, honest or telling the truth because there is no evidence to the contrary.
example: Although he found it hard to believe the suspect’s explanation, the police officer gave him the benefit of doubt.

definition: To say that someone is not in their right mind means that they are not behaving in a logical or sensible way.
example: He wasn’t in his right mind when he decided to leave this company.

definition: This idiom means to cause someone to be out of breath because of shock or surprise.
example: The view took my breath away.

definition: If an idea or thought crosses your mind, you suddenly think of it.
example: It just crossed my mind that the local store is closed today.

definition: If people get their wires crossed, they misunderstand each other or are confused about what was said.
example: I thought you were at the party. Sorry, we got our wires crossed.

definition: To refer to a question or statement as a shot in the dark means that it is a complete guess, but at the same time it might be close to the truth.
example: Mentioning her name was just a shot in the dark.

definition: Someone who lays down the law tells people very forcefully and firmly what to do.
example: The people were acting in a disorganised way. They needed someone to lay down the law.

definition: Something which is out of the question is impossible and is therefore not worth discussing.
example: Buying a new car is out of the question for now.

definition: If you are out of touch, you no longer communicate with someone or are unaware of recent developments.
example: I’ve been out of touch with Natalie since we left primary school.

definition: A passenger in a car who gives unwanted advice to the driver is called a backseat driver.
example: I can’t stand backseat drivers like my girlfriend.

definition: If someone cuts loose or is cut loose, they stop being influenced or controlled by another person or group.
example: She’s thirty-five years old and still hasn’t cut loose from her family.

definition: If you have to face the music, you have to accept the unpleasant consequences of your actions.
example: She was caught cheating. She has to face the music now.

definition: If you are first out of the gate, you are the first to make a start at something that others have also accepted to do.
example: I was so enthusiastic about going to another club that I was the first out of the gate.

definition: to have a great time, enjoy yourself a lot, or have a lot of fun
example:
Thanks again for inviting me! Your party was great. We had a ball.
Go to the concert—you’ll have a ball! (You’ll really enjoy it)

phrase: if it’s the last thing I do
definition: This expression indicates determination to achieve something.
example: I’m going to buy that BMW if it’s the last thing I do.

definition: This idiom literally means “go away”.
example: I’ve had enough of you! Take a hike!

definition: To take someone for a ride means to cheat or deceive them.
example: The service operator charged me double the normal price. He really took me for a ride!

definition: This idiom means to stop working hard or to take things slow and easy.
example: After a hard week, I like to veg out during the weekend.

definition: If you walk on eggshells with someone, you are careful not to hurt or offend them.
example: I don’t want to offend Maria, so I walk on eggshells with her.

definition: When people temporarily stop doing something or put an end to an activity, they call it quits.
example: I see that you are all exhausted, so let’s call it quits for today.

definition: The sum of money something sets you back is the amount it costs you.
example: Changing the car will set us back about 10000 dollars.

definition: This expression is usually used sarcastically to someone who is constantly complaining.
example: You can cry me a river, we are still not going to the party.

definition: If you push your luck, you try to get more than what you have already obtained and risk spoiling the situation.
example: You’ve got your mother’s permission to go to town. Don’t push your luck by asking another thing.

definition: This refers to something or someone that adds an unexpected twist to an activity or situation.
example: They added us as a wild card just to make the game more interesting.

definition: If you have to cough up something, such as money or information, you give it reluctantly or unwillingly.
example: She refused to say who embarrassed her until her mother made her cough up the names.

definition: This expression refers to the time when an unpleasant situation has to be dealt with.
example: This is the day of reckoning. We have to take a decision with regard to financial costs.

definition: If you criticize someone severely because you are angry with them, you eat them alive. (One can also be eaten alive – bitten repeatedly by insects).
example: The manager will eat me alive if I am wrong.

definition: This idiom refers to something that a particular person finds especially annoying.
example: One of my biggest pet peeves is poor customer service.

definition: If you are dying for something, you have a strong desire for it.
example: I’m dying for a cup of coffee!

definition: If you abandon someone who is in difficulty, without giving any assistance or support, you hang them out to dry.
example: You won’t get any help from her. She will hang you out to dry if your plan fails.

definition: To talk about being in someone’s shoes means to imagine how you would react if you were in a similar situation.
example: Their store sales have dropped by 20% this month. I wouldn’t like to be in their shoes.

definition: If you tell someone to let sleeping dogs lie, you are asking them not to interfere with a situation so as to avoid making matters worse.
example: It’s time to let sleeping dogs lie and move on. We have another challenge ahead.

definition: This means prevent someone from enjoying an event or to spoil somebody’s plans.
example: I won’t let this new situation to rain on my parade.

definition: This idiom means a share of something like money or profits.
example: If you invest in this company, you will get a big piece of the pie.

definition: This idiom means to insult someone.
example: The little boy got into trouble for calling the teacher names.

definition: When you roll up your sleeves, you get ready for hard work.
example: The house is a mess. We have to roll up our sleeves and start cleaning.

definition: This idiom means to accept a bad situation.
example: She will never come back. Suck it up and move on.

definition: If you develop a sudden interest or enthusiasm for something, you are bitten by the bug.
example: My dad decided to take up computer games and was immediately bitten by the bug.

definition: A bone of contention is a matter or subject about which there is a lot of disagreement.
example: The wages have been agreed on, but opening on Saturdays is still a bone of contention.

definition: This idiom means to provide or offer a useful skill or attribute.
example: She brings years of leadership experience to the table.

phrase: go through a rough / bad / difficult / sticky patch
definition: This expression means to experience a lot of problems in a period of life.
example: Their marriage is going through a rough patch nowadays.

definition: A parting shot is a final remark, often incisive, made just as one is leaving.
example: She has a way of making parting shots that can be discouraging.

phrase: pull the rug from under someone’s feet
definition: If you pull the rug from under someone’s feet, you suddenly and unexpectedly remove all help or support.
example: When his mother stopped sending him money, she practically pulled the rug from under his feet.

definition: This expression is said when a previously promising enterprise goes irretrievably wrong.
example: It was pretty easy to get a loan that period, but soon the wheels came off the world banking system.

definition: If a person, especially a child, throws a tantrum, they become angry and behave in an unreasonable way.
example: Her child is always throwing tantrums – he’s so spoilt!

phrase: draw a line in the sand
definition: If you draw a line in the sand, you establish a limit beyond which a certain situation or activity will not be accepted.
example: This won’t happen again. Now, let’s draw a line in the sand!

definition: When you laugh about something that has upset or hurt you, to make it seem less important or to try to show that you do not care, you laugh it off.
example: I heard his critical remark, but I laughed it off.

definition: If you are not cut out for something, you are not the sort of person to succeed or be happy in a particular activity.
example: She started studying medicine but quickly realized that she wasn’t cut out for it.

definition: When trying to find something, if you cast a wide net, you cover an extensive area or use a wide range of sources.
example: The firms cast a wide net in their search for compatible engineers.

definition: If you dig in your hells, you refuse to do something, especially of someone is trying to convince you to do so.
example: My grandmother dug in her heels and refused to move to a smaller place.

definition: If you tell someone to get off your back, you are annoyed and ask them to stop finding faults or criticizing you.
example: You are forever criticizing me! Get off my back, will you?

phrase: not touch with a ten-foot pole
definition: If you decide not to touch something with a ten-foot pole, you prefer to stay far away from it.
example: I wouldn’t touch mathematics with a ten-foot pole!

definition: This expression refers to a time of the day that is extremely early or late.
example: I have to get up at stupid o’clock tomorrow morning.

definition: If you press the panic button, you raise the alarm too quickly or react too hastily in a difficult or stressful situation.
example: There’s no need to press the panic button for the moment!

definition: To settle a score means to retaliate against someone or take revenge for a past wrong.
example: I’ve made an appointment with my lawyer – I need to settle a score with my neighbour.

definition: This expression means to aggressively raise your middle finger at someone as a sign of displeasure.
example: I stopped the car a little too close and he flipped the bird as a response.

definition: This expression means to go crazy.
example: Why do you keep quarrelling with the manager? Have you gone mental?

definition: If you are in the doghouse, someone is angry with you because you have done something wrong.
example: I am in the doghouse because I’ve broken my girlfriend’s smartphone.

definition: This expression refers to someone thinking about something else when important issues are being discussed.
example: Just by looking at his facial expression, I can tell you that he is miles away.

definition: A project or action which involves blood, sweat and tears requires a lot of effort and hard work.
example: Her success wasn’t due to luck; it was blood, sweat and tears all the way.

definition: The expression is used when you mention something without intending to cause offence.
example: I don’t think she is old enough to mow the lawn – just saying…

definition: This idiom means to do something that prevents an activity from continuing, especially by no longer giving money to support it.
example: It’s time to pull the plug on this business.

definition: This expression refers to a vulnerable area or a weak spot, in an otherwise strong situation, that could cause one’s downfall or failure.
example: She’s extremely intelligent, but her inability to speak in public is her Achilles heel.

definition: To kick the bucket is a lighthearted way of talking about death.
example: She will inherit the house when her grandmother kicks the bucket!

definition: Something that happens once in a blue moon happens rarely.
example: I speak to her once in a blue moon.

definition: If you find a solution to a serious problem and ensure the success of something that was expected to fail, you save the day.
example: Sheila saved the day by figuring out the problem.

phrase: send a shiver down your spine
definition: If something sends a shiver down your spine, it makes you feel anxious, nervous or excited.
example: That beautiful song always sends a shiver down her spine!

definition: It means to improvise or to deal with a situation without preparation.
example: She didn’t expect to be questioned so she had to wing it.

definition: A momentary lapse of memory, especially in older people, or an absent-minded action such as putting cereals in the refrigerator, is humorously referred to as having a senior moment.
example: I found my laptop in the bathroom. I must have had a senior moment.

definition: This idiom is used when asking someone to repeat what they have said. Informal and expressive surprise
example: - Please hand me that glass- Say what?

definition: Someone who is very excited about something, or full of nervous energy, is said to be bouncing off the walls.
example: I can’t wait to start the new project. I’m bouncing off the walls.

definition: To put one’s foot down means to exert authority to prevent something from happening.
example: She wanted to go to the club with her friends, but her father put his foot down.

definition: If something is up for grabs, it is available for anyone who wants to compete for it.
example: Let’s enter the competition – there’s about $10000 up for grabs.

definition: This expression refers to someone who is excited and ready for action.
example: The big day has come and she’s amped up.

definition: When people are in stitches, they are laughing a lot.
example: The joke was so funny that everyone was in stitches.

definition: If something is beside the point, it does not relate to the topic or is irrelevant.
example: I appreciate your story but it’s beside the point.

definition: If you get on someone’s nerves, you annoy or irritate them.
example: The kid next door is so noisy. He’s getting on my nerves.

definition: This phrase is a comic reference to kneeling and vomiting down the toilet.
example: When I entered the bathroom, she was praying at the porcelain altar.

definition: Someone who wears many hats has to do many different types of tasks or play a variety of roles.
example: Being a small company, our employees wear many hats.

definition: If you keep the lid on something, you hide it or control it to prevent people from finding out about it.
example: The firm tried to keep a lid on the merger, but word got out to the press.

definition: This expression means to make peace after an argument.
example: We fight from time to time, but we always kiss and make up.

definition: If you sweep something under the rug/carpet, you try to hide it because it is embarrassing.
example: The group tried to sweep the scandal under the carpet.
