definition: This is said when you want people to realize you are speaking seriously, when they might otherwise think you were joking.
example: All kidding aside, things are getting worse and worse within this company.

definition: If someone means business, they are serious about what they announce.
example: The manager says that any missing object will be reported to the police and he means business.

definition: If you paint yourself into a corner, you put yourself into a situation that restricts what you can do or say.
example: I painted myself into a corner when I said that I was busy that night.

definition: This idiom refers to something that makes you feel extremely embarrassed and ashamed for someone else.
example: Their performance was absolutely toe-curling.

definition: This expression means that if you do something bad, something bad will happen to you eventually.
example: I felt guilty and I knew that one day I would be hurt. What goes around comes around.

definition: If you take the plunge, you finally decide to venture into something you really want to do, in spite of the involved risks.
example: I finally took the plunge and opened a local store.

phrase: fall between / slip through the cracks
definition: This expression means to be ignored or unobserved.
example: She was so caught up with the broth that she let the salad fall between the cracks.

definition: If someone gives you the run-around, they deliberately give you confusing information or evasive answers.
example: I tried to contact Adam, but the secretary gave me the run-around. Something must have happened.

phrase: not take no for an answer
definition: Someone who will not take no for an answer is very insistent in the way they make their request or offer and is unwilling to accept a refusal.
example: I want you to come with me and I won’t take no for an answer.

definition: The expression describes a person with very little ability trying to help or guide a person with no ability.
example: Don’t ask Maria to translate it. She barely speaks a word of Russian herself. It would be a case of the blind leading the blind.

definition: If a person has tunnel vision, they focus on only one aspect of something, or they are unable to see more than one way of doing things.
example: Their boss has tunnel vision. He doesn’t see any reason to change the marketing policy.

definition: If you are in a pickle, you are in a difficult situation and need help.
example: My motorbike won’t start, so I’m in a pickle today.

definition: If there are problems in a relationship, we may say it’s on the rocks.
example: I wonder if they will break up. Their relationship seems to be on the rocks.

definition: If you know important or influential people in business or government, you have friends in high places.
example: I can help you with that. I have some friends in high places.

definition: If you muddy the waters, you make something less clear by giving confusing information.
example: I had difficulty in understanding her because her explanations muddied the waters.

definition: This idiom means to no longer be in danger or difficulty.
example: After two years of struggle, we are finally out of the woods.

definition: This expression means to stop needing somebody else to look after you and start acting independently.
example: Developing countries might cut the cord and stop asking for financial aid.

definition: If you go berserk, you go crazy.
example: I went berserk when I was told that the flight had been cancelled.

definition: If a person or organization is “ahead of the pack/game”, they are better or more successful than their rivals.
example: Our services will have to be more innovative if we want to stay ahead of the pack.

definition: This expression means everything, all of it.
example: Send in the whole nine yards against them. We will destroy them!

definition: This idiom means to make public something embarrassing that should be kept secret.
example: I don’t understand why they go and air their dirty laundry in public.

definition: When different elements fall into place, they fit well together or become organised so that progress can be achieved in a satisfactory manner.
example: It was the last thing I needed. Now, everything falls into place.

phrase: the ball is in your court / have the ball in one’s court
definition: If the ball is in your court, it is your turn to speak or act next.
example: I gave the customer relations manager a list of complaints, so the ball is in his court now.

definition: This idiom means to make people worried or frightened by being too close.
example:
You are too close for comfort.
Having only ten dollars left in savings until payday is too close for comfort

definition: This expression means to make a great deal of money easily or very quickly.
example: With a temporary monopoly in urban market, our company could coin money.

definition: This idiom means that being inquisitive can lead you into an unpleasant situation.
example: You should mind your business! Curiosity killed the cat.

definition: This idiom refers to music with an instant appeal but with little lasting significance.
example: I like this song but I’m sure that it will turn into an ear candy.

definition: If you are in over your head, you are involved in something that is too difficult for you to handle.
example: I accepted to organize the campaign, but I quickly realized that I was in over my head.

definition: This idiom means to make money, but not necessarily a lot of it.
example: I make good coin at my job.

definition: If you tell someone to save their breath, you are telling them not to waste their time speaking because their words will have no effect.
example: I’ve spoken to her so you might save you breath.

definition: Someone who is down in the dumps is depressed or feeling gloomy.
example: I have been down in the dumps since she left me.

definition: A Freudian slip is a mistake made by a speaker which is considered to reveal their true thoughts or feelings.
example: So, have you got the job? Yes, I’ve got it. Congrats, I’m so sad! Oh, sorry! I meant “glad”!

definition: If you get a grip on yourself, you try to control your feelings so as to be able to deal with a situation.
example: After the crash, I got a grip on myself and called the police.

definition: This expression means to remain positive in a tough situation.
example: Keep your chin up, my friend! It will be fine in the end.

definition: This idiom refers to the space, time or freedom to make changes as needed.
example: We must leave ourselves some wiggle room when we negotiate the deal.

definition: If someone hits the ground running, they are ready and eager to start immediately a new activity.
example: She plans to hit the ground running when she start the job.

definition: If you speak your mind you express your opinion very frankly.
example: She always speaks her mind and this might upset you.

definition: The tip of the iceberg is the part that is known of a problem or situation which is thought to be much more serious.
example: Your report on corruption examines the tip of the iceberg.

phrase: to go in one ear and out the other
definition: This expression means to not remember something or to not listen to something.
example: It’s always the same with you! In on ear and out the other!

definition: This expression refers to finding somebody extremely attractive.
example: Nadine has the hots for her new colleague.

definition: If you buckle down, you apply yourself with determination to work hard and give it your full attention.
example: If you want to pass the exam, you will have to buckle down and do serious work.

phrase: pull yourself up by your bootstraps
definition: This idiom means to improve your situation by your own efforts.
example: Next year I will pull myself up by my bootstraps. You have my word!

definition: If you fight tooth and nail for something, you fight with energy and determination.
example: I will fight tooth and nail for this mission’s success.

definition: People use this expression when it becomes obvious that success or victory is going to be achieved.
example: Two hours before the polling stations closed, victory seemed in the bag for the Liberal candidate.

definition: Something that is like pulling teeth is extremely difficult to obtain, especially if trying to extract information from someone.
example: Getting him to talk about their relation was like pulling teeth.

definition: If you turn a blind eye to something, you pretend not to notice what someone is doing.
example: I turn a blind eye when I see children taking apples from my garden.

definition: If something such as a product or method works like a charm, it functions very well or has the desired effect.
example: I tried cleaning it with lemon juice and it worked like a charm.

definition: This expression refers to what you will do if the situation becomes critical and you have to take action.
example: There is enough space for everyone, but if push comes to shove I can go to a hotel.

phrase: like a deer / rabbit caught in the headlights
definition: When you are so surprised that you are momentarily confused or unable to react quickly, you are like a deer (or rabbit) caught in the headlights.
example: Surprised by the officer’s questions, she was like a deer caught in the headlights.

definition: The “new kid on the block” is someone who is a newcomer to an area or a new member of a group.
example: Even after several months in the company I am still regarded as the new kid on the block.

phrase: cost an arm and a leg
definition: If something costs an arm and a leg, it is very expensive.
example: This laptop cost me an arm and a leg but I don’t regret buying it.

definition: You say this to somebody when you think that the final decision on a matter should ultimately be theirs.
example: I prefer the local restaurant for this evening, but it’s your call.

definition: This idiom is used for something or someone that you think is extremely good.
example: This business is the dog’s bollocks.

definition: A person who flies off the handle becomes suddenly very angry.
example: My wife flew off the handle when I told her that I had damaged her car.

definition: If you wipe the slate clean, you make a fresh start and forget all past offences, disagreements or mistakes.
example: As brothers, we have to wipe the slate clean in order to build something profitable.

definition: This idiom means to try your absolute hardest to succeed.
example: I’ve sworn to give it my best shot!

definition: If one person is at odds with another, they disagree with each other.
example: She’s at odds with her father over the purchase of a new smartphone.

definition: This is an informal way of telling someone to run in order to evade capture.
example: You shouldn’t be here! Leg it!

definition: If you pick up the tab, you pay the bill or pay the cost of something.
example: There was a anniversary party and the manager picked up the tab.

definition: This idiom means to try to gain an advantage by drawing attention to someone’s race or to issues of race.
example: There’s no other way. Play the race card!

definition: This idiom means extremely drunk.
example: I got completely rat-arsed at her party.

definition: If you walk out on somebody, you leave your partner and end the relationship.
example: She has certainly walked out on him.

definition: If you bend over backwards, you try very hard to do something, especially to please somebody.
example: The general manager bent over backwards to make James stay, but he wouldn’t change his mind.

definition: If a style or tradition is in keeping with, it is suitable or appropriate in a particular situation.
example: People exchange presents at Christmas in keeping with tradition.

definition: If you go to pieces, for example after a terrible shock, you are so upset or distressed that you cannot lead a normal life.
example: I nearly went to pieces when my cousin died in a car accident.

definition: This idiom is used when someone enjoys themselves very much.
example: Thank you for inviting me to that party! I had the time of my life!

phrase: to make a big deal of something
definition: This expression means to exaggerate a situation, put a lot of focus on something or someone or build up the importance of something.
example: Don’t make a big deal of my words. I was a little bit nervous. I’m sorry.

definition: If you have a bone to pick with someone, you are annoyed with them and want to talk to them about it.
example: Twain wants to see the director. He says he has got a bone to pick with him.

definition: If you miss the point you fail to understand the essential part of what has been said.
example: Could you repeat, please? I’ve missed the point.

definition: This idiom means to increase someone’s or one’s own excitement, confidence or mental preparation.
example: The coach pumped up all of us.

definition: This is an exclamation that is used, primarily by children but also by adults, to establish a claim on something. The first person to call out “first dibs” has the option on the first use or the ownership of the item claimed.
example: First dibs! The plate is mine now!

phrase: if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it
definition: This expression is said when you recognize that something is in a satisfactory state, and there is no reason to try to change it.
example: I’m not touching the operating system. As the saying goes: if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it!

definition: If something is referred to as the pits, it is considered to be absolutely the worst.
example: The hotel we stayed in was the pits.

definition: This idiom means to be irritating or to bother a person.
example: The new financial manager is getting under my skin.

definition: If you give someone the benefit of the doubt, you choose to believe that the person is innocent, honest or telling the truth, because there is no evidence to the contrary.
example: Although she found it hard to believe his explanation, his wife decided to give him the benefit of the doubt.

phrase: in one ear and out the other
definition: To say that information goes in one ear and comes out the other means that it is immediately forgotten or ignored.
example: I keep telling them about the risks but it goes in one ear and out the other. It will be their problem.

phrase: like something the cat dragged in
definition: If you compare a person or thing to something the cat dragged in, you think they look dirty, untidy or generally unappealing.
example: My cousin often looked like something the cat dragged in.

definition: When working on a plan or project, if it suddenly goes wrong or fails, it blows up in your face.
example: Our plans blew up in our face when the airline company went on strike.

definition: If you call someone’s bluff, you challenge them to do what they threaten to do (while believing that they will not dare to do it).
example: After the neighbour’s threats to call the police, when she decided to call his bluff, there were no more complaints.

definition: If you go bonkers, you go crazy.
example: When I was told to wait for another two hours, I went bonkers.

definition: This phrase is used to invite audience members to the stage to become contestants in game shows.
example: I need two men. Come on down!

definition: If something does the trick, it does exactly what is needed or achieves the desired effect.
example: Let’s try this application. It should do the trick and solve our problem.

definition: If people drop like flies, they fall ill or die in large numbers.
example: The heat was overwhelming and peoplewere dropping like flies.

definition: This idiom means to reduce the impact of something.
example: Have this drug – it will take the edge off the pain.

phrase: not the brightest bulb in the box / not the sharpest knife in the drawer / not the sharpest tool in the shed
definition: These expressions are used to say that somebody is not very intelligent.
example: She has failed the exam for the second time! She’s not the brightest bulb in the box.

definition: If you sit on the fence, you avoid taking sides in a discussion or argument.
example: We need your opinion. You can’t continue to sit on the fence!

definition: If a plan or project goes up in smoke, it is spoiled, fails, or ends before producing a result.
example: When they told us the price of implementing our marketing plan, everything went up in smoke.

definition: This idiom means to surprise someone in a way that makes the person feel confused or uncertain.
example: The news caught me completely off guard.

definition: This idiom refers to something that is visually pleasing or someone who is intellectually sharp and stands out above the rest.
example: That woman jumps off the page for sure!

definition: If someone gives a ballpark figure, they give an approximate number or a rough estimate of the cost of something.
example: She doesn’t know exactly how much it will cost, but a ballpark figure would be around $5.000.

definition: This expression means “absolutely never” or “at no time in my life”.
example: I will never in a million years understand why she married him.

definition: This idiom means to understand something.
example: I can’t get my head around the fact that she is leaving me.

definition: This idiom means insane or intensely mad.
example: Your neighbour is barking mad.

definition: This idiom refers to a relatively trivial problem only affecting the affluent.
example: This is a First World problem, so let’s not worry about it.

definition: Someone who is behind bars is in prison.
example: If you keep hanging around with that gang, you’ll find yourself behind bars!

definition: If someone becomes very emotional and starts behaving in a crazy way, they go bananas.
example: If you tell your parents that you want to drop out of university, they will go bananas!

definition: If something (mainly a movie or show) lives up to the hype, it means that there is enough interest in it.
example: The latest Star Wars movie lives up to the hype.

definition: A person or organisation who has deep pockets has a lot of money.
example: My business is doing well at the moment. I have deep pockets nowadays.

definition: This expression means that someone or something gets out of our control.
example: Things got out of hand at her party and one window was broken.

definition: This idiom means not traceable through any means of commerce or communication that could be linked to one’s identity.
example: The whistle-blower from the intelligence agency was forced to live off the grid.

definition: This idiom means that you are ready to participate.
example: Just let me get my car keys and I’ll be good to go.

definition: A person who lets off steam releases surplus energy or strong feelings either through intense physical activity or by talking in an unrestrained manner.
example: Let’s have a drink so you can let off steam.

definition: When you get the message, you understand what someone is trying to tell you even if it is not stated clearly.
example: By the way she looked at me, I am sure she got the message.

phrase: as useful as a chocolate teapot
definition: Something which is of no practical use at all is about as useful as a chocolate teapot.
example: In our village there are no roads. Therefore, a car is about as useful as a chocolate teapot.

definition: If something is just around the corner, it will happen very soon or is nor far away.
example: There’s a restaurant just around the corner. Good times are just around the corner.

definition: A starter marriage is a short-lived first marriage that ends in divorce with no kids, no property and no regrets.
example: John really knows what starter marriage is.

definition: This idiom means you are sexually attracted to someone, whom you wouldn’t normally find attractive, because you are drunk.
example: Get your beer goggles off! She’s not beautiful!

definition: When somebody’s days are numbered, they are expected to die soon.
example: Unfortunately, her days are numbered.

phrase: you don’t know the half of it
definition: This expression is used to tell someone that they know some of the facts but they don’t know how bad the situation is.
example: You don’t know the half of it! He beat her two days ago and that was the last straw.

definition: This idiom means to come up against an immovable or insurmountable difficulty or obstacle.
example: Our project hit a brick wall in the end.

definition: If you play your cards right, you do all that is necessary in order to succeed or to obtain what you want.
example: If I play my cards right, I’ll get the biggest contract!

phrase: in the heat of the moment
definition: If you say or do something in the heat of the moment, you say or do it without thinking too much of it, at a time when you are experiencing strong emotions.
example: In the heat of the moment I said things that I later regretted.

definition: This expression means to be in a situation where the outcomes can either be to win or to lose.
example: The budget division is a zero-sum game.

definition: When you hit the road, you begin a journey.
example: I know it’s morning, but we should be going. Let’s hit the road!

phrase: scare the living daylights out of someone
definition: If something scares the living daylights out of you, it terrifies you.
example: The screaming scared the living daylights out of me.

definition: This idiom means in the future, in a few years.
example: Somewhere down the road, I think she will make the business big.

definition: This expression refers to something that has happened and was so strange that one never thought it would happen.
example: Never in my wildest dreams did I think she’d return home.

definition: A person with a plastic smile is wearing a forced smile which makes them appear happier than they really are.
example: The receptionist greeted us with a plastic smile.

definition: If a person goes from rags to riches, they start off being very poor and become very rich and successful.
example: By working hard, she finally went from rags to riches.

definition: This idiom means to do something quickly before you run out of time.
example: I managed to beat the clock and complete the task.

definition: If a person bends the rules, they change the rules in order to help somebody.
example: Ok! I will bend the rules for you, but only this time.

definition: This idiom refers to something that has a physique or structure that is strong and physically imposing.
example: Take my car, it’s built like a tank!

definition: If you have a lump in your throat, you have a tight feeling in your throat because of a strong emotion such as sadness or gratitude.
example: The graduation speech was so touching that we had a lump in our throats.

definition: If something makes your blood boil, it makes you really angry.
example: His attitude made my blood boil!

definition: If you tell someone to “get their act together”, you mean that they need to organize their affairs more effectively in order to be more successful.
example: You’d better get your act together if you want to find a better job!

definition: A person who is not just a pretty face is not only attractive but intelligent or talented as well.
example: I’ve realized that Nicole is not just a pretty face.

definition: If someone tells you to step on the gas, they are encouraging you to accelerate or hurry up in order to get something done quickly.
example: We need the report in one hour. Let’s step on the gas!

definition: If you are dead set against something, you are strongly opposed to it.
example: I wanted a cat but my girlfriend was dead set against the idea.

definition: This idiom means to perform to the best of your ability.
example: This is an important match for us. Bring your A game, players!

definition: This idiom refers to an event that triggers a sense of urgency or the motivation to make a change.
example: Her chest pain was the wake-up call she needed to see a doctor.

definition: When a person is so madly in love with somebody that they can’t see the persons faults or negative characteristics.
example: You explain it to him in vain. He is blinded by love.

definition: The term refers to something that will have effect over or after a long period of time.
example: Learning German is going to be difficult, but it’ll be worth it in the long run.

phrase: champagne taste on a beer budget
definition: Someone who likes expensive things that they cannot afford has champagne taste on a beer budget.
example: John borrows money to buy expensive car parts – champagne taste on a beer budget!

phrase: hang / hold on for dear life
definition: If you hang/hold on for dear life, you grip something firmly so as not to fall.
example: I took my girlfriend on the back of my motorbike where she hung on for dear life.

definition: This expression refers to a quick, automatic and sometimes emotional response.
example: Following the attack, the knee-jerk reaction was to bomb them back.

phrase: put money where your mouth is
definition: If you put your money where your mouth is, not only do you express your interest, but you give financial support to causes that you believe in.
example: If people are really interested in helping the poor, they should put their money where their mouth is.

definition: Someone who is snowed under has so many things to do, usually work, that they are unable to cope with it all.
example: Doctors and nurses are completely snowed under these days.

definition: To say the sky’s the limit means that there is no limit to the possibility of success or progress for someone or something.
example: Keep in mind that in this profession the sky is the limit.

definition: If you face your demons, you have the courage to confront your fears or some cause of anguish that you normally try to avoid.
example: Daniel has a problem with dogs. He should face his demons and play with one.

definition: If you go all out to achieve or obtain something, you make a great effort, using all possible strength and resources.
example: We went all out to finish the mission.

definition: Someone who is very wealthy or has access to great amounts of money is rolling in money.
example: They don’t have any financial problem. Their parents are rolling in money.

definition: To say that someone is back to square one means that they have not succeeded in what they were trying to do, so they have to start again.
example: When the plans were turned down, it was back to square one for the officer.

definition: If you relax a rule, treat a person less severely or allow someone to do something which is normally not permitted, you cut them some slack.
example: Our professors are very strict; I wish they would cut us some slack before the exams.

phrase: look or feel like a million dollars
definition: If you look or feel like a million dollars, you look or feel extremely good.
example: With a tan and a new suit, she looked like a million dollars.

definition: This expression refers to something that has a relaxing outcome.
example: You need to take a chill pill. This flight is safe.

definition: When you hit the hay/sack, you go to bed.
example: As soon as they reached the chalet, the girls hit the sack.

definition: This idiom means breathtakingly beautiful.
example: The woman was drop-dead gorgeous.

phrase: put the pedal to the metal
definition: When you put the pedal to the metal, you accelerate or make something go faster.
example: If we put the pedal to the metal, we will finish this project till tonight.

definition: This idiom refers to a short period of time.
example: I will fulfill this task in a New York minute.

definition: When something happens that in your opinion is not a cause for worry, you can say that you will not lose any sleep over it.
example: I’ve made a blunder today, but I won’t lose any sleep over it. Tomorrow I will solve it.

definition: This question is addressed to someone who is inexplicably silent.
example: Tell me the truth! Has the cat got your tongue?

definition: Although you don’t quite agree with someone, it’s their choice and you think they should do whatever makes them happy.
example: Are you going fishing? Well, whatever floats your boat.

definition: This is a disparaging term for an accountant or anyone who compiles statistics.
example: The bank offered me so much money that I accepted to be their bean counter.

definition: This idiom means to warn or alert someone about something.
example: Heads up! There’s a snake in the garden.

phrase: call the shots / call the tune
definition: The person who calls the shots or the tune is the one who makes all the important decisions and is in control of the situation.
example: He shows much authority but in fact it’s his wife who calls the shots.

definition: This is a very rude way of telling someone to stop doing something that you don’t like.
example: Cut the crap and tell us what really happened!

phrase: if it’s not one thing, it’s another
definition: This expression is used after more than one thing goes wrong.
example: The washing machine broke and now my smartphone is out of battery. If it’s not one thing, it’s another…

phrase: a hard / tough nut to crack
definition: This idiom refers to a person, thing, situation or problem that is particularly difficult to understand, solve or deal with.
example: I’ve been dating her for two months and I still believe she’s a tough nut to crack.

definition: When you are excessive in your efforts to be helpful or generous, you can harm someone or kill them with kindness.
example: He is overweight, but his mother continues to give him chocolates – she will kill him with kindness!

definition: listening very attentively.
example: It’s obvious that I want to know – I’m all ears!

definition: This idiom means to pointlessly try to convince a person or group to accept an opinion that they already agree with.
example: Speaking about this project is like preaching to the choir.

phrase: there’s no such thing as a free lunch
definition: This expression means that nothing is free. If somebody helps you, they always expect some form of payment in return.
example: If you accept it, she will ask some favours in time. There’s no such thing as a free lunch!

definition: If a person or organisation jumps on the bandwagon, they decide to do something when it is already successful or fashionable.
example: When eco-coffee became fashionable, certain stores were quick to jump on the bandwagon and promote it.

definition: If you paint the town red, you go out and enjoy a lively evening in bars, night-clubs etc.
example: To celebrate her birthday, she painted the town red.

definition: This expression means to continue to stay awake when feeling exhausted.
example: I haven’t slept for twenty hours and I’m running on fumes.

definition: If you shoot yourself in the foot you do or say something which is against your own interests.
example: Be careful not to shoot yourself in the foot during this interview.

definition: This means to supply missing words or information (this can be used in conversation or writing).
example: Could you fill in the blanks for me, please?

definition: This idiom means that other people are free to like different things or have different preferences.
example: I don’t care about tennis, but to each their own.

definition: A person who is on cloud nine is very happy because something wonderful has happened.
example: When the director announced my promotion, I was on cloud nine!

definition: This phrase is a defiant challenge for an adversary to escalate a dispute.
example: You don’t like my work? So sue me!

definition: This idiom means to love someone very much.
example: I was prepared to do anything for her. I loved her to death.

definition: If you drop a bombshell, you make an unexpected announcement which will greatly change a situation.
example: I don’t like to be in this position and drop a bombshell, but the company is going downhill.

definition: When someone is in a race against time, they have to work very quickly in order to do or finish something before a certain time.
example: Sorry, I can’t talk to you now. I’m in a race against time.

definition: This idiom means to sniff an item of clothing or food to check if it might be suitable to wear or eat.
example: I wore this T-shirt two days ago. I gave it the sniff test and it was okay to be worn again.

definition: If you are caught with your pants down, you are caught doing something bad or forbidden.
example: He was caught fiddling with the water meter – caught with his pants down!

definition: This is an emphatic way of telling someone that what they are saying is absolutely correct, without doubt.
example: This is a bad time to leave a job, considering the economic context. Yes, you are dead right.

definition: This idiom is used in reference to a person’s ability to judge what is right and wrong and act accordingly.
example: Let’s ask him. He’s a veritable moral compass.

definition: If you report an illegal or socially-harmful activity to the authorities, and give information about those responsible for it, you blow the whistle or you are a whistle-blower.
example: Brian refused to blow the whistle on his boss for fear of losing his well-paid job.

definition: The expression means that it’s better to be too cautious than to be careless and have regrets later.
example: Let’s book plane tickets in advance – better safe than sorry!

phrase: at the top of your lungs
definition: If you shout at the top of your lungs, you shout as loudly as you possibly can.
example: That moment I was utterly scared. Therefore, I shouted at the top of my lungs.

definition: A smoking gun is a piece of evidence or the indisputable sign of someone’s guilt.
example: The fingerprints were the smoking gun that enabled the police to arrest them.

definition: This expression means to stop or slow down an activity.
example: The man insulted my mother, so I had to put the brakes on.

definition: If you turn the tables on a person or organisation, you reverse the situation so as to be in a position of superiority.
example: The success of our new car has turned the tables.

definition: Something that is a stone’s throw away is just a short distance away.
example: The local shop is a stone’s throw away.

definition: This idiom refers to a subject about which one is ignorant or biased.
example: Foreign languages are her blind spot.

definition: If a person or organisation has a hidden agenda, they have hidden interests or ulterior motives.
example: I can’t guarantee that they don’t have a hidden agenda. Be careful!

definition: If someone goes off the rails, they go out of control and begin to behave in a manner that is unacceptable to society.
example: They are lucky that none of their children went off the rails, given nowadays temptations.

definition: When you get the hang of an activity, you understand how to do it correctly.
example: I found the job difficult at first but I soon got the hang of it.

definition: This expression means that a particular opportunity has passed by and now it’s too late.
example: Sorry, that ship has sailed – you missed the promotion this year.

definition: This idiom refers to the anticipation of the weekend after a hard working week.
example: I’m ready for a few beers at the pub – I’ve got that Friday feeling.

definition: If you bend the truth, you say something that is not entirely true.
example: Ok, she bent the truth a bit. She told him that it was her natural hair colour.

phrase: pull a rabbit out of a hat
definition: This means to do something unexpected that may have seemed impossible.
example: My business partner pulled a rabbit out of his hat and we got a new contract.

definition: This idiom means extremely, offensively rich.
example: She is stinking rich and that’s why so many people hate her.

definition: If a person asks you to bear something in mind, they are asking you to remember it because it is important.
example: You must bear in mind that the cost of living is higher in Paris.

phrase: off the top of your head
definition: To say something off the top of your head means that you are giving an immediate reaction and not a carefully considered opinion, so it might not be correct.
example: How much do you think it cost? Well, off the top of my head, I would say around $2000.

definition: If you concentrate on something in an effort to understand, you wrap your brain around it.
example: I need this project to be finished as soon as possible so please wrap your brain around it.

definition: This idioms means to look at all the possibilities and then to make a final decision.
example: At the end of the day, I decided to start the law school.

definition: If you make a scene, you cause a disturbance.
example: I know that she is here with her new lover, but don’t make a scene.

definition: The expression is used as a reaction to something you find amazing or difficult to understand.
example: He crossed the Atlantic all alone – can you imagine that? My mind boggles!

definition: This phrase means to help somebody.
example: Could you give me a hand with this project?

definition: This idiom refers to someone who is rich beyond measure.
example: He is a filthy rich guy.

definition: This idiom means to keep a part of one’s life hidden, especially a part that would not be approved of.
example: For years, she has led a double life.

definition: This idiom means to begin or cause something to begin.
example: I’m going to kick-start the party with some wine.

definition: This is a more emphatic version of “absolutely”.
example: Would I want to go to the party? Abso-bloody-lutely!

definition: This idiom means “automatically thinking or behaving in a particular way”.
example: Babies are hard-wired to pay attention to anything that is brightly colored.

definition: If you do a roaring trade, your business is very successful.
example: Dentists are doing a roaring trade these days.

definition: This expression means all the people, collectively and individually.
example: I don’t want all and sundry to know about us.

definition: A person who calls a spade a spade speaks openly and truthfully about something, especially difficult matters.
example: What I like about the new colleague is that he calls a spade a spade. Therefore, he makes things so much easier for everyone.

definition: This expression refers to the activities of spies and undercover agents.
example: Do we need to go for cloak-and-dagger way?

definition: If something comes thick and fast, it comes in rapid succession with little time to respond between events. It may refer to physical objects, like raindrops or non-physical, like commands.
example: The orders were coming thick and fast.

definition: This idiom means to terrify someone.
example: That horror movie curdles my blood so badly…

definition: If you cut things fine, you leave barely enough time to do something.
example: You’re counting just an hour between the hotel and the train station – isn’t that cutting things a little bit fine?

definition: If you begin something enthusiastically, without thinking about the possible consequences, you dive in headfirst.
example: She accepted the project without a thorough analysis. She always dives in headfirst.

definition: If someone gets pink-slipped, it means that they are dismissed from employment.
example: Marry is quite sad. She got pink-slipped two days ago.

definition: If something goes for a song, it is sold at an unexpectedly low price.
example: I was able to buy the motorcycle because it was going for a song.

definition: When you grease the skids, you facilitate something or smooth the way for its success.
example: A little snack was organized before the meeting in order to grease the skids for the talks.

definition: If you harp on about something, you tire others by talking continuously and tediously about it.
example: My wife is always harping on about my job.

definition: To say that one person is head and shoulders above the others means that they are much better than the rest of them.
example: The winner was head and shoulders above the competitors.

definition: A person who has their heart in their mouth feels extremely anxious or nervous faced with a dangerous or unpleasant situation.
example: I had my heart in my mouth when I saw that snake.

definition: If you hit/strike pay dirt, you are lucky and suddenly find yourself in a successful money-making situation.
example: I finally hit pay dirt with my store.

definition: If you tell somebody some home truths, you tell them some unpleasant facts about themselves.
example: She needs to be told some home truths. It will help her.

definition: Feel annoyed, indignant or embarrassed.
example: If you contradict him, he gets hot under the collar.

definition: This idiom means in a superior or advantageous position.
example: I like to be in the catbird seat, I have to admit.

definition: A person who licks or smacks their lips is showing that they are excited about something and are eager for it to happen.
example: She was licking her lips at the idea of the car she was going to buy.

definition: This expression refers to a period of time after an illness or accident which could have caused death.
example: After a major surgery, most patients feel that they are living on borrowed time.

definition: This idiom means to cope with something even though the circumstances are not ideal.
example: We will have to make do with the new guy in our team.

definition: If you make the right noises, you behave as if you support or agree with something by making suitable or conventional remarks.
example: She seemed to approve of our idea; she made the right noises.

definition: This saying expresses the belief that being the most powerful person or country gives you the right to do whatever you want.
example: There are many managers who believe that might is right.

definition: a way of describing an older woman who is dressed in a style that is more suitable for a younger woman:
example: This style doesn’t suit Nicole – she looks like mutton dressed as lamb.

definition: To say that someone or something is no great shakes means that they are useless, ineffective or not very good.
example: Overall, she is a good actress, but her last film was no great shakes.

definition: Something that does not show the true value of someone or something, does not do justice to them/it.
example: This picture doesn’t do them justice; they are taller.

definition: A situation or person who stays on an even keel manages to remain calm, stable and untroubled in all circumstances.
example: I find it hard to keep my life on an even keel this period.

phrase: one swallow does not make a summer
definition: This phrase means that you should not assume that something is true just because you have seen one piece of evidence for it.
example: I got a good grade on this exam! Well, one swallow does not make a summer.

definition: If you pack something in, you abandon it or give it up.
example: I found city life so stressful that I decided to pack it in and move to the countryside.

definition: To roll out the red carpet means to give special treatment to an important visitor.
example: The general manager is going to roll out the red carpet.

definition: This idiom refers to somebody who runs very fast.
example: Have you seen the athlete? He runs like the wind.

definition: If you run the gamut of something, you cover the entire range of what is possible.
example: He has run the gamut of hotel work, from porter to owner of a large chain of hotels.

definition: Something that is second to none is excellent or much better than any other.
example: The food was second to none. Thank you!

definition: If you show somebody the ropes, you teach or explain to them how to do a particular job.
example: Oh, I’m sorry. The team leader is busy showing the ropes to the new trainee.

definition: A person who sits up and takes notice become alert and attentive.
example: The announcement of their wedding made everyone sit up and take notice.

definition: If you splash out on something, you spend a lot of money on it.
example: Her parents really splashed out on her birthday party.

definition: People who split hairs pay too much attention to differences that are very small or unimportant.
example: I don’t like her because she always splits hairs.

phrase: take a turn for the worse
definition: If a person who is ill takes a turn for the worse, their illness becomes more serious.
example: Unfortunately, she has taken a turn for the worse.

definition: When, in a difficult situation, you take things in your stride, you deal with the situation calmly and without any special effort.
example: When the accident was announced, John stayed calm and took it in his stride.

definition: If you take something lying down, you suffer as a result of an offensive act without reacting or protesting.
example: I won’t take this accusation lying down!

definition: This is a mythical land where we travel to so as to sleep.
example: Please be quiet. She’s in the land of nod now.

definition: When a person has difficulty understanding or realizing something, and then the penny drops, they finally understand.
example: They continued for some time until the penny dropped and the woman understood that it was a joke.

definition: To say that there wasn’t a soul means that there was nobody.
example: We thought the cinema would be crowded but there wasn’t a soul.

definition: If you are big headed, you are conceited or arrogant.
example: He’s big headed and that’s why I don’t like him at all.

definition: This idiom means “not enough of something that should have been provided earlier”.
example: The official described the aid for the refugees as too little, too late.

phrase: turn up like a bad penny
definition: If someone turns up like a bad penny, they appear at a place or event where they are not welcome or not wanted.
example: Wherever I go she turns up like a bad penny.

definition: If you can walk and chew gum (at the same time), you are able to do more than one thing at a time. Keep in mind that this expression is often used negatively.
example: She can’t walk and chew gum at the same time! I don’t know why she has been hired.

definition: This expression means to have a drink so as to celebrate the birth of a baby.
example: Our colleague invited us to a local bar to wet the baby’s head.

definition: When somebody visits a number of places quickly, only stopping at each for a short period of time, it is called a whistle-stop tour.
example: We’re going to visit her family but it will only be a whistle-stop tour.

definition: Someone who pretends to be your friend while actually betraying you is a snake in the grass.
example: She turned out to be just a snake in the grass.

definition: This idiom means to behave in a manner appropriate to your stage in life.
example: I wish she would act her age.

definition: A person who is afraid of his/her own shadow is very nervous or easily frightened.
example: I’ve never seen anyone so easily scared. Sarah is afraid of her own shadow.

definition: This idiom means to foreshadow a successful outcome, indicated by some circumstance or event.
example: The sales figures for the first months augur well for the rest of the year.

definition: This idiom means to be very hardworking, enthusiastic and/or skillful.
example: He’s no slouch when it comes to maintaining the company’s IT systems.

definition: If you blackball someone, you exclude them or ostracise them socially.
example: Bill has been blackballed after doing that horrible thing.

definition: This idiom refers to someone who makes things difficult for others and opposes their views for no good reason.
example: Why are you so bloody-minded today?

definition: When you butter someone up, you flatter them or you are very nice to them, especially if you want to obtain something.
example: She was so keen to get the contract that she spent much time buttering up the boss.

definition: If you buy something, especially a car, that is defective, unsatisfactory and constantly gives you trouble or stops running after a short time, you buy a lemon.
example: The motorcycle I bought was a real lemon. It broke down four weeks later.

definition: If you can’t stand the pace, you are unable to do things well when there is a lot of pressure.
example: He once worked for a famous company but he couldn’t stand the pace.

definition: This expression refers to an effort to do something which was a good attempt but not quite enough to succeed.
example: The ball almost entered the net – close but no cigar!

definition: If something happens, or is avoided or missed, with very little margin, it is called a close call.
example: He won the local election with 0.3% of the votes. It was a close call.

definition: To say that something may come in handy means that it may be useful some time.
example: Don’t throw away those old screwdrivers; they may come in handy one day.

definition: A person who has come up in the world is richer than before and has a higher social status.
example: My old faculty friend has bought an apartment overlooking Sibiu Central Park. He has clearly come up in the world.

definition: To say of someone that they are feathering their nest means that they are taking advantage of their position in order to obtain money and enjoy a comfortable life.
example: Many people think that politicians use their position to feather their nest.

definition: This idiom means to find a romantic partner for somebody.
example: I want to be single, so stop trying to fix me up with your female friends.

definition: When people get down to brass tacks, they start to discuss the essential aspects of a problem or situation.
example: After a few polite exchanges, we quickly got down to brass tacks.

definition: If you are able to pronounce a difficult word or phrase, you can get your tongue round it.
example: He’s from Ilafkaufpheleins. Try getting your tongue round that!

definition: This idiom means to do something thoroughly, enthusiastically or extravagantly.
example: They really went to town on their wedding.

definition: This phrase refers to a sign, warning of bad thing to come.
example: This was clearly a harbinger of doom.

definition: When someone hems and haws, they are very evasive and avoid giving a clear answer.
example: The little girl hemmed and hawed when the police officer asked her where she had spent the night.

definition: This idiom refers to a wealthy person or company who spends their money in a risky way, often by making risky investments that can offer large rewards.
example: If I were a high roller, I would invest in casinos.

phrase: hoist with / by your own petard
definition: This idiom means to be injured by the device that you intended to use to injure others.
example: Hoisted by his own petard. He deserves it!

definition: This expression means to be upset or angry about something.
example: Alice is in a huff because her boyfriend has just broken up with her.

definition: If you are in two minds about something, you have difficulty in deciding what to do.
example: I’m in two minds about whether or not to buy an apartment this year.

definition: If you continue driving when the traffic lights turn red, you jump the lights.
example: It’s not so dangerous to jump the lights if you pay attention.

phrase: lights on but no one home
definition: This is a humorous way of referring to someone who is lacking intelligence or sanity, or to someone who is simply preoccupied and not paying attention.
example: Forget about Nicole today – the lights are on but no one is home.

definition: This expression means everything or every single item.
example: Don’t worry. I’ve taken everything – lock, stock and barrel. Let’s go!

definition: A person who is long in the tooth is a bit too old to do something.
example: He’s a bit too old for a football player, isn’t he?

definition: This is something you say when advising someone to think carefully about the possible problems before doing something.
example: Don’t act too quickly. Look before you leap!

definition: This idiom means feeling very happy, loved by other people and loving other people, sometimes after taking drugs such as ecstasy.
example: He is just a loved-up guy. Don’t mind his words!

definition: This phrase refers to a minority group of adherents showing extreme support for a political movement or a set of beliefs.
example: They are bolstered by a lunatic fringe consisting of around two thousand people.

definition: If you make a beeline for something, you hurry directly towards it.
example: I was so thirsty that I made a beeline for a cold drink.

phrase: make a song and dance about something
definition: If someone complains in an annoying way or becomes unnecessarily excited about something unimportant, they make a song and dance about it.
example: I’ve understood. You don’t like apples. Don’t make a song and dance about it.

definition: This term refers to anything moderate or inoffensive that avoids extremes and appeals to the majority of people.
example: Mary is a middle-of-the-road artist. My father wouldn’t miss a show!

definition: When there is never a dull moment, something is always changing or happening.
example: I like my job because there’s never a dull moment.

definition: People who say this believe that it is better to do something now than leave it for later.
example: You should buy that car now. No time like the present!

definition: Someone who is on the mend is recovering after an illness or injury.
example: My uncle hasn’t been very well recently but he’s on the mend now.

definition: A place referred to as a one horse town is a small, boring town where nothing much ever happens.
example: I wish my parents didn’t live in that one-horse town.

phrase: pass over to the other side
definition: This phrase means to die.
example: Last week she passed over to the other side.

definition: A person who can put two and two together is capable of reaching the right conclusion based on the information they have.
example: There’s no need to help her. She can put two and two together.

definition: Someone who is anxious, runs a mile to avoid something.
example: He said he would run a mile if he saw her in the area.

definition: If someone siphons something off, they transfer something from one place to another, often illegally.
example: She siphoned off money from the business.

definition: When you take your cue from someone, you wait for a signal or follow someone’s example, so as to know what to do yourself or when to act.
example: The waiter took his cue from Steve and started serving the food.

definition: This idiom means the real thing – not a substitute.
example: I’ve got you the smartphone and it’s the real McCoy.

definition: This expression means that you are free and able to enjoy the pleasures and opportunities that life has to offer.

definition: This idiom means to be against someone or something.
example: The manager has stacked the deck against me.

definition: This idiom means to avoid someone or something.
example: Steer clear of the manager today – he’s yelling at everyone he sees.

definition: When you prevent a situation from deteriorating, especially in business or politics, you stop the rot.
example: A new marketing manager has been appointed to stop the rot.

definition: If you take a stand, you adopt a firm position on an issue and publicly declare whether or not you support it.
example: The liberal politician was asked to take a stand on that measure.

phrase: take the bread out of somebody’s mouth
definition: If you take the bread out of somebody’s mouth, you take away their means of earning a living.
example: The decision took the bread out of the mouths of many people.

definition: To refer to an event or action as the thin end of the wedge means that it is thought to be the beginning of something that will become more serious.
example: Economists say that outsourcing is just the thin end of the wedge.

definition: Someone who is thrilled to bits is extremely pleased about something.
example: She was thrilled to bits when she was selected for the final.

definition: To offer a worm’s eye view of a situation is to give your opinion based on what you see at close range from an inferior position, so it is therefore not a general view.
example: I can only offer you a worm’s eye view if that’s all right for you.

definition: Someone who speaks with an upper-class accent is said to have a plum in their mouth.
example: She speaks just like an aristocrat – with a plum in her mouth.

definition: This idiom refers to a discussion that is not supposed to be heard by others.
example: Then she told me as an aside that she was bored.

definition: completely flat.
example: The garden was as flat as a pancake.

definition: This idiom refers to someone who enters into an amorous relationship with a much younger person.
example: Anne can easily be called a baby snatcher as her lover is 26.

definition: A bar fly is someone who spends a lot of time drinking in bars and pubs.
example: You’ll find her at that newly-opened bar. She’s a real bar fly.

definition: This phrase means to make a speedy departure from a difficult situation rather than deal with it.
example: Cut and run is not a solution to this problem!

definition: This idiom means to spend your time doing a lot of things that are not important instead of the thing that you should be doing.
example: Stop faffing about! Do something useful!

definition: Something that is suitable for a particular function and is fully operational is said to be fit for purpose.
example: The manager promised that the gym would be ready on time and fit for purpose.

definition: If you get someone’s drift, you understand in a general way what they are trying to say.
example: Honestly, I didn’t understand all of it, but I got your drift.

definition: When you go the whole hog, you do something thoroughly or completely.
example: That Christmas, I put up some decorations but then I decided to go the whole hog and buy a tree.

definition: A person who has the makings of something has the qualities and potential that could be developed.
example: The teacher says Carla has the makings of an artist.

definition: A place where there are lots of things happening and everyone is very busy, is called a hive of activity.
example: When I entered the office there was a hive of activity.

definition: If an event or a situation is hunky-dory, it is very satisfactory and pleasant.
example: I’m very satisfied with this party. It’s hunky-dory.

definition: If you are in a rut, you have a monotonous and boring way of life.
example: If you feel you’re in a rut, why not look for a more challenging job?

definition: If you keep a level head, you remain calm and sensible no matter how difficult or distressful the situation may be.
example: All through the mission the officer kept a level head.

definition: This idiom means to treat someone roughly or disrespectfully.
example: It’s not fair to kick him around after what he has done for you!

definition: If turkeys were allowed to vote, they would never vote for Christmas because turkey is often eaten at Christmas. This expression is used to say that a particular option is unlikely to be chosen because it would be against the interests of the people concerned.
example: Accepting an increase of working hours would be like turkeys voting for Christmas.

definition: This means to find the time to do something that should take priority.
example: Everyone should make time for their children.

definition: This expression is used to let someone know to pay attention to what you are saying because it is very important especially when you are certain something would happen in future.
example: Mark my words, one day she will become a great businesswoman.

definition: A subject which gives rise to argument or debate is called a moot point.
example: Whether he did the project by himself or not is a moot point among colleagues.

definition: To say that a person’s name is mud means that they have acquired a bad reputation because of something they have done or said.
example: The president’s name is mud now after the article in the newspaper.

definition: If a person never misses a trick, they are very alert and aware of everything that is happening around them.
example: This street is safe. Our neighbour never misses a trick.

definition: This expression is used to indicate surprise at another person’s likes or dislikes.
example: He fell in love with a girl who is short, fat and poor … there’s no accounting for taste!

definition: A fact that is supposed to be a secret but is actually widely known is called an open secret.
example: It’s an open secret that they are living together.

definition: to take a subordinate, lesser, or more supportive role in relation to them
example: She liked to play second fiddle to the marketing director. She has learned a lot.

definition: A person who preaches to the converted is encouraging people to support an idea that they already agree with.
example: Talking to athletes about the benefits of sport is preaching to the converted.

definition: If you sleep like a log, you sleep deeply or soundly.
example: After a fishing day, I sleep like a log.

definition: If you stick to your guns, you show determination when faced with opposition.
example: I stick to my guns in spite of your opinion.

definition: This idiom is used when many people believe something that is not true.
example: I don’t believe her. It’s like the emperor’s new clothes.

phrase: the squeaky wheel gets the grease
definition: This idiom means that to get something fixed, it is required to make a noise so as to get attention.
example: In this competitive industry you should know that only the squeaky wheels gets the grease.

phrase: to start / get off on the right / wrong foot
definition: This expression means to start a relationship well or badly.
example: I was looking forward to working with you, but it seems we started off on the wrong foot.

definition: a situation is extremely uncertain, risky, or precarious, and the outcome could easily turn out badly
example:
Common Use Case: critical medical conditions (e.g., “His condition was touch and go after the surgery”)
tight financial situations (e.g., “It was touch and go whether the company would survive”), or close competitive events.

definition: If you are treading water, your situation remains stationary in spite of your efforts, with no sign of any progress.
example: I’ve been treading water this year, trying to find a better job.

definition: This idiom means to choose not to do what has been committed.
example: The customer has been given a commitment so we cannot turn back on the project now.

phrase: two can play at that game
definition: You say this to tell someone that you can behave towards them in the same unpleasant way that they have behaved towards you.
example: You should reconsider your behaviour. Don’t forget that two can play at that game.

definition: If one person walks all over another, they treat them very badly or unkindly, especially by showing no consideration for their cares or needs.
example: You must learn to express your opinion. Don’t let her walk all over you!

definition: If something is or falls wide off the mark, it is incorrect or inadequate, or it is not what was expected.
example: Your price offer is wide off the mark.

definition: This is a rude way to tell somebody to be quiet and / or calm down.
example: Wind your neck in! You’ve made enough troubles already.

phrase: wish the ground would swallow you up
definition: When you are so embarrassed by something that you would like to disappear, you wish the ground would swallow you up.
example: When I realized what I had done, I wished the ground would swallow me up.

definition: If two people or groups have a running battle with each other, they argue or disagree about something over a long period of time.
example: There’s been a running battle between the local authorities and citizens over the parking lots.

definition: A person who has a lot of friends and acquaintances and likes to flit from one social event to another is called a social butterfly.
example: Nicole is a social butterfly.

definition: If a situation, business or person is described as above board, it is open, honest and legal.
example: There aren’t secret negotiations within this company. Our dealing have always been above board.

definition: If someone is as keen as mustard, they are very eager, enthusiastic or motivated.
example: We should ask him to join our department. He’s as keen as mustard.

definition: This expression means that something is comfortably and cozily warm, especially when the weather outside is very cold.
example: The house should be as warm as toast by the time we get there.

definition: This idiom refers to a political contest in which the result is influenced by personality and image more than by policy.
example: These debates are just PR tactics – nothing more than beauty parades.

definition: This idiom means to say things that make your own self look good.
example: I don’t like people who are always blowing their own trumpet.

definition: If the authorities crack down on something, they enforce the law by taking severe measures to restrict undesirable or criminal actions.
example: To reduce road fatal accidents, it has been decided to crack down on speeding.

definition: If something is given or done for good measure, it is given or done in addition to other things.
example: They offered me a good wage and a company car for good measure.

definition: If you deliberately isolate someone or prevent them from participating in a social or business activity by treating them unfairly or harshly, you freeze them out.
example: That’s not ok. She has been frozen out of the project and we have to find a solution.

phrase: from the sublime to the ridiculous
definition: If something goes from the sublime to the ridiculous, it deteriorates in quality from serious or admirable to absurd or unimportant.
example: This situation is going from the sublime to the ridiculous.

definition: A business which is conducted in a deceitful, dishonest or unethical manner is called funny business.
example: We’ve got some suspicions about that firm. We think it’s a funny business.

definition: If someone or something goes into overdrive, they begin to work very hard or start to perform intensely.
example: As I had little time to finish the book, I went into overdrive.

definition: People who go to extremes behave in a way that lacks moderation.
example: My wife goes to extremes when it comes to holidays. She spends a lot of money on holidays.

definition: If you make or lose money hand over fist, you make or lose a lot of money very quickly.
example: Business was good and we were making money hand over fist.

definition: This idiom means to frown because you are thinking carefully or because you are angry or worried.
example: She knitted her brows in concentration.

definition: If someone knuckles down to something, they start to work on it seriously.
example: If you want to implement this project, you’ll have to knuckle down to some serious work.

definition: If a situation is nip and tuck, someone or something in that situation comes very close to failing or ending.
example: For several years it was nip and tuck, but I managed to pull the company out of bankruptcy.

definition: This idiom means to find a companion.
example: Let’s partner up and dance to the rhythm.

definition: This idiom means very hot, usually referring to food.
example: This pizza is piping hot.

phrase: put on a brave face / a bold face
definition: If you put on a brave or bold face, you pretend that something upsetting or worrying is not as unpleasant as it really is.
example: When I was fired, I put on a brave face and announced that I would easily find a better-paid job.

definition: If something is smack dab in the middle, it is right in the centre.
example: I couldn’t hide the stain on my suit. It was smack dab in the middle.

definition: This idiom means to make someone or something cleaner and tidier or to improve his, her or its appearance generally.
example: I’d have a shave and generally spruce myself up for the interview.

definition: This idiom means to discuss something honestly and directly.
example: Ok, let’s talk turkey! What do you want from me?

definition: This term means after midnight or the very early hours of the day.
example: I worked until the small hours on my project.

definition: This idiom refers to actions done intentionally to punish other people because they have done something unpleasant to you.
example: He strongly believes in tit for tat and will do the same thing to you if you do something wrong to him.

definition: A person who is getting too big for their boots is behaving as if they were more important than they really are.
example: Simon is really getting too big for his boots since he got a promotion.

definition: If someone is waiting in the wings, they are waiting for an opportunity to take action, especially to replace someone else in their job or position.
example: There are many students waiting in the wings ready to prove themselves.

definition: This idiom means rich.
example: Out family is well heeled.

phrase: your sins will find you out
definition: This expression means that things you do wrong will become known.
example: He usually cheats his customers by selling duplicate material. His sins will find him out one day.

definition: This expression means “all that stuff”, “other similar things” or “everything of that kind”.
example: Let’s get out the tinsel, the lights and all that jazz to decorate the Christmas tree.

definition: This simile means very cold.
example: You are as cold as stone. What’s the matter?

definition: If something, especially meat, is as tough as old boots, it is hard to cut and difficult to chew.
example: The steak was as tough as old boots. This expression can also refer to a person who is strong either physically or in character.

definition: To say that someone is a bag of bones means that they are extremely thin.
example: When she came home from university she was a bag of bones.

phrase: bite off more than you can chew
definition: If you bite off more than you can chew, you try to do something that is too difficult for you, or more than you can manage.
example: As soon as I started to translate the financial report, I realized that I had bitten off more than I could chew.

definition: If you participate in negotiations and bring nothing to the table, you have nothing of interest to offer the other side.
example: We won’t reach an agreement if you don’t bring something to the table.

definition: If you chime in, you interrupt or join a conversation, especially to repeat or agree with something.
example: As I explained to the police officer what had happened, the other men chimed in and gave their version.

definition: This idiom means to return to an earlier position or decision.
example: After changing more jobs, Jane came full circle in her first company.

definition: This idiom means to pay the bill.
example: Don’t be angry. I will foot the bill for you.

definition: This idiom means in effect or for all practical purposes.
example: For all intents and purposes, the project is completed.

definition: This expression is used when a player intends to shoot into the goal but hits the crossbar or the post of the goal instead.
example: He almost had it! It hit the woodwork…

definition: To say that a person, a business or the economy in general is in the doldrums, it means that the situation is gloomy and that nothing new is happening.
example: Despite the recent economic measures taken by the government, the economy is in the doldrums.

definition: Something that is in the offing is likely to appear or happen soon.
example: A new law on labour conditions is in the offing.

definition: When you knock sense into somebody, you use strong words or methods in order to make that person stop behaving stupidly.
example: When she announced that she was going to drop out of university, her mother managed to knock some sense into her.

phrase: like a hole in the head
definition: This expression means to have absolutely no need for something.
example: I need a new friend like a hole in the head.

phrase: like two peas in a pod
definition: To say that two people are like two peas in a pod means that they are very similar in appearance.
example: It wasn’t difficult to identify the sisters – they were like two peas in a pod.

definition: A person who is at a loose end has some spare time and feels quite bored by having nothing in particular to do.
example: When the meeting was cancelled I found myself at a loose end.

definition: An activity which is organised in a deceitful or dishonest way is called monkey business.
example: The results seem suspicious – I believe there’s some monkey business going on.

phrase: nail your colours to the mast
definition: This idiom means to defiantly display one’s opinions and beliefs. Also, it means to show one’s intention to hold on to those beliefs until the end.
example: What do you think about it? It’s easy for you to answer as you are always nailing your colours to the mast.

definition: When you are one step ahead of someone else, you achieve something faster than they do or have an advantage over them.
example: We’ve always tried to be one step ahead of our competitors.

definition: If you paddle your own canoe, you do what you want to do without help or interference from anyone.
example: She decided to paddle her own canoe and set up her own business.

definition: If you pay lip service to an idea or cause, you give verbal support or approval, but fail to actually do anything.
example: This company is paying lip service to the promotion of women’s rights.

phrase: put in a good word for someone
definition: If you put in a good word for someone, you say positive things in support of that person in order to help them.
example: I can help you. I will put in a good word for you.

definition: Someone who is quick or slow on the uptake is quick or slow to understand what is meant.
example: Don’t explain the problem again. I’m quick on the uptake!

definition: To refer to something, usually a place, as spick and span means that it is very clean, neat and tidy.
example: The flat must be spick and span before we rent it.

definition: To strain at the leash is to be enthusiastic to free oneself from the restrictions that bar one’s progress.
example: We are straining at the leash to get away. Help us!

definition: This expression means that there are many people in the world who are stupid or easily fooled.
example: "Too good to be true" deals are currentlyall over the Internet, providing proof that there is one born every minute.

definition: This idiom means to be the first to attack a sinner.
example: Why do you always want to cast the first stone?

definition: This phrase is used in expressions to mean completely full.
example: By the time the fifth course was served, I was stuffed to the gills.

definition: showing or accepting a person, place, or thing honestly, including all bad parts and mistakes.
example: He tried to paint the lady as she really was, warts and all.

definition: If you tell a white lie, you say something which is not true in order to protect someone or to avoid hurting their feelings.
example: I prefer to tell my wife a white lie so as to avoid useless discussions.

definition: A fly in the ointment refers to something that prevents a situation from being completely satisfactory.
example: My cousin’s poor English was a fly in the ointment when he applied for becoming an air traffic controller.

definition: If you bide your time, you wait for a good opportunity to do something.
example: She’s not hesitating. She’s just biding her time, waiting for the price to plummet.

definition: This idiom refers to something completely ordinary, without anything special added.
example: My last car was just a bog-standard model.

definition: This idiom means completely dry.
example: The soil is bone dry.

definition: If you drop someone a line, you write a letter to them.
example: This year I will drop them a line to wish them a Merry Christmas.

definition:
to get rid of something, cancel it, reject someone, or refuse to serve someonAmerican
Common in restaurants
example: Unfortunately, they have eighty-sixed that item.

definition: An idea, plan or project which is gathering dust is in fact stagnating or has not attracted attention for some time.
example: We should cancel that project. It has gathered too much dust!

definition: If you obtain something or manage to contact someone, you get hold of them.
example: I want to contact the network administrator. Do you know how could I get hold of him?

definition: If you give someone or something a quick visual examination to see what they are like or to check if everything is all right, you give them the once-over.
example: I gave the room a quick once-over before letting her in.

definition: This idiom refers to an ostentatiously virtuous or well-behaved person.
example: She was such a goody two shoes.

phrase: haul / rake someone over the coals
definition: If you haul / rake someone over the coals, you rebuke them harshly because they have done something wrong or incorrectly.
example: She was hauled over the coals for the poor quality of the project.

phrase: it is always darkest before the dawn
definition: This expression means that things are going to get better.
example: This won’t last for ever. It is always darkest before the dawn.

definition: This idiom means to get someone drunk.
example: Tonight I want to liquor her up and find more about her past.

phrase: march to the same tune / sing from the same songsheet
definition: This is used when everyone follows the same plan or says the same thing.
example: If we want to succeed with this robbery, we will have to march to the same tune.

definition: During a course of action, if someone moves the goalposts they change the rules or conditions.
example: We’ve set the objectives for next year. Let’s hope the manager won’t move the goalposts.

definition: A no-go area is an area, particularly in a city, where it is dangerous to go.
example: Tourists have been advised to avoid no-go areas.

definition: to look around a place, often in order to find something
example: I caught him nosing around in my office.

definition: An informal test or leak of a proposal to see if people like it or push back against it
example: Before restructuring the entire department, the manager floated a trial balloon to see how the team would react to new roles

definition: If someone has to sink or swim, they have to do something alone, and their success or failure depends entirely on their own efforts.
example: This sink-or-swim attitude in the organisation can be very difficult for new employees.

definition: To ask someone if they have taken leave of their senses means that you think their behaviour is crazy.
example: You’re going fishing in such weather? Have you taken leave of your senses?

definition: This idiom refers to a priceless or valuable discovery.
example: Finding the ruins of the old city was his treasure trove.

definition: This idiom means to deliberately broadcast some news so everyone can hear, with the intent to boast about something.
