example: For three weeks I will trumpet our promotion.

definition: This idiom means to win a war, a fight or a competition.
example: Our team win the day in the debate.

definition: This means incomprehensible, as Greek is to someone who cannot speak it.
example: Steve says the machine isn’t so puzzling, but it’s all Greek to me.

definition: An isolated place located far from any town is said to be in the back of beyond.
example: It took me hours to find Maria’s house. She lives in the back of beyond.

definition: If you blow hot and cold about something, you constantly change your opinion about it.
example: The manager keeps blowing hot and cold about the marketing campaign – one day she finds it excellent, the next day he wants to make changes.

definition: If you cash in your chips, you sell something, especially shares, either because you need the money or because you think the value is going to fall.
example: Adrian cashed in his chips as soon as business started to slow down.

definition: When you have your day in the sun, you get long-awaited attention or some form of well-deserved appreciation.
example: Steven got his day in the sun when his study was published.

definition: When you drop names, you mention the names of famous people you know or have met in order to impress others.
example: I hate when she starts dropping names! It’s completely useless.

definition: A field day refers to a day or period of great excitement and activity.
example: We’ll have a field day with the latest crime suspect.

definition: This idiom refers to a criminal act that results in serious damage or injury, especially murder.
example: The police didn’t suspect foul play.

definition: If you get cold feet about something, you begin to hesitate about doing it; you are no longer sure whether you want to do it or not.
example: I wanted to enter the competition but when I found out that there was no prize I got cold feet.

definition: This expression means to get married.
example: Marry and Steve are getting hitched this weekend.

definition: People who are used as guinea pigs are people on whom new methods, treatments or ideas are tested.
example: They were asking for students to be guinea pigs in their marketing research.

definition: Someone who is high and mighty behaves in a haughty manner as though they were superior to others.
example: No, I don’t like her. She is high and mighty and I hate that.

definition: People who are holier-than-thou think that they are morally better than anyone else.
example: I can’t stand holier-than-thou people.

definition: This idiom means in a confused and excited state.
example: When economic forecasts are first published they put markets in a flutter.

definition: If something is in the balance, the situation is uncertain and it is not clear what is going to happen.
example: The future of this small store is in the balance as the sales are plummeting.

phrase: lie your way in / out of something
definition: If you obtain something or get out of a situation by telling lies, you lie your way in or out of it.
example: She lied her way into a very well-paid position.

definition: If you opt for the line of least resistance, you choose the easiest way of doing something.
example: I chose the line of least resistance and broke off her.

definition: a large task becomes easier and faster to finish when people work together
example: I’ve seen that many hands make light work when your group faces difficulties.

definition: Something described as a millstone around your neck refers to a problem or responsibility that becomes a burden and a source of worry.
example: I hope that the money I’ve borrowed won’t become a millstone around my neck.

definition: Something which is on the cards is very likely to happen.
example: An agreement between the parties is still on the cards.

definition: If you play footsie with someone, you tough their feet lightly, especially under the table, to show your sexual interest.
example: Steve played footsie with Ana at the office Christmas party.

definition: If someone prolongs the agony, they make an unpleasant or tense situation last longer than necessary.
example: Please, don’t prolong the agony. Just tell me what I have to do.

definition: This idiom means to finish or destroy something.
example: A knee injury has put paid to her career.

definition: This idiom means “easily influenced by someone else or excessively willing to do what someone else wishes”.
example: As soon as he learnt the truth from them, he became putty in their hands.

definition: If you reap the harvest, you benefit or suffer as a direct result of past actions.
example: When she won the championship, she reaped the harvest of all hard training.

definition: If you shop around, you visit a number of shops selling similar articles in order to compare the prices.
example: I like shopping around because this way I save money.

definition: When something such as a plan or project begins to take shape, it starts to become organised and acquire a definite form.
example: Our new office has begun to take shape.

definition: This idiom refers to the authorities.
example: The powers that be are assessing the crisis.

definition: This phrase is said when you want to emphasize that real events or things are sometimes stranger than imaginary ones.
example: Have you heard about their sexual adventure? Well, truth is stranger than fiction.

definition: If someone is up and about, they are out of bed or have recovered after an illness or an injury.
example: She is up and about now. You can visit her.

definition: When you wax lyrical about something, you speak enthusiastically about it in a poetic or sentimental way.
example: Suddenly he started to wax lyrical about good old days.

definition: Two or more groups or organisations who are in complete agreement are said to speak with one voice.
example: The local council and local stores are speaking with one voice.

definition: If you say that something is a necessary evil, you don’t like it but you understand that it has to exist and be accepted.
example: Vaccination is a necessary evil if you want to travel to Brazil.

phrase: beat / knock the (living) daylights out of someone
definition: If a person beats the (living) daylights our of another, they hit them very hard and repeatedly.
example: “If I catch you stealing again I’ll beat the daylights out of you!”, she yelled at him.

definition: This idiom refers to a husband or a wife.
example: I think a house would suit us better, but I will ask my better half too.

definition: to achieve victory, win a competition, or successfully prevail in a debate, struggle, or election
example: The team carried the day well.

definition: When a person or activity cranks/gets into gear, they start to work or become effective.
example: Immediately after the announcement regarding the promotion, the workers cranked into gear.

definition: This idiom means to talk or writing that is nonsense.
example: Nothing can be understood from this. It’s double Dutch.

definition: If someone has a face like thunder, they look very angry.
example: She entered the office having a face like thunder.

definition: If something you say falls on deaf ears, it is either ignored or attracts no attention.
example: Her warning about the need to repair the car fell on deaf ears.

definition: If a person, usually someone in difficulty, goes from pillar to post, they move constantly from place to place.
example: When I decided to make a career change, I moved from pillar to post in search of a challenging job.

definition: When you get cracking, you start doing something immediately.
example: I’d better get cracking on the mission analysis.

phrase: get something out of your system
definition: This expression means that you get rid of a strong emotion or desire by expressing it openly or trying to fulfill it.
example: Oh, come on. Tell me what you are thinking about. Get it out of your system!

definition: If someone gets the sack, they lose their job, usually because they have done something wrong.
example: You are lucky if you just get the sack. Don’t forget that you have stolen from them.

definition: To say that somebody is in hot water means that they have done something wrong and people are angry with them.
example: I’ve been in hot water since she discovered that I had lied to her.

definition: Someone who lives out of a suitcase travels a lot, moving from place to place, and is therefore restricted to the contents of their suitcase.
example: My job involves much travelling so I live out of a suitcase.

definition: Something which is neither here nor there is considered to have no effect on the situation.
example: You like her, but that’s neither here nor there. We are talking about her results which aren’t good.

definition: If you are off colour, you look or feel ill.
example: What’s the matter with John? He looks a bit off colour today.

definition: An effort to redress the balance is an attempt to make things equal.
example: With too few women applying for public jobs, the authorities declared that an effort would be made to redress the balance.

definition: Something which is rough and ready is adequate but rather rudimentary or unrefined.
example: The chalet is rough and ready but the landscape is fantastic!

definition: A person who is good-natured but lacks polished manners and/or education is said to be a rough diamond.
example: She’s a great girl but a bit of a rough diamond!

definition: This idiom means to calm down after anger or excitement.
example: Let it go and simmer down now! It’s over.

definition: If you stem the tide of something, you stop the development of something bad or undesirable.
example: The authorities seem unable to stem the tide of violence in the outskirts.

definition: If something you say strikes or hits a raw nerve, it upsets someone because they are very sensitive about the subject.
example: You hit a raw nerve when you mentioned that disease. She is ill.

definition: If you talk shop, you talk about your work or business in a social situation with someone you work with, and thus you make the conversation boring for the others present.
example: We ended up talking shop at the date.

phrase: those who can, do; those who can’t, teach
definition: This is a very famous phrase for teachers everywhere, but perhaps not for the right reasons. The phrase implies that teachers only do their profession because they weren’t good enough to do it as their main job.
example: No wonder she’s a teacher. Those who can, do; those who can’t, teach.

definition: If you are on your last legs, you are in a very weak condition or about to die.
example: I’m sorry to inform you that our grandmother is on her last legs.

definition: If something is up or down you alley, it is exactly the sort of thing that will suit your tastes or abilities.
example: Cristina loves reading, so the job in the library is right up her alley.

definition: If you do something with your eyes wide open, you are fully aware of what you are doing.
example: I took the mission with my eyes wide open so I’m not complaining.

definition: A dog and pony show is a marketing event or presentation which has plenty of style but not much content.
example: I though it would be an interesting campaign, but it turned out to be a dog and pony show.

definition: This means that something is very old. The expression is used often in exaggerated statements.
example: Their technology is as old as the hills.

phrase: as pure as the driven snow
definition: This simile means entirely pure.
example: The water was as pure as the driven snow.

definition: If you bare your soul / heart to someone, you reveal your innermost thoughts and feelings to them.
example: Maria couldn’t keep things to herself any longer. She decided to bare her heart / soul to me.

definition: This phrase refers to someone with no friends.
example: He is a Billy no-mates.

definition: This humorous expression means that you are wearing nothing.
example: The bathroom door opened suddenly and there she was in her birthday suit.

definition: If you change what people expect from a (traditional) situation, especially by doing something original, you break the mould.
example: After generations of farmers in the family, he broke the mould by becoming a medical doctor.

definition: This expression means to rudely tell someone to be quiet.
example: Button it! I’m trying to solve this puzzle.

definition: In a business relationship, if you clinch a deal, you reach agreement on a proposal or offer.
example: My final argument enabled our company to clinch the deal.

definition: If a remark or comment is close to home, it is so true, or it affects you so directly, that you feel uncomfortable.
example: She appears embarrassed. His comment must have been close to home.

definition: This idiom means no comfort or consolation at all.
example: I know that there is somebody stupider than me, but that’s cold comfort.

definition: If something covers or hides a multitude of sins, it prevents others from seeing the less pleasant reality.
example: Loose-fitting clothes can be tricky as they cover a multitude of sins!

definition: If you cut your own throat, you do something that will be the cause of your own failure or ruin your chances in the future.
example: She has already missed a lot of German classes. She’s cutting her own throat.

definition: When someone is down in the mouth, they look unhappy, discouraged or depressed.
example: Hey! You look down in the mouth. What has happened?

phrase: get blood out of a stone
definition: This expression refers to something that is very difficult to obtain.
example: Negotiating a discount from that company is like getting blood from a stone!

definition: If a project or activity gets off the ground, it starts to be successful.
example: Bluntly speaking, I don’t consider that this project will ever get off the ground.

definition: If someone or something gets short shrift, they are given little attention or sympathy.
example: When Marry is very busy, she gives short shrift to anybody.

definition: When you are determined to do something in spite of the difficulties involved, you grit your teeth.
example: We had to grit our teeth and agree with their conditions because we wanted that contract.

definition: A person who has a new lease of life has a chance to live longer or with greater enjoyment or satisfaction.
example: Moving closer to his friends has given the man a new lease of life.

phrase: not give the time of day
definition: If you dislike someone so strongly that you ignore them and refuse to speak to them, you do not give them the time of day.
example: I dislike her boyfriend and I won’t give him the time of day.

definition: If you put something out of harm’s way, you put it in a safe place where it won’t be damaged.
example: I’m going to put your glasses out of harm’s way.

definition: If someone is out of sorts, they are upset and irritable or not feeling well.
example: The baby is out of sorts today.

definition: means to gain an advantage over someone by deceiving them.
example: The street vendor pulled a fast one while the customer was not paying attention.

definition: This idiom means to correct someone’s attitude, belief or behaviour, to make sure someone understands something correctly.
example: She told me an absurd thing, so I had to put her straight.

phrase: sticks and stones may break my bones
definition: This phrase is a response to an insult, implying that “you might be able to hurt me by physical force but not by insults”.
example: You are so stupid! Sticks and stones may break my bones…

definition: This expression means that a quiet person may have deep feelings or an interesting personality when one gets to know them.
example: Though she barely speaks in the meetings, still waters run deep.

definition: This idiom means that the process is underway.
example: The whistle has just been blown – the game is afoot.

definition: This idiom means overconfident in one’s importance, skill or authority; behaving as if one is more important or influential than one actually is.
example: Since she won the championship she has become too big for her britches.

definition: This expression refers to an event which people think will be exciting but which is disappointing when it happens.
example: The party was a damp squib.

definition: To refer to something as “the acid test” means that it will prove how effective or useful something is.
example: The training course was interesting but the acid test will come when we start the new job.

definition: If you say that you will do something come hell or high water, you mean that you will do it in spite of the difficulties involved.
example: I said that I would succeed, come hell or high water. And here I am!

definition: This idiom means to make plans based on events that may or may not happen.
example: It’s not good to start counting your chickens when you don’t have any money.

definition: Something that cuts both ways has both a positive and a negative effect at the same time.
example: Banning diesel cars in the town centre can cut both ways: less pollution but fewer customers in the shops.

definition: A plan or project that is dead in the water is at a standstill or has ceased to function and is unlikely to be reactivated in the future.
example: Because of the war, the planned housing development is dead in the water.

definition: Two or more people who are in collusion or work in close association, are said to be hand in glove.
example: After the competition, it was discovered that she was hand in glove with the referee.

definition: If you have influence or power over someone, you have them in your pocket.
example: Don’t worry. I have her in my pocket.

definition: If you do something in fits and starts, you do it in an irregular manner, often stopping and starting again.
example: You’ll never make much progress in German if you work at it in fits and starts.

definition: This idiom means in abundance; very much.
example: They have money in spades.

definition: This expression means to be completed.
example: More than eighty per cent of the project is in the can.

definition: If someone is left holding the baby, they are made responsible for a problem that others don’t want to deal with.
example: When that furious customer started to complain, I disappeared and left my colleague holding the baby.

phrase: not have a penny to one’s name
definition: This idiom means to be extremely poor, to have very little or no money to spend.
example: There was a time when I didn’t have a penny to my name.

definition: Something which is not up to scratch fails to reach the expected standard.
example: The quality of iron is not up to scratch. We’ll need to change our supplier.

definition: If someone pads the bill, they add false items to a bill or invoice in order to increase the total amount.
example: Check the invoice before paying – this store tends to pad the bill!

definition: The term pester power refers to the power children exert over their parents by continually nagging or pestering them until they accept to buy advertised toys or products.
example: Marketing specialists know how powerful pester power can be.

definition: The price you have to pay is what you have to endure in return for something you gain or achieve.
example: This is the price you have to pay for obtaining the position.

phrase: take the sting out of something
definition: If you take the sting out of something, you manage to reduce the severity or unpleasantness of something.
example: A relaxing voice can take the sting out of bad news.

definition: If you are tongue-tied, you have difficulty in expressing yourself because you are nervous or embarrassed.
example: At the beginning of the date I was tongue-tied.

definition: This idiom refers to a woman’s much younger male lover.
example: She set up house with a 22-year-old toy-boy. That’s strange, isn’t it?

definition: This term refers to a clever or expert way of doing things, especially a job.
example: She is a good negotiator; she knows the tricks of the trade.

definition: If you twist someone’s arm, you make them do something that they might not want to, without using physical force.
example: I had to twist her arm so as to accept my offer.

definition: This term is a humoristic way of referring to someone who is not very tall.
example: Basketball is not a game for vertically challenged people.

definition: This idiom refers to the particular time when a crucial act is supposed to take place.
example: The military forces were waiting for the zero hour to start the operation.

definition: This idiom means a fight.
example: There has been a dust up in this place.

definition: When something is “all the rage”, it has become very popular or trendy.
example: Sending Facebook messages is all the rage these days, both among individuals and companies.

definition: If you use your bag of tricks to do something, you try all the clever methods you know in order to succeed.
example: Let’s call on Sophia and her bag of tricks. Maybe she can help us out.

definition: This idiom refers to a difficult position from which it is unlikely one can escape.
example: With all the pressure and credits, he is behind the eight ball.

definition: This expression refers to a very angry argument, a big fight or a big quarrel.
example: After having a blazing row with Ann, he stormed out of the room.

definition: If you blow your top, you suddenly become very angry.
example: When my father saw the state of the house after the party, he blew his top.

definition: In a situation which has deteriorated, if you claw your way back, you gradually regain your former position through determination, energy and hard work.
example: After a serious accident, the player clawed his way back to the top.

definition: This idiom literally means to be too tired to do any more.
example: I am done in for today.

definition: If you drop someone or something like a hot potato, you leave them or immediately stop associating with them.
example: She dropped me like a hot potato and I don’t even know why.

definition: This idiom means to put every resource into getting a particular result.
example: The team needed a goal so they went for broke to score.

definition: A person who goes off the deep end becomes suddenly very angry or emotional.
example: She started throwing things around the office. She really went off the deep end.

definition: If someone goes postal, they lose their temper and express their anger in a violent way.
example: My husband will go postal when he sees the state of the car.

definition: This idiom refers to working hours that extend overnight.
example: We are on shift-work. One week of days and then one on the graveyard shift.

definition: If you memorize or practise something until you know it perfectly or have it exactly right, you have it down pat.
example: I rehearsed the song until I had it down pat.

definition: a controversial, sensitive, or difficult issue that no one wants to handle or take responsibility for
example: The new manager hasn’t been confronted with any hot potato yet.

definition: If something has someone’s name written on it, it is intended for that person or it is ideally suited to them.
example: That suit would be perfect for you – it has your name written on it!

definition: This idiom refers to someone who might claim to be of good behaviour but has in fact a sordid past.
example: She was critical of the new girls, but she is no saint.

definition: This expression means to bear the ill-effects of something that was enjoyable at one time.
example: She took my services, but now refuses to pay the piper.

definition: After a disastrous event, if you pick up the pieces you do what you can to get the situation back to normal again.
example: After the flood destroyed our house, it took us a long time to pick up the pieces.

definition: If you do something to prevent a plan or activity from happening or developing, you put the kibosh on it.
example: The rain put the kibosh on my plan.

definition: To say that there are smoke signals means that there are indications that something is probably going to happen.
example: All the smoke signals seem to indicate that the business is going to be bankrupt soon.

definition: A person, usually a man, who sows their wild oats, goes through a period of carefree pleasure-seeking while they are young.
example: I advised him to sow his wild oats before he got married.

definition: If you spin a yarn, you tell a story, usually a long improbable one, with distorted truths.
example: She failed the exam and spun a yarn about it.

definition: When people stand on ceremony, they behave in a very formal way.
example: Don’t stand on ceremony! It’s not necessary.

definition: If you step out of line, you do something unacceptable or break the rules.
example: Be careful not to step out of line!

definition: This term refers to secrecy of a company’s production methods but is often used teasingly.
example: Can you give me the recipe for this delicious cake? No, it’s a trade secret.

definition: This idiom means under someone’s control.
example: She has got the board firmly under her thumb.

definition: This idiom means that things sometimes go wrong, despite out best efforts.
example: Don’t be sad. Nobody was hurt. Accidents will happen.

phrase: be two / three sheets to the wind
definition: This idiom means drunk.
example: Margret was three sheets to the wind by the time I arrived to the party.

definition: If you bite your tongue, you try not to say what you really think or feel.
example: It was difficult for me not to react to her words; I had to bite my tongue.

definition: A discussion among a group of people who try to determine who or what is to blame for a particular mistake, failure or wrongdoing, is called blamestorming.
example: A blamestorming session took place following the poor reviews in the press.

definition: This idiom means “according to the information or reports that are available or from what people are saying”.
example: By all accounts, they should be dead right now!

definition: A person or company who carves out a niche concentrates on a particular segment of the market, to which they supply a product or service, and develop their expertise in that area.
example: In nowadays market it is better to carve out a niche and try to become the best in that area.

definition: If a problem or difficult situation comes to a head, it reaches a point where action has to be taken.
example: The quarrel between us came to a head yesterday.

definition: If you cramp someone’s style you do something to prevent them from behaving freely or performing to the best of their ability.
example: I can’t do it with people watching me – it cramps my style!

definition: This idiom refers to a cup of coffee.
example: Yes, I would like a cup of joe! Thank you!

definition: This idiom is used to tell someone to take action or to stop saying that they will.
example: The politician promised voters that he would support gun control. Now, it’s time to fish or cut bait!

definition: If you get/have the jitters, especially before an important event, you become very nervous or anxious and begin to shake.
example: I got the jitters when I had to make a speech in front of such a large audience.

definition: something is useful, beneficial, or helpful for a specific purpose or advantage
example: Don’t worry about the broken item. It’s grist to the mill for me.

definition: When a sports player hangs up their boots, they stop playing and retire. This expression is often used to refer to retirement in general.
example: Steve says he’s going to hang up his boots at the end of the year.

definition: You can say this when you think something should have been done already and is overdue.
example: It’s high time you finished the project.

definition: This idiom means to overcome an addiction, especially of an addiction like drugs.
example: He couldn’t kick the habit of drinking.

definition: This means to suffer a bad experience and know not to do it again.
example: I learnt my lesson to not make a joke at someone else’s expense many years ago.

phrase: like a dog with two tails
definition: If someone is like a dog with two tails, they are extremely happy.
example: She was like a dog with two tails when she was given that special award.

definition: If you lose your touch, you no longer have the ability to do something skillfully.
example: My grandmother used to make great pancakes but she has lost her touch.

definition: If you are on all fours, you are down on your hands and knees.
example: I don’t like being on all fours, but I must play with my child.

definition: When someone wants a piece of the action, they want to participate in what other people are doing and benefit from it.
example: The police officer wanted a piece of the action.

definition: This idiom means to suddenly become very active or busy.
example: With this contract I have springed to life.

definition: Someone who is as straight as an arrow is a morally upright person who is extremely honest.
example: You can leave the money here. He’s as straight as an arrow.

definition: If you tear a strip off someone, you reprimand them severely for doing something wrong.
example: The professor tore a strip off the student for not doing his homework.

definition: This idiom refers to a way of saying or describing something.
example: That was a nice turn of phrase. Congrats!

phrase: Left (s/o) to twist in the wind
definition: If someone is left to twist in the wind, they are left to face a difficult situation without any assistance or support.
example: After the meeting, I left my assistant manager to twist in the wind.

definition: This idiom refers to a issue that is the subject of continuous argument or controversy.
example: Retirement age is a political football in the United States of America.

phrase: a square peg in a round hole
definition: To say that a person is a square peg in a round hole means that they are not suitable for the job they are doing or the situation they are in.
example: The employee was a bad match for the job – a square peg in a round hole.

definition: When there is much more of something than necessary and it is difficult to make a choice, you have an embarrassment of riches.
example: The hosts presented us with an embarrassment of riches at the reception.

definition: A person who is bulldozed into doing something is forced to do it, especially by being bullied or intimidated.
example: They bulldozed the immigrants into accepting the work.

definition: A person who drinks like a fish is one who drinks a lot.
example: I don’t like hanging around with them because they drink like a fish.

definition: If something, such as work, is farmed out, it is sent away to be done by others.
example: We decided to farm out the marketing campaign to another company.

definition: If you go out of your way, you take particular care or make a special effort when doing something.
example: Every time we are invited to their house, they go out of their way to make us feel comfortable.

definition: This idiom means to lose momentum and stop.
example: The athlete grinded to a halt.

phrase: lead someone up the garden path
definition: If someone lead you up the garden path, they deceive you by making you believe something which is not true.
example: Unfortunately I haven’t got the promotion I was promised. I think my manager is leading me up the garden path.

definition: When somebody makes light work of something, they do it very easily or with little effort.
example: The girls made light work of the cleaning up in no time.

definition: Something that makes your flesh crawl fills you with disgust or makes you feel very nervous.
example: The memory of all those dead people made my flesh crawl.

definition:
This expression means that you don’t care if something happens.
мне от этого ни жарко ни холодно
example: It’s no skin off my nose if she doesn’t accept my invitation.

definition: A nosy parker is a person of an overly inquisitive or prying nature.
example: We don’t like him because he’s a nosy parker.

definition: If you play the market, you buy stocks and shares in the hope of making a profit when you sell them.
example: She made a fortune by playing the market.

definition: This idiom means to admire or love someone so much that you believe they have no faults.
example: Most people put movie stars on a pedestal.

definition: If something unpleasant reappears after lying dormant for some time, it rears its ugly head.
example: It is feared that communism is rearing its ugly head again.

definition: This idiom means just right; exactly on target or at exactly the right time.
example: She was right on the button when she said that.

definition: If you see eye to eye with somebody, you agree with them.
example: I’m glad that we see eye to eye on the choice of car colour.

definition: A person who is doing or saying the opposite to most other people is said to be swimming against the tide. A person who is doing or saying the same to most other people is said to be swimming with the tide.
example: Don’t worry. She always swims against the tide and somehow succeeds.

phrase: the old school tie / oldboy network
definition: This idiom refers to the way in which men who have been to the same expensive private school help one another to find good jobs.
example: The old school tie has enormous power in this city.

phrase: two wrongs don’t make a right
definition: This expression refers to the fact that responding to a negative situation in the same manner will not make things better in any sense.
example: You can’t leave him because he was a little bit rude to you. Two wrongs don’t make a right.

definition: This idiom means “in or into one’s protective care”.
example: The little boy has been taken under her wing.

definition: If something withers on the vine, it comes to an end or ceases to exist because people do not support or encourage it.
example: In the end my project withered on the vine.

definition: Somebody who is wrapped up in cotton wool is over-protected from dangers and risks.
example: Their child is kept wrapped up in cotton wool, which is not good in my opinion.

phrase: a sledgehammer to crack a nut
definition: Using a sledgehammer to crack a nut means using disproportionate force to solve a problem.
example: She called the police because her next door neighbour was rude? That’s using a sledgehammer to crack a nut.

definition: This idiom refers to someone who is trying too hard to make other people admire your artistic knowledge or ability.
example: I won’t meet with them. I don’t want to talk with art-farty people.

definition: Someone who is as sober as a judge is not drunk at all.
example: That night he was as sober as a judge.

definition: If something happens or develops by degrees, it happens gradually or little by little as time goes by.
example: Our business relationship grew into friendship by degrees.

definition: Someone who is champing at the bit is ready and eager to start an activity and is showing impatience at being delayed.
example: The conference was delayed and the journalists were champing at the bit.

phrase: dangle a carrot in front of someone
definition: This idiom means to try to persuade someone to do something by offering them a reward.
example: The team dangled a two million dollars carrot in front of the man to remain.

definition: This expression means that everyone can be successful at something at some time in their life.
example: I know I’ll be luckier one day. Every dog has its day!

definition: If you fall on your sword, you accept the consequences of an unsuccessful or wrong action.
example: The campaign organiser resigned after the failure. She said that she had fallen on her sword.

definition: This is a slang term for road.
example: Move the car – I can see a traffic warden coming down the frog and toad.

definition: This expression means from the very start of an activity.
example: Right from the word go she was rejected by the group.

phrase: get to first base / reach first base
definition: When you get to first base or reach first base, you make progress or begin to have success with someone or something.
example: If you speak like that, you won’t get to first base at the interview.

definition: This expression refers to falling in love with somebody the first time you see them.
example: They met at a party. It was love at first sight.

phrase: not all it’s cracked up to be
definition: not as good as something is said to be:
example: This window isn’t all it’s cracked up to be.

definition: This expression means that you are no longer on friendly terms with someone.
example: I’ve been off her Christmas list since I accidentally hit her cat.

definition: If you pay dearly for something that you do or say, you suffer a lot as a result of it.
example: If you leave this company, you may pay dearly for it.

definition: to pack up your belongings and move to a different home, job, or city
example: Next month I need to pull up stakes. I’m sorry!

definition: If you rub shoulders with someone, you have an opportunity to meet and talk to that person, especially someone wealthy, famous or distinguished.
example: As a journalist, she sometimes rubs shoulders with famous people.

definition: This idiom means to start your own business.
example: She set up shop in 1995.

definition: If you annoy or irritate someone by intervening in a situation that is their responsibility, you step on their toes.
example: I can offer some advice, but I’m afraid of stepping on someone’s toes.

phrase: strike while the iron is hot
definition: If you strike while the iron is hot, you act immediately because now is the ideal time to do it.
example: The price of property has slumped. You should strike while the iron is hot.

definition: This idiom refers to a small or insignificant event that is over-reacted to, as if it were of considerably more consequence.
example: Oh, move on! It’s just a tempest in a teapot.

definition: To say that the party is over means that a period of happiness and enjoyment is over and life is going to return to normal.
example: We had a wonderful time here but the party is over.

phrase: big fish in a small pond
definition: A big fish in a small pond is an important or highly-ranked person in a small group or organization.
example: I could get a better job in a big company but I enjoy being a big fish in a small pond.

phrase: born with a silver spoon in one’s mouth
definition: A person who is born with a silver spoon in their mouth is born into a very rich family.
example: They never have to worry about money; they were born with a silver spoon in their mouth.

definition: This idiom refers to a sound of contempt or derision, made by blowing through closed lips, usually with the tongue protruding.
example: They have been greeted with some Bronx cheers.

definition: If you say that you will do something by hook or by crook, you means that you will succeed, no matter what.
example: I’ll get my revenge, by hook or by crook!

definition: If someone or something comes to grief, they either have an accident, are destroyed or end in failure.
example: Our plans for a golf course came to grief.

definition: This expression means everything imaginable.
example: The flat had everything but the kitchen sink.

definition: When an agreement is neither written nor signed, because the two parties trust each other completely, it is called a gentleman’s agreement.
example: There’s no need to sign this. I propose to have a gentleman’s agreement.

phrase: get the short / wrong end of the stick
definition: If you get the short end of the stick, you are treated unfairly or receive less than what is due or deserved.
example: After the negotiation, I felt like I got the short end of the stick.

phrase: go to hell in a handcart / handbasket
definition: it is in a bad state and continues to deteriorate.
example: This used to be the best place in town, but now it’s going to hell in a handbasket.

definition: This idiom means to tackle a difficult problem boldly.
example: Grasp the nettle and call him!

phrase: have a soft spot for someone or something
definition: If you have a soft spot for someone or something, you particularly like them.
example: I have a soft spot for fishing rods.

definition: This idiom refers to a serious conversation between two people, usually close friends, in which they talk honestly about their feelings.
example: We had a heart-to-heart over a bottle of wine.

definition: This phrase means following closely behind someone.
example: The suspect was running with a detective hot on his heels.

definition: This idiom means having a passionate nature or being inclined to quick temper.
example: He’s a hot-blooded guy.

definition: This expression is used in a situation where a person with a fault denounces someone else for having the same fault.
example: The competitor accused another player of cheating; it was the pot calling the kettle black!

definition: If a person pours oil on troubled waters, they do or say something to calm a tense situation or make people stop arguing.
example: He’s a good negotiator and can pour oil on troubled waters.

definition: This expression means to celebrate or enjoy oneself.
example: Having finished the exams, they decided to push the boat out.

definition: If a project or plan is put on ice, all further action has been suspended or postponed for an indefinite period of time.
example: The plans for the new marketing strategy have been put on ice.

definition: If a person is spoon-fed, they are helped too much rather than encouraged to think by themselves or use their own initiative.
example: Some parents tend to spoon-feed their children.

phrase: take the wind out of one’s sails
definition: If someone or something takes the wind out of your sails, they make you feel less confident by doing or saying something that you do not expect.
example: The leader’s rejection of our financial strategy took the wind out of our sails.

definition: If you describe a remark as “tongue in cheek”, you mean that it is not meant to be taken seriously; it is meant to be gunny or ironic.
example: My remark was taken seriously, even if it was supposed to be tongue in cheek.

definition: To say that someone is as slippery as an eel means that they are difficult to catch and they manage to avoid answering questions.
example: That woman is as slippery as an eel.

definition: A person who has to bear the brunt of something is the one who suffers the most when something bad or unpleasant happens.
example: When things go wrong, their assistant always has to bear the brunt of their anger.

definition: If you end or withdraw from something that is already failing, in order to reduce the loss of money, time or effort invested in it, you cut your losses.
example: As I see, the project is heading towards failure. Let’s cut our losses before it’s too late.

definition: This expression refers to assorted bits and pieces of rubbish, especially items that are found in the sea and are useless or discarded.
example: There were flotsam and jetsam all over the beach.

definition: This expression means to have a sudden burst of energy after being tired.
example: I got a second wind after I saw the sign for the final lap.

definition: A golden handshake is a generous sum of money given to a person when they leave a company or retire (sometimes given to encourage early retirement).
example: When you leave this company, you are entitled to a quarter of your salary as a golden handshake.

definition: to completely, totally, or unconditionally believe or accept something—often a lie, trick, or practical joke—without any doubt or reservation
example: I didn’t think she’d believe my story, but she fell for it hook, line and sinker.

definition: To say that something will never fly means that it will not be successful.
example: She has always had good ideas, but the last one will never fly.

definition: When you help someone to remember something they have forgotten, you jog their memory.
example: Don’t you remember who was with us that day? He’s a pilot to jog your memory.

definition: A task that is done for your own pleasure and satisfaction and not for reward or profit is called a labour of love.
example: Solving English grammar exercises is a labour of love for me.

phrase: like the cat that ate the canary
definition: If, after an achievement or success, a person seems very self-satisfied or pleased with themselves, you can say that they look like the cat that ate the canary.
example: When the manager complimented her on the project, she looked like the cat that ate the canary.

definition: When something happens nine times out of ten, it is what usually happens.
example: The public transport system is very bad. The means of transport arrive late nine times out of ten.

phrase: ride it outride out the storm
definition: If you manage to survive a dangerous or very unpleasant situation, like a ship sailing through a storm, you ride it out.
example: Our business was hit by the recession but we managed to ride out the storm.

definition: This idiom refers to the daily life and work where you learn more than you would by going to university.
example: My grandfather learnt everything from the university of life.

definition: If you go somewhere with bells on, you are delighted and eager to go there.
example: Of course I’ll be at the party – with bells on!

definition: This idiom refers to a young person who has many new ideas and wants a reform. It can also refer to a young person eager for rigorous reorder to the established order.
example: He was a young turk within the organization.

definition: To refer to an idea or plan as a flight of fancy means that it is imaginative but not at all practical or sensible.
example: I deeply appreciate your effort, but this plan is a flight of fancy.

definition: This idiom refers to a reliable person, who can be trusted not to fail in a task.
example: This problem is quite intricate, so we need a safe pair of hands.

phrase: alarm bells start to ring / set the alarm bells ringing
definition: If something “sets the alarm bells ringing”, it makes you begin to worry, because it shows that there may be a problem.
example: Alarm bells started to ring when the old man next door didn’t open his shutters all day and didn’t answer his phone.

phrase: as good luck would have it
definition: If something is as good luck would have it, it has come about by some fortunate chance.
example: My promotion is as good luck would have it.

definition: This idiom means to begin to understand a situation of fact.
example: I’ve just cottoned on the fact that they are lying.

definition: A dead cat bounce is a small and temporary recovery in a financial market following a large fall.
example: It’s not over. It’s just a dead cat bounce.

definition: This expression refers to a situation in which you must take a big risk in order to avoid failure.
example: Yesterday I was in a do-or-die situation when a car nearly hit me.

phrase: eat somebody out of house and home
definition: This is a humorous way of saying that someone is eating large quantities of your food.
example: I stock up with food when my friends come to my place. They would eat me out of house and home!

definition: If someone who is admired is found to have a weakness, fault or defect of character, they are said to have feet of clay.
example: No one is perfect. Every man has feet of clay.

definition: A person who is as hard as nails is unsentimental and shows no sympathy.
example: Don’t expect anything from them. The boys are as hard as nails.

phrase: know better than to do something
definition: If you know better than to do something, you are experienced or wise enough not to do it.
example: You should know better than to go fishing in stormy weather.

definition: An officially authorized activity which enables people to make a lot of money without much effort is called a licence to print money.
example: The contract to supply water and food to schools was a licence to print money.

definition: To say that something is like nailing jelly to the wall means that it is extremely difficult to do, if not impossible.
example: He works so much that obtaining a meeting with him is like nailing jelly to the wall.

definition: If you pay over the odds, you pay too much or you pay more for something than it is really worth.
example: I am willing to pay over the odds for an original perfume.

definition: This phrase means to annoy someone.
example: Ignore them! They are only trying to put your back up.

definition: When someone is extremely scared, it is said that they are quaking in their boots.
example: When she saw the snakes in the water, she started quaking in her boots.

definition: A person who has a saving grace has a quality that prevents them from being totally bad.
example: He’s a horrible person but he has one saving grace, his passion for plants.

definition: Pleasant but unimportant words that lovers say to each other are called sweet nothings.
example: She whispered sweet nothings in his ear as they danced.

definition: This term is used to describe a person who is very helpful and supportive during difficult times.
example: My brother has always been a tower of strength.

definition: If somebody is so excited that they talk non-stop, they are wound up.
example: They had so much to tell us after that impressive holiday that they were wound up.

definition: If something difficult, unpleasant, or strange is all in a day's work for someone, it is a usual part of their job
example: When you're a nurse, cleaning up vomit is all in a day's work

definition: If someone is as weak as water, they can be easily influenced.
example: I wouldn’t trust her if I were you. She is as weak as water.

definition: This idiom means to leave a place in order to avoid a difficult or unpleasant situation or to avoid paying for something.
example: I heard that her father did a runner soon after she had been born.

definition: When you know the score, you are well-informed about a situation and know what to expect.
example: If he damages the car, I won’t lend it to him again. He knows the score.

definition: If you behave so stupidly that you appear ridiculous, you make an ass of yourself.
example: He made an ass of himself by drinking way too much.

definition: If you make mincemeat of someone or something, you completely and utterly defeat or destroy them.
example: A good lawyer will make mincemeat of her accusations.

definition: If you tell someone to mind their Ps and Qs, you are advising them to be careful about how they behave and what they say.
example: Mind your Ps and Qs when you meet her. That’s my advice for you.

definition: A story, joke or an idea that has been repeated so often that it has lost its novelty is referred to as an old chestnut.
example: The story about her latest boyfriend has become an old chestnut.

definition: If you are not completely honest or behave in a way that is insincere, evasive or intentionally misleading, you are playing games with someone.
example: Stop playing games with us. Just tell us the truth.

definition: If you put or set the records straight, you provide facts or an explanation to correct a mistake or misunderstanding.
example: An interview on television enabled the politician to set the records straight.

phrase: sing a different tune / change your tune
definition: If somebody sings a different tune, they change their opinion about something or their attitude towards something.
example: She had no sympathy for people out of work until her father lost his job. Now she’s singing a different tune.

definition: If someone gets steamed up about something, they become very angry, excited or enthusiastic about it.
example: Please, calm down. There’s no need to get steamed up.

definition: If you stop dead in your tracks, you stop suddenly because you are frightened or totally surprised.
example: When I saw the alligator, I stopped dead in my tracks.

definition: This idiom refers to the particular state, arrangement or condition of something or the way a situation exists or has developed.
example: It would be prudent to understand the lay of the land before we agree to invest.

definition: This idiom means to entertain someone by giving them food and drinks, in a high class restaurant.
example: The whole period we were wined and dined every night for free.

definition: This idiom might either refer to the flip of a coin to decide on something or to a result, usually between two courses of action, which is uncertain and could go either way.
example: Who will win the Presidency? It’s a toss up.

definition: If you wait for something with “bated breath”, you are both anxious and excited about an imminent event.
example: We waited with bated breath for her to come back home.

definition: it is not what matters most or what is most essential.
example: Good kindergartens are not the be-all and end-all of educating a child.

definition: This expression refers to something that is not an acceptable way to behave.
example: They broke up because his behaviour was simply beyond the pale.

definition: If you find something so dull and uninteresting that it makes you sad enough to cry, you are bored to tears.
example: I could see that she was bored to tears by the historical documentary.

phrase: by no stretch of the imagination
definition: This expression is used to describe things that are definitely not possible or correct.
example: By no stretch of the imagination could the woman be called beautiful.

definition: If someone has a chink in their armor, they have a weakness that other people can take advantage of.
example: The opponents are busy looking for chinks in my armor.

definition: If you have a chinwag with someone, you have an opportunity to chat with each other.
example: “Let’s meet on Friday.” “That’s a good idea. We can have a good old chinwag!”

definition: If something is a crying shame, it is very sad or unfortunate.
example: It’s a crying shame that some children cannot have at least two meals per day.

definition: If someone has been doing something for donkey’s years, they have been doing it for a very long time.
example: She knows the town inside out. She has been a taxi driver for donkey’s years.

phrase: get a rise out of someone
definition: If you make someone react angrily by jokingly saying something that you know will irritate them, you get a rise out of them.
example: This morning, I got a rise out of my wife by asking her about her latest diet.

phrase: have a bee in one’s bonnet
definition: Someone who has a bee in their bonnet has an idea which constantly occupies their thoughts.
example: She’s got a bee in her bonnet about moving to Germany.

phrase: have a brush with the law
definition: When you have a brush with something, such as the law, you encounter or experience it briefly.
example: I had a brush with the law for excessive speeding last year.

definition: This idiom is used to describe somebody who keeps talking about the same story over and over again.
example: Stop saying this story again! You’re like a broken record.

phrase: make a monkey out of somebody
definition: If you humiliate someone by making them appear ridiculous or foolish, you make a monkey out of that person.
example: Don’t make a monkey out of him. He could be your manager one day.

definition: If something is out of whack, it is not working properly or is not in good order.
example: The washing machine is out of whack.

definition: This idiom refers to a worthless or stupid person or group.
example: These racist fans are pond life.

definition: A pregnant pause is a moment of silence full of unexpressed meaning.
example: There was a pregnant pause before he answered the question.

definition: If you rack your brains, you try very hard to think of something or to remember something.
example: I don’t like this period of the year. I have to rack my brains to find ideas for presents.

definition: If someone gets a rap on/across the knuckles, they are punished or reprimanded, but not very severely, as a reminder not to do something again.
example: She got a rap on the knuckles for doing that.

definition: This idiom means to make it clear that somebody must leave.
example: It’s enough! Please, show her the door.

definition: When somebody’s comments or remarks strike home, they make you fully understand the situation.
example: The seriousness of her arguments struck home as he listened to her.

phrase: strike the right note with somebody
definition: If you strike the right note, you say or do something suitable or appropriate.
example: She struck the right note with her boyfriend when she bought him a book on fitness.

phrase: take a load / weight off your mind
definition: If something takes a load/weight off someone’s mind, it brings great relief because a problem has been solved.
example: Finding a new job took a load off my mind.

definition: If something is there for the taking, it is easy to obtain.
example: When they went out of business, the market was there for the taking.

definition: This idiom refers to the nominal span of a human life. In the days that this expression was coined that span was considered to be seventy years.
example: She hopes to exceed three score and ten.

definition: If somebody throws something over the wall, they deal with part of a problem or project, then pass the responsibility to another person or department without any communication or coordination.
example: You can’t throw this project over the wall. You’ve promised to finish it.

phrase: variety is the spice of life
definition: This expression means that life is more interesting when you try to do different things.
example: You should try more sports. Variety is the spice of life.

definition: This idiom refers to a good possibility of succeeding if you try hard.
example: You clearly have a fighting chance of getting that job.

definition: This idiom refers to two parties which are almost ready to fight.
example: The two high-schools have been at daggers drawn for months.

definition: This expression means to hate someone very much.
example: Following the divorce, they couldn’t stand the sight of each other.

definition: This idiom means to be very similar.
example: Both brothers are mean; they seem to be cast in the same mould.

definition: This idiom means no longer in use.
example: Alcatel cellphones are dead and buried.

definition: This expression is used to describe someone’s sentence in prison.
example: She is doing time for the crime she committed.

phrase: drastic times call for drastic measures
definition: When faced with a difficult situation, it is sometimes necessary to take actions which in normal circumstances would appear extreme.
example: After Maria’s fourth accident, we decided to confiscate her car. Drastic times call for drastic measures!

phrase: every cloud has a silver lining
definition: This idiom means that you should be optimistic because even difficult times will lead to better days.
example: This is just a transient situation. Every cloud has a silver lining.

definition: This idiom means for ever.
example: She has given her car for keeps.

definition: If a person goes under the knife, they have surgery.
example: I’m not worried about it. Going under the knife is the only solution.

phrase: keep your finger on the pulse
definition: If you keep your finger on the pulse, you are constantly aware of the most recent events or developments.
example: As an investor, I have to keep my finger on the pulse of the market.

definition: If you make headway, you make progress in what you are trying to achieve.
example: The police officers have made little headway in their investigation.

definition: To describe someone as the salt of the earth means that they are kind, honest and reliable.
example: She is the salt of the earth, always ready to give a helping hand.

phrase: there’s more than one way to skin a cat
definition: This expression means that there are many different ways of achieving something.
example: You should try another method. There’s more than one way to skin a cat.

definition: This idiom means to the utmost degree; without limit.
example: He tests the cars to the nth degree.

definition: If you weigh your words, you choose your words carefully in order to express exactly what you means and avoid any misunderstanding.
example: During the press conference I had to weigh my words.

definition: This idiom means not occur to one, not consider.
example: Even if it were lying on my desk, I wouldn’t dream of taking another person’s smartphone.

definition: This is a humoristic way of saying that you are willing to do whatever the other person asks.
example: Do you want breakfast in bed? Sure, darling. Your wish is my command!

definition: A person referred to as a shrinking violet is a timid or shy person.
example: The young lady was a shrinking violet who had difficulty expressing herself.

definition: If you back or bet on the wrong horse, for example the loser in a contest, match or election, you support the wrong person.
example: When I voted for her I was deeply convinced she would win, but I backed the wrong horse.

definition: Someone who lies easily, with a total lack of shame, is a barefaced liar.
example: That barefaced liar stole my Rolex and said he had found it! It’s incredible!

definition: To say that someone is beating a dead horse means that they are wasting time and effort trying to do or achieve something that is impossible.
example: Maria is beating a dead horse trying to get her money back. The company has gone bankrupt.

phrase: between the devil and the deep blue sea
definition: If you are between the devil and the deep blue sea, you are in a situation where there are two equally unpleasant alternatives.
example: When the new product didn’t take off, we were caught between the devil and the deep blue sea: craft a new marketing campaign or drop the product.

definition: Information passed on through conversation is transmitted by word of mouth.
example: The bad news was spread by word of mouth.

definition: If someone tells you to get a move on, they are asking you to hurry up.
example: Hey! Get a move on or you’ll be late!

definition: If you get wind of something, you hear about something you were unaware of, usually a private or secret matter.
example: The manager didn’t want the media to get wind of the merger.

phrase: more fun than a barrel of monkeys
definition: If something is very amusing or enjoyable, you can say that it is more fun than a barrel of monkeys.
example: This quiz is more fun than a barrel of monkeys.

definition: A museum piece is something or someone that is so old, antique and out of place that it should belong in a museum rather than as a part of everyday life.
example: Your hat looks like a museum piece. Why don’t you buy a new one?

definition: You cannot expect to achieve anything if you risk nothing.
example: I’m going to ask my manager for a promotion even though I know I have little chance of getting it. Nothing ventured, nothing gained.

definition: This idiom means absolutely accurate.
example: Your prediction was absolutely on the mark.

definition: This idioms means to go crazy.
example: I have something important to tell you. Pay attention and don’t pop your cork.

definition: This idiom means to be rude to someone and cause a tiff or a fight.
example: The guy rubbed me in such a wrong way that I don’t want to see him again.

definition: This expression refers to the offices of the powerful leaders or the higher echelons of government.
example: It’s utterly hard to get inside the corridors of power.

definition: This idiom means “in a difficult situation”.
example: If the company doesn’t pay for the damage, I’ll be up a tree.

definition: If somebody is after your blood, they desire to catch you in order to hurt or punish you.
example: As he has lied to them, they are after his blood now.

definition: If someone is as right as rain, they are in excellent health or condition.
example: I called on my grandparents thinking they were ill, but they were as right as rain.

definition: This phrase means on the whole, generally speaking or all things considered.
example: By and large our company is doing well.

definition: If something good falls into your lap, it happens to you without any effort on your part.
example: You should search for a job. Do you think it will fall into your lap?

definition: Something that get someone’s goat annoys or irritates them.
example: By saying that, you really got my goat!

phrase: get your knickers in a twist
definition: If you get your knickers in a twist, you are angry, nervous or upset faced with a difficult situation.
example: Marry, don’t get your knickers in a twist! We still control this situation.

phrase: Have half a mind to do smth
definition: If you have half a mind to do something, you are thinking seriously about it but have not yet reached a decision.
example: He’s half a mind to quit that job and start his own business.

phrase: learn to walk before you run
definition: This idiom means to take smaller steps initially.
example: The loan was denied because our company needs to learn to walk before it runs.

definition: This is a slang term for head.
example: Betting your wage on the toss of a coin isn’t the best way to get more money – use your loaf, mate!

definition: Someone who looks daggers at another looks at them very angrily.
example: He looked daggers at me when I invited his girlfriend to dance.

definition: make a lot of fuss about something which is not important.
example: There was a meeting to discuss the name for the new school mascot. “Much ado about nothing”, my friend said.

phrase: six of one and half a dozen of the other
definition: This expression means that there is no real difference between two choices; both are equally good or equally bad.
example: I didn’t know who to vote for last year. It was six of one and half a dozen of the other.

definition: This phrase means to coy explanations of basic information about sex and reproduction to children.
example: The little boy knew what the birds and the bees were.

definition: If someone or something is the worse for wear, they are in poor condition, either worn, damaged or tired.
example: After several months, the truck drivers were looking the worse for wear.

phrase: to be in tune with somebody
definition: If you are in tune with somebody it means that you completely understand them and you can speak to each other without words.
example: I like my girlfriend because I was in tune with her from the very first moment.

phrase: to have something coming out of your ears
definition: This expression means to have a lot of something.
example: I’ve been studying English all morning so I’ve got idioms coming out of my ears.

definition: This idiom refers to a man with large genitals.
example: The legend is that he was well hung.

definition: When something provides an opportunity to observe and learn about people and life in other countries, it is called a window on the world.
example: The internet is the best window on the world.

definition: A business or activity that is dynamic and successful is a going concern.
example: Four years ago, we opened a store that is a going concern today.

definition: Someone whose vision is very poor, or who is unable to see anything, is as blind as a bat.
example: Without her glasses, my grandmother is as blind as a bat.

phrase: as snug as a bug in a rug
definition: This is a humorous way of saying that you are warm and comfortable.
example: When I got home, my wife was wrapped up in a blanket, looking as snug as a bug in a rug.

definition: This expression refers to a process by which a message or piece of information (especially gossip, rumours or scandalous news) is passed on from one person to another, and changes along the way, so that the final version is often very different from the original.
example: Don’t believe what you hear. It’s Chinese whisper!

definition: To talk about what to do if or when a situation comes to the crunch means when it becomes critical and a decision has to be made.
example: If it comes to the crunch, I will sell my car.

definition: If you refer to two people as a dream ticket, you think they would work well together and be successful.
example: Two champions teaming up for this cause, is clearly a dream ticket.

phrase: fire a warning shot across somebody’s bow
definition: This idiom refers to a warning shot, either real or metaphorical.
example: Employees have fired a warning shot across the company’s bows. They want bigger wages.

definition: If your heart sinks, you feel very unhappy and despondent.
example: My heart sank when I saw her with another man.

definition: If something is off the mark, it is incorrect or inaccurate.
example: Her estimation of the mission cost was off the mark. I’ve made another one.

definition: If a place becomes well-known, it is put on the map.
example: The president’s visit has really put this place on the map.

phrase: put / throw a spanner in the works
definition: To put a spanner in the works means to cause problems and prevent something from happening as planned.
example: A new road through the forest was planned but some ecologists put a spanner in the works.

definition: If you put your best foot forward, you do something as fast as you can.
example: It’s a long way home, but if I put my best foot forward I should be there on time.

definition: When someone is as quiet as a mouse, they make no noise at all.
example: The burglar was as quiet as a mouse.

definition: This idiom refers to someone who is certain to win an election or a competition.
example: She’s a shoo-in for the White House.

definition: This idiom means to do something to prevent somebody embarrassed.
example: He saved the team’s blushes by scoring.

definition: If you spend time trying to do something that is impossible to achieve, you are said to be spitting in the wind.
example: You’ll never make me change my mind. You’re just spitting in the wind.

definition: If you stir up a hornet’s nest, you do something which causes a commotion and provokes criticism and anger.
example: My letter to Nicole stirred up a hornet’s nest.

definition: a secret plan, trick, or dishonest activity has been discovered, and the person can no longer continue it
example: We’ve reached a conclusion. The game is up!

phrase: a little learning / knowledge is a dangerous thing
definition: This means that people who don’t understand something fully are dangerous.
example: I wouldn’t trust her with this job. A little learning is a dangerous thing.

definition: If you apply the same rule to different situations, you judge them by the same token, or in a similar way.
example: I don’t think that prices will go up but, by the same token, I don’t see them going down either.

definition: verbally scold someone.
example: I regret that I have chewed her out.

definition: If something is collecting dust, it hasn’t been touched or used for a long period of time.
example: Lately, my fishing poles have collected dust.

definition: This idiom means to do what someone else wants or has requested, to the point of servitude.
example: The boy hated how his mother wanted him to do her bidding.

definition: Someone who is full of hot air is full of nonsense and talks a lot without saying anything worthwhile.
example: It’s not a good idea to listen to her. She’s full of hot air!

definition: If you are in a desperate situation and you grasp at straws, you try any method, even if it has little chance of success, in an attempt to find a solution.
example: In her search for a cure, she tried a traditional healer, knowing that she was grasping at straws.

definition: Something that has the works contains everything that is possible or the full range of options.
example: I ordered a new laptop with the works.

definition:
This expression describes a person who has strong feelings of fear or worry.
OR a state of acute nervousness, apprehension, unease, or jumpiness
example: Don’t talk about ghosts – they give me the heebie-jeebies.

definition: If a subject or plan is at the top of somebody’s agenda, it is the most important thing they want to discuss or deal with.
example: They have finally realized the need for placing the educational reform at the top of their agenda.

definition: This term refers to busy energetic activity in an atmosphere of general excitement.
example: I prefer to live in the city. I like the hustle and bustle of city life.

definition: If you look the picture of health it means that you look extremely healthy.
example: It’s nice to see you again! You look the picture of health.

definition: If someone or something makes your hackles rise, they make you angry.
example: My manager’s constant observations make my hackles rise!

definition: This expression refers to a stimulation that causes you to want additional of something, mostly food.
example: These advertisements are meant to whet your appetite.

definition: This expression means to make a derisive or contemptuous sound with your lips.
example: We were sitting at the table and all of a sudden she blew a raspberry.

definition: If you dance to someone’s tune, you do whatever that person tells you to do.
example: He is the company’s major shareholder so the employees tend to dance to his tune.

definition: Term used to refer to a rich, powerful, self-satisfied person who uses his/her money and power in a way that you disapprove of.
example: The place was full of fat cats in their luxury cars.

definition: This idiom means to describe something in exceptional detail.
example: In front of the officer, the man gave a blow-by-blow account of their criminal activity.

definition: This phrase means to put someone in a very difficult situation in which the person has no choice about what they do.
example: She knows I need the job so she’s got me over a barrel in terms of what she pays me.

definition: Dealing with or treating people with a heavy hand means acting with discipline and severity, with little or no sensitivity.
example: She ran the prison with a heavy hand.

definition: A company, organization or bank account that is in the black has made a profit.
example: Our company has been in the black ever since the new manager took over.

phrase: like a bear with a sore head
definition: If someone is behaving like a bear with a sore head, they are very irritable and bad-tempered.
example: When his team lost the match, Brian was like a bear with a sore head.

definition: If you say something off the record / books, you don’t want anyone to repeat it publicly.
example: My comment was made off the record and shouldn’t have been published.

definition: What you lose on the swings you gain on the roundabouts. This expression means that there are as many advantages as there are disadvantages.
example: The more you earn, the more tax you pay. It’s swings and roundabouts.

definition: Someone who is toing and froing is either repeatedly going from one place to another and coming back, or is constantly changing their mind about something.
example: After several months of toing and froing, the agreement was signed.

definition: When you vent your spleen, you release or express all your anger about something.
example: From time to time, it’s good for you to vent your spleen.

definition: This idiom means to work for very little money.
example: I used to work for peanuts two years ago.

definition: This expression is said of something or someone so unappealing that one wouldn’t want to go anywhere near.
example: No, I wouldn’t touch that thing with a barge-pole.

definition: This idiom refers to something that people do not like to question; a taboo subject.
example: The trial remains a sacred cow.

definition: A person who is behind the times has old-fashioned ideas and does not keep up with modern life in general.
example: Jennifer doesn’t have a smartphone. She’s completely behind the times.

definition: This expression is used to tell someone not to worry about a mistake or problem because it won’t have any serious effect and everything will work out all right.
example: They were furious when it happened, but don’t worry – it will all come out in the wash.

definition: When a project, task or activity is done and dusted, it is completely finished or ready.
example: I’ve finished analyzing the indicators, so I can say that this task is done and dusted.

definition: To say that someone is going places means that they show talent and ability that will no doubt lead to a successful future.
example: Even at university it was clear that Nicole was going places.

definition: This idiom refers to a word or name that everyone knows.
example: KFC quickly became a household word.

definition: When people jump for joy, they express their happiness through excited movements and gestures.
example: I jumped for joy when I was awarded the prize.

definition: This expression means that the subject or plan is a secret and must not be revealed.
example: We’re planning to flee the country, so mum’s the word – ok?

phrase: put pants on one leg at a time
definition: To say that someone puts their pants on one leg at a time means that the person is a human being no different from anyone else.
example: I don’t understand why you are scared to speak to her. She puts her pants on one leg at a time.

definition: If you weather the storm, you succeed in surviving a difficult period or situation.
example: Given the current economic conditions, our company is weathering the storm.

definition: This idiom refers to someone or something that is blamed or punished for problems that are caused by someone or something else.
example: Brian is our whipping boy.

definition: If you have another think coming, you are greatly mistaken. This expression is used to tell a person that they’re wrong and should consider changing their mind.
example: If you think I'm going to pay for everything, you've got another thinkcoming.

definition: If someone is as free as a bird, they are completely free to do as they want.
example: I’ve been so happy since I retired. I am as free as a bird.

definition: Someone who is as pretty as a picture is very attractive or appealing in appearance.
example: He looked as pretty as a picture in that suit.

definition: This expression means very cheap.
example: In this country, the beverages are dirt cheap.

definition: A person or organisation is difficulty and unable to manage without help is called a lame duck.
example: Local firms have become lame ducks in recent years.

phrase: like a cat on hot bricks
definition: very nervous or restless.
example: The week before the results were announced, he was like a cat on hot bricks.

phrase: make hay while the sun shines
definition: This expression is used as an encouragement to take advantage of a good situation which may not last.
example: Successful fighters are advised to make hay while the sun shines.

definition: This term means that there is no way you would accept to do what is proposed.
example: Would you like me to work on Sunday? Nothing doing!

phrase: out of sight, out of mind
definition: This expression refers to the reduced importance and emergence of something that is not within eyesight.
