example: I will speak to her when she is back. For now, she is out of sight, out of mind for me.

definition: This is a euphemistic way of saying that a person is dead.
example: Nobody lives in that house since the old woman popped her clogs.

phrase: take the mickey out of someone
definition: If you take the mickey out of someone, you tease them or make fun of their behaviour, sometimes in an unkind way.
example: My last girlfriend used to take the mickey out of me.

definition: This expression refers to the perceived absence of someone who is recently deceased.
example: Some days I see the empty chair and the grief comes back. I miss her!

definition: If you throw caution to the wind, you start taking risks and stop worrying about the danger involved.
example: I decided to throw caution to the wind and join army.

phrase: to have a face like a bulldog chewing a wasp
definition: means that you find them very unattractive because they have a screwed-up ugly expression on their face.
example: I don’t like him. He has a face like a bulldog chewing a wasp.

phrase: when the going gets tough, the tough get going
definition: When faced with a difficult or dangerous situation, and the going gets tough, strong people take action to solve the problem.
example: He is a strong man. He strongly believes that when the going gets tough, the tough get going.

definition: If you are “all the better for something”, you benefit from it or feel much better as a result of it.
example: I’m sure you’ll be all the better for a good night’s rest.

definition: This expression means to waste time on a task or project that is unnecessary, not worth doing or impossible to achieve.
example: I expect you to do the job well but please don’t boil the ocean!

definition: To say that something is (as) dead as a dodo means that it is unquestionably dead or obsolete, or has gone out of fashion. A dodo is a bird that is now extinct.
example: The floppy disk is an invention which is almost as dead as a dodo.

definition: If someone or something disappears into thin air, they vanish in a mysterious way.
example: After being accused of spying, the woman disappeared into thin air.

definition: If you let bygones be bygones, you decide to forget about past disagreements.
example: When she arrived home, she decided to ley bygones be bygones and called on him.

definition: When a person says that their dogs are barking they mean that their feet are hurting.
example: I’ve been running all day. My dogs are barking!

definition: This idiom means just at the limit of acceptability, especially regarding sexual morals.
example: Your behaviour is near the knuckle. Be careful!

definition: pretend to be dead or asleep in order to avoid something they don’t want to do.
example: She’s not asleep. She is just playing possum.

definition: completely crazy
example: You’re stark raving mad to go fishing in this weather.

definition: This idiom refers to enthusiastic Christian believers.
example: Every Friday when the doorbell rings it’s the god squad.

definition: A yes-man is someone who always agrees with a person in authority in order to please them.
example: He’s a typical yes-man. Nobody likes him.

definition: If something is beyond redemption, it is such a poor state that there is no hope of improvement or recovery.
example: With the latest scandal, her reputation is now beyond redemption.

definition: This idiom means to overcome an obstacle.
example: I cleared a hurdle by getting the paperwork completed.

phrase: do something off your own bat
definition: This phrase means to do something without anyone else telling you or asking you to do it.
example: I didn’t want a present – she did it off her own bat.

definition: This expression means to try to get extra support/business/interest by various means.
example: I’ve tried to drum up support from local citizens.

definition: If you have forty winks, you have a short sleep or rest, generally during the day.
example: After having lunch, my grandfather has forty winks.

definition: If you hear of something through the grapevine, you learn about it informally, for example through friends or colleagues.
example: How did you hear about that job? Oh, through the grapevine, as usual.

definition: If you hedge your bets, you choose two or more courses of action in order to reduce the risk of loss or error.
example: I think we should hedge our bets by developing a new product.

definition: If you take time until the next day to think something over before making a decision, you sleep on it.
example: I don’t know the answer now. Can I sleep on it?

definition: If something sounds or smells fishy, you are suspicious about it.
example: His story sounds fishy to me.

definition: If one person is the spitting image of another, they look exactly like each other.
example: Steve is the spitting image of his father.

phrase: take a dim view of something
definition: If you take a dim view of something, you dislike or disapprove of it.
example: My future boss takes a dim view of wearing smart casual clothes to work.

definition: This is a good expression to show expertise about a certain subject or speak with authority.
example: Take it from me, I used to be like you until I realized that constant learning is the key.

phrase: (Has/full of) the milk of human kindness
definition: Someone who has or is full of the milk of human kindness, is naturally kind and compassionate to others.
example: They like my wife – she’s full of the milk of human kindness.

definition: If you say that someone is a thorn in your side, you mean that they continually irritate or annoy you.
example: Anna finds her father-in-law a real thorn in her side.

definition: This means that you are someone worth marrying/having.
example: The man is taking me out tonight. He’s such a catch…

definition: If someone is big hearted, they are kind, caring and compassionate.
example: My mother is too big hearted for her own good.

definition: This idiom means in a home that belongs to someone.
example: While you’re under my roof, you have to live by common sense rules.

definition: This is a slang term for small child.
example: She’s pregnant again. There’s soon going to be four ankle biters around the house.

definition: If your eyes are on stalks when you look at something, they are wide open with surprise or amazement.
example: The children’s eyes were on stalks as they watch the movie.

definition: Someone who is in the firing line is in a position to be criticized because of their responsibilities or the position they hold.
example: The security manager is in the firing line since the robbery.

definition: If someone or something gives up the ghost, they die or stop working.
example: My old PC has finally given up the ghost.

definition: To say that a company, organisation or country is going to the dogs, it means that it is becoming less successful or efficient than before.
example: There are some who believe that the firm will go to the dogs if it is sold.

definition: The most important part or aspect of a situation is called the heart of the matter.
example: We need to get to the heart of the matter – what caused this problem?

definition: This expression is used to refer to the police, because of the colour of their uniforms.
example: Don’t worry! Men in blue are coming.

phrase: put / lay one’s cards on the table
definition: If you put your cards on the table, you speak honestly and openly about your feelings and intentions.
example: It was time for her to put her cards on the table and reveal the truth.

definition: This idiom refers to a handsome grey-haired man.
example: Richard Gere is a real silver fox these days.

definition: This phrase refers to the acceptance of the unpredictable fortunes of existence, often spoken with an air of weary resignation.
example: Don’t be so sad. After all, such is life.

definition: This is a way of saying that there is need to finish a story because everyone knows what happened next.
example: This car was launched in 2007 and was initially restricted to Japanese market. The rest is history.

phrase: too many chiefs, not enough indians
definition: This expression refers to a situation where there are too many people giving instructions and not enough people doing the work.
example: The company wasn’t successful. There were too many chiefs and not enough indians.

definition: This phrase means to change a situation, especially so that you begin to win instead of losing.
example: Local authorities have decided to turn the tide against drugs.

phrase: a few / many irons in the fire
definition: If you have a few or many irons in the fire, you are involved in several projects at the same time.
example: This is not my sole business – I’ve got a few irons in the fire.

definition: This idiom means shy or reluctant to do something.
example: She will tell you her opinion. She is not backward in coming forward.

definition: If you say that somebody has bats in the belfry, you mean that they are eccentric or crazy.
example: She comes up with the craziest ideas – she’s got bats in the belfry!

definition: If you break out in a cold sweat, you begin to perspire a lot, usually from anxiety.
example: I used to get nervous at the dentist’s and break out in a cold sweat.

definition: Someone or something described as a dead loss is absolutely useless or a complete failure.
example: When it comes to painting, my sister is a dead loss.

definition: do the same as another person has just done.
example: The first suspect pointed the gun at the officer. The other followed suit.

definition: This idiom means to have a romantic relationship with someone.
example: They have been going steady with each other for the past few years.

definition: If you are in somebody’s good or bad books, you have their approval or disapproval.
example: I’m in my girlfriend’s bad books at the moment because I forgot about our anniversary.

definition: When someone behaves in such a foolish way in public that they look ridiculous, they make an exhibition of themselves.
example: Please, stop doing that! You’re making an exhibition of yourself!

definition: Circumstances or events that will make or break someone or something will cause either total success or total ruin.
example: This mission will make or break his career.

definition: If a person is over the hill, they have reached an age when they can no longer perform as well as before.
example: You are quite over the hill, but still dance very well.

definition: This term refers to a protected budget and only able to be used for a particular purpose.
example: Without a ring-fenced budget it is hard to implement these projects.

definition: This idiom means to have achieved a small victory which has made you believe you can win a more important victory.
example: Their team tasted blood in the local championship and now they want more.

definition: to be interested in something, to enjoy something a lot or to think something is particularly important.
example: Make sure you thank her. She’s big on politeness.

phrase: where there’s a will, there’s a way
definition: This expression means that willpower will defeat any difficulty.
example: I drove through five countries in my car. Where there is a will, there is a way.

phrase: whole caboodle / whole kit and caboodle
definition: This expression means everything.
example: I like everything about summer – the light, the warmth, the nights – the whole caboodle.

definition: Someone or something that is a cut above the others is better or of higher quality.
example: The watches in this store are a cut above the others.

definition: If you are all fingers and thumbs, you are clumsy and do things incorrectly.
example: Would you mind wrapping this gift for me? I’m all fingers and thumbs!

definition: This phrase means to persuade someone to accept something that is of a low quality or different from what they really wanted.
example: She fobbed the cupcakes off on her boyfriend.

definition: This idiom refers to a person who adopts a deliberately androgynous appearance, by use of unisex make-up, hair-style and clothing.
example: David Bowie was the archetype gender bender.

definition: This idiom means to give credit to an opponent’s merits, grudgingly or not.
example: I don’t like what they have done, but give the devil his due, sales have improved.

definition: This idiom means to say or do something in a very complicated way when it could be very simple.
example: Don’t go all round the houses. Just tell me what’s wrong.

phrase: are going it all hammer and tongs
definition: they are arguing fiercely, with a lot of energy and noise.
example: They are going it all hammer and tongs again. We should call the police.

definition: This expression refers to the way of life of another social group, especially a wealthier one.
example: She has spent two year showing TV viewers how the other half lives.

phrase: like water off a duck’s back
definition: Criticism, comments or warnings that have no effect on somebody are referred to as being like water off a duck’s back.
example: People are warned of the dangers of smoking but it’s like water off a duck’s back.

definition: If you make up for lost time, you increase your efforts or work harder to complete something or meet a deadline.
example: I haven’t made any progress with my book these days, but I will make up for lost time.

definition: To say that someone is no spring chicken means that they are quite old or well past their youth.
example: “How old is she?” “I don’t know, but she is no spring chicken.”

definition: This expression means that there is only one suitable way of dealing with something.
example: There are no two ways about it. You can’t accept the favor, so you must refuse the gift.

phrase: Be on a wing and a prayer
definition: This idiom means that one is in a difficult situation and is reliant on luck to get out of it.
example: He was on a wing and a prayer to get to the end of the marathon.

definition: This idiom means exactly on time.
example: I was asked to be there at three on the dot.

definition: doing something dishonest or fraudulent to get money, avoid taxes, or gain an unfair advantage
example: They could be on the fiddle, as the police claims.

definition: A black day is a day on which something terrible has happened.
example: Every person has a black day at least once in their lifetime.

definition: This term refers to an unsuccessful competitor whose performance is so much poorer than the winner’s that it appears insignificant.
example: She entered the contest hoping that she wouldn’t end up as an also-ran.

definition: This idiom refers to something that one knows or understands nothing about.
example: This intricate formula is a closed book to me.

definition: This term refers to the higher levels of government or administration where important decisions are made.
example: The matter is being discussed in the corridors of power nowadays.

definition: This phrase means to moderate one’s language, to keep within the bounds of what is prudent or polite. Minced words are usually referred to in the negative “do not mince your words”.
example: Don’t mince your words. Say whatever you think is necessary!

definition: This phrase refers to diarrhea that is often suffered by tourists when travelling to foreign parts of the world.
example: She suffers from Montezuma’s revenge. She will be fine.

definition: This expression means very near to where somebody lives.
example: The biggest park in the city is right at my doorstep.

definition: This idiom means “showing or experiencing a noticeable or conspicuous increase, improvement or expansion”.
example: Our small county has been one of the few in the region to be on the upswing since the recession.

definition: if you have had an unpleasant or hurtful experience doing something once, you will be much more cautious or hesitant to do it again.
example: I’m never going to get fooled again. Once bitten, twice shy!

definition: If something such as news, rumours or gossip spread like wildfire, it becomes widely known very fast.
example: As soon as she married him, the news spread like wildfire.

definition: If you tide someone over, you support them through a difficult period for a certain length of time.
example: I have enough food to tide you over for two days.

definition: To say that a person could do something till the cows come home means that they could do it for a long time.
example: You can ask me till the cows come home but I’m not buying you a car!

phrase: to be shown the red card
definition: This expression derives from football terminology and means to be dismissed from your job.
example: The financial manager was shown the red card yesterday.

definition: When someone does something up to the hilt, they do it completely, fully or to the maximum degree.
example: They were involved in the mission up to the hilt.

definition: a life protected by extreme luck or magic, where a person easily avoids danger or hardship
example: She won’t have a charmed life, that’s for sure.

definition: If you are a sport, you are generous and/or sportsmanlike.
example: Sorry that our ball is in your garden again. Be a sport and throw it back over the fence.

phrase: botch up / make a botch of
definition: If you spoil something, or make a mess of it, by doing a job badly or incorrectly, you make a botch of it or you botch it up.
example: I tried to assemble the new desk, but I botched it up.

definition: This idiom means to get ready for action.
example: Our company is clearing the decks for setting up new projects.

definition: If you fish in troubled waters, you try to gain advantages for yourself from a disturbed state of affairs.
example: After the French revolution, some statesmen were accused of fishing in troubled waters.

definition: Someone who has got it made is so happy and successful in life that they have no worries.
example: With a healthy family, a new car and a well-paid job, he has got it made.

definition: A traditional belief or idea which has been proved wrong by science is called an old wives’ tale.
example: The belief that eating a lot of chocolate causes acne is an old wives’ tale.

definition: A person who is on tenterhooks is in a state of anxious suspense or excitement.
example: The candidates were kept on tenterhooks for days.

definition: An activity or task that is plain sailing is without difficulty or free from trouble.
example: Once the mission was approved, it was plain sailing.

phrase: put / pull the wool over somebody’s eyes
definition: This idiom means to deceive someone into thinking well of them.
example: I’m too smart for you to try and put wool over my eyes.

definition: Treatment or justice that does not seem fair or is too severe, is called rough justice.
example: The way the politician was treated by the media was rough justice.

definition: This refers to a physical or moral characteristic that is common to many members of a family.
example: Blonde hair and green eyes – the combination runs in the family.

definition: This refers to a very basic or foolish mistake.
example: I made a schoolboy error yesterday, but in the end everything was fine.

definition: If you take stock of a situation you assess all the aspects in order to form an opinion.
example: I took time to take stock of the situation before taking a decision.

phrase: take the words out of someone’s mouth
definition: If you say exactly what someone else was going to say, you take the words out of their mouth.
example: You have taken the words out of my mouth.

phrase: your guess is as good as mine
definition: When you talk to another person and say “your guess is as good as mine”, it means that neither of you knows the answer.
example: What happened between them? Have they broken apart? Your guess is as good as mine!

definition: If something is as stiff as a poker, it is very straight, rigid or inflexible.
example: She stood as stiff as a poker after her name was called.

definition: This means that it is very dark and it is hard to see anything.
example: There was another power cut last night; it was as black as night in my apartment.

phrase: cut off one’s nose to spite one’s face
definition: This phrase means to disadvantage oneself through a wilful attempt to gain an advantage or assert oneself.
example: I will do anything except for cutting off my nose to spite my face.

definition: People with the herd mentality tend to do what everyone else does, no matter how ridiculous or stupid it might be.
example: There are many examples of herd mentality nowadays. Just pay more attention and you’ll observe them.

definition: If something such as a statement, saying or theory holds good, it continues to be true, valid or applicable.
example: The suspect’s statement still holds good.

definition: This expression, which derives from wrestling, is used to describe something done with no restraints, limits or rules of conduct.
example: It’s a live talk show with no holds barred, so you have to be prepared.

definition: If someone is on the gravy train, they have found an easy way to make money, one that requires little effort and is without risk.
example: Since the little town has become fashionable, she charges for every photograph taken of their mansion – she’s on the gravy train.

definition: Someone who is sitting pretty is in a good or fortunate situation, especially compared to others who are not so lucky.
example: She sold her shares at the perfect time so she’s now sitting pretty.

definition: This idiom means to use force and threats to make people do what you want.
example: I never strong-armed anybody.

definition: This idiom refers to anything that is available or is found by chance, rather than something chosen, planned or prepared.
example: I had no idea which hotel would be best, so I took pot luck with the first one.

phrase: things that go bump in the night
definition: This phrase refers to frightening but imagined supernatural events.
example: Don’t be scared! This is just one of those things that go bump in the night.

phrase: Give someone or smth wide berth
definition: If you give someone or something a wide berth, you stay at a prudent distance from them in order to avoid unwanted consequences.
example: The only way to be there on time is by giving the town centre a wide berth.

definition: This idiom refers to a glamorous blonde.
example: Is Melania Trump a blonde bombshell?

definition: This expression refers to an irresistible victory or an easy success.
example: The analysts are predicting a clean sweep for the ruling party in the approaching elections.

definition: This expression means to request someone to repeat what has just been said.
example: Come again? I didn’t understand.

definition: Someone or something exceptionally good will eventually attract attention or stand out from the rest, just as cream rises to the top in coffee or tea.
example: I knew you would succeed. Cream rises to the top!

definition: Something that is certain to happen or be achieved is a dead cert.
example: After such praise, his appointment as a commander is a dead cert.

definition: When you scold someone severely, you give them a tongue-lashing.
example: The professor gave her a tongue-lashing when she arrived late.

phrase: give him an inch and he’ll take a mile
definition: if you let someone have a small favor or a tiny bit of freedom, they will abuse your kindness and demand much more
example: If you let the kids stay up later on the weekends, they'll want to do it all the time. Give them an inch and they'll take a mile

definition: If you go against the tide/stream, you refuse to conform to current trends, or the opinions or behaviour of other people.
example: It might be difficult to work with her. She usually goes against the tide.

definition: If a quality, principle or opportunity goes out the window, it disappears, is lost or abandoned.
example: When the big company closed down, all hopes of finding a job in that little town went out the window.

definition: When you hit the panic button, you raise the alarm too quickly or react to a situation with fear and confusion.
example: Mary, calm down! There’s no need to hit the panic button.

definition: This expression means to go out of sight, usually after having done something bad.
example: She should lie low after having done that…

definition: If someone or something makes inroads, for example in a new field or area, they advance successfully or make progress.
example: Electric cars have made inroads into the European market.

definition: If you make yourself scarce, you go away from a difficult situation in order to avoid trouble.
example: When they started to quarrel, I decided to make myself scarce.

definition: Someone who is not all there behaves strangely at times or seems a bit odd.
example: Our neighbour wears a hat even in summer; he’s not all there!

definition: When a group or organisation is run in a well-ordered and disciplined manner, the person in charge runs a taut/tight ship.
example: The general manager runs a taut ship.

definition: This expression can be used in a situation where timing and meeting any deadlines are essential and required.
example: We must finish this draft. Time is of the essence.

phrase: tongues are wagging / set tongues wagging
definition: When tongues are wagging, people are beginning to spread gossip or rumours, often about someone’s private life.
example: That photo really set tongues wagging.

definition: If you vote with your feet, you show your dislike or disapproval of something by leaving.
example: If this year’s conference is boring, people will vote with their feet.

definition: If something is worth your while, it is a useful thing to do and deserves the time spent on it.
example: It will be worth your while to attend the meeting.

definition: This expression means thirteen.
example: I want a baker’s dozen candies.

definition: If someone tries to blind you with science, they confuse you with their knowledge by using difficult or technical words.
example: When you ask him for a simple explanation, he blinds you with science.

definition: The term grass roots refers to the ordinary people who form the main body of a society, movement or organisation.
example: I spent two years trying to design education policy for grass roots.

definition: To have pins and needles means to have a tingling sensation in a part of the body, when it has been in the same position for a long time.
example: I’ve been in the same position for hours. I have pins and needles.

definition: Something that is in mint condition is in such perfect condition that it looks new or as good as new.
example: My car is five years old but according to her, it is in mint condition.

definition: This idiom is used to say that one has learned something from an experience that is surprising and usually unpleasant.
example: I thought I could trust her, but it turned out that I was wrong. Live and learn!

definition: a harsh, unreasonable, or merciless demand for repayment or revenge, insisted upon even if it causes great harm or suffering to the debtor
example: I need the money back. I know it’s a pound of flesh.

definition: If you sail close to the wind, you do something dangerous or act just within the limits of what is legal or acceptable.
example: They seem to invest their money well, although they often sail close to the wind.

phrase: take your courage in both hands
definition: If you take your courage in both hands, you make yourself do something very brave.
example: When I saw the children in the burning house, I took my courage in both hands and rescued them.

definition: If someone is tearing their hair out, they are extremely agitated or distressed about something.
example: She’s been tearing her hair out all day trying to contact him.

definition: If you are in a tight squeeze, you are in a cramped or crowded situation.
example: I managed to get to the market but it was a tight squeeze.

definition: This idiom means “kind and loving, especially by touching and holding people more than is usual, often in a way that makes other people uncomfortable”.
example: He has a touchy-feely approach which I don’t like.

definition: This idiom refers to an unpleasant or painful situation or person that you have to accept and deal with.
example: The villagers lost all their crop to heavy rain. It was a heavy cross to bear.

phrase: an iron (fist/hand) in a velvet glove
definition: This expression is used to describe someone who, behind an appearance of gentleness, is inflexible and determined.
example: To impose the necessary company reforms, the manager used persuasion followed by wage reductions – an iron fist in a velvet glove.

definition: If you carry the can for another person, you accept blame or take responsibility for something that goes wrong, even if it is not your fault or only partly.
example: The writer didn’t show for the interview and his agent had to carry the can.

definition: If something costs a pretty penny, it costs a lot of money.
example: His new car must have cost a pretty penny!

definition: To go over something with a fine-tooth comb means to examine it closely and thoroughly so as not to miss any details.
example: We have to examine the crime scene with a fine-tooth comb.

phrase: get on like a house on fire
definition: Two people who get on like a house on fire have similar interests and quickly become good friends.
example: I hope to meet a girl with whom I would get on like a house on fire.

definition: This idiom means drunk.
example: He’s really ginned up this night.

phrase: it’s not over until the fat lady sings
definition: This is one of the most well known and most used idioms from the show business. When you say this expression it means that nothing is over until it is truly over.
example: Don’t lose focus now. It’s not over until the fat lady sings.

definition: If you make light of something, you behave as though it is less serious than it really is.
example: You shouldn’t make light of this dangerous mission.

definition: This idiom means not brave enough to say what you mean directly and honestly.
example: The mealy-mouthed politician lost the election.

definition: A person who is as proud as a peacock is extremely proud.
example: When my brother won first prize, I was as proud as a peacock.

definition: If someone is as stubborn as a mule, they are very obstinate and unwilling to listen to reason or change their mind.
example: I’ve talked to her, but she won’t change her mind. She is as stubborn as a mule.

definition: This expression is used when the result of a contest or election is difficult to predict.
example: Who do you think will win? It’s anyone’s call.

definition: This is a slang for dead.
example: That bird has just landed on the power cable. It’s brown bread for sure.

phrase: get / have someone by the short hairs
definition: If you get/have someone by the short hairs, you put them in a difficult situation from which they cannot escape, so you have complete control over them.
example: I wasn’t in a position to refuse them; they got me by the short hairs.

definition: If you say that something is the last thing on your mind, you mean that it is not an important matter at all, especially when you have more serious problems to consider.
example: I’m so busy that preparing dinner is the last thing on my mind.

definition: If you lose your shirt, you lose all your money or possessions, especially as a result of speculation or gambling.
example: Our friend has lost his shirt by gambling and we can’t help him much.

definition: The mental power to influence one’s body and overcome physical difficulties is said to be a question of mind over matter.
example: She knew she couldn’t be cured, but she managed to live until the baby was born – a case of mind over matter.

definition: This phrase refers to someone who is old fashioned. It can also directly refer to old fashion too.
example: The store keeper is an old hat. You won’t be given a discount.

definition: This phrase means to induce someone to join the military. More recently, the phrase is used to mean “make impromptu use of” some article or person to fulfil some task – usually someone or thing that isn’t normally used for such a task.
example: Steve has been pressed into service by his manager.

definition: This idiom means to ask/aim for the best or the most you could hope for.
example: You might shoot for the moon and ask for a promotion.

definition: Someone who has a sweet tooth enjoys eating sweet things like sugar, pastries, chocolate etc.
example: Marry will be delighted if you bring her chocolates – she has a sweet tooth.

definition: If you take steps, you start a course of action in order to accomplish something.
example: The government is taking steps to improve social security.

definition:
a decision or action is final, and you cannot change it or go back.
Point of no return
example: From the moment the peace negotiations failed, the die was cast.

definition: If you say that there’s nothing to it, you mean that something is very simple or easy to do.
example: I’ll show you how to make fries. There’s nothing to it!

definition: This idiom refers to a team whose players showed a lot of determination to succeed.
example: They got stuck in and truly deserved to win.

definition: A simplified response that is memorized or prepared in advance is called a pat answer.
example: Most journalists at the press conference found her pat answers frustrating.

definition: If you get a rude awakening, you are forced to accept the unpleasant truth or reality.
example: She thought I would want her back, but she got a rude awakening.

definition: Someone who is as bold as brass behaves without shame or embarrassment.

phrase: break every rule in the book

definition: A person who is a chip off the old block resembles one of their parents in appearance, character or behaviour.

definition: If you collect your thoughts, you try to think calmly and clearly in order to prepare yourself mentally for something.
example: Mary stopped to collect her thoughts before speaking to her boyfriend.

phrase: come in all shapes and sizes
definition: Something that can be found in many different forms, types or varieties, comes in all shapes and sizes.
example: Laptops come in all shapes and sizes these days.

definition: If two people are cut from the same cloth, they are very similar in character or behaviour.
example: Although the sisters look alike, they are not cut from the same cloth.

phrase: cut the ground from under someone’s feet
definition: When someone cuts the ground from under another’s feet, they do something which weakens their position or spoils their plans.
example: When we launched the new digital product, I think that we cut the ground from under our competitors’ feet.

definition: If a person goes stir-crazy, they become very agitated or nervous because they have been confined to a place for too long.
example: After several days in the camp, I went stir-crazy.

phrase: hit one where it hurts most
definition: This idiom means to attack one in the area is most vulnerable or that will result in the most harm.
example: By questioning his skills, Gina hit Kim where it hurt most.

definition: This expression means these modern times.
example: It’s hard to find your soul mate in this day and age.

definition: This expression highlights disbelief or the idea that miracles might happen but are extremely unlikely.
example: My grandfather using a smartphone? Yeah…and pigs might fly!

definition: A show of hands is a method of voting where people give their opinion by raising a hand.
example: How many of you agree to this plan? Could we have a show of hands, please?

definition: If you take something upon yourself, you do it without asking for permission or agreement.
example: My colleague took it upon himself to rearrange the office.

definition: This idiom refers to the person or people with the most authority, power or influence in a group or organization.
example: You’ll obtain the answer only if you talk to the top brass.

definition: This idiom means to be completely conscious of the real status of situation.
example: I am under no illusion that living in that country is hard.

definition: This refers to a jumble of words or letters, often referring to organisations known by their initials, like NASA or BBC.
example: Institutions of the European Union are confusing – a real alphabet soup.

definition: If you decide to clear the air, you try to remove the causes of fear, worry or suspicion by taking about the problem openly.
example: The atmosphere at work became so unpleasant that we decided it was time to clear the air.

definition: If you need some elbow room, you need more space to move.
example: I can’t stand this office anymore. I need some elbow room.

phrase: fish rots from the head down
definition: This expression refers to failing organizations and how the blame of it should be on its “head” (leadership).
example: The company was bound to be closed. A fish rots from the head down after all.

definition: This expression is used to describe people or things that are difficult to classify, that are neither one thing nor another.
example: I really don’t know what species this living creature is. It’s neither fish nor fowl.

definition: This idiom refers to a day of significance, like a birthday or anniversary.
example: Tomorrow is his red letter day. He always celebrates it with a big party.

phrase: take your life into your hands
definition:
to do something extremely dangerous where you face a serious risk of death or severe harm

example: If you drive on this dangerous road, you will be taking your life into your hands.

definition: This idiom means that a particular opportunity has passed by and now it is too late.
example: She waited too long to apply for this well-paid job and now the ship has sailed.

phrase: the writing is on the wall
definition: This phrase is used whenever an inevitable result or imminent danger has become apparent.
example: They have officially declared war on us. The writing is on the wall.

definition: This idiom means that you have lots to say, but you are not willing to engage in a fight.
example: There’s always a guy who disappears when trouble starts – all bark and no bite.

definition: This idiom means “in control, in charge”.
example: He is the first man to be at the helm of this company.

definition: This phrase means to do whatever is necessary to get something.
example: I will get a new smartphone, whether I have to beg, borrow or steal.

phrase: don’t count your chickens before the eggs have hatched
definition: This idiom is used to express that you shouldn’t make plans for something that might not happen.
example: Let’s wait another month. Don’t count your chickens before the eggs have hatched.

definition: This idiom refers to an act of treachery, perpetrated on a previous partner in a deceit.
example: The diamond thief double-crossed his partners.

phrase: let smth slip through your fingers
definition: If you let something slip through your fingers, such as a good opportunity, you fail to obtain it or keep it.
example: That a good price. I won’t let this apartment slip through my fingers.

phrase: like a lamb to the slaughter
definition: If someone does something or goes somewhere like a lamb to the slaughter, they do it without knowing that something bad is going to happen and therefore act calmly and without fighting against the situation.
example: He was heading towards prison like a lamb to the slaughter.

phrase: like ships that pass in the night
definition: This expression refers to people who meet briefly and are not likely to meet again.
example: We met once, like ships that pass in the night.

definition: This expression means to fail to keep in contact.
example: Don’t ever lose touch with your best friends.

definition: This idiom means to do something that will cause a series of actions to start.
example: It’s the manager’s task to set the wheels in motion.

definition: If two or more people speak the same language, they have similar opinions or ideas, so they understand each other very well.
example: We work very well together because we speak the same language.

definition: This expression is said when trying something for the third time.
example: Two divorces and now I’m planning to engage again. It’s third time lucky!

definition: When there are two options or possibilities to choose from, and both are equally good, the choice between the two is called a toss-up.
example: Both athletes are in excellent condition. It’s a toss-up.

definition: People use this expression when complaining about a situation or job which they find unpleasant or unsatisfactory.
example: I strongly believe that it’s a dog’s life working in the accounting department.

phrase: above and beyond the call of duty
definition: If a person does something which is above and beyond the call of duty, they show a greater degree of courage or effort than is usually required or expected in their job.
example: The police officer received a medal for his action which went above and beyond the call of duty.

definition: Two people who are like chalk and cheese are completely different from each other.
example: I’m surprised that they get on well. They are like chalk and cheese from my point of view.

definition: This idiom refers to an awkward, unsophisticated man.
example: He’s just a country bumpkin.

definition: If you avoid or miss something by a hair’s breadth, you only just manage to escape from a danger.
example: The window fell and missed the kid by a hair’s breadth.

definition: Something that is hard to come by is rare or difficult to find.
example: Experienced mechanics are hard to come by nowadays.

definition: This idiom means to be ill, unhappy or in a bad state.
example: She was thin and generally in a bad way.

phrase: no use crying over spilt milk
definition: This expression means that it is useless to complain or have regrets about something that is done and cannot be changed.
example: I regret not accepting the job, but it’s no use crying over split milk.

definition: If something you do pays dividends, it brings advantages or rewards at a later date.
example: The time he spent learning German paid dividends when he started looking for a job.

definition: If you run the show, it means that you are in charge of every part of it.
example: It has been decided that I am to run the show with this project.

definition: When the heavens open, it suddenly starts to rain heavily.
example: As soon as the final competition started, the heavens opened and the runners were soaked.

definition: The knowledge that you have done the right thing, or that you have acted in a moral way, is a sufficient reward and you should not expect more.
example: I’m glad that you’ve helped the poor man. Virtue is its own reward!

definition: If you meet or find your match, you encounter someone who is equal to you in skills or abilities.
example: She is an excellent billiards player but she met her match.

definition: When someone tries to soften the blow, they do something to make an unpleasant event or action easier to accept.
example: In spite of the extra payment given to soften the blow, the loss of my job was a catastrophe for me.

definition: If something stands the test of time, people continue to find it valuable or useful after many years.
example: This teaching method has stood the test of time.

definition: This idiom refers to a person who comes to the aid of another when other hopes have faded, like the knights in romantic stories.
example: Oh, thank you so much, Oliver! You are a knight in shining armour!

definition: If something is described or defined with/in broad strokes, it is outlined in a very general way, without any details.
example: She explained the situation in broad strokes.

phrase: can’t make omelette without breaking eggs
definition: This expression means that it is impossible to make important changes without causing some unpleasant effects.
example: A lot of people will lose their jobs after the merger, but you can’t make an omelette without breaking eggs.

definition: If a person does something come rain or shine, they do it regularly, whatever the circumstances.
example: Come rain or shine, I have to take my dog for a walk.

definition: If you refer to a situation, problem or solution as cut and dried, you mean that it is clear and straightforward with no likely complications.
example: When the new financial manager arrived, she didn’t find the situation as cut and dried as she had expected.

definition: A person who is dead to the world is fast asleep.
example: Don’t worry because you won’t disturb her. She’s dead to the world.

phrase: get into the swing of something
definition: When you get into the swing of something, you become involved in it or get used to it and begin to enjoy it.
example: It will be more fun when you get into the swing of cycling.

definition: If you give the slip to somebody who is following you, you manage to hide or get away from them.
example: The police were chasing him, but somehow he gave them the slip.

definition: activating your personal charm, confidence, energy, sex appeal, or magical touch to succeed or attract someone
example: I won! I’ve got my mojo working again.

definition: If you know someone inside out, you know them very well.
example: We’ve been friends since childhood. We know each other inside out.

definition: If you make someone see reason, you persuade them to stop acting foolishly and behave more sensibly.
example: She wanted to drop out of school last year, but I managed to make her see reason.

phrase: not for all the tea in China
definition: To say that you would not do something for all the tea in China means that you would not do it under any conditions.
example: I wouldn’t leave this company for all the tea in China.

phrase: sting someone for an amount of money
definition: If you sting someone for an amount of money, you make them pay for something, usually in a deceitful manner.
example: Not only was the date boring but I was stung for $30.

definition: If something is murder, it is very difficult or uncomfortable.Now sounds dated
example: The journey home through that poor country was murder!

definition: This phrase means to progress from one success to another higher level of success.
example: That’s my life: from strength to strength.

definition: This expression is used to express relief at becoming free of an unpleasant or unwanted person or thing.
example: I’ve got rid of the old laptop. Good riddance!

definition: This idiom means to contrive a secret plot or scheme, especially with selfish motives.
example: I think they have designs on my marketing project.

definition: A person who has their heart in the right place has kind feelings and good intentions, even if the results are not too good.
example: My wife’s cake wasn’t wonderful but she’s got her heart in the right place.

phrase: rise for one’s years / wise beyond your years
definition: Someone who is wise for their years or wise beyond their years has more knowledge and experience than most people at their age.
example: You will be surprised. He’s wise beyond his years.

definition: This expression means that when you see something you can be sure it exists. It can also mean that what you have been told is really true.
example: Steve says cherries grow in his garden, but seeing is believing.

definition: If you whistle in the dark, you try to hide your fear and pretend to be brave in a scary or dangerous situation.
example: Steven seemed confident but we all knew he was whistling in the dark.

definition: If you are wrapped up in an activity, you are totally concentrated on it.
example: I was so wrapped up in my work that I didn’t realize they had gone.

phrase: you can’t take it with you
definition: This expression is a suggestion that you should spend money and live life now as it will be no use to you after you die.
example: You should buy that car that you like. You can’t take it with you, remember?

definition: A statement or expression that is easy to understand or has an obvious meaning is as clear as crystal / daylight.
example: I’ve got it. It’s as clear as crystal.

definition: A busman’s holiday is when you spend your spare time or your holidays doing the same sort of activity as you do in your job.
example: My wife is a babysitter, so for her time off with the family is often a busman’s holiday.

definition: This idiom means to stop speaking.
example: Please, button your lip!

definition: If things come up roses, the end result is successful or positive, even if there were difficult times.
example: After several hard times, everything seems to be coming up roses for the officer.

definition: This idiom refers to a roughly organized assembly of individuals of various backgrounds, appearance and character.
example: The organization was best described as a motley crew.

definition: If something such as an organisation or sports team needs “new blood”, it needs to recruit people who come with new ideas, energy and enthusiasm in order to improve it.
example: We need new blood this year. Many people within our organisation are retiring.

definition: A silver-tongued person is a smooth talker who speaks so convincingly that they manage to persuade others to do what they want.
example: A silver-tongues salesman persuaded my father to buy a new laptop.

definition: This humorous expression, based on superstition, is used to avoid bad luck, often while touching something made of wood.
example: The parcel will arrive soon – touch wood.

phrase: as thick as two short planks
definition: This simile means exceedingly stupid.
example: Your cousin is as thick as two short planks!

definition: The term dead wood refers to people or things which are no longer considered useful or necessary.
example: The financial manager wants to reduce costs by cutting out the dead wood.

definition: To describe someone’s achievement as a feather in their cap means that it is something they can be proud of or something that may serve as an advantage.
example: Passing the interview was another feather in her cap.

definition: Someone who lives high off/on the hog has a lot of money and a very comfortable lifestyle.
example: As far as I know, they are living high off the hog now.

definition: A loan shark is a person who lends money at extremely high interest rates to people who are unable to obtain a loan from the bank.
example: The man was threatened because he was late paying back money to a loan shark.

definition: If you attach a lot of importance to something, or make it a special occasion, you make a big thing of it.
example: It’s her birthday but she doesn’t want to make a big thing of it.

definition: This idiom refers to a complex, tricky or odd person.
example: My best friend has the weirdest opinions; he’s a real piece of work.

definition: This idiom means excessively rigid in matters of conduct; narrow or over-precise in one’s behaviour or moral judgement.
example: Our new manager is a strait-laced man.

definition: When there is a need for all hands on deck, everyone must help, especially if there’s a lot of work to be done in a short amount of time.
example: Next week we will have a lot of work to do, so it will be all hands on deck.

definition: Someone who is as pleased or proud as punch is delighted or feels very satisfied about something.
example: He was as pleased as punch after winning the championship.

definition: This idiom is used when you complain about a loss from the past.
example: The hard times are over. There’s no use crying over spilt milk!

definition: Someone who has their heart set on something wants it very much.
example: From an early age I had my heart set on becoming a professional driver.

definition: If you try everything possible in order to achieve or to find something, you leave no stone unturned.
example: The police left no stone unturned in their efforts to find the murderer.

definition:
This expression means engaged in active fighting or dispute.
a state of direct, unmasked combat between opposing forces or severe, overt conflict following a period of truce, tension, or covert hostility
example: Whenever they see us they throw stones at us and we do the same – it’s open warfare.

definition: To say that someone is papering over the cracks means that they are concealing a problem rather than dealing with it effectively.
example: The measures taken to reduce air pollution are just paper over the cracks.

definition: If you test the waters, you try to find out how acceptable or successful something is before becoming involved in it.
example: You should test the waters first.

definition: This idiom means loyal and unwavering on one’s opinion or support for a cause.
example: You don’t need to worry about her – she’s true-blue.

definition: This expression means that what you eat affects you health.
example: Be careful how you plan your meals. You are what you eat!

definition: This idiom means that there is more than one way to achieve something.
example: Take any route because all roads lead to Rome.

definition: When people who have had a disagreement decide to forget their quarrel and become friends again, they bury the hatchet.
example: I didn’t agree with her decision, but I decided to bury the hatchet.

definition: If you use a carrot-and-stick approach, you use the promise of reward and the threat of punishment to make someone work harder.
example: Many parents use a carrot-and-stick approach to obtain good results from their children nowadays.

definition: An amount of money considered small or unimportant is called chicken feed.
example: I got a job during summer weekends but the pay was chicken feed.

definition: If two or more people come to blows, they start to fight.
example: The debate was so intense that the participants came to blows.

definition: This expression is used when a lot of work needs to be completed.
example: We still have a lot of ground to cover so as to finish the project on time.

definition: This expression is used when you can afford to wait before doing or achieving something.
example: I failed yesterday, but I have time on my side. I will try again soon.

phrase: know which side your bread is buttered
definition: to understand where your best interests, profits, or advantages lie so that you can act to keep yourself in a favorable position
example: Shelia never argues with her mother-in-law. She knows which side her bread is buttered.

definition: This idiom means to try and improve a bad relationship with another party.
example: After the nasty fight with his brother, Steve decided to mend fences.

definition: This is an informal way to tell someone to stop talking and/or make less noise.
example: Will you tell your children to pipe down?

definition: People who run round in circles have difficulty in achieving something because of lack of organisation.
example: Running round in circles will lead you nowhere! You need to conceive a plan and follow it.

definition: If you have a one-track mind, you have a tendency to think about only one subject.
example: The girl has a one-track mind; all she thinks about is dancing.

definition: When a person does everything they are engaged in completely and thoroughly, they are said to do nothing by halves.
example: She cooks seldom but when she does it, it’s a three-course meal – she does nothing by halves.

definition: This idiom means to accept and participate with an idea or in a project.
example: After I heard his case, I got on board and did my best to help him.

definition: This expression is used to humorously say that someone has died.
example: Have you heard that the old lady went to meet her maker?

definition: Someone who pounds the pavement walks the streets or goes from company to company, usually in search of employment. One can also pound the pavement in an effort to raise funds or gain support for a cause.
example: I’m going to pound the pavement until I find a better job.

definition: This idiom means to act in a wild or dangerous manner.
example: With the teacher absent, the children were running amok in their class.

definition: Something that does not need to be discussed because it is already understood or agreed upon can be taken as read.
example: We’re going on holiday and please take it as read that you are all invited.

phrase: throw / toss your hat in / into the ring
definition: If you throw or toss your hat in the ring, you announce that you are going to enter a competition or take up a challenge.
example: She finally threw her hat in the ring. The fight was about to begin.

definition: If a task or activity is a doddle, it is very easy to do or perform.
example: How did the test go? No problem, it was a doddle.

definition: When you come into your own, you finally obtain rightful recognition of your ability or talent and begin to have success.
example: She is a talented actress who has finally come into her own.

definition: When you are in your element, you are doing something that you do well and you are enjoying yourself.
example: My cousin, who is an estate agent, was in his element when I asked him to search for a new house for a friend of mine.

phrase: money burns a hole in your pocket
definition: To say that money burns a hole in somebody’s pocket means that they are eager to spend it quickly or extravagantly.
example: As soon as he is paid he goes shopping. Money burns a hole in his pocket!

definition: This expression refers to someone or something that brings hope into the lives of others.
example: Her son is a real ray of sunshine for her.

definition: This expression refers to an unpleasant situation that frequently occurs in the same way as before.
example: It’s the same old story: she borrows money from me and “forgets” to pay me back.

definition: If you watch someone like a hawk, you keep your eyes on them or watch them very carefully.
example: For two hours I watched the children like a hawk.

definition: If you whitewash something, you cover up or gloss over faults or wrongdoings.
example: The government was accused of trying to whitewash the scandal over stolen funds.

definition: When everything is ready for an activity or event to begin, you can say that “all systems go”.
example: She’s got an office, a mobile phone and the internet, so on the next Monday it’s all systems go.

definition: If a person build bridges between opposing groups, they help them to cooperate and understand each other better.
example: The mayor is trying to build bridges between the local community and the owners of the new plant.

definition: This idiom has a metaphorical sense and means to chat in an aimless manner.
example: I don’t want to meet with them. They are always chewing the cud.

definition:
A day spent relaxing at home, often in bed.
This idiom refers to a work day which an employee is allowed to spend at home relaxing.
example: The manager rewarded us with a duvet day to do whatever we wanted.

definition: If you get a foothold somewhere, you secure a position for yourself in a business, profession or organisation.
example: We are still trying to get a foothold in the American market.

phrase: have a frog in one’s throat
definition: A person who has a frog in their throat has difficulty in speaking clearly because they have a cough or a sore throat.
example: Speaking was difficult for me today. I had a frog in my throat all day.

definition: If a person or organisation holds out an olive branch to another, they show that they want to end a disagreement and make peace.
example: In the evening, the group held out an olive branch to the other.

definition: This idiom refers to a hierarchy of status seen among members of a group of people or animals, originally as observed among hens.
example: She started as a clerk but gradually rose in the pecking order.

definition: This idiom means to demonstrate your true character.
example: In difficult times you can show your mettle.

definition: This can either refer to a cat that lives wild in a town or to a prostitute.
example: He spends all his money on alley cats.

definition: If you chew the fat with somebody, you chat in an informal way about unimportant things.
example: The amount of time my parents can spend chewing the fat with our neighbours is amazing.

definition: If a company dominates an area of business and leaves no room for competition, it is said to have cornered the market.
example: By importing extremely large quantities and selling at dumping prices, they have cornered the market in the end.

definition: This expression means that even though you have had a negative experience, you will have another chance in the future to try again.
example: I’ve been defeated in this championship but there no problem. I live to fight another day.

definition: When you defend or support a person, a belief or an idea, you stand up for them.
example: A growing number of citizens are standing up for civil rights.

phrase: give oneself airs / put on airs
definition: This idiom means to be pretentious / showy.   to behave as if one is better or more important than others
example:
You should stop giving yourself airs.
She gives herself such airs that everyone dislikes her.

definition: This idiom refers to an unseasonably warm, dry and calm weather, usually following a period of colder weather or frost in the late Autumn.
example: Indian summer has been forecast for the next period.

definition: To say “it’s beyond me” means that it is impossible for you to understand.
example: It’s beyond me why Maria still wants to marry him.

definition: If you prick up your ears, you suddenly pay attention to what is being said.
example: The little girl pricked up her ears when she heard the word “candy”.

phrase: put / set the cat among the pigeons
definition: This expression means to do or say something that causes trouble and make a lot of people angry or worried.
example: The new financial report sets the cat among the pigeons.

definition: This idiom refers to the ordinary members of a group, as opposed to the group leadership.
example: The rank and file didn’t agree to the plan.

definition: This idiom refers to one’s spoken opinion on a particular matter.
example: Ok, I’ll just throw in my two cents’ worth.

definition: If you learn something straight from the horse’s mouth, the information is given to you by someone who is directly involved in that situation.
example: I got this straight from the horse’s mouth – the police officer told me.

definition: to take a quick, casual look at something
example: The heating system isn’t working. I will take a gander at it in five minutes.

definition: A person who turns a deaf ear to something such as a request or a complaint refuses to pay attention to it.
example: I tried to explain the report to my manager but she turned a deaf ear.

phrase: absence makes the heart grow fonder
definition: This means that our feelings for people and things grow when we are apart from them.
example: I enjoyed visiting the city but I soon missed my girlfriend. As they say – absence makes the heart grow fonder.

phrase: get a kick out of something
definition: If you get a kick out of something, you feel enjoyment or excitement from something.
example: She gets a kick out of listening to other people’s conversations.

definition: This expression refers to a significant part of the effort or work needed to achieve something.
example: I’ve already obtained a loan for the flat – that’s half the battle.

phrase: little fish in a big pond
definition: This idiom refers to someone considered unimportant as compared to their more significant peers.
example: When the girl got to high-school, she was a little fish in a big pond.

definition: If you play by the rules, you behave in a fair and honest way with people.
example: You can trust her. She always play by the rules.

definition: When you put your feet up, you sit down and relax.
example: Come in and put your feet up.

definition: If you put the squeeze on someone, you put pressure on them to force them to do something.
example: She was reluctant to work with me until the manager put the squeeze on her.

phrase: the dice are loaded against someone
definition: If everything seems to work to your disadvantage and you are not likely to succeed, the dice are loaded against you.
example: I applied for the job, but being over fifty, the dice were loaded against me.

definition: A person who watches a situation without being noticed is called a fly on the wall.
example: I would love to be a fly on the wall when they discuss the matter.

definition: A person who is bright-eyed and bushy-tailed is very enthusiastic and full of energy.
example: She arrived bright-eyed and bushy-tailed at 7 am and worked with us all day long.

phrase: living off the fat of the land
definition: This idiom means living well.
example: Being wealthy, they are living off the fat of the land.

definition: A person who moves up in the world becomes more important in society or successful in their career.
example: My neighbour has moved up in the world since we were kids.

definition:
Literal balance: The physical adaptation required to adjust one's stance and inner ear to the rolling and pitching of a vessel at sea.
Idiomatic usage: Becoming accustomed to any new, unstable, or unfamiliar environment or task.
example: Usually, it takes a while in a new job to find your sea legs.

definition: If something sticks in your throat, it is very difficult to accept it and it makes you angry or resentful.
example: The way she treats me sticks in my throat. I think about resigning.

definition: If someone does something through thick and thin, they do it in spite of all the difficulties and problems.
example: I will help you through thick and thin.

definition: Someone who is in a tight spot is in a very difficult situation.
example: The recent crisis has put the company in a tight spot.

definition: A done deal refers to an agreement or decision which has been reached on a certain matter.
example: I am still considering all the available options, so it is not a done deal.

definition: This idiom means nonsense.
example: She says she has seen them together, which is a load of cobblers.

definition: This term refers to word-for-word details or very specific facts, especially the exact place where the information can be found.
example: This phrase is attributed to him, although I can’t give you chapter and verse.

definition: If you eat humble pie, you are forced to admit that you were wrong and apologize.
example: After criticizing her work, I had to eat humble pie when the results were announced.

definition: If you get or give the low-down, you get or give complete information or facts about something.
example: Don’t worry. I will call you after the meeting and give you the low-down.

definition: This means to make a significant improvement or dramatic advancement.
example: Our store has taken a quantum leap from where it was three years ago.

definition: If someone’s behaviour or something they say, sows the seeds of suspicion, it leads people to suspect that they are guilty.
example: The fact that the woman spent a lot of money after the robbery sowed the seeds of suspicion.

definition: If you tie yourself up in knots, you become totally confused or confuse others when trying to explain something.
example: He tied himself up in knots trying to explain the rules of the mission.

definition: This idiom means of the best quality; of the highest social standing.
example: The manager brought together a team of top-drawer designers and engineers.

phrase: why keep a dog and bark yourself?
definition: This expression means that if someone or something can do a task for you, there’s no reason to do it yourself.
example: My wife has an electric mixer but she continues to make cakes by hand. Why keep a dog and bark yourself?

definition: This idiom means to work very hard.
example: I worked like a dog to publish this book.

definition: This idiom is used when a woman is pregnant.
example: She has a bun in the oven; the baby is due in 3 months.

definition: To say that you don’t give a hoot means that you don’t care at all about something.
example: Have you noticed that Marry wears eccentric clothes every time? Oh, I don’t give a hoot.

definition: When you prepare the ground, you try to make it easier for a future event or action to happen or be accepted.
example: The team prepared the ground for negotiations.

definition: Someone who is ready to drop is nearly too exhausted to stay standing.
example: I’ve been training all day in the gym. I’m ready to drop!

definition: This idiom refers to something that is worn out, cheap or insignificant. To give someone the rinky-dink means to cheat them.
example: Their family business is a rinky-dink one.

definition: This idiom is used to tell someone to hurry or act more quickly.
example: Come on, Marry, shake a leg or we’ll be late.

definition: This expression is used to refer to an important, successful or influential person. However, it can have negative connotation and is often used sarcastically.
example: I heard you had become a big shot in the city. I’m surprised you still have time for me.

definition: If you get a slap on the wrist, you receive mild punishment or you are reprimanded for something you have done.
example: I got only a slap on the wrist.

definition: If you can eat all sorts of food and drink what you like, without any indigestion, discomfort or bad effects, it is said that you have a cast-iron stomach.
example: She is renowned for her cast-iron stomach.

definition: This idiom refers to the hottest days of the summer season.
example: These are the dog days of summer. That’s why it’s so hot.

phrase: err on the side of caution
definition: When uncertain about what to do, if you err on the side of caution you do more of what is adequate rather than take any risks.
example: Given the volatility in the market, I think we should err on the side of caution this period.

definition: This idiom means to earn a merit point for doing well.
example: Well done, team! You will get a gold star for this action.

definition: Someone who is getting on in years is growing old.
example: My aunt is getting on in years. Unfortunately, she needs help now.

definition: If you do something in your own sweet time, you take as long as you please to do it, in spite of the wishes of others.
example: Ok. I’ll do your project but in my own sweet time.

phrase: keep the wolf from the door
definition: To keep the wolf from the door you need to have enough money to buy food and other basic essentials in order to survive.
example: The family earned scarcely enough money to keep the wolf from the door.

definition: The darkest hour is the time when bad events are at their worst and most dispiriting.
example: Judging by the its seriousness, this is the darkest hour.

definition: This idiom means to do something very quickly.
example: It’s hard to understand him. He talks at a mile a minute!

definition: When someone does something late, this remark means that it is better to do it late than not do it at all.
example: You promised you’d come early to help me – but better late than never!

phrase: get off to a flying start
definition: If something gets off to a flying start, it is immediately successful.
example: I hope that the sales of my book will get off to a flying start.

definition: If somebody has a green thumb, they have an exceptional aptitude for gardening or for growing plants successfully.
example: Call Steve. He has a green thumb and he will help you.

definition: This idiom means to maintain strict or tight control over someone.
example: The manager has kept his assistant on a short leash.

definition: If you are so shocked, surprised or scared that you are rooted to the spot, your reaction is so strong that you are unable to move.
example: Nicole stood rooted to the spot as the plane landed abruptly.

definition: If an explanation, apology or promise sounds hollow, it seems false or insincere.
example: Her apology sounded hollow to me. I don’t believe she was sorry.

phrase: turn back the hands of time
definition: This idiom means to go back to the past, usually in moments of reminiscence or regret.
example: If you could turn back the hands of time, would you do anything differently?

definition: If somebody is whistling Dixie, they talk about things in a more positive way than the reality. This idiom is mainly used in the US.
example: Even if they know the truth, they are still whistling Dixie.

definition: This means a radical change.
example: There clearly was a sea change when Obama came in after Bush.

phrase: at the touch of a button
definition: If you can do something at the touch of a button, you can do it very easily, often thanks to technology.
example: From now, the security team can be alerted at the touch of a button.

definition: This expression means to write a paper or essay in a mechanical way.
example: She had to crank out a paper every two weeks to pass the course.

definition: If you are getting in someone’s hair, you are annoying them so much that they can’t get on with what they are doing.
example: I would have finished the report more quickly if she hadn’t got in my hair.

definition: If you get wise to something, you learn something that you were not aware of before.
example: I finally got wise to the fact that my wife was cheating on me.

definition: When trying to achieve something, if you go to great lengths or great pains, you do everything that is possible in order to succeed.
example: The parties went to great lengths to reach a draft agreement.

phrase: the shoe is on the other foot
definition: When the circumstances have reversed and one person is now doing what the other did in the past, you can say that the shoe is on the other foot.
example: As a team leader I used to advise her what to do. Now, the shoe is on the other foot.

definition: This idiom refers to an issue, law or matter that is no longer important or that no longer has force or power.
example: The peace agreement was a dead letter as soon as it was signed.

definition: This phrase refers to the number of people who have paid to watch a performance.
example: Lowering the prices should increase the number of bums on seats.

definition: This idiom means the greatest or most beautiful thing.
example: The crowning glory of his career came ten years after he got hired.

definition: This idiom means to make an individual contribution to an overall effort.
example: It’s our job to do our bit during each mission.

definition: If you eat crow, you admit that you were wrong about something and apologize.
example: Now I know that I’ve made a mistake. Therefore I had no option but to eat crow.

definition: To say that someone has fallen from grace, means that they have done something wrong, immoral or unacceptable, and as a result have lost their good reputation.
example: The manager fell from grace as a result of a sex abuse.

definition: If you give somebody all the information necessary to enable them to fully understand a situation, you put them in the picture.
example: Some things have been changed. Let me put you in the picture.

definition: If someone has stars in their eyes, they are looking extremely happy.
example: Having won, she had stars in her eyes.

definition: This idiom means under suspicion. It may also mean to become out of favour or to be in trouble.
example: Until proven innocent, every employee is under a cloud.

definition: To achieve something with flying colours means to do it very successfully.
example: I passed the entrance exams with flying colours.

definition: If you do something cap in hand, you ask for something in a very respectful manner.
example: I went to the manager, cap in hand, and asked for more time to complete the project.

definition: This idiom refers to a beard that has grown for one or two days and is then kept at this length in order to look fashionable.
example: She likes my designer stubble.

definition: When something, such as an event, gets into full swing, it is at its busiest or liveliest time.
example: When we got back home, the party was in full swing.

definition: To say that someone is pushing up the daisies means that they are dead.
example: Madame Smith? She’s been pushing up the daisies for over five years!

phrase: separate the wheat from the chaff
definition: This phrase means to separate things or people that are of high quality or ability from those that are not.
example: The first test really separates the wheat from the chaff.

definition: This idiom refers to asking serious questions and/or giving someone rough treatment to get information.
example: I got the third degree when I got home after missing for two weeks.

definition: If you consider something without giving it serious thought, you toy with the idea.
example: I toyed with the idea of moving abroad.

phrase: Have a whale of a time
definition: When people have a whale of a time, they enjoy themselves a lot.
example: I had a whale of a time that night.

definition: Someone who has eagle eyes sees or notices things more easily than others.
example: If she is there, she will be spotted by him. He has eagle eyes.

definition: Items, places or events which are rarely found or do not happen very often.
example: Fast food restaurants are few and far between in this part of the city.

definition: If you force someone’s hand, you make them do something unwillingly or sooner than planned.
example: The inspector forced Brandon’s hand and made him reveal the plan.

definition: This idiom means not to be able to do anything about a situation.
example: I feel like my hands are tied in this particular situation.

definition: This expression means that people with a lot of money have power and influence.
example: Be careful with the owner – money talks!

phrase: when it rains, it pours / it never rains but it pours
definition: when one bad thing happens, it is quickly followed by many other bad things, making a difficult situation much worse
example: I understand that when it rains, it pours. Therefore, that’s why I save as much as I can of my salary every month.

phrase: a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
definition: This means that what you have is worth more than what you might have later.
example: You should be happy now that you have a car. A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

definition: This idiom means “an unwelcome intruder in a place or situation”.
example: For us, Peter was a cuckoo in the nest.

definition: If you explore all avenues, you try out every possibility in order to obtain a result or find a solution.
example: I don’t know what to say about this mission. Let’s explore all avenues.

definition: to have a slight idea, hint, or vague feeling that something is true or about to happen, even if you are not entirely sure.
example:
Ask him. He may have an inkling.
I didn't have the slightest inkling that she was planning a surprise party.

phrase: in for a penny, in for a pound
definition: This expression means that once you start doing something, you might just as well do it wholeheartedly and not stop at half-measures.
example: She accepted to be on the committee and then she accepted to be the chairwoman – in for a penny, in for a pound.

definition: This term refers to the height of a very young or small child.
