example: Look how tall you are! A year ago you were knee-high to a grasshopper!

phrase: marry in haste, repent at leisure
definition: If you marry someone without knowing the person well, you will later regret your decision to marry.
example: It’s you choice, but don’t forget: marry in haste, repent at leisure!

phrase: mighty oaks from little acorns grow
definition: This phrase means that great things may come from small beginnings.
example: You should try! Mighty oaks from little acorns grow.

definition: If somebody is as busy as a bee, they are very busy and active.
example: My mother is as busy as a bee around Christmas time.

definition: If someone has a change of heart, they change their attitude or feelings, especially towards greater friendliness or cooperation.
example: She was against smoking but she had a change of heart.

definition: This idiom refers to something that appears valuable but really isn’t, like iron pyrites – a worthless material that resembles gold.
example: That investment was just fool’s gold.

definition: This idiom means “arrogantly or inconsiderately overbearing”.
example: The new manager is unbearably high-handed.

definition: This term refers to people in power who take an active part in making things happen.
example: Movers and shakers are assembling in Berlin for the summit.

definition: If you risk life and limb, you are in danger of death or serious injury.
example: This mission is dangerous; you risk life and limb if you go by car.

definition: This idiom means excellent – the highest quality.
example: This car is definitely the mutt’s nuts!

definition: This idiom refers to good times and bad times.
example: Every relationship has its ups and downs and ours makes no exception.

definition: Someone who is chasing their (own) tail is spending a lot of time and energy doing many things but achieving very little.
example: She has been chasing her tail all week sending e-mail. Therefore, the report isn’t ready.

definition: This idiom refers to an exciting and eventful lifestyle, especially one bringing wealth and success.
example: He now lives in the fast lane. It was his dream.

definition: This expression means to reach a logical conclusion.
example: It stands to reason that you will reach home in 10 minutes since there is no traffic.

definition: If you stay one jump ahead, you keep an advantage over others by making sure you are better informed or taking action before they do.
example: She’s a successful police officer because she always stays one jump ahead of the criminals.

definition: This idiom means to be surprised or confused by something unexpected.
example: We were all taken aback by his decision.

definition: This phrase refers to the bottom of the sea, the mythical resting place of drowned mariners.
example: Be careful not to go to Davy Jones’ locker.

phrase: done up / dressed up like a dog’s dinner
definition:
This phrase means dressed or displayed in an ostentatiously smart manner.
wearing very formal or decorativeclothes in a way that attracts attention
example: She’s dressed up like a dog’s dinner.

phrase: if the (cap/shoe) fits, then wear it
definition: You can say “if the cap fits, wear it” to let someone know that the critical remark they have just heard applies to them.
example: “Are you referring to me when you say that terrible things?” “If the cap fits, then wear it!”

definition: This expression is often used when somebody is so shocked, surprised or touched by something that they don’t know what to say.
example: What do you think about her performance? Words fail me, sorry.

phrase: all downhill / downhill all the way
definition: If something is all downhill or downhill all the way, it is very easy to achieve considering the difficulties encountered beforehand.
example: The hardest part of the mission has passed. Now it is downhill all the way.

phrase: do as I say, not as I do
definition: This idiom is straight from the parent’s handbook. It means to do what you are told and not what you see somebody else is doing.
example: I don’t care what Mark does. You have to respect the speed limit. Do as I say, not as I do!

definition: If you use a word which you say is “in inverted commas”, you indicate that the word is not quite true or appropriate.
example: During that time, sick prisoners were “cared for”, in inverted commas, by guards.

definition: If you shrug something off, you dismiss it as being unimportant.
example: I was aware of the danger but I just shrugged it off.

definition: If something is obtained or won fair and square, it is done in an honest and open manner, the rules are respected and there is no cheating or lying.
example: Kevin won the position within our company fair and square.

definition: Someone who foams at the mouth is extremely angry about something.
example: When I entered the room, the director was foaming at the mouth.

definition: Someone who is scared stiff is so frightened that they are unable to move.
example: My father is scared stiff of heights.

definition: This idiom means to talk or deal honestly.
example: I’ve worked with her for ten years and I had no reason to doubt her words. She always shoots straight.

definition: A sore point is a subject to be avoided because it causes anger or embarrassment.
example: Don’t talk about weight – that’s a sore point for her.

definition: If you walk into the lion’s den, you find yourself in a difficult situation in which you have to face unfriendly or aggressive people.
example: After the failure of my project I had no other thing to do than walk into lion’s den.

phrase: a leopard can’t change his spots
definition: This idiom means that you cannot change your innate self.
example: She was a cheater in her twenties and she’s a cheater now – a leopard can’t change his spots!

definition: If you get your feet wet, you start to do something new or unfamiliar or explore new territory for the first time.
example: This mission involves parachuting into the town?! Well, I can’t wait to get my feet wet!

definition: This idiom means “in many small fragments”.
example: We heard about the deal in bits and pieces from the secretary.

definition: To say that someone is as mad as a hatter means that they are very strange or insane.
example: The women next door is as mad as a hatter.

definition: To say that something is as scarce as hen’s teeth stresses the fact that it is extremely rare, to the point of non-existence.
example: Water is as scarce as hen’s teeth where we’re going. Take enough supplies.

phrase: too much of a good thing
definition: The fact that something pleasant becomes unpleasant because you have or do too much of it.
example: You can have too much of a good thing,

definition: This expression refers to the depression that is caused to new mothers after childbirth.
example: She is going through some baby blues now and needs compassion from you.

definition: If you crack the whip, you use your authority to make someone obey you or work more efficiently, usually by threatening them.
example: I don’t like when I have to crack the whip so as to make sure we meet the deadline.

definition: If you fall over backwards to accomplish something, you do everything you possibly can to please and impress.
example: The manager fell over backwards to make the event a success.

definition: This is a dramatic way of expressing worry, anxiety or fear.
example: His wife nearly had kittens when Steve announced that he wanted to be a police officer.

definition: If a person or organisation is in dire straits, they are in a very difficult situation.
example: He is in dire straits so I suggest that we should help him.

definition: If you say that you cannot or will not do something for love or money, you mean that you will not do it under any circumstances.
example: I would not leave this organisation for love or money.

phrase: to be a hop, skip and a jump away from
definition: To say that a thing or place is only a hop, skip and a jump away from another, it means that they are very close to each other.
example: The church is a hop, skip and a jump away from our house.

definition: This expression means that you were told something by an undisclosed source.
example: How do I know that? A little bird told me.

definition: If you count your blessings, you focus your thoughts on all the good things in your life rather than on the negative ones.
example: My grandmother would always advise me to count my blessings.

definition: If you do something in leaps and bounds, you make rapid or spectacular progress or growth.
example: The number of customers has grown in leaps and bounds.

phrase: keep one’s feet on the ground
definition: A person who keeps their feet on the ground continues to act in a sensible and practical way, even if they become successful.
example: Being successful hasn’t changed her. She still keeps her feet on the ground.

definition: If you look on the bright side, you view a mostly unpleasant situation in a positive and optimistic way.
example: Your car has broken. Look on the bright side – you will walk more.

definition: To say that there is no love lost between two people or organisations, it means that they do not like each other at all.
example: There is no love lost between me and Mary.

definition: If someone helps you, it is natural and right to help them in return.
example: I helped her when she moved into her new house, just as she helped me two years ago; one good turn deserves another.

phrase: chill to the marrow / chill to the bone
definition: This idiom means to be very cold or to be very scared.
example: The movie gave him a chill to the marrow.

definition: If you tell someone to get their skates on, you want them to hurry up.
example: We are late! Get your skates on!

definition: If you are on nodding terms with someone, you don’t know them very well.
example: I haven’t made any friends yet but I’m on nodding terms with my next door neighbour.

definition: This idiom refers to a leader, boss, chief person in a group or the head of a project.
example: Ask him about this. He’s the top banana here.

definition: This idiom refers to a person who has an important or powerful position.
example: I was invited at the reception by a bigwig.

definition: This idiom means to disappear or change very slowly.
example: Her bad habits die hard.

definition: This expression refers to a patch of stubble on the face of a man who hasn’t shaved for at least a day.
example: My grandfather look tired and had a five o’clock shadow.

definition: This term refers to idle talk, or pretentious, untrue or insincere statements that nobody can believe.
example: I’m sure they think it’s a load of baloney! It seems that they don’t believe a word of it!

definition: If someone wears out their welcome, they stay too long as a guest, causing inconvenience to their host.
example: They invited me to stay for a few days, but I didn’t want to wear out my welcome.

definition: If you face or feel the chill wind of something, you are beginning to encounter the problems or trouble it causes.
example: Many businesses are facing the chill wind of the recession.

phrase: let someone stew in their own juice
definition: If you let someone stew in their own juice, you leave them to worry about the consequences of their own actions.
example: Being punished, she spent last night at home. They let her stew in her own juice.

phrase: not a hair out of place
definition: If someone does not have a hair out of place, their appearance is perfect.
example: Nicole is forever impeccably dressed – never a hair out of place.

definition: This idiom refers to a situation where things are not really clear.
example: People should avoid getting involved in deals that have different shades of grey.

definition: This expression refers to a person or thing that you are happy to see.
example: Steve! You are a sight for sore eyes!

definition: to sing with all your power, joy, and deep emotion. It is an invitation to let go, be loud, and express your true feelings through music without holding anything back.
example: Do what you really enjoy. Sing your heart out!

definition:
an informal expression for imaginary credit or approval you get for doing a good deed, helping someone, or trying to please an authority figure
(humorous) approval for something helpfulyou have done:
example: I earned some Brownie points for washing the car.

definition: If you rise to the occasion, you manage to do something successfully in difficult circumstances.
example: I had to sit in for my colleague and take some important decisions. Fortunately, I rose to the occasion.

definition: This idiom refers to a person who is widely admired.
example: Bobby is now the toast of the town.

definition: This phrase refers to something that spoils the view or ruins a previously comfortable situation.
example: Her coming was just a blot on the landscape.

definition: To feel blue means to have feelings of deep sadness or depression.
example: I’m going to see my grandfather. He’s feeling a bit blue at the moment.

definition: A person who is on the up and up is becoming increasingly successful.
example: The police officer has been on the up and up since he left the academy.

definition: When a person decides to even the score, they try to get their revenge on someone who has cheated or done them harm.
example: When I found out that my wife had cheated, I was decided to even the score.

phrase: you’ve made your bed, now lie in it
definition: This idiom means to make a decision and to accept the consequences of it.
example: They are your mistakes! You’ve made your bed, now lie in it.

definition: This idiom means to be captivated or to be held spellbound by pleasing qualities.
example: I was enthralled by her beauty.

definition: If people reach an agreement, then change their minds immediately afterwards, the change occurs “before the ink is dry”.
example: You can’t ever tell when she is serious. She is capable of changing her mind before the ink is dry.

definition: This means everything will happen as it is supposed to, at the appropriate time.
example: You’ll find out the results in due course. Just be a little more patient.

definition: If you tell someone to like it or lump it, you mean that they will have to accept something even if they don’t like it, because the situation is not going to change.
example: We are spending a week this summer at the mountain – like it or lump it!

phrase: tell someone a thing or two
definition: If you tell someone a thing or two, you express your thoughts (usually criticism) very clearly.
example: I will tell her a thing or two. This situation cannot go on.

definition: This idiom refers to favouritism where jobs or other benefits are given to friends and acquaintances.
example: I have some jobs for the boys. Please call them.

definition: If you are skating on thin ice, you are doing or saying something risky, or something that could cause trouble.
example: I advise you not to say that. You may be skating on thin ice.

definition: If you throw money at something, you try to solve a problem by spending money on it, without using any other method.
example: The refugee situation can’t be solved by throwing money at it.

definition: This idiom refers to a young person who turns out to be beautiful or talented against all expectations.
example: Seeing the old photos, she has realized that she turned into an ugly duckling.

phrase: answer the call of nature / answer nature’s call
definition: When a person answers the call of nature, they go to the toilet.
example: I had to get up in the middle of the meeting to answer the call of nature.

definition: If somebody gets a five-finger discount, they take something without paying; in other words, they steal.
example: - Can you afford that watch?- Yes, with a five-finger discount.

phrase: far be it from me to
definition: This expression means that the speaker does not feel in a position to say or do something. It is usually used before giving advice or expressing an opinion.
example: Far be it from me to mislead you, but I think you should reconsider the position.

definition: This expression refers to a choice forced upon someone.
example: There was only one room left when I arrived, so I got Hobson’s choice.

definition: If you make a pig of yourself, you eat and drink too much.
example: That’s enough. Thank you! I don’t want to make a pig of myself.

definition: This expression means that someone’s behaviour is not as irrational as it seems.
example: I can’t believe she’s efficient despite her way of working. There’s a method in her madness.

definition: This expression is used when someone is very successful.
example: You’ve won the big prize. Now you’re riding high!

phrase: speak softly and carry a big stick
definition: If you speak softly and carry a big stick, you express your views in a quite non-aggressive manner, but you make it clear that you are in a position to use force if necessary.
example: I was recommended to use the speak softly and carry a big stick method.

definition: This expression means that even if everything is not satisfactory at present, there will be opportunity for things to improve.
example: Don’t be sad about this little thing. Tomorrow’s another day.

definition: This idiom means “not a subject for levity”.
example: This is no laughing matter! Get out!

definition: If you rob the cradle, you have a romantic relationship with someone who is much younger than yourself.
example: My aunt is dating a twenty-year-old boy. That’s really robbing the cradle.

definition: If you manage to escape from serious danger or trouble, you save your skin/neck.
example: She saved her skin by being late. The area was subject to a terrorist attack.

definition: This idiom means to leave or abscond.
example: When I got up this morning Ann had gone. She shot through without a word.

definition: If you find a place in the sun, you reach a position which provides you with wealth and happiness, or whatever you have been hoping to obtain in life.
example:
I hope one day I will find a place in the sun with the triumph of my books.
He certainly earned his place in the sun.

phrase: get to the bottom of something
definition: If you get to the bottom of a problem or mystery, you solve it by finding out the true cause of it.
example: Someone is stealing from our company. We will get to the bottom of this problem, soon enough!

definition: This idiom means to mark yourself ready to take responsibility.
example: You need to step up to the mark and show the management what you are worth.

definition: If you have a nest egg, you have a reserve of money which you put aside for future needs.
example: I consider the money from the sale of my motorcycle as a nest egg for difficult times.

phrase: a riddle wrapped up in an enigma
definition: This idiom means a puzzle difficult to solve.
example: This problem is like a riddle wrapped up in an enigma.

definition: This means eating one’s lunch while still working.
example: This time I’ll be eating al desko.

definition: To refer to something as a bolt from the blue means that it happened totally unexpectedly.
example: The manager’s resignation came as a bolt from the blue.

definition: This idiom means to respond to an attack by using a similar method as one’s attacker.
example: No, this is not the best solution! Let’s fight fire with fire!

definition: This expression means that you’ll make mistakes if you rush through something.
example: Take your time to finish this project. Haste makes waste!

definition: If you have an axe to grind, you have personal reasons for becoming involved in something or adopting a particular attitude.
example: It was decided that the best employee would be selected by a HR agency which had no axe to grind within the company.

phrase: have one foot in the grave
definition: A person who is either very old or very ill and close to death has one foot in the grave.
example: Unfortunately, she has one foot in the grave.

phrase: it takes one to know one
definition: This expression is used for saying that someone must have a bad quality themselves if they can recognize it in other people.
example: She’s a cheater. Well, it takes one to know one!

definition: People who have ants in their pants are very restless or excited about something.
example: I wish she would relax. She has hos ants in her pants about something today.

definition: If you choose the lesser of two evils, you opt for the less unpleasant of two poor options.
example: Choosing the train instead of driving was the lesser of two evils; at least we could have a drink.

definition: This idiom denotes a person who tries to get favours from those in authority through flattery.
example: Mike is such an apple polisher!

definition: This idiom means to ask for too much.
example: Hoping for a permanent peace in this area it’s like asking for the moon.

definition: If the media, through press releases, interviews and announcements, is instrumental in facilitating dialogue between two or more countries, this is called megaphone diplomacy.
example: When it comes to the United States and North Korea, I think we should use megaphone diplomacy.

definition: This idiom means to seek shelter.
example: We ran for cover as soon as the bombing began.

definition: If you bet your bottom dollar on something, you are absolutely certain of it.
example: John is utterly punctual. You can bet your bottom dollar he will be here at 10 o’clock on the dot.

phrase: go / be put through the mill
definition: If you go or are put through the mill, you experience a very difficult period, or are exposed to rough treatment.
example: A good part of this year I’ve been put through the mill within this organisation.

definition: This idiom refers to calm, peaceful days.
example: There have been some halcyon days this period.

definition: If a project or process picks up steam, it starts to develop or become more active.
example: The marketing campaign started slowly, but soon it picked up steam.

definition: If you say that the door swings both ways, you mean that the same principle or argument applies to both sides of a situation.
example: I had enough of this conversation. I don’t want to speak to you anymore. The door swings both ways, bye!

definition: Something as clean as a whistle is extremely clean. This can also mean that a person’s criminal record is clean.
example: I spent the afternoon washing my car until it was as clean as a whistle.

definition: You can use this expression when you want something to be done slowly and carefully.
example: “Easy does it” said he as we were carrying the sofa through the house.

definition: The expression means that you should not reject an offer if it is the only possibility you have. You have no other choice.
example: She will be lucky if she finds a job. Beggars can’t be choosers!

definition: If something is as clear as a bell, it is very clear or easy to understand.
example: The instructions were clear as a bell.

definition: This expression refers to a person whose presence is unnecessary and as a result they feel useless.
example: At the beginning I felt like a fifth wheel.

definition: to make a process, system, or interaction run more smoothly, easily, and successfully
example: This programme was established to oil the wheels of economic reform.

definition: This means that people’s intentions can be judged better by what they do than what they say.
example: You shouldn’t jump to conclusions. Don’t forget that actions speak louder than words.

definition: If you are duty bound to do something, you are required to do it as part of your obligations.
example: Like a teacher, I am duty bound to report a student’s absence from school.

definition: If you talk about how a situation is for the time being, you mean that it is temporary and will probably change in the future.
example: She has left me and is living with her sister for the time being.

definition: When you travel light, you travel with as little luggage as possible.
example: If you go trekking, travel light. It will be better.

definition: A person who is made of money is very rich and can buy whatever they want.
example: I can’t afford to spend that much on a laptop. I’m not made of money.

definition: This idiom means you cannot find out the truth, the answer or the result of something. You have to wait and find out in the future.
example: Only time will tell whether out marriage will last.

phrase: when in Rome, do as the Romans do
definition: This expression means that you should adopt the customs of the people or country you are visiting and behave in the same way.
example: Pay attention when visiting Brazil. Don’t forget: when in Rome, do as the Romans do!

definition: When someone takes the floor, they rise to make a speech or presentation.
example: Marry, please, take the floor.

phrase: be in the lap of the Gods
definition: This phrase means to be out of one’s control or power.
example: Her recovery is now in the lap of the Gods.

definition: If you learn the ropes, you learn how to do a particular job correctly.
example: She’s an intelligent woman. It won’t take her long to learn the ropes.

phrase: why buy a cow when you can get milk for free?
definition: This refers to not paying for something that you can obtain for free. Sometimes it refers to a decision not to marry when you can have the benefits of marriage without any commitment.
example: Rent is very high so I’m still living with my parents. Why buy a cow when you can get milk for free?

definition: The expression means to learn something by memorising it without giving any thought to what is being learnt.
example: I had no other choice but to learn it by rote.

definition: A remark that appears to express admiration but could also be interpreted as an insult is called a backhanded compliment.
example: My manager said my presentation on marketing strategy was surprisingly clear! How’s that for a backhanded compliment! Does that mean that I am usually not clear?

definition: This expression means to improvise or do something without preparation, according to the demands of the situation.
example: I don’t know what we should do here, so let’s play it by ear.

phrase: take to smth like a duck to water
definition: If you take to something like a duck to water, you do it naturally and easily, without fear or hesitation.
example: When I first tried skiing, I took it like a duck to water.

definition: If someone is as gentle as a lamb, they are pleasant, caring and calm.
example: Every time I have a problem I talk to him because he is as gentle as a lamb.

definition: If you say that chickens have come home to roost, you mean that bad or embarrassing things done in the past by someone are now causing problems for that person.
example: Be careful what you do in this life. Don’t forget! Chickens come home to roost.

definition: This idiom is used to describe Christians who sing, talk and shout enthusiastically during their religious ceremonies and who try to persuade other people to join them.
example: There was a bunch of happy-clappy people.

definition: If you describe someone as a bundle of nerves, you mean that they are very nervous, tense or worried.
example: My girlfriend is doing her driving test today. She’s a bundle of nerves.

definition: If you grab a bite to eat, you get something to eat quickly.
example: You should grab a bite to eat before going out.

phrase: as a handbrake on a canoe
definition: If something is as much use as a handbrake on a canoe, it is completely useless or serves no purpose.
example: With no fuel, a car would be as much use as a handbrake on a canoe.

definition: This phrase means that I haven’t slept at all.
example: I’m so tired. I haven’t slept one wink.

definition: People who have money to burn have so much money that they can spend it on anything they want.
example: A new phone is not a problem for Steven. He has got money to burn.

definition: This expression is used to describe a person who has the ability to persuade someone to accept something totally unnecessary or useless.
example: It’s not a surprise that Michele was named the saleswoman of the year. She can sell ice to Eskimos!

definition: To talk about the whys and wherefores means to discuss the reasons.
example: We should discuss the whys and wherefores of this failure.

definition: If you burn your fingers (or get your fingers burnt), you suffer financially as a result of foolish behaviour.
example: Jack got his fingers burnt playing poker.

definition: If something fits like a glove, it fits you perfectly.
example: Thank you for the gift. The trousers fit me like a glove.

definition: To say that s statement or action is like a red flag to a bull means that it is sure to make someone very angry or upset.
example: Don’t mention that issue today. It would be like a red flag to a bull!

definition: This idiom refers to a much loved person.
example: Have I ever told you that you are the light of my life? I love you!

definition: This idiom is used when something or someone develops completely and reaches maturity.
example: He has come of age now and is ready to take the company.

definition: A geographical area where law enforcement is practically impossible, because people ignore all rules, is called “bandit territory”.
example: There are some certain bandit territories in the world where travellers shouldn’t go.

definition: This expression is used to stress that something or someone is definitely dead.
example: Violence has escalated and as a consequence they’ve started fighting again. The peace agreement is now as dead as a doornail.

definition: If you do something intentionally, but pretend it was an accident, you do it accidentally on purpose.
example: I accidentally-on-purpose erased her email address so I couldn’t contact her again.

definition: When you have no choice, any port in a storm refers to a solution you accept, which in normal circumstances you would find unacceptable.
example: The motel was a little bit dirty, but it was a case of any port in a storm; all the others were full.

definition: This idiom means that it’s too soon to make a judgment about something.
example: My latest book sells well, but it’s early days yet.

definition: This expression means to assume that since there is no news, it will not be bad news.
example: The results are not out yet and I feel no news is good news.

definition: This phrase means easy to prove or answer.
example: The detective thought it was an open and shut case.

definition: you are overconfident and spoil your chances of success by trying to obtain too much.
example: I’m hoping for a bonus for my good results, but I might overplay my hand if I ask for a promotion.

definition: This idiom can either refer to something sadly neglected or to a person or thing of untidy appearance.
example: These houses were beautiful some time ago, but now they make a sorry sight.

definition: This is an affectionate way of wishing someone a good night’s sleep.
example: I’m going to bed now. Good night, sleep tight.

definition: This idiom means to get something exactly right or be on target.
example: Her speech on women rights hit the bull’s eye.

definition: To say that you will move heaven and earth means that you are prepared to do everything that is possible to achieve something.
example: I promise I will move heaven and earth to buy an apartment.

phrase: take each day as it comes / take one day at a time
definition: This idiom means to deal with things as they happen and not to make plans or worry about what will happen in the future.
example: I’ve been through a lot of changes in my life recently and I have learnt to take each day as it comes.

definition: If you are at loggerheads with a person or organisation, you strongly disagree with them.
example: I was at loggerheads with my neighbours over the decision to close the parking garage.

definition: If something goes against the grain, it is difficult to accept because it is very different from what is considered normal or natural.
example: Having to import potatoes in our county goes against the grain.

definition: When you want to mention a different or contradictory aspect of a situation, you refer to the other side of the coin.
example: The apartment is lovely and spacious, but the other side of the coin is that it is far from shops.

definition: If you pour cold water on someone’s plans, opinion or ideas, you discourage them by showing little enthusiasm.
example: The manager poured cold water on the idea of changing the sales plan.

definition: This idiom refers to the inclination to become unfaithful after seven years of marriage.
example: She’s got the seven-year itch.

phrase: there are other fish in the sea
definition: This expression means that it’s ok to miss an opportunity. Others will arise.
example: Oh, don’t be so sad! There are other fish in the sea.

definition: This expression is used to describe someone who is seriously ill or very close to death.
example: My friends was so ill that he was at death’s door for several days.

definition: When someone gets their comeuppance, they receive the treatment they deserve (usually punishment or retribution) for their behaviour or actions.
example: I’m sure she will get her comeuppance.

definition: Someone who does not have a stitch on is wearing no clothes and is therefore completely naked.
example: When the doorbell rang, they didn’t have a stitch on.

definition: Two people who are at each other’s throats are always fighting or arguing.
example: Candidates for the presidential election are constantly at each other’s throats.

definition: Someone who does the preparatory work or the preliminary research.
example: I’ve done all the spadework and thus I want my name to be mentioned in this project.

definition: When you give all your attention to something and become so engrossed in it that you don’t realize what time it is, you lose track of time.
example: Whenever I start reading a good book, I lose track of time.

phrase: give the shirt off one’s back
definition: This expression is used to describe a kind-hearted or generous person who would give you anything he/she owns to help you.
example: For my few friends, I would give the shirt off my back.

definition: This phrase means the more people who are present, the better an occasion or situation (especially a party) will be.
example: It’s perfect that you will be able to join us! The more the merrier!

definition: This idiom means to seek to gain advantage by flattery.
example: It’s not a good idea to curry favour with him. He simply doesn’t like this type of people.

definition: This idiom means to fail to achieve a result.
example: The initiative seems to be running into the sand.

definition: To say that you could hear a pin drop means that it is so silent you could hear the slightest noise.
example: They were waiting so silently that one could hear a pin drop.

definition: This idiom is used to refer to a person who is a troublemaker or a criminal.
example: He’s a bad apple. I wouldn’t hang out with him.

definition: This idiom refers to a position where someone is observing a situation rather than being directly involved in it.
example: You have never been there for me. You have always watched from the sidelines.

definition: If you have something on the brain, you think or talk about it all time.
example: Stop talking about computer games. You’ve got games on the brain!

phrase: life and soul of the party
definition: The life and soul of the party is the most lively and amusing person present at an event.
example: I am so glad that he is here. He is the life and soul of the party.

definition: This expression is used for describing someone who is immature or inexperienced.
example: She can be green sometimes. I don’t think she’s ready to be promoted.

definition: If you say that a storm is brewing, you mean that the atmosphere indicates that there is going to be trouble, probably with outbursts of anger or emotion.
example: As soon as I saw her face, I knew there was a storm brewing.

phrase: let your heart rule your head
definition: This idiom means to do something based on emotions rather than logic.
example: It’s better not to let your heart rule your head.

definition: If you rake in the money, you make money in large quantities.
example: Their business is so successful; they’re raking in the money.

definition: This term refers to a person who is considered to be dishonest or immoral and had a bad influence on others in the group.
example: In any group there is always a rotten apple.

definition: An attempt to conceal or distort the truth (like a magician) in order to confuse people is called smoke and mirrors.
example: The politician used smoke and mirrors to make the situation look better.

phrase: get out of the wrong side of the bed
definition: This expression means to be grumpy because you are having a bad day.
example: She has got out of the wrong side of the bed today.

definition: This idiom refers to someone very unhappy about something.
example: With a heavy heart, we left the funeral ceremony.

definition: To say that someone is out to lunch means that they seem to be either unaware of what’s going on around them or unable to understand what is happening.
example: My former boss was clearly out to lunch.

definition: If an activity takes your mind off something that is worrying you, it helps you to stop thinking about it for a while.
example: Fishing takes my mind off unimportant problems.

definition: This expression means lively and active.
example: Don’t worry! I’ve spoken to him and he’s alive and kicking.

phrase: a picture is worth a thousand words
definition: This expression means that a picture can give just as much information as a large amount of descriptive text.
example: Look at this picture of her. A picture is worth a thousand words, isn’t it?

phrase: may you live in interesting times
definition: This phrase means “may you experience much disorder and trouble in your life”. Pay attention as this phrase is rather a curse.
example: It’s your choice. May you live in interesting times!

definition: A person whose agitated mental state leaves them helpless or unable to cope with things is called a basket case.
example: I will turn into a basket case if this utterly stressful situation continues.

definition: If you hold your tongue, you remain silent and say nothing.
example: Please, Harry, hold your tongue during this meeting.

definition: If someone or something plays havoc, they cause disorder and confusion.
example: The flood played havoc with the construction site.

definition: If you use your noodle, you use your brain or your common sense.
example: How have I solved the problem? I’ve used my noodle!

definition: This term refers to a natural event or accident, for which no person is responsible (such as an earthquake, lighting and similar acts of nature).
example: The insurance company refused to pay for the damage because it was caused by an act of God.

definition: The departure of highly qualified people for other countries, where they have better opportunities and usually better pay, is called brain drain.
example: Think about Eastern-European countries. There is an obvious brain drain trend.

definition: This idiom refers to the feeling of hate between people because of any arguments in the past.
example: The attack may be the result of bad blood between the two groups.

definition: This expression is used to indicate that you are not as foolish or as easily deceived as some people seem to think.
example: Stop lying to me! I wasn’t born yesterday.

definition: This means that if you don’t know about a problem or unpleasant fact, you won’t worry about it.
example: I didn’t know that she had been convicted – ignorance is bliss.

definition: Someone who knows the ropes is familiar with the way something is done and/or knows how to do it.
example: Let’s call on him to help us. He knows the ropes.

definition: This idiom refers to the far-reaching power of the authorities.
example: The long arm of the law will reach you some day.

definition: This expression refers to animals that are of use to human beings, mostly used to address dogs.
example: A dog is undoubtedly a man’s best friend.

phrase: there are clouds on the horizon
definition: This idiom means that trouble is coming.
example: Haven’t you spoken with her? There are clouds on the horizon.

definition: This phrase means to do or undertake something redundant, pointless or futile, usually in the context of bringing something to a location where it is abundant or unnecessary.
example: I don’t know why you are keep doing that. You might just as well bring sand to the beach!

definition: This idiom means all of it; the whole thing.
example: I’ve got money and I want the whole shebang!

definition: A problem that no one wants to discuss but is so obvious that it cannot be ignored, is called an elephant in the room.
example: Her project is quite unsatisfactory. It’s an elephant in the room that we need to discuss.

definition: A chance in a million is a very small chance, or no chance at all, that something will happen.
example: There’s a chance in a million of finding the phone I lost in this town.

definition: Someone who smokes a large amount of tobacco on a regular basis is said to smoke like a chimney.
example: My father smokes like a chimney.

definition: This term means all the details or facts.
example: I know she was involved in a car accident, but I don’t know all ins and outs.

definition: This expression refers to a situation where there is a reversal of roles, with the small or minor element having a controlling influence on the most important element.
example: If you let your kid decide on important matters, it will be a case of the tail wagging the dog!

definition: If a person is as nice as pie, they are surprisingly kind and friendly.
example: Even if we argue sometimes, she is as nice as pie.

definition: A person who is a tough cookie is someone with a strong and determined character who is not easily intimidated, discouraged or defeated.
example: I’m not worried about her future at all. She’s a tough cookie!

definition: This idiom refers to a serious error of judgement.
example: She committed the cardinal sin of criticizing Bob’s decision.

definition: Someone who is away with the fairies is in such a dreamy state that they are not totally in touch with reality and give the impression of being slightly mad.
example: It’s no use trying to explain the strategy to her. She’s away with the fairies.

definition: This expression means to inspire with enthusiasm.
example: His speech really fired the imagination of those who listened.

definition: A victory obtained in unsatisfactory conditions, which as a result seems worthless or without significance for the winner, is called a hollow victory.
example: It was a hollow victory – he won the case but lost all his savings in legal fees.

phrase: nurse / bear / hold a grudge against someone
definition: If you nurse/bear/hold a grudge against someone, you have a feeling of resentment or ill-will towards them.
example: Ever since I got the job, he has been holding a grudge against me.

definition: When people talk about a square meal, they mean a substantial and satisfying meal.
example: Do you know a place where I can get a square meal?

definition: Someone or something that is worth their weight in gold is considered to be of great value.
example: We couldn’t run the business without her. She is worth her weight in gold.

definition: If you see somebody’s true colours, you understand their actual character, often for the first time.
example: I thought that I knew her well, but during the mission I saw her true colours.

phrase: see something in a new light
definition: If you see something in a new light, you view it in a way that makes you change the opinion you had before.
example: After listening to her, I began to see their problem in a new light.

phrase: as sure as death and taxes
definition: If something is as sure as death and taxes, it is certain to happen.
example: This firm will go bankrupt next year. It’s as sure as death and taxes.

definition: Something that is badly torn, in very poor condition or damaged beyond repair is in tatters.
example: After this scandal, her reputation is in tatters.

definition: This idiom means to be very tired, exhausted.
example: Now, I am dog tired after 16 hours of work.

definition: If you eat or dip into your savings, you spend part of the money you have put aside for future use.
example: I had to dip into my savings to have my bike repaired.

definition: A golden opportunity is a favourable time or an excellent occasion which should not be missed.
example: An internship in our company could be a golden opportunity for you.

definition: To have green fingers means to be good at gardening.
example: My mother was born with green fingers. She’s great with plants.

definition: If you reach for the moon, you are very ambitious and try to achieve something even it is difficult.
example: I like my cousin because he is talented and ambitious; he always tends to reach for the moon.

phrase: face that would stop a clock
definition: Someone who has a face that would stop a clock has a shockingly unattractive face.
example: He’s fat and short, with a face that would stop a clock!

definition: This idiom means to have an affinity for one’s home over every other place.
example: The woman always tells her children that for her, there’s no place like home.

definition: This refers to a time when someone really needs something, almost a final chance.
example: I was there for Olivia in her hour of need.

definition: A person who lives in an ivory tower has a lifestyle that preserves them from the problems and difficulties experienced by others.
example: I don’t like her because she has been living in an ivory tower and thus she has no life experience.

phrase: slow and steady wins the race
definition: This expression means that reliability is more important than speed.
example: It doesn’t matter when we arrive. Slow and steady wins the race.

definition: This idiom refers to new members that provide various new schemes and ideas for the organization.
example: He managed to succeed because he is open to bringing young blood in the company.

definition: This means clumsy or physically inept.
example: He can’t tie that bow tie – he’s all thumbs.

definition: If something puts your nose out of joint, it offends or annoys you.
example: I discovered that my wife wasn’t on the invitation list, which put my nose out of joint.

definition: If you have a passing fancy for something, you become fond of it for a short time.
example: My father started collecting coins a few years ago, but it was just a passing fancy.

definition: If you take a trip/stroll/walk down memory lane, you remember pleasant thing that happened in the past.
example: Every Eastern is a trip down memory lane for the family.

definition: If it’s raining cats and dogs, it is raining very heavily.
example: We’ll have to cancel the meeting – it’s raining cats and dogs.

phrase: throw the baby out with the bathwater
definition: This expression refers to getting rid of something valuable while trying to get rid of something considered worthless.
example: Olivia quitting her job because her ex started working there is an example of throwing the baby out with the bathwater.

phrase: more by accident than by design
definition: Something that happens more by accident than by design is done without deliberate intention.
example: I became an interpreter more by accident than design; nobody else could speak their language.

definition: This term refers to a person who is very knowledgeable about a lot of subjects.
example: Ask Tim – he’s a walking encyclopaedia.

definition: Something that is as dry as dust is very dry indeed. This expression can also refer to something dull and uninteresting.
example: Her speech was as dry as dust.

definition: This expression means that laughter can help cure negative feelings such as stress, anger, worry, depression etc.
example: Laughter is the best medicine! Don’t forget that!

definition: The term golden handcuffs refers to a large sum of money or a generous financial arrangement granted to an executive as an incentive to stay in their job or to ensure long-term cooperation after their departure.
example: Her six-year golden handcuffs are released next year.

definition: This idiom refers to something that is very difficult to do and needs a lot of effort and determination.
example: Rehabilitation of the affected areas will be an uphill task for the local authorities.

phrase: at this stage of the game
definition: This expression refers to the current point reached in a process, activity or developing situation.
example: At this stage of the game we think that further intervention would be unwise. We propose to wait and see how things develop.

definition: If something goes tits-up, it fails completely.
example: The economy went tits-up and my wife lost her job.

phrase: take matters into your own hands
definition: If you take matters into your hands, you take action yourself rather than waiting for others to invervene.
example: When I saw the lack of progress, I took the project into my own hands.

definition: If you send someone packing, you tell them to leave, in a very forceful and unfriendly way.
example: When my last girlfriend discovered that I was unfaithful, she sent me packing.

definition: This idiom refers to an unrealistic hope or fantasy.
example: I was thinking of her kissing me…what a pipe dream!

definition: When comparing two things or situations, the expression a world of difference means that there is a vast difference between them.
example: An air conditioner would make a world of difference in this room.

definition: This simile means pure white.
example: Her dress was as white as snow.

definition: A situation in which people are prepared to use unscrupulous methods in order to succeed or survive is called the law of the jungle.
example: Most businesses today seem to be governed by the law of the jungle. Don’t you think so?

definition: This idiom means to discover and pursue one’s true and inherent passion, skill or vocation.
example: Most students leave college and realize that they haven’t found their calling.

definition: If something happens without a hitch, it takes place exactly as planned, without any difficulties.
example: The conference went off without a hitch.

definition: This phrase refers to a punch in the mouth.
example: If you keep doing that, you’ll get a knuckle sandwich.

definition: If you say that someone is a cog in the machine, you mean that, while they are necessary, they only play a small part in an organisation or plan.
example: The police officer realized that the man was just a cog in the machine.

phrase: lock the barn door after the horse has bolted
definition: This idiom means to take precautions after damage has occurred.
example: After the burglary they installed the latest alarm system. There’s no additional need to lock the barn door after the horse has bolted.

definition: If you are in uncharted waters, you are in a situation that you have never experienced before, so you don’t know what’s going to happen.
example: Nuclear fusion took physicists into uncharted waters some time ago.

phrase: if you can’t stand the heat, get out of the kitchen
definition: This expression means that if you feel there is too much pressure, you can leave.
example: Amid the growing tension, the commanding officer declared: If you can’t stand the heat, get out of the kitchen!

definition: This expression refers to something/someone which/who has a very good effect on a thing or a situation.
example: Working with a nice team can make all the difference to your job.

definition: Someone who acts as a friend when times are good and is not there when you are in trouble, is called a fair-weather friend.
example: I thought I could count on you but it appears you are a fair-weather friend.

definition: This expression means that something is very dark or black in colour.
example: I can’t believe that her hair is as black as coal.

definition: If something is open around the clock, it means it is open 24 hours a day.
example: The store is open around the clock.

phrase: good things come to those who wait
definition: This expression means to be patient.
example: Well, I would wait another year before buying a house. Good things come to those who wait.

definition: When someone strikes it lucky, they run into good luck.
example: I had a sunny weekend at home – I struck it lucky!

definition: This phrase refers to the devil in human form.
example: He seems to be the devil incarnate.

definition: This idiom means to ease, solve or remove minor difficulties, trouble or problematic details.
example: They are seeing a counselor to iron out the wrinkles in their marriage.

definition: If you get on your high horse, you start behaving in a haughty manner, as though you should be treated with more respect.
example: I got on my high horse when I was asked to show my ID.

definition: To describe a person or a problem as a horse of a different colour means either that the person does things differently from others or that the nature of the problem is entirely different.
example: I expected to negotiate with the marketing manager, but the manager turned up instead – it was a horse of a different colour.

phrase: shut the stable door after the horse has bolted
definition: you try to prevent something bad from happening when it is already too late.
example: I decided to insure my car after the accident. Now that’s shutting the stable door after the horse has bolted.

definition: It refers to something that is unpleasant at first but later turns out to have advantages.
example: Missing the train was a blessing in disguise – that’s how I met my girlfriend.

phrase: kill the goose that lays the golden egg
definition: This idiom means to destroy something that is profitable to you mostly because of greed.
example: By selling her business, she killed the goose that lays the golden egg.

definition: This idiom refers to the dull daily routine.
example: It’s another morning again – time to get to work and start the daily grind.

definition: This idiom means that somebody has many things to do at one time.
example: I can’t meet with you this week as I have a lot on my plate.

definition: This term refers to a person who invests in a business without taking an active part in its management, and whose association with the enterprise is not public knowledge.
example: I work alone but my business is financed by a sleeping partner.

definition: This idiom is used to describe someone who thinks they are the best. This could also be used in a positive way to compliment someone who is very skillful.
example: Her talks about herself all the time. It’s a really hot shot.

definition: This expression means that it is often better to say nothing at all.
example: This will stay between us, ok? Silence is golden.

definition: If something difficult or unpleasant is over and done with, it has now been successfully accomplished, so you don’t have to worry about it any longer.
example: It wasn’t easy, but I had to tell her. Now, that’s over and done with.

definition: An appointment or event that is entirely devoted to business, with no leisure or relaxation, is called strictly business.
example: We had dinner together but it was strictly business.

definition: An armchair critic is someone who gives advice based on theory rather than practice.
example: That girl is an armchair critic – no life experience but a lot of advice.

definition: Someone who reads books or watches TV programs about other places and countries, but doesn’t actually travel anywhere, is called an armchair traveller.
example: A large number of adventure books are bought by armchair travellers.

definition: A smokescreen is an action or tactic intended to conceal or divert attention from your real intentions or activities.
example: Their business was just a smokescreen for their forbidden activities.

phrase: price yourself out of the market
definition: If you price yourself out of the market, you charge such a high price for your goods or services that nobody wants to buy them.
example: We were so eager to make money rapidly that we priced ourselves out of the market.

definition: When an innovation, discovery or event changes the face of something, it alters it completely or in a major way.
example: Social networks have changed the face of online marketing.

definition: If something you do is second nature to you, it is something that you do easily or automatically because you have done it so often or for so long.
example: Cycling is second nature to me.

definition: When someone spreads their wings, they become independent, begin to use their abilities and develop their interests.
example: There comes a time when you have to spread your wings.

definition: If you open or reopen old wounds you revive memories of an unpleasant event, situation or dispute that took place in the past.
example: She avoided the subject in order not to open old wounds.

definition: This is another expression for somewhere that is very dark and you are unable to see anything.
example: I was afraid to do downstairs because the corridor was pitch black.

definition: If someone does something “before your very eyes”, they do it in front of you without attempting to hide what they are doing.
example: Before my very eyes the child took the rubbish and threw it into our garden!

phrase: failing to plan is planning to fail
definition: This idiom has a literal meaning.
example: Why didn’t you forecast the sales? Failing to plan is planning to fail!

definition: When two people tie the knot, they get married.
example: Tim and Sarah are going to tie the knot!

definition: a test in which a single factor (such as an attitude, event, or fact) is decisive
example: The party is using attitudes about gun control as a litmus test for political candidates.

definition: This idiom literally means “thinking about of something”.
example: I have been lost in thought ever since I finished that book.

definition: This idiom means to set aside an irreconcilable difference in order to maintain a civil dialogue.
example: Let’s agree to disagree and go on to the next topic.

phrase: have the world at your feet
definition: If you have the world at your feet, you are extremely successful and greatly admired.
example: The talented singer had the world at his feet.

definition: This expression means that people are often reluctant to change the way they do something, especially if they have been doing it for a long time.
example: My grandmother refuses to use a smartphone – old habits die hard!

phrase: stand on your own two feet
definition: If you stand on your own two feet, you are independent and need no help from anyone.
example: Seven years ago I started to stand on my own two feet.

definition: If someone is all skin and bone, they are very thin or too thin.
example: After trekking in the Himalayas, Brian was all skin and bone.

definition: If something is just what the doctor ordered, it is extremely pleasant and will help you feel better.
example: Going to the gym three days per week? Perfect! It’s just what the doctor ordered!

phrase: hot on the trail of somebody or something
definition: If you are hot on the trail of someone or something, you are very close to finding them.
example: The local police are hot on the trail of the murderer.

definition: This expression is used to describe dark red, usually the colour of a face.
example: Before the speech, her face was beet red.

definition: This expression means that you cannot undo what has been done, so you must live with the consequences of your actions.
example: You should move on. You can’t unring a bell!

definition: This idiom might either refer to one’s family or to the bodily stuff we are made of.
example: We won’t put her into a home. She’s our flesh and blood after all.

phrase: even a broken / stopped clock is right twice a day
definition:
This is used when people get lucky but don’t deserve it.
People use this phrase to describe someone who is generally unreliable, unsmart, or full of bad ideas, but who still manages to say or do something correct by accident.
It serves as a reminder that a correct statement from a bad source does not make that source reliable overall.
example: She didn’t deserve that job but even a broken clock is right twice a day.

phrase: add fuel to the flames / fire
definition: If you “add fuel to the flames / fire”, you do or say something that makes a difficult situation even worse.
example: She forgot their wedding anniversary and her apologies only added fuel to the flames.

phrase: all good things must come to an end
definition: This saying means that everything that is deemed nice, ends.
example: We’ve broken up. All good things must come to an end.

definition: To say that something is music to your ears means that the information you receive makes you feel very happy.
example: The comments I heard were music to my ears.

definition: This idiom means to make plans or hopes that have very little chance of happening.
example: Don’t build castles in the air; just find a job for now.

definition: If you say this referring to a person, it means that they are very wise.
example: You can count on his advice. He’s as wise as an owl.

definition: If you bury your head in the sand, you refuse to face the unpleasant reality by pretending that the situation doesn’t exist.
example: It’s no use burying your head in the sand. We’ve got a problem and we need to solve it.

definition: This idiom means to quarrel.
example: They have crossed swords for watching their favorite TV show.

definition: Something that you dislike when you first taste it, but begin to like after trying it several times, is “an acquired taste”.
example: Maria has always loved potatoes, but for me it was an acquired taste.

phrase: the devil is in the details
definition: This expression refers to a task or a job which appears simple but is in fact more difficult to accomplish.
example: Farming looks easy but the devil is in the details.

definition: If someone meets their Waterloo, they are defeated by someone who is stronger or by a problem that is very difficult to surmount.
example: Steven met his Waterloo when he was challenged by the youngest contestant.

definition: spending too much time and energy on small, unimportant details instead of the big things that matter most
example: He majored in the minors, polishing his résumé font while missing the application deadline

phrase: Take the ball and run with it
definition: to continue an activity or process that someone else has started, often when that person could not finish it or make it work
example: We had a very vague idea of what we wanted, but the marketing team just took the ball and ran with it.

definition: to pursue a mistaken course of action, make a wrong assumption, or blame the wrong person.
example: She thinks it'll solve the problem, but I think she's barking up the wrong tree.
